column1: How is it so easy for a narcissist to walk away from a partner, family, and friends? Will they not miss them?
column3: One of the characteristics of narcissism (as in narcissistic personality disorder) is the inability to mourn. They will lose a pet, and not feel anything. Close relatives will pass away, with no impact. One of the first weird things I noticed about the narcissist I know best, before learning what her condition was, is her mother suffered a delibitating stroke, and she exhibited no sign of grief whatsoever. When she cried, it was self referential, how she was being inconvenienced or unfair treated, things like that. If you think in terms of how a neurotypical misses someone, no, they won’t experience that. Their feelings are self referential, so they could miss the things the given person did which they found to be pleasant. However, narcissists lack object constancy. They also lack the ability to hold an integrated view of one’s personality, whether their own or someone else’s. In simple language, they don’t view people as having both positive and negative traits. Depending on their mood, it’s one or the other. If they’re walking away from someone, it’s because they’re in the “100% bad” zone. Something unpleasant has happened, for which they blame the other person, and they are unable to bring to mind any of the positive things that person has done for them. To summarize, they don’t perceive feelings of loss as neurotypicals do. They blame others for anything and everything negative in their lives, and expect things will improve for them if they discard the friend or family member, so they do so with no second thoughts. They do not mourn the loss of the other, as a neurotypical would, and they do not feel any pain whatsoever for the suffering they cause the other person by discarding them.
column9: They automatically / involuntarily repress and redirect those feelings of rejection. My father directed his shame and guilt into self-pity and violent rage, he also projected his fear of death onto me, along with his guilt. It made him very paranoid and cynical. Due to their personalities being dominated by such rigid defences against any vulnerability, they lack the kinds of insight and perspectives needed to process emotional information, which is not the same as a lack of emotion or being perfectly invulnerable.

column1: What is it like to lose a child?
column3: I will pray that you never go there yourself, it is truly one of the most difficult things life can throw at a person or couple. I suspect how and why has an impact on the ensuing journey, so I'll cover a bit of that, and the rest would take a book to cover. We lost our son 10-1/2 years ago. James at 20 years old when he died. He was a always a wonderful son and brother to our other child an older sister. James was an exceptional student, had won a prestigious scholarship to University and was home for the first summer break. As soon as he turned 18, he had become a volunteer firefighter in our small semi-rural town, and a space and equipment was open when he came home, so he signed on. James died in a tragically stupid water rescue training accident in early June 2005. He was ejected from the boat in an unplanned stupid cowboy move driven more by testosterone of the driver than skill or logic, struck on the head by the prop and died quickly and without lingering. The official inquiry highlighted badly equipped, badly trained and badly planned exercise. A tightly knit waterfront community of 5,200 went from idyllic pastoral life to TV trucks and National Press coverage overnight. Massive Civic funeral with full honors, we were caught up and swept up. When quiet came, we struggled and were numb for a long time. Anger, depression, guilt, denial, you name the emotions and we dealt with it often at different phases to each other. Statistics point to loss of a child as a trigger fro a very high divorce rate, higher risk of suicide, shorter life span, poorer health. If you've got cracks or weaknesses, you could be shattered as an individual or as a couple, or as a family. The best description I have of life after the loss of a child is that when James died a 500 lb weight was strapped to each of us. We still must carry that weight each and every day. At first we couldn't stand up, when we tried to move we stumbled and collapsed under the weight. Slowly, we healed and became stronger. For a very long time, I didn't recognize myself when I saw myself in the mirror, I had dead eyes and little facial expression. I was experienced at grief, I had mourned the suicide of my younger brother a few years prior, and also the untimely sudden death of my best friend and key employee with my small company for over 20 years. I had spent good time in therapy after my brother's suicide, and had tools and I knew the journey I was on. But the death of a child includes the death of your dreams for their future and also their future sons and daughters. If you have a reason to live and love underlying your life, you will find your way back. Honestly, it took 5+ years to laugh easily, and 9 years before I was full re-engaged in my business and planning a future again. I'm shocked that it took that long, I knew where to go and how to head towards that logical place called acceptance, but this was a huge undertaking. Within grief, there is the opportunity for massive destruction. But there is also the opportunity to understand yourself, learn and grow at a level those who haven't traveled these roads will never know. We chose survival, we chose love, we stayed together as a couple and a family, and we feel we have probably accomplished the hardest tasks life could give us. We refuse to take it personally, as hard as that is, this was a random act of the chaotic universe that happened to fall on our shoulders. It has been a terrible curse and a wonderful blessing from what we've learned at the same time. And the rest of our lives will seem somehow easier, even eventually confronting our own deaths. I was asked to write for the local weekly, produced over 200 columns on all subjects and helped heal the community. I have quietly connected with and helped others in deep grief from similar events. I have grown, but underneath my soul is scarred and broken and only those few close friends who stayed with us really understand how deep that damage is. I have grown around the wounds in ways I never imagined, and I am proud of who I was, and now who I am. If you asked this question from need of your own journey, do not be shy to seek help. May none of you need to journey where I've gone, gut if you do I have a deep understanding of the inner strength in every human who chooses to survive and seek life after loss. Be well and seek peace. I had spilled this out in one quick sitting, and am submitting it without even a proof read. I think that give you my off the cuff prioritized spill of my guts rather than a planned structured response.
column9: I am so, so sorry

column1: How do you know that you have completely moved on?
column3: As I was reading through your messages last night, I realised one thing — I no longer felt anger, frustration or sadness at the thought of losing you. I felt content. Acceptance is probably the better word. It's not moving on that I did. It was moving forward. Moving on would imply that your existence in my life was meaningless, that you were simply memories or pictures in an album that I needed to hide in my attic. Moving forward meant that I had, with time and patience, reached the end of the five stages of grief: denial, anger, depression, bargaining and acceptance. With or without you in my life, moving forward meant that every day became easier. The thought of you no longer brought me sorrow. I could understand what went wrong, and how to grow from the lessons you taught me. I no longer resented you; I started wanting the best for you. If I had moved on, I would have deleted your messages and acted as if you never changed me; that you never existed. What I did was move forward, and begin to cherish all the good and bad we had — both of which I'm grateful for.No one completely moves on… ‘Moving on' is an endpoint, but grief does not come with a timeline. At the time of a loss, the feeling of grief is burdening. Over time, it isn't that our grief shrinks, we just learn how to evolve around it.
column9: That’s a great way of putting it, Alisha. Moving forward—because that’s the only way to go. 😊

column1: Can a mother in law destroy a good marriage?
column3: The role of mothers-in-law in marriages, constructive or otherwise, has significant cultural underpinnings. I will answer from the Indian cultural context and include both mothers-in-law (husband’s mother and wife’s mother), as is the right things to do, in my assessment.Husband’s mother:Competing with the daughter-in-law for the attention of your sonA mother and a wife, occupy very different roles in a man’s life. As long as you understand this, you have no reason to worry about “losing relevance” in your son’s life. It’s only when you make it a there’s-only-room-for-one-of-us situation, that you run the risk of being phased out. There’s space for both your inputs, there’s areas where she is entitled to have a greater say. And, for the love of god, there’s more than enough room for both your versions of <insert dish here>. Doesn’t have to be just your recipe or BUST.Trouble relinquishing controlIf you believed, the only strong female presence in the life of your son was going to be you, that’s a problem. Again, it is not a competition, there’s plenty of ways to remain involved in an adult son’s life, without stepping on the toes of his wife. Don’t expect to maintain a tight leash on your son’s life.Not supporting the daughter-in-lawAny mother, that puts her son in the uncomfortable, stressful position of having to pick between mother and wife, is signing up for a lot of grief. You want to be a positive, desirable presence in your son’s life? Start by treating his wife with respect, love and a sense of belonging.Discouraging independence/ interferenceThe family affairs of adult sons are not under your jurisdiction. Yes, you nursed him and made him who he is, sure. But if your goal was not to raise an independent, capable adult, who is able to handle his life and affairs without your constant consultation, you need to re-assess your expectations. Offer to be there for any conversations or guidance and back the hell off.Not letting sons participate in choresThis is a HUGE problem in India. Mothers-in-law will not accept their golden boys doing any household chores. Listen, no one liked doing chores. But, they need to get done and everyone needs to chip in. By coddling your adult son, you are creating resentment in your daughter-in-law and needless friction in their marriage. Teach your sons to participate in running a smooth household. No man ever died, because they washed a few dishes or (gasp!) cooked a meal.Constant negative feedbackYes, it’s appalling to you, that your daughter-in-law does not prepare 3 dishes for every meal. How is that even acceptable?!?! Please realize that your approval is not required for every decision your son and daughter-in-law make in their marriage. If it works for them, it works for them. Stay out of it.Pressure/ guiltingSubtle pressuring or guilting your son’s family into doing things you want done, isn’t subtle at all. Having a genuinely warm, loving, open and supportive relationship with your adult children, will make them want to keep you involved in their life. If you’re having to force it, you’re doing something wrong.Not being open to feedbackYes, sometimes you DO say things that hurt others and being the matriarch doesn’t make that go away. When told you slipped up, consider the corrosive impact it can have on a relationship, to stubbornly refuse to accept any fault, ever. A simple apology, consideration and acceptance can go a long way.Open discrimination between your children and your daughter-in-lawThis is a BIG one. The daughter-in-law will perhaps, never be as dear to you as your children and that’s ok. But if your (adult) children take rest after work and your daughter-in-law is expected to come straight from work and go into the kitchen, you’re actively discriminating. Treat your daughter-in-law like the human being she is. She gets tired too. She works too. She needs rest too.Cooking clashesThere are multiple ways of making every single dish. You may be great at it, but yours is not the World’s Best Way of making said dish. Get over it. Make cooking a bonding exercise, not a turf war. For more on competition, read item 1. Cook together, learn from her, teach her your specialties.Your son is not perfect and neither was your parentingIf valid criticism comes up, don’t act like your son can do no wrong or like it is an attack on you as a mother. It isn’t about you. Yes, the person on whom the sun rises and sets- your son has issues, just like everyone else. Allow, facilitate and accept improvement. In everyone. Including yourself.Wife’s mother-Stop it with the multiple calls a dayIf you are receiving a verbal transcript of every little thing that happens at her in-law’s, that’s not normal. Give her room to deal with her problems. Stop acting like an agony aunt. We all have problems and the more we know a person will listen to it, the more we whine.Do not disregard legitimate issuesIf your daughter is being harassed, abused, insulted, disrespected, don’t ask her to “just adjust”.A baby is not a solution to marital issuesNever, never tell your daughter that having a child will resolve her marriage issues.Don’t coddle your daughterIt is heartbreaking to see one’s child go through problems, but to believe that a person’s life will be entirely smooth sailing, is unrealistic. Trust her to face her problems, learn and overcome them.Don’t treat your son-in-law like a VIPThis is SO common in Indian families. The overly lavish, almost fawning treatment of sons-in-law is disgusting and needs to STOP. And don’t think your daughter doesn’t notice and feel bad about it. When they visit, make some of her favourites too. After all, she IS your child and this was her home.Don’t interfereWhat your son-in-law makes, in terms of salary, is not information that you can feel entitled to. No, you’re not. You’re not allowed to “remind” him that your daughter was raised in a golden cradle and that he should keep her plush. Don’t comment on their standard of living, the size of their house, the sort of car they drive. And DO NOT insert yourself into the personal decisions of the couple.Indian families, struggle with the concept of healthy boundaries. Boundaries are often seen a alienating, distancing and cause a LOT of distress in the cultural framework of India. Mothers, your contribution, role and ongoing importance in your child’s life is in no way diminished by taking a more passive approach to their lives. Parental relationships NEED to evolve over time, as children grow up. Asserting the sort of control you had on a teen’s life on an adult child, is not a sign of love. It is a sign of poor adjustment to a new reality. As your children grow up, you now have the opportunity to see the fruition of your parenting efforts. Trust their capabilities, perspectives and preferences. Take a step back. Take joy in their independence and give them the opportunity to explore their life paths as they see fit. And remember, a mother doesn’t necessarily always know best. That’s why she raises children, who can determine that for themselves.
column9: Enjoyed your write-up. Yes, alas, we still have to understand these relationships. Women’s achievements are usually belittled at their in-laws, sometimes even by their own mothers, the sons and sons-in-law are considered Gods, even if they frequently abuse their wives. I think the only way out is to put up a fight. I know a young girl who responded thus to her MIL when the blame for the son being over-weight was immediately put on her unhealthy cooking— “Sorry, I do not subscribe to your regressive culture, I do not force your son to eat!”

column1: Why would grief continue growing more painful and stronger after a couple of years?
column3: Grief that gets worse over time is not a sign of a healthy psyche’. It a sign of depression and a person who is mentally stuck. They are using that loss as an excuse not to move forward. They dont think they deserve to be here, living their best life out of fear that it would be seen as an act of betrayal to their dead love one. Grief really is nothing but a heart filled with love when a person has nowhere to go with it!. Once it finds its rightful place you will begin to heal. I just turned 71 this year and I have outlived all of my friends except 2. We have been friends for 60 plus years. When they go it will be my turn. Think about all the funerals I have attended. If i counted them all it would be 60 to 70. Maybe 15 were close, and 12 were family members and If I allowed grief to overtake my existance, I would have been in a looney bin by now. One death in particular was really bad because it was my son. He was killed 28 years ago, when he was murdered. All I can say is losing a child is life altering and I have not been the same, but I was lucky enough to have a NDE and saw where he went to after he died. column1: What are the basic signs of having depression?
column3: The symptoms of depression can be complex and vary between people. But as a general rule, if you are depressed, you feel : Sad,hopeless and lose interest in things you used to enjoy. The symptoms persist for weeks or months and are bad enough to interfere with your work, social life and family life.There are many other symptoms of depression and you're unlikely to have every one listed below.continuous low mood or sadness feeling hopeless and helpless having low self-esteem feeling tearful feeling guilt-ridden feeling irritable and intolerant of others having no motivation or interest in things finding it difficult to make decisions not getting any enjoyment out of life feeling anxious or worried having suicidal thoughts or thoughts of harming yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual change in appetite or weight (usually decreased, but sometimes increased) constipation unexplained aches and pains lack of energy or lack of interest in sex (loss of libido) changes to your menstrual cycle disturbed sleep(for example, finding it hard to fall asleep at night or waking up very early in the morning) not doing well at work taking part in fewer social activities and avoiding contact with friends neglecting your hobbies and interests having difficulties in your home and family lifeIf you experience some of these symptoms for most of the day, every day for more than two weeks, you should seek help from your GP.Depression can come on gradually, so it can be difficult to notice something is wrong. Many people continue to try to cope with their symptoms without realizing they are ill. It can take a friend or family member to suggest something is wrong. Doctors describe depression by how serious it is: mild depression has some impact on your daily life moderate depression has a significant impact on your daily life severe depression makes it almost impossible to get through daily life – a few people with severe depression may have psychotic symptoms Grief and depression It can be hard to distinguish between grief and depression.They share many of the same characteristics, but there are important differences between them. Grief is an entirely natural response to a loss, while depression is an illness. People who are grieving find their feelings of loss and sadness come and go, but they're still able to enjoy things and look forward to the future. In contrast, people who are depressed have a constant feeling of sadness. They don't enjoy anything and find it hard to be positive about the future.

column1: My friend’s mother wants to cut her first born child out of her will and give everything to her second born child. Isn’t she better giving the first born a trivial amount to stop a court case?
column3: Wrong!!! The idea of giving an heir $1 or some other negligible amount “to stop or discourage a court case” is a bad idea —- because it makes that person, usually already an heir, a beneficiary under the Will. At least in Washington, an heir wanting to file a Will Contest has four months after the date of the Order Admitting Will to Probate to file a Will Contest else they are barred. Contest of probate or rejection-Limitation of action-Issues. Consequently, if the heir fails to timely file a Will Contest, they lose their position as a person “interested in the estate” and, among other things, entitled to notice of any court proceedings regarding the estate. Had that person been given $1 or anything else, they would remain an “interested person” and entitled to notice. Furthermore, the Personal Representative sooner or later is going to want to close the estate, and to do so, they will often need to file a Receipt signed by anybody entitled to any distribution from the estate. Just how motivated will the recipient of $1 be to sign such a Receipt —- NOT AT ALL —- causing the Personal Representative grief and delaying the estate’s closing. Yes, I have read a ton of Wills saying something to the effect of “My son John or my daughter Mary has caused me nothing but grief during my life, so I disinherit them and give them the sum of one dollar.” Stupid, stupid, stupid. They should simply say, “I disinherit my son John (or my daughter Mary)” and leave it at that. The same argument applies to anyone saying something to the effect of “If anyone contests my Will, I disinherit them and instead give them the sum of one dollar.” If you want to disinherit someone, expressly disinherit them and leave it at that. No need to explain and, for goodness sake, don’t give them anything at all. Richard Wills, retired probate attorney originally licensed in CA & WA
column9: My long-term friend was a Yale undergraduate and Harvard Law School graduate who specialized in Wills, Trusts and Real Estate law. One of his strategies to deter someone, who was disinherited, from successfully contesting a will was to have his client make a video recording stating precisely WHY the potential heir was being disinherited. The recording showed that the person making the will was lucid and not being subjected to undue outside influence.

column1: Is anger a sign of healing from narcissistic abuse?
column3: The stages of healing from narcissistic abuse are identical to the stages of grief from losing a loved one to death, divorce, disconnection, etc. Denial Anger Bargaining Depression Acceptance Understand and study these neurotypical reactions to loss. Understand the person you thought the narcissist was never existed in the first place. You loved a projected image, a false self, an idealized image. We all want to deny our mother, father, spouse, relative, sibling is actually one of these people, however life isn't fair. I am wrong, they do exist and i was luckily removed day one of my birth by someone who cared, loved, and had the foresight to see the damage that no doubt would occur. Others rejected this person, others may have warned you, you may have disconnected from true friends because of this narcissist. Admit what you have done to those you hurt along the way that loved you, those you had responsibility for and let down, those you needed to protect and didn't. Be a DO'r in life NOT a talker. Do not play the victim card for your own poor decisions. Most people after this abuse go right out spewing victim stories and like a cry in the forest wolves will come not a friend. Be a recipient not a victim. Learn from abuse and mistakes if they are your choosing. Get help to change yourself not a pity party. Be around people that make you feel good. Do things that make you feel good. Narcissists always make others feel bad. It is their source of power. A cruel abusive selfish self destructive pattern of conduct that you will now recognize in others in the future. Do not hesitate to remove abusive people from your life. Have agency, self respect, independence. Do not use others financially or emotionally. Create, serve others, build, love without expectation. Study yourself and why you fell for this fake abusive person. Do not be fake or feel you need to be fake around other people with strong personalities. If you have an opinion be ready to say why you have this opinion. If you feel like you have low self esteem DO things that build esteem, read, exercise, work, serve others, create. Love yourself and be yourself.

column1: How can you identify a narcissist?
column3: Good question! Like many others, I had a very painful experience with my ex. Everyone knows breakups are painful and they can bring the worst out of you. Why did this one damage you so much? Why does this person feel like an addiction rather than a friend you can trust. You question your sanity. You question whether their love was real at all. I found so many of the same types of narcissistic behaviour in her and now I think there is defiantly some kind of BPD or NPD. However, I am not a professional by any means. I will save diagnosis for the professionals. That doesn't mean I can't have an educated point of view. So here it is. The gas-lighting, fragmented reality and devaluation arguments. This one is so damn bad. It fucked up my head forever after the breakup. All those arguments about absolutely senseless or basic stuff. You start getting confused and the stories are twisted and suddenly whole scenarios are flipped around and blame is placed on you. Not just once but every time. (How about those odds) Even when you feel like you were trying to do a favour sometimes like clean the house or buy her favourite meal you might be getting brainwashed into thinking you have done something wrong. I found myself trying to explain normal things like I was talking to a child who doesn't understand responsibility consequences or boundaries. The aftermath feels like you are suffering from serious brain damage. She would be defensive even if I approach her gently about a problem. It is always an all or nothing situation. The thing I noticed here, is the constant communication breakdown. Nothing makes sense. It is so difficult to remain calm in this cycle. Complain, scream, physical abuse, retreat, punish, repeat. I could not make progress searching inward or outward to find the problem. (If that makes sense) The problem is forever changing and you feel like the problem is you. You have been broken and the confidence you once had is gone. I started walking on eggshells, becoming very straightforward with my words and talking bluntly because I was getting no understanding. I also became really persistent to understand her.. I don't know if anyone else did this, but I would try to find out why she would create such a problem first and then not be constructive in finding a solution together. She just expected me to fix all her problems like I was an object for use. Communication did not work no matter how I simplified things. After a while, I started jumbling my answers in fear of saying the wrong thing and feeling like no matter what I say to her she will not accept it and let things just be normal again. I would say: "Please stop taking every single point I make as an attack and just hear me out" She would look for a way to misunderstand me and fragment the story. I feared her rage as it went from 0–60 in a second. I was scared of her. It was confusion after confusion to the point you are saying sorry like 10 times a day. I would jump on my bike and ride to work shaking sometimes. I began venting to my friend asking him if this kind of thing is my fault and to be straight with me because I thought I was seriously losing my mind. My friends would tell me I need to break up with her. I had all the red flags but I was loyal and in love and too weak to dump her. She was just misunderstood in my mind we were the same kind of people and she depended on me even tho I wasn't getting a healthy kind of love in return I believed she would notice me again soon if I kept trying. Before meeting this person you were confident had a jump in your step and going in a direction in life. Now you are somehow under this person. In a strange way you work for them and can not get a single point you have across when discussing things that they do to hurt you. Somehow after the one-way argument, it's all your fault. Every time you attempt to fix a problem you make zero progress. You do however become a great negotiator, especially when avoiding the rage this kind this person can dish out. You just say sorry again and do something nice for them like you usually did before. Get pushed around then blamed and accept it for fear of the person leaving. Piece by piece you gave in to them and your self-esteem and confidence is missing. It is defiantly them avoiding responsibility because you know they don't want to be blamed for anything. Getting an apology was like squeezing water from a stone. And when it happened the weak attempt might make them feel shame or insulted to have apologised to you. Hurting you again is the only way to get that feeling out. It's uncomfortable for them to feel sorry. They aren't the problem. It's you of course. they will not stop until you acknowledge it. Sometimes after she raged at me she would start crying and say she became a monster she was really sorry. I could see that she was fighting something in her mind. But after the way she disposed of me in the end its impossible to know if any feelings was genuine. I find that with any of my former relationships. 2 main ones being quite long and very loving, When an argument did happen, we both wanted to fix the problem. With a possible Narc, the arguments were like a routine almost. No learning or growing. “You aren't doing enough or showing enough dedication to them and their expectations. You feel less and less valuable with each week that passes. Things got worse and worse and then the mask finally falls. You might find something dishonest like signs of unfaithful activity or an ex-text or something that the narc can't really explain in a simple gas-lit argument. They are getting back to single life in their minds already because they now have a stain on their name and you are too difficult to manipulate from this point on. The rest is doomed. Eventually, you are hearing words like “I hope you die on your motorbike today” or “I should have left you a long time ago” much more than usual. Somehow you allow this evil behaviour, even making excuses in your mind like “She doesn't mean it”. Deep down you think maybe she actually does. If you are honest with yourself, you don't really feel respectful love to her anymore, there is no admiration. Something is wrong the person you knew is gone and their stories just don't add up. The person they were trying to prove they were in the beginning has disappeared completely and you are forced to accept the irresponsible, aggressive person you have already fallen madly in love with. This relationship is clearly hurting you and you are probably so depressed and anxious at this point you just feel like a dysfunctional tool. She is using the foundations of your life as ammo this might be using your past, your issues at work, your family situations. It's all ammo verbally fired to keep you in line. Combine your own personal pains from the past with gas-lit and fragmentation. Tossed at you by a person you trust and love. It is causing huge mental strain that will consume you after the discard. You may have even picked up her bad habit and are trying to throw it back at her the same way. Dangerous, very dangerous. After you are totally devastated, possibly kicked out of your house or something equally difficult. The pressure to keep them happy with you is impossible now. The arguments get intense fast the words are weapons, they are standing over you trying to dominate you and possibly hitting or pushing you away dividing both of you so they can think about their next selfish move. The discard. The one-way street. I was working full time and paying for all her basic needs already. But somehow I give her another gift, lend her more money, its expected of me and she feels no need to pay it back and it doesn't even cross her mind. I am doing so much more for her then she is doing for me. I feel like if I stop doing these things she will leave me on the spot. I know she is taking advantage of my kindness. Her actions say “yes it is a gift he gave me but I deserve it, I don't need to do anything to pay him back for this and I am with him at the moment so I deserve this”. Cooking a gourmet dinner again after finishing a 12 hour day at work exhausted. "Thank you" it sounds like you handed them a napkin. You never actually feel appreciated. Even you know this is a sure sign that you are dealing with abuse. You just keep making excuses for their behaviour all the time. But everyone else around you respects your boundaries. Except for the Narc, they are the misunderstood victim. They are allowed to walk over you for some reason. (Behind closed doors) Sometimes it's not just you. The Narc’s family members and friends are aware of her and the expectations she has for the people around her. There are always a few that just can not be in a room with them. Her stepmother would totally avoid her. Her father apologised to me after the break-up and in his broken English said: "It's my fault, don't blame her". The confident ones who are working hard or in a steady relationship will only be visited when she has money and something to boast or possibly complain about.. (if they still believe her bullshit..) The ones that are not confident and want her around for their own ego boost, will happily pay with cash, compliment, sex or whatever it is that the Narc is after that particular day. (Probably all 3). She ditched her friend to have a drink with me at our first meeting like he was nothing. I even felt bad for him and he wasn't my friend. I found out later she borrowed money from him and they had a falling out because he was persistent in getting his $10 back I ended up paying it back for her. After the discard, she looked him up and tried to make friends with him again just to speak badly about me. (We were talking for the first time since breaking up) She was suicidal in her text. I also had 3 missed calls so I called back. Supposedly her family refused to give her money to leave the city and go back to Australia where we had just finished a holiday from. I asked her if she would go on a holiday with me and see if we can get back to communicating. She said she could go on a holiday but only as friends and was not interested in talking about “us”. I wanted to go because I thought it would give us a chance to communicate. (Something I have yet to experience with her) the conversation was changed when she asked me for 10,000 dollars as a joke (but not a joke at all). Then asked me for my camera and laptop 1 min after. I could tell she was looking for more gifts or money to take from the relationship as she didn't have anything to show for it. I responded “baby I have unlimited love for you but I am not giving you money anymore. The attitude changed immediately from friendly to goodbye. I later found out she was in a relationship and building a life raft with the house owner from our last trip together. She was more surprised that I found out about it then actually acknowledging the betrayal. It wasn't hard to find out, she was telling everyone she is returning to Australia where we had just left and I had already found texts from her to an old partner previous to our relationship suggesting they meet up while we were staying at my family home back in Australia. Her excuse to those was “that day we had a fight”. My suspicion of her was on point. She was sneaky and selfish and would do anything to make herself feel better if things were not going her way. Victim Mentality If you listen to them carefully you might hear things like this. She said: “I had a friend who invited me to her birthday dinner party at a restaurant last year. We all finished eating and drinking and it was something like $50 each but I didn't want to pay her because I only had a small amount of food and drinks and she has asked me for this money 3 times. God, she is annoying. Shouldn't I have to pay her right? It's her birthday again and I'm not going this time If she invited me then why is she asking me to pay for that anyway”. 2 Choices ~ Choice A - Tell her what you actually think. At first, you might be agreeable to these kinds of things, but in your heart you know it is her friends birthday and she shouldn't make such a big deal about money because everyone else paid their share. Others at the party might not have had an equal share also. But it is a friend after all. She invited you to her party because she wanted to share the moment with you and believes you are in her support group. She is not making a profit. Money is not the point. The point is it is her birthday. She doesn't want to pay your bill for her birthday. Choice B - Agree and nod your head and say something like “wtf... that's really weird”. If you are afraid of the reactions from Choice A, then I think you might be dealing with a Narc. Avoiding responsibility and then shifting all the blame to someone else is a sign of Narcissism. Sometimes it is someone else's fault. Other times you might have been in the wrong but normally people can compromise. With a possible Narc like this, you can not ever have a constructive conversation because it will end in rage. Its been happening to you via gas-lighting and it also happens to other people she manipulates. Its just with you she spends the most time and has to keep the game of charades going. You get this behaviour constantly and the math doesn't add up after a while. You start realising the Narc is full of manipulation tactics like this. You are ready for it and thus the Narcs mask is slipping. Once again the discard follows soon after. They expect special treatment even in a soft way sometimes innocently and very subtle. But in the end, it's just not their fault. Its day and night. How much did this person actually support you ? Think about the things that matter to you and ask yourself if this person actually cared at all about those things. The Narcissists prayer: That didn't happen. And if it did, it wasn't that bad. And if it was, that's not a big deal. And if it is, that's not my fault. And if it was, I didn't mean it. And if I did... You deserved it. Discard I'm sorry, did you get discarded? Did this person break up with you as if it were a punishment that they had to dish out? You have crossed the line and you will be punished as many before you. You ask yourself and others, how can this person have ever loved me seriously? You might not even realise how badly you are craving this selfish, greedy persons attention. You never felt loved toward the end and are just on autopilot trying to please them so they give you the scraps they used to. You get a little smile or laugh, sometimes its a kiss or whatever but you reek of desperation. I believe it was deliberately made that way so that when this discard comes it's a guaranteed victory for the Narc. look at the way they change into a monster and have endless fuel and motivation to destroy you. You are so confused and lost. You want to be accepted back into their arms and you will do anything to stop this torture. Telling them this is like talking to a robot. I don't know why my ex started contacting my friends and made an army of haters against me. She was angry overtime I contacted her. Even calling her balling my eyes out in despair. I told my side of the story to my friends and I somewhat exposed one of her secret affairs with a friend and customer from my barbershop. I needed support but nobody could understand why I was so hung up over a chick. To be honest I had no idea either. Until I started googling question after question and read stories exactly like mine. I watched broken as she moved on at a record pace. There were no boundaries of who she met. Stories of her with my friends are still common today. So many coincidences I lost count of the number of times she went to parties I was invited to by former close friends. (These were people she didn't even know personally) She tells them I abused her and I am violent and a stalker. I admit I did sent her too many texts but have never done anything even close to stalking her. In fact I fear her to the point I will not go out of my shop and stay close to home regularly avoiding any chance to see her in public. I would just get smashed down again for trying to communicate with love and understanding. They want you to know they have moved on. They want you to know you cant effect them emotionally with your begging and pleading. There is no way to talk it out. They are numb to it. Showing you that you really are worthless and have no power. (I also read many people experience a very strange situation here) The Narc will not allow you to feel your own grief. You may be really hurt, in your house or room just trying to keep your self together but they are looking for attention from the people around you. Telling everyone that they are so hurt absorbing all the attention that you might have needed to rely on. Basically mimicking your grief. When you speak to them its like a cold heartless robot putting you down with passive aggressive insults and accusations. Spewing fragmented versions of everything you wish to talk about. Then being bored with you again and dismissing you to add some more pain. My ex-contacted all my friends and started telling everyone I was the abusive person. Her story changed from bad to worse to absolute lies. All over her facebook and anywhere else she could get my attention there were victim stories and I still to this day have not posted a single thing about the situation except a single apology to her when I was blaming myself. I woke up the next day and received call after call telling me to take that “bullshit” off my wall. Nobody close to me believed I was capable of the things she was telling people. That made me change my mind a bit. If I sent her texts to defend myself and tell her to stop posting stuff about me I would say “its heartless and not necessary as I am already fucked up”, the next bit of gossip I receive is of me being a stalker for contacting her. (This is why as hard as it is, No Contact immediately after discard, might be the best advice you can receive. My close friends did not agree with her, some made it clear by walking past her in the street without saying hello. That made her even more motivated to build an army against me. Still to this day she is trashing my name, turning people against me and it has been a year. I am still trying to find myself again so I stopped talking to 90% of people as the gossip is so painful. In the first 4 months, I had stomach cramps, nightmares, anxiety and wake up every morning just feeling stressed, hurt and unhappy. I was loyal to her and I was also in love with the former beautiful version of her. She was sexy, proud and had such confidence. I wondered where she went and was patiently waiting for her to come back. She just got angrier and angrier before discarding me. (That wasn't natural confidence. It was the tip of her secret inflated sense of grandiosity and arrogance.) Closet Narcissism. A flash back of her once telling me she really needed therapy and blames her family for her not being able to share. At the time I remembered it, a year after she said it. I thought this is too honest to be her deepest thoughts. But then again, doesn't it always feel like there was more then one personality with them ? I sure as hell felt that way and I still do. What exactly happened to start such a vengeful cycle? Why did this person suddenly break up with me over me not buying her some art paints? Surely she is aware I am busting my ass everyday for her. I love her so I work my ass off to show her a life and be the supportive person she claims she needs. When you get dumped, you think they are bluffing at first. You didn't know people can turn love off like a switch. Oh, wait it doesn't stop there. They are only starting. You will lose everything possible within her reach now. That includes friends, money, reputation, business, house, belongings.. there seems to be no end. I feel for those that shared more then I did with a person like this. I can not image the pain you are dealing with. They are the victims still and always will be. They are incredibly cold and able to scare you with rage and revenge. (This is a person you believed loved you, how could this have been love?) I think if you experienced any of these you may be dealing with a very unstable person who could possibly be a real Narcissist. I am not a professional and I only know what I experienced to be totally unhealthy. It has taken me over a year to get back to a half day of normal self-esteem by knowing there are really fun, honest, attractive, sexy, smart, vibrant people all over the world who will share compassion, love and understanding with you. I tell myself this every day. Why waste yourself on a person who means to use you and trash you. They are already wasting their lives. Don't let them waste the rest of yours. Weather they can help it or not is not up to you to dedicate your life to find out. Just be silent, allow them to leave without emotions. Prey to god and say thank you for the discard. Use the pain to build yourself again. It is not easy and I am aware these words are also painful to some of you who have tried to pick yourself up and fallen more then once. But as the wise Albert Einstein exclaimed “The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again, but expecting different results”. I made a little self-love project to make sure I do not get depressed at the start of every day. It really works! I bought a plain notebook and write a list before bed of the positive things I need to do to better my life and every morning I focus on that. Alcohol, drugs and other means like sex and lots of parties will not help you long term. You need to build your self-esteem back up. The real source of my pain was that I believed her to be better than me. But once I realised I was a capable man and believe I can change myself and my self doubt. I started getting my confidence back. The bad days slowly disappear. Write the story in all its details, post it here and re-read it everytime you need confirmation again. I know how those moments feel when you start doubting yourself. give yourself a break. You are recovering from abuse and need to focus on healing yourself. Hope this helps some people suffering you were dealing with a taker. That's what they do best. TAKE! Apologies for my spelling and grammar. Godspeed.

column1: What are the symptoms of narcissistic abuse?
column3: 1. Noticeable Behavior Change. They become a person who they were not. The person who you once knew will no longer be there. Somebody who you might know so deeply will turn into a complete stranger. That productive colleague you once admired may turn into an incompetent worker. A once doting and devoted wife will become indifferent. That one optimistic friend who is always living life daily will become gloomy and hopeless. This happens because narcissistic abuse makes a person feel inadequate and unappreciated. Such feelings of inadequacy will then become a root that sprouts the change in a specific person's behavior. They will lose interest, which will reflect on their way of living. They think that their shift in behavior will fit their abuser's standards and change how they are treated. 2. Withdrawal. They feel the safest when they are alone. Socializing becomes minimal or not engaged at all. The abuse has caused them to not easily trust other people. Also, having experienced such abuse is quite embarrassing on their part. In effect, they isolate themselves to avoid judgments and criticisms from others and the abuser. At the same time, believing that further abuse or identical ones would be avoided if they submit into complete solitude. Withdrawal is a means of achieving comfort; it protects them from fake connections, although it cuts off the genuine ones. However, withdrawal is not always voluntary; it could be that the narcissist isolates their victims to seize total control. 3. Emotional Outbursts. Abuse of any form is deeply traumatizing. Trauma will result in rage and outbursts, typical symptoms of narcissistic abuse or any type of abuse. Emotional outbursts could be intense feelings of rage and grief. This trauma could be misunderstood by anybody; being misunderstood is just utterly sad and frustrating. You may be labeled oversensitive or that you have victimized yourself too much. In effect, an emotional outburst takes place. This emotional outburst can be directed to the abuser, the people around who seem not to care, or oneself. Of course, who does not snap when one is slapped with a feeling of insignificance, knowing that the world could go on turning despite your suffering. 4. Panic and Anxiety Attacks. Panic and anxiety attacks are common aftermaths of narcissistic abuse. It is losing control of your own thoughts, actions, and emotions, resulting in sudden feelings of intense fear and anxiety. This may include physical reactions like palpitation, heavy breathing, and shaking. It could occur regardless of the presence or absence of immediate danger. Panic and anxiety attacks often come unannounced; one may feel the calmest of the calm but then unexpectedly lose control. 5. Examples of such trigger reactions could be dramatically walking out of the room or trembling because they saw a whip. Or they may get mad out of a purely thrown joke for humorous purposes. column1: Does ADHD medication also improve ADHD-related emotional dysregulation?
column3: To a point. I'm pretty sure theres a really thin line here, especially with abandonment issues. Just a bit too much medication and you become super sensitive to it. And be very careful of people with ADHD taking medication who lose it emotionally. The first conclusion people come to when they see a man crying is that he is weak. You couldnt be more wrong. A person with adhd feels emotions approximately 100 times more strongly than you. The pain and ,loss they feel is like the world going dark. The tears they shed are the sign of a strong man tortured or driven to the breaking point but holding on. When a person without adhd is hurt emotionally there’s a point at which they disconnect. The normal person will allow someone to emotionally abuse them until the get tired of it and decide they dont like you and put up a wall. The person with adhd doesnt have that ability. It's a funny thing but someone not close to a person who has adhd can say or do anything to him and it's like “who cares". That makes them appear in some cases to be more stable than normal. But in many case that same person can be plunged into the darkest despair by rudeness or in consideration from a SO or someone seriously close. It's because he is in a catch-22 with no way out. When a person with adhd let's someone in his life they mean about 100 times what the same relationship would mean to normal people. Rejection or disapproval is a betrayal at the very deepest level felt 100 times more strongly than you without adhd will ever feel. A person with adhd who allows you to be friends with them values you as highly or more so than him or herself. Accepting rudeness or rejection from someone thought so highly of is incomprehensible. Disconnecting from a person who has been accepted so deeply into their life is equal to that person's death - a loss felt 100 times more than normal. Unable to assimilate that level of grief and loss the person with adhd shuts down and his world goes dark. They cry to let the pressure out rather than remove the source of the pain. Those are not tears of weakness they are a warning that this person's next move is to hurt himself or the person inflicting the pain and he doesnt want to do either. People with adhd are very seldom accepted and understood. That ability or curse of feeling more strongly than others makes them more committed, more able to love unconditionally and more loyal than any friend you'll ever have. They are funny and interesting and usually have extremely high intelligence. They just cant put it all together at the same time and often appear like a juggler with a couple too many balls. But theres a flip side too - in an emergency or high stress situation this person van go into hyperfocus and think and make rational decisions without hesitation. They think at a rate 1p0 times greater than normal people and while you're still recognizing the problem they have analysed it and the consequences of every option and know what to do. In today's society people make the mistake of considering them weak because they cant handle society and the pressure it creates. The reality is they are a throwback to a different type of person with a different type of brain. We have developed a society of farmer-growers where everyone is invested in him or herself and people in general live within a beneficial set of rules. The adhd person, however, has the brain of a hunter - protector. His time is over, and hes forced to live in a way that is foreign to everything he is. He seems grossly inept and often forgetful of little things, highly emotional over what most people take in stride but completely unemotional over things outside of his “group". But put this adhd mind where it belongs and see something worth respecting. In his world people didnt get their own food, it was provided by a hunter in the group who had exceptional skills. In that world a normal person would die of starvation or be killed by the animal they tried to get. That's because the normal person thinks linearly - one thing follows another. The hunter however, must be aware of many things at the same time and needs to be hyperactive and alert to the highest degree. His tribe or people was dependent on him for food and protection and his ability to “foresee the future" or more correctly, see the consequences of actions before they were done. A hunter couldnt make mistakes and had to be supremely confident in what he did - the welfare of hi people people depended on him and it was his responsibility whether they lived or died. Everything we see as a detriment now in adhd was an essential ability for a hunter to survive and keep his people safe. Yes, adhd medication does improve the ability of a person with adhd to live within social norms and expectations. At the same time it takes away the abilities that let us survive in a former time. To have calm feelings you give up connection and commitment and loyalty. To have an ordered mind you have to give up the ability to hyperfocus. To integrate into society you give up self reliance and responsibility for even people you dont know. Those things arent important to most of us because our world has moved on and we think differently and people with adhd are out of place and often rejected and shunned for the way they are. Most feel accepted, and out of place for being who they are. Consider though, if the situation was reversed. You would be the one unable to cope and be dependent on them to live. Do you think they would sneer at you and ,laugh at your inability in their world? Jeremiah

column1: What is the grimmest fact about people?
column3: 1982: With my dad, who raised two girls but never risked being alone with any of our friends. Most of us are too scared of the backlash to speak out against injustice if it isn´t politically correct to do so. Self-interest is paramount, as we value survival and popularity above doing the right thing. That said, one of the most upsetting facts about the people I know personally is the appalling sexism against men in the Western world, especially in the UK and Spain. I´m particularly concerned about fathers’ rights, but am also referring to men as victims of domestic violence, rape, and false allegations from ex-partners that want to ‘bring them down’. Men, on the whole, die younger than women. Maybe they need to do some midnight hikes in codpieces to raise awareness of prostate cancer. Prostate cancer now kills more people than breast cancer, UK figures reveal Women beat up men, too. It´s not a one-way street. Don´t know the statistics on that? That´s because you won´t read about them in the media. It´s not considered ‘sexy’ ie popular as a topic - and if referred to at all, it´s often to poke fun at the male victim. Help for Men Who Are Being Abused I bet you all know the word misogynist, but how often do you hear of misandrists? I had to look it up. It means females who demean or are prejudiced against males. You know, like the idiots who claim that ‘all men are rapists’. You´ve heard of feminism, right? However, there is no equivalent for men’s rights before the law, especially as fathers. If you call yourself a feminist but don´t pay your share according to your income, you´re a sexist hypocrite. Here are some of my personal experiences to illustrate why I feel men often get a raw deal:I know of two women whose fellas didn´t want children. They both admitted in private to faking an accident with the Pill, meaning that they got the baby they wanted, and their partner could like it or lump it - either way, they would be financially responsible the rest of their lives.In any break-up with children involved, I´ve seen ex-wives refuse to allow fathers access, even in defiance of the courts. The man generally gets thrown out of the family home, but still has to pay to support his ex and his kids. One guy I knew had been working two jobs and had done nothing ‘wrong’ - his wife just didn´t love him anymore. Shit happens. But why did SHE get to stay in the house he built, while he had to go to his mum´s? Why was he only allowed to see his son two weekends a month?In Spain, lawyers will advise husbands whose wives try to kick them out to stay in the family home til the divorce terms are settled. “But she wants me gone!” Yes - but then she can sue you for deserting the family. I kid you not. My partner´s ex refused to open the door when he came at the allotted time to visit his kids. They remember hearing the phone ring and their mum threatening to hit them if they dared pick up. He took his case to court. She didn´t show up and was fined a pittance for contempt. She carried on playing games to ‘punish’ him (although she was the one who had left him for a younger man), inevitably punishing her children into the bargain.Also in Spain, there is a special new law designed to protect women from ‘gender’ violence - however it doesn´t prevent child or elder abuse, people in same-sex relationships or victims who are men. Quite the opposite - it´s appallingly sexist. In a recent case, a woman punched and kicked her husband, and was sentenced to three months in prison. He slapped her in response, but got double the jail time, because he had committed ‘gender violence’. Not all women are weaker, smaller or kinder than men. Violence should be violence in the eyes of the law, regardless of gender. www.rtve.es/noticias/20190108/constitucional-fija-cualquier-agresion-hombre-su-pareja-constitutiva-violenciagenero/1865380.shtmlBack to the UK - a women´s husband (my friend) was in a serious plane crash while on duty with the RAF. She changed the locks and sued for divorce while he was in hospital. She then refused him access to spend time alone with his child due to his PTSD and depression, although he had never done anything violent. My friend fought, and lost. He never saw his son again.Also in England, my mum´s boyfriend obtained an injunction against his ex-wife after she broke his nose in a fit of jealousy. She was (is) taller, bigger and stronger than him. She still got custody of the children. She later broke into my mother´s flat and beat her up after weeks of threats. It took two neighbours to pull her off, but she didn´t lose her job as a social worker in Child Protection. My mum was too scared to press charges.I have M.E. (chronic fatigue syndrome) and observe that my male friends with the illness receive less support than their female counterparts. They should be breadwinners, and ‘strong’, right? Society makes them feel like failures, just for being ill. I don´t suffer that sexism, because I´m a ‘girl’ so, you know, poor me. I can curl up quietly and look pretty without being seen as a loser. One of my ME mates prefers his girlfriends to think he´s lazy rather than admit to having a chronic illness. He says they ‘can´t handle it’ - roughly translated: it´s not considered manly.Apart from my mother’s ex-boyfriend, I have known several men who have been physically attacked by their girlfriends. None of them went to the police. Imagine the shame! Imagine what the woman might claim he had done to them. Hell hath no fury like an aggressive woman challenged.Back to Spain. As an English teacher, I work with a lot of National Police - both male and female. Anecdotally, all tell me the same thing. That eight out of ten women who report abuse from their partner don´t have a case due to ‘lack of evidence’ (ie no bruising or other marks on the body). However, in almost every case, the man will spend a night in a prison cell and appear before the judge in the morning. To be fair, if he has bruises or she is aggressive to the police, she might also get a free night´s accomodation at the cost of the State. How many women are prosecuted in Spain for wasting police time or making false accusations against their male partner? Er - none. It's against the law, but nobody wants to go there. Analysis of 8 years of Gender Violence Law in Spain | Gender violence and justiceA female friend of mine once hit a stranger over the head with her shoe, because his dog was bothering hers. He reacted by punching her. She received enormous sympathy and support while he was chased off. I was furious. Did she honestly believe that because she was a woman, she could hit a man without facing any consequences? Well, yes - she did. She felt untouchable and put herself in great danger as a consequence of her arrogance. She remains indignant that he ‘dared’ to hit her back.Yes, I am aware that in many less developed countries - especially Muslim ones - women have few rights, no voice, no power. It´s disgusting. I have also physically dragged away a female friend while her boyfriend was beating her. My sister, as the breadwinner, had to ‘pay off’ her ex husband with a luxury property before he would sign the divorce papers. He sold it, blew the money and is broke again. He insisted on joint custody but refuses to spend more than one night with his son. He can't be bothered. So, I’m not trying to claim that women behave worse than men in relationships. My argument is that it should never be about gender, and that the law - at least in the UK and Spain - unjustly favours mothers over fathers and women over men in domestic situations. Women also abuse children, and partners, in many different ways - using children as pawns to make their ex suffer til he bends to their will or flips out and does something she can get him locked up for. I´ve also observed women-friends ‘fall in love’ with their newborn baby and consequently lose interest in their partner. His role is to pay for everything. No, they don´t want to have sex with him anymore. But why can´t he earn more money? One friend told me she only wanted her son and wished her partner would just disappear (but keep paying the mortgage - she hasn´t worked since her baby was born four years ago and desperately wants to stay in the gorgeous house near her parents that they bought). A bit of context. My sister and I were raised by our Dad after our parents’ divorce, and we only got away with it cause Mum agreed. He wouldn´t have stood a chance in court. Yet, he was the more stable parent at the time. He never dared be alone with one of our teenage friends, in case of a false accusation or misunderstanding. Despite this, we still got a lot of grief from social workers who didn´t approve of dads raising girls back in the 70s. I was a real tomboy, always in scraps and a social worker interviewed me to find out if Dad had caused my bruises. I thought this was hilarious. He told one to ‘f*ck off’ which was monumentally stupid of him, and he quickly learnt his lesson. Play nice, or risk losing everything.
