column1: What is the 8th house in astrology?
column3: LORD OF THE 8TH HOUSE From one film,“Know that nothing remains the same.” The problem is how to accept change, especially if it is not in the plans. The role of the ruler in the signs: The lord of the 8th house is the first significant significator (situation) of transformation in the natal chart. He talks about what crises a person will face, how he will go through them and what will happen in the end. It gives one of the characteristics of what we are afraid of and what dangerous situations we look for on a subconscious level. It is very important in which sign the owner of this house is located. Crises in the lives of fire signs burst in unexpectedly and transformation occurs quickly. One traumatic event or shock changes a person. These signs are most afraid of a bland life. The fear of waking up and not feeling passion for every moment pushes them to rash actions. Together with extreme sports, they attract irreparable situations. For earth signs - a crisis lasting forever. It does not come suddenly, it seems to creep up. Problems can become chronic, and when transformation occurs it is more like giving up. For air signs , crises pass quickly and so does transformation. But without depth. For these signs, crises occur in relationships and they begin to understand something only after they step on the same rake several times. For water signs, crises pass not only quickly and eventfully, but also emotionally deeply. These signs feel that what may await them, therefore, some events are not shocking for them, but if they do not listen to their premonitions, the transformation is painful, although they do not show it. In general, fire and air signs are not afraid of crises; sometimes they themselves are the instigators. Without crises, life will be boring for them. Naturally, everyone has their own boundaries and limits. But earth and water signs, having experienced a crisis once, can make a lot of efforts not to experience something like this again. Crises cause them trauma, which they either take a long time to heal or hide. Lord of the 8th house in the 1st house: You feel a strong need to show the world how you feel about things in the eighth house. If you have occult abilities, then you may have a desire to demonstrate your skills. Many people with this situation in the horoscope have an innate sexual attractiveness. Perhaps it is not entirely clear to you what it is, but still there is some kind of magnetic, irresistible charm that influences people. If the aspects of the ruler are disharmonious, and especially if there are many of them, then even with your wonderful sexuality you will ultimately find yourself devastated. Such people often talk about death, and sometimes even invite it. They are not afraid of death, but it occupies them very much. If the ruler is well located in the horoscope, then you will enjoy the support of other people who help you not only in words, but also in money. If there are severe aspects, sexual excesses can cost you quite a lot, and not only in terms of monetary costs. So you should think about it and reconsider your system of values ​​and priorities. Appearance and behavior have a great influence on the themes of the eighth house - a person can attract extreme situations with his choice. The ability to take big risks and overcome any dangers along the path of development. The need to demonstrate to the whole world your attitude to the problems of death, transformation and rebirth, sex. There is a danger of personality destruction. Lord of the 8th house in the 2nd house: You may become rich through your partner or receive an inheritance. This may also happen because you are lucky, for example with some debt obligations, especially if Jupiter and Saturn are involved and the lords of the second and eighth houses are well aspected. Many people in this situation find themselves protected after they get divorced because they will receive good alimony or keep their job with their ex-partner. 2nd house is the house of words and oratory, but these words can be very superficial if they are not mirrored through the 8th house. If there are planets in the eighth, but not in the second, then you can remain silent for a long time, but when you speak, your words can be so deep, so internally worked out, pumped up, that you will be able to convey deep meanings to people. Income is associated with extreme, crisis, turning point, catastrophic situations. Good luck in banking, insurance business, politics and usury. Often sexual activity becomes a source of income. Lord of the 8th house in the 3rd house: When the ruler of the eighth house is in the 3rd house, the person seeks self-expression in connection with the sphere of the eighth house, and in this case, he also wants to talk, write, draw or sing on these topics. You may turn out to be the life of the party, as you are good at telling all sorts of titillating stories and passing on intriguing rumors. You may have a husky voice that is constantly tinged with sexual desire, sometimes called the “bedroom voice.” When the 3rd and 8th houses are connected in a horoscope, a powerful viparita raja yoga arises. These qualities of the two houses are connected through conflict. But if this conflict is overcome, then you have no equal in collecting information and analyzing this information. Through the third house we collect information (we come into contact with different sources), and in the eighth house we “get” this information and bring it to such an extent that it becomes some kind of powerful scientific breakthrough. This is exactly how viparita raja yoga works when there is a connection between the third and eighth houses. Lord of the 8th house in the 4th house: In the man’s chart there is an idealization of his wife, because he had the same attitude towards his mother. The woman’s card shows independence and independence, asceticism. Such women can live or think that they can live without a man. Good position for real estate. A person can deal with other people's property (eighth house), land, houses and anything else that comes under the scope of the fourth house. Lord of the 8th house in the 5th house: Children can play an important role in your spiritual growth and transformation - more than parents, partners or career. You are able to grasp the meaning of life at the moment of their birth, and you can use this to completely transform your views. Lord of the 8th house in the 6th house: You are able to put a lot of work into running a household and managing the property of your partner or other people. In many cases, you work with your partner at the same job or are involved in some of your partner's other activities, and this is not necessarily a relationship that concerns only the two of you. Since the ruler creates a lot of tension and you have not learned to manage the aspects, your digestive system may be disrupted or some other health problems may arise. An orderly sex life is very important for your physical tone, and if the position of the ruler is strong, your work will give you the opportunity to satisfy all your needs. You can do some research and work hard in this field, but it should not be your official job, but something related to helping others. The connection between the 8th and 6th houses is an equally powerful viparita raja yoga. When there is a problem on the surface level, and you understand with your mind what it is. The 6th house is about routine obligations; this problem is presented to you as some kind of obstacle that needs to be overcome. And the lord of the sixth in the eighth says that you will overcome an obstacle by destroying it to the ground. The eighth house is the third from the sixth house, which means the effort made for the sixth house. This is the yoga that makes a person invincible. For example, a disease is destroyed by fasting. Solving the problem using radical methods.Lord of the 8th house in the 7th house: Many people with such a situation in their horoscopes, one way or another, begin to take care of their partner’s property. They often become financial managers, then the partner takes care of the relevant aspects of the common business. We have a sufficient number of clients who work as lawyers and specialize in industrial property law. Lord of the 8th house in the 8th house: Many people who are sexual symbols of our time may encounter such a situation in their horoscopes. Then you may get tired of adapting to all your partner’s sexual desires, or you will think that sex and everything connected with it is an excess, that you can completely do without it all. If the aspects to this house are not harmonious, you need to be especially careful with monetary transactions and governing bodies. It may turn out that you will get into trouble because of some trifle. Lord of the 8th house in the 9th house: Everything connected with the eighth house gives you a certain optimism, and you have somewhat abstract ideas about these subjects. In this case, the usual mystical and occult inclinations must be multiplied by a religious and philosophical scope. Intellectual abilities can play an important role in your transformation. If there are difficult aspects, you may not be able to fully complete your academic education, which may be due to a lack of financial support or an overly optimistic assessment of your capabilities. This may prevent you from using your original abilities, which could be used in managing the property affairs of other people. The ninth house has a more positive meaning - a time of activity when 8th Lord is still high above the horizon. This is a good time to study and produce various thoughts, including those of a philosophical nature. This is the time when we see our path clearly and imagine life in a positive way. 8th house is considered to be more negative and indicates that we need to look at the other side of things, which will be associated with observing various kinds of dangers in our lives. Lord of the 8th house in the 10th house: This situation can be considered classic for a successful politician who seeks or receives the support of other people in order to achieve his goals, including those related to his career. Sometimes your sex life may become the object of public attention, and if you fail to properly use any unfavorable aspect of the ruler, then it may even lead to a scandal. It is possible that you will choose some profession related to the eighth house. Lord of the 8th house in the 11th house: Your friends can be a great support to you, and with their help you could learn a lot. Many of the feelings associated with your eighth house are directed towards some goal. If you study astrology, you do it not for fun, but to understand your problems. The same applies to the occult sphere, which becomes the object of your research. You can do research in other areas, but usually you need it to solve some other problems, for example, to satisfy your vanity. If not now, then perhaps in the future, but it may inspire you so much that you will immerse yourself in your work and enjoy it. Your views about sex may depend on how much you think you are loved. This is typical of the eleventh house - if you are not loved, then sex has no meaning for you. But this does not mean at all that you have to love another, it is only important that you feel needed and desired. The position of the Moon, Venus and Saturn is of great importance here. Lord of the 8th house in the 12th house: It is difficult for you to show your true nature in sex, which may be due to fear of misunderstanding or increased vulnerability. However, under certain circumstances, the opposite will be true, and you will find yourself involved in a large number of love affairs, although most of them will be secret. If the ruler aspects are heavy, you may focus too much on sex and this will cause problems that will affect your relationships with other people. Your feelings are deep, but not always clear, especially if the Moon has something to do with it. Sun, Mars. They are an integral part of you, but their manifestations may not be noticeable for a long time. Often this situation entails a fear of death, the reason for which may be unclear to you. Eighth house in Aries: Explosion. This man marries, gets divorced, and enlists as a paratrooper; then, however, he has to spend a long time sorting out and disentangling such a quickly and energetically brewed mess, but this happens under other houses. With the defeat of Aries and the corresponding negative experience, a secret fear of any significant changes and generally marginal (that is, borderline, very tense) states is possible; at the same time, they still sometimes inevitably, actively and energetically come, but plunge a person into a state of fear, lethargy and apathy, and he, like an ostrich, hides his head in the ground in a moment of danger, dreaming only that the storm will quickly sweep past and where Somehow she took him out, which, however, soon happens. With harmonious Aries, on the contrary, there is the ability to behave accurately and correctly in marginal states; for example, an athlete who knows how to give his all to the finish line. Psychological crises are of two types: sharp, energetic and fleeting, over which a person has practically no control, and, conversely, depressive-sluggish, which can last a very long time, and here the role of a person’s consciousness and his attitude to what is happening to him and in his subconscious is very important. A person is very passionate about group ethics; when Aries is defeated, he is inclined to oppose himself to the collective and do this, at least at the beginning of life, very stupidly; after outbreaks of protest, the group can completely suppress it, which it sometimes takes advantage of. Elaboration, on the contrary, provides the opportunity to energetically influence group ideology and morality. Good ability to manipulate energy flows, but there is a danger that the flow will suddenly intensify and get out of control, becoming stronger than a person and begin to manipulate him. Eighth house in Taurus Earthquake. Imprisonment. Changes in life do not come easy to this person. They usually drag on for a long time, and he perceives them as hard work that needs to be done both inside himself, gradually adapting to new conditions (a new egregor), and outside, finding, with difficulty and not immediately, his place in the changed environment. Marriage, divorce, change of residence, getting a job and dismissal, even with the most harmonious aspects of Taurus, when everything happens naturally and at the right time, will not pass easily and quickly, and will not go unnoticed in a person’s emotional memory; tense aspects will aggravate the difficulties and troubles of perestroika, and it will sometimes seem to a person hopelessly difficult and, in principle, impracticable, and marriage will be for him a prospect as unrealistic as digging a canal connecting the Black and Caspian seas alone. In borderline states, this person will be required to exert very heavy and prolonged tensions, with a harmonious Taurus this is feasible, with a defeat it is often not; and you need, overcoming your inertia and stubbornness, to look for indirect ways out of tense situations. Psychological crises are severe and long-lasting, it is possible to fixate on certain circumstances that seem to be huge and unshakable obstacles, and until this point of view is changed, overcoming the crisis may be impossible. When Taurus is affected, this is a very difficult patient for a psychologist and psychiatrist; certain physical exercises and labor associated with a psychological problem are shown. A person has difficulty getting along with a group, but if and when this happens, he can defend its interests with the strength and consistency of a caterpillar tractor: in the event of a conflict, this tractor runs over him, he needs to learn flexibility of behavior and thinking and balance personal ethics (second house in Scorpio) with the collective, rather than pitting them against each other. This person has a good sense of the magic of things, objects, and has an ability for massage, especially oriental massage; when he perceives the astral plane, the latter is real to him and filled with completely living beings. Eighth house in Gemini Ruined anthill. With harmonious aspects of Gemini, this person overcomes marginal states easily and brilliantly; at the same time, mental modeling of transitional situations helps him a lot; in particular, he will carefully consider all the details of the upcoming marriage (divorce), change of city or country of residence, proposed work or study. If Gemini is defeated, a person’s ideas about the future circumstances of his life will be distorted, but he will trust them no less; Affected Geminis are generally characterized by lightness and frivolity of thinking, which briskly jumps from one incorrect judgment to another, without worrying at all about its contradictions and inconsistencies. In full accordance with this, the essential circumstances of a person’s life will change: wife, profession, city, country, religion. Psychological crises will be diligently (and often completely unsuccessfully) reflected by a person, but it is much more difficult for him to understand himself than it seems at first. The fact is that an internal problem, located deeply, in this case manifests itself in a large number of small ones, which often replace each other, overall creating a beautiful kaleidoscope that successfully distracts a person (and a psychologist) from the essence of what is happening in the subconscious. The main problem here is the superficiality of analysis and judgment, which can result in a prolongation of the crisis and its transition to a chronic state. This person can very well express in words public opinion on issues of group ethics and ideology, and it is good if it does not contradict his own, which is typical for the opposition of the eighth and second houses, and then they need to be (difficultly) reconciled. In general, the attitude towards the needs of the team is rational, without unnecessary (and often minimally necessary) emotions, which, however, can change during specific group work (second home). There is a mental interest in the occult; a person first of all strives to know a lot, then to mentally manipulate in subtle planes (astral, mental, causal). Ability to hypnosis, auto-training. Eighth house in Cancer Whirlpool funnel. When Cancer is affected, major changes, borderline states and stress will cause a person to feel a sense of mystical horror and a feeling of his inability to protect himself and cope with the emotions and experiences coming from the bottom of the subconscious. Here the level of self-awareness is usually low, and after getting married or moving to a new place of work, a person must simply come to his senses for some time, while his psyche itself is rebuilt (with harmonious aspects of the eighth house quite successfully), adapting to new conditions, and the result is usually can be unexpected for everyone, including the person himself. When Cancer is defeated, phobias associated with any major changes and an extremely negative attitude towards them are likely: Cancer tenaciously clings to existing conditions (but, nevertheless, having matured for changes, he usually rushes into them with all determination). column1: What are some signs of emotional instability?
column3: To be emotionally disturbed is to have your emotions out of your control in a damaging way or to not be able to access or identify your emotions at all. Basically, it’s any state that does not constitute normal functioning. Some aspects of normal functioning, such as grief and anger, look very different when experienced by an emotionally disturbed person. For example, while I feel grief, I also grieve deeply and inappropriately over things like my video games becoming dull or losing interest in a celebrity. Emotional disturbances can also occur to people who otherwise apparently function normally. To be suddenly overwhelmed with your anger until you shake with rage and your vision changes is one such example. Breaking into spontaneous tears and being unable to stop is another. The thing is, emotional disturbances can be controlled through medication, therapy and meditation or a combination of these three. Some emotional disturbances are a result of vitamin deficiency, while others are a chemical imbalance in the brain. Some come from patterns of negative thought. There is not one single way to stop all emotional disturbances, but they can be controlled if the person having them is willing to get help and open about the symptoms they are experiencing.

column1: How can I feel comfortable around my best friend and her new boyfriend? Since he appeared, we barely talk or spend time together.
column3: When I was in my late teens my best friend and I were inseparable. We went to college together, had many classes in common and lived in the same general area of Mexico City. Days after meeting each other we fell into an easy routine: she’d pick me up in the morning, we’d drive to campus, wave at each other during the day, drive back home together in the late afternoon. This natural, effortless rhythm went on for a few years. Those days were a formative time for us both. Of course we spent obscene amounts of time talking about whoever we were dating, but also we described to each other our intricate internal architecture, what we wanted out of life, and who we’d be when we grew up. Everything I know about true friendship I learned from her. She was unfailingly, enthusiastically, wholeheartedly supportive and aggressively believed in me. She was lucid and strong, in possession of an innate ability to move in quantum leaps. I think we had an enormous influence over the people we would become. One day, she met a guy. I didn’t like him, maybe because I recognized him as a threat. Sure, I was jealous, but mostly I knew he was a change agent that would tip over the fortunate balance of my life. My distaste for him - I wear my heart on my sleeve - was hard for her. She experienced it as me being possessive and unable to be happy for them, and I guess maybe she was right. In one of our arguments she told me in total exasperation that I never liked any of the guys she dated. It hurt to hear this because it was true. In my defense, aside from preferring having her all to myself (I have always been a one on one sort of a person) it was also that I knew the men she chose to give herself to were not good enough for her. Time would prove me right. Back then I didn’t have the vocabulary or the emotional skill to do things well. I should have sat down with her and clearly voiced my feelings, instead of so desperately trying to hide what I found unbearably exposing and a sign of weakness. It would have sounded like this: “I am scared shitless. I feel like I am losing you. I feel displaced. Can we please talk this out so we can find our way together?” Instead I was irritated and resentful and difficult to be with. I pulled away. She retreated too and for a few years our friendship became a wistful wisp of what it once was. A few years later she and the guy broke up and my friend and I found our way back to each other. In subsequent life twists, including marriages, divorces, children, grief, triumph, moving to different countries - we became better at making room for each other, letting go of each other, at navigating the fact that life has a tendency to pull you in different directions. We learned to build drawbridges we could lower across vastly varied terrain. Today, many decades later, she is still my best friend. She lives in Costa Rica and her life is very different from mine. Every time we talk I feel in my heart this cosmic drawbridge instantly recreate itself. I experience it in the center of my chest like a shooting star. When either of us feels despair we consider the other the antidote. She lives in my soul - heck, I think she contributed to creating it - and I know I live in hers.

column1: How did Paul McCartney react after the Beatles broke up to the accusations that he had been too heavy-handed?
column3: It must have been hard, relatively speaking, to be Paul McCartney for awhile. Regarded as a villain for ‘breaking up the band,’ he was the one, after ‘67, that propelled the group to keep making music. Post Pepper After the Beatles manager, Brian Epstein died in ‘67, the group was shaken. After all, he handled managing, business arrangements, personal errands, and took care of any unpleasant activities that needed to be dispatched. When he died, the Beatles lost the person chiefly responsible for their financial affairs, but also one of their closest confidants. It hurt the Beatles personally to lose a friend, but it was also a blow to their collective confidence. Lennon Less Sure The one most impacted by Epstein’s death was John Lennon. Brian was closest to John and supported his leadership. So, the death of his friend made Lennon less secure about his future. He was having trouble in his marriage and said later that he’d already been thinking about leaving the band since ‘66. Brian’s death only added to his uncertainty about remaining a Beatle. Paul to the forefront After Brian died and in light of John’s increasing ambivalence, Paul began taking more of a lead on the group’s musical direction. Although all members contributed, Pepper was mostly his idea. So was Magical Mystery Tour, Get Back/Let It Be, and he wrote 50% of the songs on Abbey Road by himself. During the final 2+ years of the group, Paul was responsible for 5 out of the last 7 singles. He lead the way musically. Because he had to. After Aug. ’67 (Brian’s death), the rest of the group devoted less of its energy to being Beatles. All participated in solo film projects. George became interested in India/Indian philosophy. In ‘68, Lennon ended his marriage and began his relationship with Yoko and with heroin. Given these many projects, personal pursuits AND without a manager to wrangle them back to Beatles activity, Paul took it upon himself to keep everyone focused on music. Paraphrasing Starr: Left to their own devices he and John would much rather hang out or stay home…then Paul would call and they would, more and more reluctantly, begin these Paul-originated (and Lennon felt, Paul-focused) ideas. As Paul, to varying degrees, had to keep pressing the others musically, they began to react to his role as musical leader. Lennon said he felt like a “sideman.” Ringo and George at times didn’t like being told how to play their respective instruments. Business creates bad blood In the wake of Brian’s death, the band didn’t replace him for a few years. But after losing money on various projects, they decided they needed someone new. In ‘69, Lennon, Harrison, and Starr wanted Allen Klein—ex-manager of the Stones, others, to take that role. Paul had heard from Mick Jagger that Klein was a crook who couldn’t be trusted (and would go to jail in the ‘70s). Paul refused to sign on with Klein and went instead with his in-laws and experienced entertainment lawyers, the Eastmans. It’s understandable why Paul would want his family to manage the band…it’s equally understandable why the others would feel uncomfortable with this set up. Paul’s family could potentially be biased for Paul and against the others in any future disagreements. This disagreement on managers tainted the personal relationships and amplified the tensions that already existed within the band. It was now John, Geo, and Ringo vs. Paul—business-wise and musically. Tensions in both areas grew. In fact, Ringo and George both temporarily quit the band for short periods. Paul the bad guy So, Paul was seen as the bad guy who bossed everyone around, the one who refused to play along and sign with Allen Klein like everybody else did. He was the bad guy to Beatles fans, too. Publicly, he was the person who announced the breakup and then sued the others to get out of The Beatles. In the early 70s, John and George both said uncharitable things about him in the press. To be fair—Paul’s perspective Every story has two sides. From his perspective, what could he do? Maybe expecting the others to put his family in charge of EVERYONE’s money was a bit cynical or naive…but from Paul’s perspective, it was better than having a crook, like Klein, in charge. He’s trying to protect their income and what does he get for his trouble? Nothing but grief from the very friends he’s trying to help. Musically, it’s much the same story. While the public, Lennon, Harrison etc. are bad mouthing Paul, think of what he went thru. He wants to make music, but he keeps having to motivate his friends to do ANYTHING together. (In their defense, the group was constantly busy from ‘63-’67–about 2 albums per year, a movie, 2 singles, a tour—so they were justifiably ready to ramp it back.) On the other hand, how exhausting it must have been to rally the troops, and then have to deal with your songwriting partner’s waning interest and increasing drug habit? (In ‘69, Lennon added only ONE new song to Let It Be. Meanwhile, he wrote 2 singles and released 2 albums with Yoko.) You have members quitting, taking more dangerous drugs, making bad financial decisions, and, from Paul’s vantage point, he’s doing everything he can to keep it all together and financially sound—and what does he get for his troubles? Criticism from all sides. He was really depressed when the band broke up, with the others criticizing/aligned against him. He would say that he loved being a Beatle and did everything he could to keep the band together. But, he couldn’t stop it from all coming apart—regardless what he did or how much energy he invested. Didn’t Let Me Down This is not to say that Paul is perfect. He could be bossy (even ex-Wings members complained of this). He could be shady—Lennon was hurt when Paul bought up songwriting stock so he owned a higher percentage of songwriting royalties than John w/o telling him (which Lennon felt he should not have done). BUT McCartney’s musical energy filled a void and helped ensure the band didn’t stop in ’67 or release significantly less music. Likewise, McCartney’s lawsuits against Klein etc. eventually saved all of his former bandmates quite a bit of money. Later on, Ringo was very complimentary of Paul’s work ethic and the resulting amount of work they accomplished thanks to him. Even Lennon, before he was killed, gave credit to Paul that the band stayed together as long as it did AND for saving their financial fortune. To the original question, Paul wasn’t always nicest in terms of considering bandmates feelings when he critiqued them. But, as the others eventually came to realize, he did help them produce a large body of work and protected their earnings as a byproduct of protecting his own.
column9: I find it extremely tough to understand how any well informed Beatles fan could have regarded Paul as the “villain” of the Beatles’ breakup. He was desperate for the band to continue, more than any one of the others. He proposed one idea after another for future projects. He urged the others to perform live again. He poured out songs and rounded everybody up for studio sessions. Ringo was OK, but John and George didn’t care any more and wanted out. Paul walked only because the other Beatles refused to be Beatles any more. I really don’t see how any of this is his fault.

column1: Does being frustrated and bored a sign that one is finished the grieving process?
column3: Of all the emotions I feel during the grieving process, frustration or boredom not there. But I empathize with yours, out of respect for you, there is no checklist of emotions that are standard issue. Nothing in the world is normal anyway, after losing your beautifully loved person. You get pushed off a cliff and don’t land for the longest time. The loss of a spouse or partner sears you on the inside and takes apart piece by piece the life you lived on the outside. The lover you spoke to endearingly any time of day or night, gone. The familiar presence, nowhere in the room you are in. The small and sweet rituals of your every day, the intimate life known only between the two of you, no longer the solid ground of your real world. The interests you shared, movies, walks, driving to new places, meals together, weekend mornings sleeping late and making love, nothing much is left to define your days of perfect ease, the paradise of before. Being frustrated or bored may be the sign that it is time to fill your life with what matters to you now. It’s a confounding step you can’t skip. It doesn’t just “happen.” And it’s not terribly exciting. It’s trial and error, hard unglamorous work, taking time. You had no control over the illness or accident that stole the major part of your heart from you. But you still have choices. It’s not a finish of grief. It’s the start of you.
column9: Beautiful. It’s all a process.

column1: What is the hardest emotion to deal with?
column3: Until recently I would not have given this answer; but since my husband died 10 months ago, I have been filled with envy. I never realized to the degree the world is comprised of couples and families. I am daily reminded that I went from being happily married to being single. Envy is a frequent, unwelcomed houseguest of my heart. It rants and raves. It storms and demands it's version of justice. My chest becomes tight with pain as I observe those around me enjoying the plentifulness of their coupledom, signing each other with their silent secret language of two. I feel the urge to yank away their sense of satisfaction and to shred it so that they too know my misery. I'm not happy and I don't want others to be happy either. Envy squirms and twists my heart until all the beautiful qualities have been squeezed out. Where once my heart was full, content, and generous, now what's left is a dried, cold lump of stone. I would have never dreamed I would struggle to be a good friend, or that I would wrestle with myself to support and encourage those around me. Instead, I am filled with the desire to curse them all. Envy is such a terrible emotion. 8/1/16 Update: Thank you for the outpouring of support. It has been three months since I wrote that answer. In the world of grief, time distorts. Every month feels like a year’s worth of living. So in light of that, I thought I would give a brief update. I'm feeling less angry and envious, but sadder. It's a hard feeling too, but there's a greater degree of tenderness to it. I'm more patient with myself, and I'm seeing the fragileness and beauty surrounding me. I'm realizing just how much losing my husband has changed me. I'm stronger yet more vulnerable. It has stretched me and is making me more. It’s a bittersweet awareness—-to know that it has taken something so tragic to cause such growth. I miss him terribly yet don't miss the old me. Such a weird feeling…. Thank you once again for the compassion shown to me and for sharing your stories. You all are amazing people!! 11/6/16 Update I didn't think it was possible, but I have met someone and have fallen in love once again. This, of course is an amazing feeling. Yes, the loss of my late husband is still present, but my heart has expanded in order to love another person. It feels wonderful. This new relationship is bringing about more change. I'm moving across several states so that I can be closer to him. This probably will happen after the upcoming holiday seasons. I am feeling less drifty and more grounded. When I lost my late husband I never dreamed I would actually find love again. I knew the odds were stacked against me: widowed, mid-50’s, highly educated, and intelligent. Yet I chose to believe that the Creator of the Universe in his sovereignty and infinteness had immeasurable resources, including bringing a new love into my life. And he did…. Thank you once again for the amazing outpouring of support you have given me these past several months. ————————-

column1: I've heard some people in the deaf community claim being deaf isn't a disability. Why?
column3: Hearing people...yup. The hearing society has said over and over again all throughout the centuries that their perspective is the only one that counts...because hey, they have all their senses! That's the absolute (and only) definition of NORMAL! The problem with that thinking is that it does not allow for different kinds of normal. This is an example of binary thinking. You see...I was born Deaf. It's genetic for me. It's in my DNA. My children are also born Deaf. It's also genetic for them. This is our normal. Deaf people are visual people. We speak American Sign Language all day, every day. We make our calls through video phones. We use text on smartphones/cellphones like anyone else. We watch captions on television sets and movie screens. We drive. We shop. We travel. We date, fall in love, have sex like everyone else. The only time I experience deviation from normality is when a hearing person or hearing people decide to treat me differently or discriminate against me simply because I'm Deaf. Deaf people also have to deal with ongoing attitudes from the hearing society in relation to how Deaf children should be educated (too many hearing people think that implanting or putting hearing aids on Deaf children solves everything. It doesn't. The only thing that consistently works is to make sure Deaf children have access to their country's signed language and to have their teachers/staff be as fluent in their country's signed language). When access to a country's signed language is intentionally withheld or blocked in favor of voice-only approach, that's when we Deaf children/people become truly disabled. Our ears simply are not the same as that of hearing people's...and expecting us to function in the same way as hearing people is misguided (at best) and ignorant (at worst). All Deaf children, regardless of their hearing level, deserve access to their country's signed language...and this should never, ever be presented as "either/or" scenario. But all too often, the medical industry, audiological industry, and too many hearing people see it that way. Deaf people are normal and not disabled...as long as they are allowed to be visual people who speak their country's signed language as early as possible. By the way, I have also met some hearing people who were born blind...and they feel the same as I do. They feel that they are normal and they aren't disabled. Unlike sighted hearing people, I wouldn't dream of telling these blind people that they're wrong. I trust that these blind people know what they're talking about, because I can relate. I know that being born without one sense does not automatically mean that my life is a permanent case of "less than" or that my life experience is poorer or diminished. That's not the case. Being born with one less sense does not result in a simple "subtraction." Most people then try to say, 'oh yeah, your other senses are enhanced.' Well...yes and no. It's not a case of me having superior sight, smell, touch, and taste. It's more of a case of me using my other senses more effectively. Less superfluous information, if you will. Less distractions...allowing me to focus on what's essential and then reacting accordingly. It helps to think of this question in context of people being born without a sense. They cannot miss what they never had. This is their normal. If you try to think of this question in terms of people losing a sense later in life, then that's where this discussion falls apart. These people do have to go through a period of adjustment when they lose a sense later in life, and it does throw them off, creating a sense of "being disabled." But like a lot of things in life, it's a question of one's attitude, one's mindset, and how one approaches losing a sense. I've seen hundreds thousands of people lose a sense and then after a period of adjustment, do just fine without that sense. It's a process for them, much like going through the famous five stages (denial, bargaining, anger, depression, and acceptance). The problem with these five stages in case of children who lose a sense is that it affects their learning process (like becoming Deaf, for example). They do not have luxury of *years* in going through these five stages, like adults do. Adults can go through these five stages at their own pace (and some of them get stuck at denial stage or other stage and never quite achieve full acceptance). These children essentially have to quickly compensate for that no-longer-there-sense in order to acquire language and be able to get their education. And that's where parental denial/grief can also interfere with the process/5 stages, resulting in their children having language delays and learning issues. column1: When people are grieving do they shut people out? And why?
column3: What is grief? We grieve because we love. No love, no grief. Deep love, deep grief. When we love someone, from the love of family and friends, to the love of a lifetime, we understand that one of us will die before the other. The person dies, the love we shared doesn’t die. Grief is the final responsibility for loving someone. Grief is a powerful teacher about life and love, as we catalog and curate the memories and lessons from a life we loved that is now lost to us. The early parts of grief are intensely personal, painful and often angry, and that pain and anger make isolation a natural response for many. Two people grieving the same loss will have widely different views on the death because they had very different personal and private love shared. They seek answers, explanations and resolution of their individual pain. When my youngest brother killed himself without prior signs or warnings in 2000 at age 43, he left a widow, two young children, two living parents, three living siblings, and hundreds of family and friends to grieve the loss of him. I came to understand that each of the survivors needed to find and form their own narrative and explanation in order to find comfort. Twenty years later, we would each offer a different understanding and explanation. When our perfect 20 year old son was killed in 2005 in a firefighter training accident in our small close knot home town, we each found a different path to comfort without losing sight of each other’s souls. The divorce rate after losing a child is very high, we remain together today because we allowed each other the space to be changed by our common but very individual grief. I say that we had to fall in love again after we each knew we would heal, because grief had so changed each of us in different ways.

column1: Is it possible to recover from the damage of narcissistic abuse without therapy?
column3: Because I have done it I say yes, BUT, having worked as a counselor I was pretty much up on therapeutic concepts and familiarized myself with the additional awareness that I needed by studying the information on Quora from other survivors who had also been through it. For me what started me on my recovery was turning everything over to my Higher Power and even though it was intimidating and I had developed a great deal of fear of being alone from being abused, I decided that since I had successfully survived alone for the majority of my adult life and even raised a child, I decided to face my fears and have faith that I could work it out day by day on my own. I suggest you start by reading through the links below. And you may find that others who have been there can often give you better ideas on how to recover than a therapist who has no experience of narcissistic abuse. Take your time, it doesn't happen instantly, I walked around for almost a year with depersonalization so bad I didn't feel like I even existed after one abusive non-relationship. Instead I felt like I was always screaming in terror on the inside, afraid to be alone yet afraid of being with most men. I know there are some good men out there but I was either not meeting them or just wasn’t attracted to them because they had other unhealthy habits. Keep studying narcissistic abuse, learning about narcissists is key and start by understanding that the devaluation and abuse you have been through was not your fault. This is just something a narcissist will work at daily to convince you that you deserve, you didn’t. No one deserves to be abused whether it be verbally, emotionally, physically, sexually, financially, legally, or any other way. “I've never met a domestic abuser or a person who engages in any kind of domestic violence who is not a narcissist and I hold to my guns on that one.” 1:33 in video: Beware of the narcissist's anger and rage (30 DAYS OF NARCISSISM) - Dr. Ramani Durvasula Spend a long time healing before trying to start another relationship so you will have a clear understanding of how to have firm boundaries in place to prevent being narcissistically abused again. So you must first admit you are powerless over a narcissist and your life has thus become unmanageable, they are not yours, they belong to the universe or to their Creator and they are not your responsibility. 2. Next you accept that only a power greater than self can restore you to sanity and help the narcissist. You may think of this power as therapy, the universe, your conscience, the truth, universal consciousness, your higher self, research into psychology (psyche means soul), the Creator, etc. 3. You make a decision to turn your will and your life over to the care of your higher power as you understand It. You begin by recognizing that you can't control others and therefore you can't control the narcissist. 4. So instead of trying to control what you have no power over you take your own moral inventory about what you need to work on. Make a list of your goals and list things you can use to build your self esteem and feeling of equality instead of using another person as a crutch for self esteem OR if not as an addiction to self esteem boosting love-bombing then for other reasons like for comfort after abuse from that person, dependence on the abuser to help with fears, anxiety, decision making, etc. 5. Admit to yourself, to your higher power, and to another human being the exact nature of areas you need to work on, and your wrongs. You embark on an honest self-evaluation of your weaknesses. This step helps to remove your egotism and helps to minimize your fear of facing life without the narcissist. Talking to someone or writing on Quora helps you begin to feel valued and heard. It helps you to stop blaming others and begin controlling what you can control – yourself. 6. You make yourself ready and willing for your higher power to remove these weaknesses and character defects from you. You may have to do this step more than once as you discover new areas that need work. You agree inwardly to adopt a willing and cooperative attitude to recovery. 7. You humbly ask your higher power to take away your weaknesses and character defects. You will need to understand what it means to become truly humble. To be truly humble you must let go of your pride in your relationship with your narcissist and cease using it to make you feel good about yourself and boost your self esteem. This step helps you see the difference between egotism and a feeling of equality and happiness with yourself. 8. Make a list of everyone you have harmed by holding on to the narcissist, and become willing to make amends to them. If your children have been harmed by this relationship or if you have neglected your friends or family you need to ask them to forgive you. Take comfort in knowing that the first seven steps have prepared you for the strength this will take. 9. Make amends to such people wherever possible. This may mean sharing on Quora, or elsewhere, what has worked for you with others to help shed light on your addiction to the narcissist. Since by participating in the process of using a narcissist to boost your self esteem you have contributed to the overall confusion as to what love is and what love is really meant for and led others to believe we can use someone as an object to boost our own self esteem. 10. Continue to take your own personal inventory and promptly admit it when you are wrong. Steps one through nine have helped you to see the truth about your behavior and how the rest of the world responds to your actions and demonstrated to yourself that you can now see more clearly how to control your actions. You are no longer willing to automatically return to the same self destructive relationship(s) with a narcissist. 11. Through meditation and prayer or supplication to your own higher power, you work on improving your conscious contact with your higher power, universal consciousness, the wisdom of your ancestors, or spirituality, as you understand it, learning to listen to that higher power, and allow Him, Her or It to inspire you, asking for knowledge of your higher power's will and the power to carry that out. 12. Having had a spiritual or inner awakening or a revolution in consciousness as the result of taking these steps, you now try to take your understanding to others who are addicted to a relationship with a narcissist, and use your new understanding of these principles in other areas of your life. You do not however take this to mean you are now strong enough to have a relationship with a narcissist as an object to boost your self esteem or return in hopes of promises being kept by an abuser. column1: Have you ever lost any respect for someone instantly?
column3: Yes. Horribly. And sadly. I don’t make friends easily. I have trust issues from many childhood disappointments. So when I made friends with Penney at church I was delighted. She wasn’t clingy but she opened up to me and I to her. It felt good. Penny was a Staff Sargent in the US Air Force. She was sharp, honest and different. She was the type that cleaned her house from top to bottom every Friday without fail. I never had that kind and of energy. She had no pictures on her walls because they “cluttered the home” and of course her home was always immaculate, even with a young child. I admired her. We leaned on each other through our divorces. We needed each other. I do thank God for her friendship but, sadly, it wasn’t to last. I’ve since learned that there will be many people to come into a life for a specific reason and a season. Penny’s husband was a subhuman like mine. They had been married about ten years. They had one daughter in grade school. Like my ex, her husband was a womanizer and a wife beater. It amazed me how a woman as well put together as Penny was, could put up with his abuse. (How could I, right?) One day, she found out through his messy phone calls, that he had yet, another mistress and that was the last straw. She confronted the mistress first, then him. He attacked her. She called the police and he was arrested. She filed for a restraining order, forthwith, and he was not allowed back into the home. Finally, she said, she’d had enough. In addition to cheating, he was hardly ever working, didn’t share her faith and didn’t seem to care about their daughter. She filed for a divorce and mourned. We talked endlessly. I would go to her home before work just to boost her morale. I would help her dress her daughter and comb her hair. Penney was struggling. I was too but in a different way. I was struggling with the first signs of depression even though I didn’t know it at the time. I was still with my husband but the end was near. We held on to each other. Both drowning in sorrow. Bonded in grief. So I thought. One day after the noise died down some, I stopped by Penney’s house for her to meet my mom. I rarely did that. I also had my youngest child with me, my son, who was my five years old. She opened the door and greeted us warmly. My son saw her daughter in another room and immediately ran to play with her. The next thing we heard was glass shattering. My son had ran smack dab into a sliding door that separated the living room from the den. It was an oddly placed, glass, room divider. The glass was so clean, (no stickers or designs) you couldn’t even see it. Especially an excited child. It was essentially a wall of glass. I was horrified. My son was bleeding profusely from his forehead. Penny grabbed paper towels. My mom almost fainted. I thought, I’ve got to get him to the ER. Penny however, did not show any real concern for my son. The first thing she said was, “That has to be fixed and it’s going to cost a lot”. I was dumbfounded and hurt deeply. My mom immediately disliked her and told me so. We left immediately. Thankfully it was just a surface wound. He doesn’t even have a scar today. But her words cut me to the heart. I could not shake her callous words in the face of my son’s injury. The next call I received from her was about a week later; sadly, it was not her asking about my son. It was to tell me the cost for repairs which I told her I would pay. She never once asked about my son. That was the end of a friendship. I paid the costs and never spoke to her again. I did let her know that she neglected to ask about my son and showed no real concern when he was injured. She apologized but the damage was done. She had shown me who she was. Not a true friend. I stopped returning her phone calls. She, later, left a message that she had been promoted to Chief and was being transferred out of state. She left her new address. I deleted the message. The end.
column9: I’m sorry to hear that it ended like that. I’m going to play devil’s advocate, and plant this thought: it sounds like Penney was still mourning. I know, when I’m upset and have been through some sort of trauma, I don’t always see the bigger picture; I have my own blinders on, which can make me say (or not say) things that I should not (or should) say. It’s possible she was in shock from the past abuse, her divorce and everything that goes along with it, and the glass shattering was just “another thing on top of it all”. It’s no excuse for her not showing concern about her dear friend’s son’s well-being, but it’s a possible explanation for how she acted and reacted. Have a good day!

column1: Can anyone list some signs of maturity?

column1: What does it feel like to lose your parents at a young age?
column3: I lost my father just before I turned nine. He contracted a rare form of blood poisoning which developed into septicemia and was dead within a week. Mostly, I remember just not taking on board what was going on - not believing it, constantly imagining he was going to come home from work. Grief is a very difficult thing to explain, but I think that, given my young age, the thing it most left me with was a massive sense of the profound insecurity of life/the universe, and the knowledge that no-one can ever tell you 'it will be okay' because no-one knows. When I was 13 I developed anorexia, which is the typical illness of people striving to exert control in what they perceive as chaos. It definitely affected my mental health and made me a more anxious person than I otherwise would have been, but I probably suffered less than my mother, or my father's brothers, in terms of missing him as a person because I only ever knew him from the perspective of a child. He was a good father and I wish I had the chance to meet him as an adult. One positive thing did come out of it - my mother won a medical negligence case against the hospital who failed to recognize clear signs of his disease. A lot of the money was put into trust for me and my brother, to be inherited as we turned 21. Because of this I was able to go back to school and earn my PhD, setting me on the career path I truly want, instead of taking any old job to get by.

column1: How do I continue living after my husband has died?
column3: The only way to continue living is to take each breath as it comes. At the beginning, that is all you can do. Breathe. No matter how much it hurts, just take one breath after another. It sounds simplistic, but truly, those first days, it’s about all we can do. Then, take each day, each task as it comes. Try not to think beyond that. If you feel the need to scream, then scream. It helps relieve the incredible stress of grief. Use the energy of anger to help you do what you need to do. As you get beyond those first weeks, try to do new things, things that the two of you never did. Take a walk in an area where the two of you have never been. Write letters to your husband, or write in a journal. Mostly, don’t fight your grief. The more we fight grief, the more stressful grief is to deal with and the longer the process takes. Ours is not a culture that values emotions except for those we label positive, such as love and joy and happiness. We are taught that being emotionally stable means to show a determinedly happy face, to hide our sorrows, to show public anger only in matters of what we deem to be injustices. Because of this cultural conditioning, the wild grief at the loss of a life mate shocks us, terrifies us, and angers us. How is it possible to feel all this emotion and not be crazy? But it is possible. And it is normal. Adding to the difficulty is that not only are we feeling all the emotions of grief, but we also fight them. The more we fight grief, the more afraid we are. The more afraid we are, the angrier we become in order to hide our fear from ourselves. And the angrier we are, the worse we feel. Accepting grief—surrendering to its power and letting it have its way—is counterintuitive. We are used to feeling in control of ourselves, so giving up control to something that makes us feel out of control should make us feel worse, but it doesn’t. As psychologist Carl Jung said, “What you resist not only persists, but will grow in size.” As grief continues beyond the first weeks and months, it becomes harder to accept and surrender because we are conditioned to believe that negative emotion is a sign of weakness. But in a wider sense, emotion is neither positive nor negative. It simply is what it is. Those chaotic emotions we feel come from all parts of our bodies and minds as the grief process does its work. The various parts of us speak to one another in the language of chemicals and hormones and waves of energy, which we feel as emotion. If we stop fighting the grief process, we will still feel all those wild emotions, but we can let go of the fear. If we understand the process, we will realize it is normal—that we are normal—and so we can more easily ride the waves of grief, much like a surfer riding ferocious storm swells. As hard as it is to believe now, you will survive the pain. You might even thrive. But you will always miss him.

column1: How does it feel to lose your pet?
column3: I’ve lost 6 dogs over the past 12 months, so I feel highly qualified to answer this question. EltoWas my buddy. He and I could carry on a conversation. We went everywhere together and we had a special bond that no one outside of us could fully comprehend. When I found his broken body on the highway, I was devastated. My whole world stopped. Williepassed away in early March. I let him out in the morning and he was just as frisky as ever. But that afternoon, he was a bit lethargic. I didn’t think too much of it at first, but as the afternoon turned to evening, he just grew worse. I actually had to carry him into the house to go to bed. I promised him I’d take him to the vet after work the next day. But when I got home, I found him dead, still in the bed where I’d left him. The heartbreak was real as I carried him out and let Waylon (his bio-brother) and S.B. sniff him. I also felt guilty for not rushing him to the doctor the night before. Speaking of S.B. (Sweet Baby), she was a Black Lab I rescued.I feel so much sadness when I think of her early life. She was unloved and left on a chain. After I rescued her, she refused to wear a collar. She and Elto were good friends. And, like Elto, I found her dead on the highway. Yes, I was devastated once again, but this time, I had a mission. See, S.B. had given birth a few weeks prior. She’d kept her puppies hidden, but I could hear them crying for her. So, I was able to retrieve them from hiding. Three beautiful, fat Black puppies. Porter had white toes and belly. Leona had a white blaze on her chest. And Helen had just a hint of a white blaze. Each had a unique personality, but Helen was just a cuddle bug. I made a promise to S.B. that her puppies would have a happier life than her. Believe me, I tried. They were a handful, but very loving. Sadly, one night, they and Waylon didn’t come home. I and some neighbors searched frantically. The next morning, Waylon came home. I asked him where the puppies were and he suddenly looked shocked. We drove out to the highway and found them. At first, Waylon thought they were OK, but as I let him sniff each body, you could see the pain he felt. I cried as I buried them in a single grave next to Mama. I also had to call the vet and cancel the appointment for round 3 of shots. Some time later, I received a card with the Rainbow Bridge poem. Every member of the staff had signed it and said how much they loved Porter, Leona and Helen. I cried as I read each message. So Waylonand I spent some time with just the 2 of us. Then he started telling me that he had mixed feelings (Yes, dogs can talk to people if said people know how to listen). He was lonely for canine companionship but afraid if I got any more puppies that I might love him less. So I told him very clearly, there is absolutely no way I could ever love him any less. He and I-though only together since December, 2016- had shared so much grief and so much love and good times, that no dog could ever come between us. So we went and got Gretchen and Bocephus last month. Yes, the pain of losing a beloved pet is powerful and devastating. But the love they give is worth the pain. BTW, if you ever get a chance to visit Saint Johnsbury, Vermont. be sure to take your dog up to Dog Mountain. This was one of Elto’s favorite places.

column1: What is it like to lose a grown child?
column3: In 2000 I lost a brother to suicide in his early 40’s without any prior warning signs or . He left behind two living parents, a wife, two children and three siblings. My father passed away two years ago, my mother is still living. In 2005 our then 20 year old son died in a firefighter training accident in our small close knit town. As a line of duty death it was seen and treated as a heroic death with a large Civic funeral, etc. So two very different causes of untimely and unforeseen deaths, an outsider might wrongly think that one was easier than the other for the surviving parents. There are no degrees of difficulty in grieving a lost child, in each case the parent will have a significant part of their soul ripped from them with great ensuing pain and suffering. In both cases in our lives, the parents felt a sense of failure to protect, failure to foresee dangers that existed, failure to hold their child back from dangerous behavior. I would imagine the same goes for parents whose child runs in front of a car, or parents who can’t find a medical solution for the disease or tumor taking their child’s life. So age doesn’t matter much in the loss of a child. When we bring a child to our world, from the moment we are aware of conception until our death, we build dreams of and for that child’s life. Those dreams form a huge part of our soul. The only difference from a child in the womb and an adult child is that many of those dreams have become reality and as reality builds we build new dreams for their ever expanding future. The death of a child forever freezes those dreams at the point of death. Nothing more can be added, nothing unsaid can be said, nothing that was wrong can be repaired. So the state of the relationship with an adult child can factor into the difficulty of the grief each parent will carry for the rest of their lifetime. I have come into contact with many parents who have lost children, we’re the club nobody wants to join, we have experienced things that nobody who hasn’t experienced wants to talk about. We have been chosen to live the nightmares of every parent. The pain never ends, but if we choose to allow ourselves to heal we will become stronger than people who haven’t experienced this loss. We will carry the load of the pain of loss every day along warmed by the memories of the love we shared. Never under estimated the strength and power of a parent who has lost a child and healed their soul. But some parents, like mine with my brother’s suicide, can never really heal the loss back to fully loving life again. So, never overestimate the healing of a parent who has lost a child, some will remain fragile for a lifetime. I have a deeply scarred but well healed and resilient soul that can still expand and fill with more love of life and the people around me. Some souls will heal with tight bands of scars that wont’ allow room for new love of life or others. They have become tough and hard to survive and their soul is closed and hard to reach. Each parent will grieve and heal differently as we each have different experiences with and dreams for the child. Many marriages will end in divorce because of the weaknesses in their marriage before the death of a child, or because of the changes that life forced on them when they lost a child. My parents stayed married, but from my outsider’s view their life was never as happy again, they never fully reached the comfortable strength to carry the loss and be really happy. So life became more of an existence than a joy because of the loss of their son. Suicide may have made it just that bit harder to heal, we’ll never know because they did they absolute best and remained loving parents of the rest of their children. My wife and I are still married. We have allowed each other to grieve differently and come to different conclusions via different paths and paces through grief. We each became very different people than we were before, and we are both learning to fall in love with someone very different than the person each of us married. I understand and don’t judge the temptation some might feel to run and seek solace in a different life and love, but I couldn’t imagine me doing more damage to our family by not staying . There are many unintentional offences in people who comfort those who have lost children. We are a society uncomfortable with death, especially untimely and unforeseen death. Example: The mayor of our small town commented in a press interview that our son was unmarried and had no children, so it could have been worse. The facts for us could never have been worse, our dreams of him married with children in the future were as real as could be and those dreams died when he did. There is no scale of pain for a parent who has lost a child. When asked the pain level from 1 to 10, we’d all answer INFINITY. Rest assured, there is no emotional pain that is greater than losing a child. We exist one breath at a time for a long time after, we reestablish life and love very slowly and at times we can look like we will never heal. But we can and do choose to heal, and then the rest of our lives can look easy to us. When you have climbed the Mt. Everest of grief from losing a child you will have a much wider view of life and bumps and hills you encounter will seem like nothing, Even my own eventual and inevitable death will be simpler than what I have lived through. The Universe is an entirely random place that distributes great and terrible things randomly without feeling or logic. With that randomness we humans construct love to link our souls to each other and common causes. The Universe can test and try to destroy those links we call love. We grieve because we love. No love, no grief. When we love someone we implicitly accept that one of us will die before the other, The prevailing logic of normalcy is that the parent wins that bet and never has to grieve the loss of their child. Grief is the final responsibility of loving someone. Grief should never end, because the love we felt should never end. So grief, especially the grief of losing a child, must be incorporated into the rest of our lives so that we may continue to enjoy and remember the beauty of the love that we shared with that child or person. Be well and seek peace from strength you find in love.

column1: How do you deal with unbearable grief?
column3: For a long time, I didn't handle grief; grief handled me. After my 20-year-old son died by his own hand in 2012, I felt not only the shock of losing him, and the gut-wrenching sadness of never seeing him again, but also mountains of guilt to rifle through and come to terms with. Add in the taboo subject of suicide, and I felt like anytime I was in public, I had a big neon sign over my head that screamed, “My son committed suicide!” Leaving me feeling like everyone was staring at me (they weren't). I was ashamed because of the societal stigma surrounding suicide and angry that I thought I should feel this way. Unfortunately for me, these feelings of guilt, shame, and desperate emptiness kept me segregated from figuring out how my life would look now that my son was gone. I began to have more and darker feelings of my own until one day; It dawned on me just how dangerous my thoughts had become. Luckily, this realization frightened me into action. Then, I started to search out reasons to make personal connections I read a plethora of self-help books and discovered what I needed was to find a way to reach out to others who are suffering in their own grief. I started writing, sharing my stories with others, hoping they might find their way to someone who might need what I have to say. Now, here I am 7 ½ years after losing my son, doing what I can to raise others up. So, that's how I deal with grief - I share it with others so we can support each other to make our burdens just that much lighter.

column1: My son died seven months ago at the age of 24 how do I know if he’s in heaven and can he see me and hear me and why have I not gotten any signs yet from him or Mom just not seeing the signs how do I know if he’s OK how do I know if he’s happy?
column3: First, allow me to say how deeply sorry I am for your loss! Go with what your heart is telling you. Do you believe he is in heaven? I strongly believe he is. Our loved ones in spirit can always see and hear us. They may not be with us in their physical form, but are very much with us every day and any time we think of and are sad from missing them. Talk to your son and tell him anything you want, he will hear you. Since his death was in the last year he may still be adjusting to his new spirit body. It could be challenging for him to learn how to send you signs and so on until he gets the hang of it. One of the best ways our loved ones in spirit can reach and visit us is in our dreams. With being completely devastated from losing your son and experiencing all of the emotions that come with it, it can be what has been preventing him from reaching you. I know it may sound strange, but going through the grieving process can put up a wall that prevents it from coming through or from us recognizing it when trying to communicate with us. I will share with you my personal experience in the hope it will help and provide a different perspective. I have shared part of this on a different answer, but left out a important piece that I think will add context here. I lost my mom at 19, she was and still is my deepest loss. I was very angry, especially at God for ripping her away from me at a young age. I still got up every day and took care of my responsibilities working and etc. But, I was dying inside in despair over missing her at a crucial age in my life where life barely begun for me. I told many people including God to allow me to see her one more time and give me the opportunity to say good-bye that I didn’t get as I wasn’t present when she died. I waited every day for her to come see me or get any kind of message through my pain and tears, but got nothing. This deepened the grief for me and the pain would not lessen. This went on for several years to the point I no longer wanted to celebrate holidays and special occasions. I want to say around the 5th to 6th year after her death I slowly started to come around to enjoying those special times again. I think it took me losing my dad at 25 to realize I needed to make the most of what time I have with the people I love who are still living. Through the first several years I would see and hear many things that made me think of my mom. But, I never took any of it as a sign or message from her. At 32 after being married for little over a decade, my husband was having a health problem that required surgery in order to save his life or he would die. As you can imagine the thought of losing my husband so young on top of already burying my parents was more than I could fathom going through. I went to bed one night and was awaken in the middle of the night with a voice speaking to me in one ear telling me everything was going to be ok, it was momma. That was the first clear sign or message I received from her since her passing. It was deeply needed and very healing to get that direct communication from her. From that moment on I felt free and more at peace. With it, I got many more signs and messages from her through dreams and when awake. After having a dream with my mom, I woke up with a song playing in my head. This song has special meaning to me from my mom. It has been many, many years since I last heard this specific song. I knew that song and music was my mom’s sign/symbol to let me know she is visiting me and for me to know the dream I just had was a real visit from her. I realized then there has been many times before I would hear random special songs of my mom’s that would be on the radio playing consistently at different times of my life that I rarely would hear before then unless I played it from a CD. Middle of last year I was driving through the mountains on my way to see my brother for my nephew’s birthday party. As I’m passing through I thought back to the times in my childhood being in the car with my mom going through the mountains to visit family. I began to cry thinking how unfair it is I’m on my way to see my nephew and mom isn’t here with me as she should be to see and meet her grandson. The next song to play on the radio is a song that always makes me think of her when I hear it. That wasn’t coincidence, it was mom telling me she is in the car with me and would be at the party in spirit. This is exactly what I needed and my mom knew this for me to not turn the car around to drive back home. It’s signs like these is how our loved ones will send messages to say hello to make us smile and think of them. What is something your son loved in life that makes you think of him every time you see or hear it? This will be his sign sending his love your way to let you know he is ok and he is always with you. If you come across it at random times or places consistently it is him sending you a sign of his presence. The days and nights you are sad and alone missing him, he is there with you. Love never dies or goes away just because our loved ones are no longer here in the physical world. Their love is eternal just as our souls are. It carries with us each and every single day. Our memories of them is our reminders of their love. Your son couldn’t be any more happier than what he is now living in paradise with God and all loved ones who left to go to heaven before him. He is dancing in the clouds just as he is forever dancing in your heart. Give it time and I assure you he will send you a clear sign he is there with you and never left. Allow yourself this time to grieve as I know it is needed. Any time you cry, know your son is there wiping away your tears telling you not to be sad and you will see him again one day.🦋

column1: Which stages of grief can be identified after narcissistic abuse?
column3: 1. Loss of identity. After meeting the narcissist, you thought this person was going to contribute to the quality of life that you were already living, and maybe they might make it better. But what happened after meeting them? Of course, they stole everything from you. They stole every single form of resource from you until you turned into a shell of yours. You were gaslit and manipulated into believing that you were the crazy one in the situation. You were made to question your thoughts, your feelings, your belief system, your perception of the world, the perception of self, the perception of this relationship. Until it completely got distorted and it became what the narcissist wanted it to become collectively. So you lost yourself in the process. You lost the things that you loved. You lost the interest in doing the things that you loved. You lost the interest in achieving things. You completely stopped living and started existing because you started surviving. So this loss of identity is one of the biggest losses that you experience in the narcissistic relationship because you stop recognizing yourself. You do not know who you are anymore. All that is left is a person with a bunch of coping mechanisms who is now supposed to adapt to this new world that they were disconnected from. 2. Loss of safety. For the narcissist, there wasn't even a single moment when you truly felt safe. Am I correct? Did you ever feel safe in the narcissist or in the relationship? I'm guessing that no, you did not because you did not know how the narcissist was going to behave when something triggered them. So you had to constantly keep adapting, and controlling the environment to make sure that you keep their reactions under control. What did that do to you? It changed you into this person who was constantly hyper-attuned with the environment, hyper-attuned with them, trying to understand how to navigate the system, how to navigate this relationship, to make sure that you are not punished or you do not experience that pain or you are not abandoned or you are not abused or you are not put down. You need to understand that this lack of safety is what keeps you stuck for a while after leaving the Narcissist because you're still trying to navigate the whole situation. Your brain is still adapting to this new and new environment and processing the presence of safety, if you have any, after removing yourself from the relationship and leaving the narcissist. 3. Loss of autonomy. The biggest weapon that a narcissist uses in a relationship to gain control over the other person is that they make them question their own capability when it comes to dealing with the affairs of life. And that is what the narcissists did with you. They attacked your confidence. They attacked your resourcefulness. They made you feel small. They made you think that you do not know how to navigate life, how to deal with life. And they made you super dependent on them. They made you completely depend on them for every single thing so that you lose your own agency and you depend on them for every single thing. They cut off your finances. Ultimately, they reduced you to this person who just became a stranger to the affairs of the world and who does not know how to navigate stuff anymore. 4. Loss of dreams.
