column1: Have you ever felt that your entire relationship was a complete lie, and how do you come to terms with the fact that you were fooled that long? How does one move on knowing that they’ve been such a fool?
column3: My short-lived marriage was an entire scam. It wasn’t real at all. He was fake. His feelings were fake. When he longer could keep the charade going, and he finally found someone that would keep his dirty little secrets with his love bombing and him receiving ego attention deficit every five seconds, he left. Acceptance is the only sure way to come to terms with the truth. Healing will come in many stages. You are experiencing the death of your marriage or relationship and all the expectations that came with it. The only way to heal and move forward is for you to decide if you are going to stay or go. If you decide to leave, going no contact is the only way to start your road to recovery. When there are children involved, it is optional to locate a mediator, and this can be a family friend, Pastor, sibling, family member or anyone that you feel comfortable with to make decisions on your behalf. This way, you will have no reason to contact to speak or see him while you are placing the pieces of your life back together. Moving on is a choice. You must put in the work to move forward with rediscovering who you used to be but just a newer and improved version of yourself. You are going to have days of wanting to quit and to give up, but you must not ever give up! It will not be easy. It is going to be rough like navigating your life through a wilderness frontier. I am speaking from a sincere experience. I am living the life that I just described. My husband left me seven months ago with my children and I discarded and left for dead. He abruptly moved in with his sea turtle chia pet mistress and her children. She is also now expecting. So, when I tell you that I understand your pain, I do. Seven months ago, if you would have told me that I would be in a much better place, I would have spit on you. This is how broken, hurt and angry I was at the time. Once I initiated the no contact rule to start the process of healing with my children and myself, life has gotten a little bit easier to handle. This doesn’t mean that I do not have my moments of rage, anger or how he left us, or how he left me with all our bills ...

column1: How can you react when someone rubs the death of a family member in your face?
column3: Unless you killed someone, there does not seem any reason for someone to “Rub their death in your face”. That reaction is how you perceive it. You may in fact, be feeling guilty over your relationship with the deceased and anything anyone says will conjure up those thoughts. You have to come to terms with your feelings, or seek grief counseling.

column1: I always ruin my days by getting sad over the past or worried over the future. How can I start to live in the moment and make myself feel better?
column3: In my humble opinion, and please be aware that I have no PhD. behind my name, just schooled from experience…sadness about the past, anxiety and worry are sometimes the results to living in a negative state of mind where the small pleasures in life cannot be appreciated and hope is non existent. Or there could be a medical explanation. I will share some food for thought. Words are powerful. They can speak life, and even death. They affect everything we are, everything we attract to ourselves, relationships, health, prosperity, faith, and more. Positive people are generally healthier, happier, have better marriages, loyal friends, and regard themselves with healthy self respect and esteem. They are the movers and the shakers, the life of the party, the incessant volunteer, and they enjoy stronger and healthier bonds with their children and other family members. Positivity can even promote longevity. Negative people, negative words are detrimental to the human experience in every way imaginable. Negativity manifest poverty, divorce, job loss, health issues, low image of self, bad relationships, short friendships and possibly effects a persons life span. That being said, it is possible that you have some type of depression that only a doctor can diagnose and if that is the case, their are many meds available these days that could improve your outlook on life and afford you more happiness. Anxiety and all that comes with it has been proven to be bad for your health, and if left untreated could keep you from enjoying life, as it can cause a variety of life changing illnesses. If it were me, I would definitely mention it to my doctor, as he can give you lots of ideas about why you suffer with profound sadness and anxiety (worry) or if that is not an option open up to a trusted friend or family member. Sometimes just knowing someone cares and will be there for you, is enough to give someone hope for the future and the ability to come to terms with their past experiences whether they were good, bad or ugly. Also there is great freedom and release in the ability to forgive others and forgive ourselves. Forgiveness is positive, healthy and life giving. We attract what we think about, obsess about. Try to put negative thoughts away, ignore them, rebuke them. And replace them with positive words and affirmations, think about what you want and not what you don't have…dream about a future filled with happiness, good fortune, love and compassion. Be passionate about something. Try being a volunteer. Volunteering is a wonderful way to serve your community and get perspective on life. It makes a difference to somebody. And it helps us see ourselves and our world in a more positive light. Prayer is powerful and effective, so depending on your spirituality, always remember God can fix all things, and people who pray to him generally have more peace about their futures. If you are not spiritual , no disrespect intended. Now, make some yummy tea, take a hot bath, then call your doctor, or trusted friend. And start feeling more positive about your human experience. I pray you feel better soon!
column9: What sincere, profound, and wise advice. You very well may have positively changed the course of a person's life. Thank you for what you do!

column1: How does a narcissist view their own mortality?
column3: This is a very subjective question. Every personality disorder is different for every person who experiences it. Coming to terms with one's own mortality is in of itself a process. Some people choose to go their whole life never looking at it (feeling invincible) while others who have experienced severe childhood trauma of witnessing a death of a family member as a young child may process and except it at an early age. I hope you are able to gather some personal stories on your quest for an answer.

column1: In Godfather Part 3, it's apparent that Connie thinks Fredo drowned. Why has Michael hidden it from her all these years? And does she really believe it?
column3: Why did Connie Corleone (formerly Rizzi) continue to believe all her life that her brother, Fredo Corleone, drowned in the waters of Lake Tahoe? She didn’t completely believe it; Connie was sort of just “toeing the Corleone company line,” as it were. Connie was repeating the story the Corleones told everyone about Fredo’s demise (even themselves.) Because Connie had become the keeper of Michael’s soul. It’s emphasized more in the original novel, but certainly not missing from the films, the idea that it’s the women in a traditional family who are the seekers of forgiveness for the sins of their husbands and sons. And, in Connie’s instance, her brother.“I made confession, Connie. I confessed my sins.” (Michael to Connie in Italy) “Why Michael, that's not like you. You don't have to confess your sins to a stranger.” (Connie) “It was the man. A good man. A true priest. He can change things.” “Michael, you know, sometimes I think of poor Fredo, drowned. It was God's will. It was a terrible accident. But it's finished.” [Michael sighs] “Michael, I love you. I'll always help you.” The Godfather Part III (1990)There is a high degree of Connie lying to herself here, no question. But, it was not a complete lie; it was how she and Michael had come to allow the memory of Fredo to be voiced. Being like her mother, Carmela, Connie kept the full truth hidden away from her conscious self, although she understood very well, in the furthest reaches of her soul, the sin Michael had committed. She just couldn’t verbalize it. But, mentioning that Fredo drowned was a way for Connie to convey that she knew what Michael had done, without having to clarify his action in her mind, and without throwing such an act in his face. Because, that is the way it is with a lot of families, let alone, just in the underworld. Brothers, sister, mothers, and fathers… very often, they know of many awful things they, or their parents, or siblings, or children have done. It’s a part of the family code that these things won’t be said out loud. So, these most awful sins are rarely discussed as they actually happened. These sins are only verbalized by what everyone has consented, usually by trial and error, and silent agreement, to repeat out loud. Because Connie probably couldn’t have gone on as she did, if she had ever wholly accepted the truth. Not after Michael had already had her husband killed, only to follow that up by killing their own brother.“Michael, I hated you for so many years. I think that I did things to myself, to hurt myself so that you'd know — that I could hurt you. You were just being strong for all of us the way Papa was. And I forgive you. Can't you forgive Fredo? He's so sweet and helpless without you. You need me, Michael. I want to take care of you now.” (Connie to Michael at the viewing of their mother, Carmela) The Godfather Part 2 (1974)Connie went through a period, after Michael had Carlo assassinated, where she was drunk, or high, or both, twenty-four hours a day, seven-day-a-week, at times getting married and divorced in the same month, and paying no attention to her children. In short, she was the female version of the Prodigal Son. After Carmela passed away, Connie returned to the Corleone family fold, making peace with Michael, who was the only person remaining who loved her without reservation, and wanted nothing financial or physical from her in return. Connie finally came to recognize Michael as the head of the family, as she had loved and recognized their father, Vito Corleone, despite knowing he was a gangster, and all that this entailed. She came to terms with what her family was, how they achieved their power and wealth, and she reached a point where she understood that Carlo was responsible for Sonny’s death, and that Michael could only respond to what Carlo did with force and violence. And, importantly, Connie came to this rationality before Fredo’s death. Remember, she begged Michael to forgive Fredo, and let their older brother back into the family after Carmela’s death. That wasn’t just an attempt to mend fences between angry brothers; Connie feared for Fredo’s life. She knew, first-hand, what the consequences for betrayal of a family member was, and she tried to remind Michael that blood should be thicker than water.“Anthony!” (Connie calling from the Lake Tahoe compound lawn) “He's here; we're goin' fishing.” (Fredo sitting with Anthony on the dock) “He can't go; Michael wants to take him into Reno.” “Ah. Okay, kid, you got to go to Reno with your Pop.” The Godfather Part 2 (1974)But, after that, there was no more express discussion on the subject; communication from that point on, was by action, not with words. Fredo was welcomed back to the compound, but, at some point, Connie probably realized that it was simply to keep him close, so Michael could keep an eye on him. Connie was no fool; when Michael decided, completely out of the blue, to take Anthony with him to Reno, Connie very likely suspected the worst. But she had done her best to convince Michael, and there was no longer any point in trying to defend Fredo further. All Connie could do from that point on was obey Michael and follow his instructions and wishes. And if she wanted to discuss anything important, it had to be in vagueries, and lies that were close to, but never completely the truth.
column9: Michael could be very cold indeed. His father was kind, caring and compassionate. But make no mistake he new how to ‘deal’ with unpleasant things. Even his bad ass son, Sonny, feared him.

column1: How did the deaths of Steffon Baratheon and Cassana Estermont affect the psychological development of Robert, Stannis and Renly? How were their behaviours shaped by the tragedy?
column3: I’d say it’s most obvious with Stannis. I don’t remember if it was a show only bit or if it was in the books too, but he says that the day his mother and father died was the day he stopped believing in the Faith of the Seven. I don’t think it really effected Stannis’s overall psychology, and Stannis would probably still be Stannis regardless of what happened to Steffon and Cassana, though it did impact his overall development as a character. Most likely if they had made it safely back to Storm’s End, then Stannis almost certainly doesn’t ever find himself turning to Melisandre (well… That and the plot also likely looks pretty different). Robert is… Tricky… Becoming the Lord of Storm’s End before he was 16 did mean Robert came into power and authority likely much earlier than expected. I don’t think he in the long term was ever truly traumatized or shaped by the deaths of his parents. It was something sad that happened in his past, yes, but Robert was already on the cusp of manhood. The biggest thing that I would say it changed was his overall perceptions of authority and power. At this point he was the one with the ability to make a marriage for himself, which meant he got to serve as his own representative when making his betrothal with Lyanna, and handle all the lordly duties. It marked an end of childhood of sorts for him, as he was thrust into lordship. I actually find it interesting as a comparison to Robb Stark, who like Robert, is based on Edward IV, and who also had to deal with the death of his father around this same age. In both cases, Robb and Robert I do think set out with the intention of trying to embrace manhood and lordship, and doing well in their new positions, though they both took power before they were completely ready and suffered for it. Both still kinda yearned to just simply have their father’s back, who could handle all the hard decisions and be someone to look up to. For Renly, it’s hard to say exactly, as he was only like 1 or 2 at the time if I recall correctly, and wouldn’t have really understood what happened. The specifics of the deaths of his father and mother aren’t all that important, as they were just simply absent in his life. For him, I’m not entirely sure Steffon and Cassana surviving would fundamentally change Renly as a character… But I think the bigger impact that it would have is just in the overall relationship with his brothers. This gets into a broader point among all three of them, but the death of Steffon and Cassana in many ways removed the strongest shared link between Robert, Stannis and Renly. Robert and Stannis obviously have very contrasting personalities, and with how Robert was fostered with Jon Arryn at the Eyrie from a young age, it’s clear that the two never really shared all that strong a bond. And Renly was about 14 and 12ish years younger than both of his older brothers. So they wouldn’t necessarily be the most tightly knit group of siblings in the world, compared to say… The Starklings of the main series… But taking Steffon and Cassana both in one go did really remove the biggest shared link the brothers had. It cemented their family dynamics. Renly would always be the baby and annoying little brother of the family, because well… Robert and Stannis weren’t parents, and didn’t see themselves as parents… Which is why even at the start of the series when Renly is a grown man in his twenties, and even as the Lord of Storm’s End and Master of Laws, Renly doesn’t really feel like a true peer to Robert and Stannis… Without Steffon and Cassana their to raise them, Robert and Stannis both to a point really had to take up soft-parenting, and trying to fill that gap for Renly, but then that also ended up getting abruptly cut short with Robert’s Rebellion as now Renly was still living mostly at Storm’s End while Robert and Stannis lived far away. And so in a way, Robert and Stannis never really saw Renly grow up, or saw him as an adult. In their eyes, they still saw themselves in the sept where Steffon and Cassana’s funeral was being held, generally feeling sad when their little baby brother who still had a wet nurse started crying and both had to struggle to avoid saying, “oh great…” aloud.Actually… I take back what I said about it not really impacting Renly’s overall psychology as an individual… For Renly, as he grew older and gradually coming to understand what happened to his parents left him already kinda disillusioned from a pretty young age. He never really had any stable parental figures in his life, with people like Robert, Stannis, Cressen, and others all coming and going, while he was basically given a castle all to himself. And while he had everything he also in many ways had nothing. It’s why Renly doesn’t seem overly attached to many people, and comes across as being so superficial, always putting on the display of the charismatic young man who cares, but deep down really doesn’t. Because of a very few selected individuals like Loras, Renly never really felt there was anyone who truly cared for him. I guess it’s also why I imagine Renly and an aged up Myrcella would be good friends. Myrcella, like Renly, didn’t have very reliable parental figures, but in how it shapes them creates a really nice contrast between the two of them. Where Myrcella finds a deeper desire to try and be better for her younger siblings and eventual children and other family members, Renly generally just puts up a more superficial exterior, with the illusion of empathy. But they both still struggle with attachment and trust issues, and for Myrcella especially, find each other to be among the few people they can really rely on.
column9: “…but then that also ended up getting abruptly cut short with Robert’s Rebellion as now Renly was still living mostly at Storm’s End while Robert and Stannis lived far away.” Pretty sure Stannis lived with Renly during this time. Stannis was the one holding Storm’s End from Mace Tyrell before being relieved by Ned after Rhaegar died. Stannis lived in Dragonstone after the rebellion, not during or before.

column1: What does it feel like to have your sibling die?
column3: I lost my younger and only sister, Morgan, almost exactly a year ago... on July 24, 2011 in a plane crash. I was 25 and she was 19. The thing that makes my story difficult is the fact that not only did I lose her, I lost my dad (who was the pilot of the plane), my mom, and our two dogs, Stan and Fran. It was my ENTIRE family, aside from our cat, Richard, who ended up passing away in March at the age of 16. Because I lost all of them, I find it hard to think of them individually sometimes which I immediately feel guilty about because I think they deserve being treated like individuals. Then, as soon as I start talking about one of them, I feel guilty for not thinking of them all. It's this odd, endless cycle of guilt and I can't help it. Anyway, I got the call the morning it happened from my mom's sister who lived out of the state. I didn't answer her first few calls because it was so early on a Sunday, but then I listened to the voicemail. I still have it and it haunts me. She just told me to call her back and that it was very very urgent but I could hear the trembling in her voice and it immediately scared me and woke me right up and I called back. When she told me the news, I was in my bed with my boyfriend who woke up after hearing me basically scream and cry into the phone. I couldn't even talk or make out any words. I couldn't do anything. My heart just literally hurt, there is no other way to describe it. I felt like all the air was sucked out of my lungs and replaced with weights. After awhile, I just kept saying "ALL of them?!" as if I thought it was some cruel joke. I can't tell you how many times I had to relive this memory in my head. My boyfriend and I ended up moving from that apartment just because I couldn't deal with being in that room anymore, too painful. I obviously still struggle with being orphaned and being deprived of my sister and I think about them every second. I remember after I found out, my boyfriend and I drove the two hours or so to where my family lived and we went straight to my grandparents house where all of our friends and family were waiting. It was also the town outside the one where I grew up where the plane crash happened. Some people chose to go to the crash site, but I never did. I didn't need to see that to know they were gone and I don't think I could've taken more pain at the time. But it was actually one of the more beautiful memories I've ever had. I remember looking around and just seeing so many close friends and family (from both sides which rarely happend) in one room, hugging and crying. No one had to say anything. The great thing about my family is that they made everyone feel pretty special, so we were all hurting just the same that day. Another thing I remember is just being furious. I remember just telling my Grandma, "Why wasn't I on that plane" and I remember how much she cried harder and it freaked her out. I was almost mad that they left me here, that I couldn't go with them (they were headed to Florida to take my sister to her internship and to relax at our family vacation home) and I even thought of how the last time I talked to my mom was on the phone and I begged her to let us watch the dogs for them, but she refused; she loved them just as much as I did. I often times get angry that they were taken so abruptly. I wanted a chance to say goodbye and tell them that I loved them, but I remember to keep myself in check and be thankful that they didn't have a chance to suffer. In fact I like to think that's why they were taken so quickly, perhaps to prevent pain that they might have experienced later on in life. In fact, I don't even know if they knew what was happening to them. They hardly made it into the air before the plane toppled over from a freak gust of wind. That I am thankful for. I'm also thankful that we were not in any fights with each other, we always said "I love you" when we hung up. We truly ended on good notes. I also find that I'm most upset about my sister because she was so young. She was super smart, athletic, talented, funny, hard-working and absolutely gorgeous. She made everyone around her happy and she never took anything too seriously and she was just an all-around really good kid. So my immediate feeling was just utter confusion and loss. Why would someone like her deserve to go so fast? She would've been a sophomore at the University of Chicago (which I loved because I live in Chicago too and I could see her often) and would've been finished with her volleyball season by now. It's the epitome of unfair. So now, after a year, I have found ways to remember her. My boyfriend and I have a new house and we brought all of her furniture in (the paint color was even the same color as her bedroom at my parents house, it was freaky) and it fits beautifully. When I'm feeling sad or when I miss her, I just walk to the room next door and take a minute, or curl up on the bed and cry. It is strange, though, because I constantly have dreams in which only my parents have passed and she is still there, or vice versa, or it's just one parent. Or sometimes they come to me, knowing they have passed away and say they've returned. I wake sometimes thinking they're still here and just a call away and it really makes mornings difficult for me. Still, though, I talk to her friends often, some of whom I've known since they were babies and toddlers. I know they hurt like I do sometimes and I know they knew the funny/awesome side of her, but I still sometimes feel very, very alone because a sister's bond is unreal. I talk to my aunt about this often because she and my mom were very close and they were the same age apart as my sister and I were; I find it really reassuring. I have yet to talk to a counselor for reasons like this; I know that no one could feel the way I do. Most people lose a sibling, a parent,or all of them, but rarely this early in life, rarely all at once, and it's an awful feeling to be that alone. For now, I try to do things like scan old family photos and share them on Facebook for our friends and family to see. It's comforting not only to me, but to everyone who knew her. I try to share her story. I don't know how I'm going to feel when I'm 50 trying to imagine what Moe would've looked like when she was 44 (probably ridiculously fabulous) but I'm hoping time will have healed some wounds by then. For now it still feels like a dagger in my heart. EDIT--- After reading Nikki Van Noy's answer to this question (which I suggest you guys read), I'm compelled to comment on a few things that she brought up that I failed to mention. 1. The "neon sign" effect, or as I have called "the kid glove" effect in which people just know what you've been through and don't know how to talk to you or deal with you. Some people ignore it and are scared of it, some people smother you with love and won't leave you alone, some treat you like some weird psychology experiment and just creepily like your Facebook statues and don't ever say anything, and some are just straight upawkward. It changes everyones view of you, good or bad, that's for sure. 2. The jealousy that involves others who have lost someone. In my case, it's when someone has lost a single family member and tells me "they know how it feels" but they don't really, because they still have other immediate family members to grieve with. I also am jealous when people lose a sibling at an older age, and try to compare our situations. You got to spend more time with your sibling, you got to have more memories! It's frustrating. I've spoken to a woman who has lost her whole family, her husband and two children. We've lost the same number of people in our family, and it was our entire family, but even then, it is not the same situation and neither of us could pretend to know how the other feels. 3. "'Broken heart' is a LITERAL term" like Nikki says. Oh my gosh yes. The feeling is indescribable and literally feels like someone squeezing your chest with a vice. The feeling subsides for me from time to time, but it always aches in the background. 4. "For those of you who still have your siblings, try your hardest to appreciate them--even during the difficult times." Enough said.

column1: What's the saddest scene in all of Star Trek and why that one?
column3: Let me introduce you to Legate Demar, former Gul and Glin of the Cardassian Union, underling to Gul Dukat the acting head of the Cardassian Union and family man with a wife and children.He served with Dukat on the freighter Groumall, which earned him a permanent place at Dukats side after the Cardassians formed an alliance with the Dominion. During the war with the Federation he was constantly the most reliable figure for Dukat to call upon.That is until Dukat went insane at the loss of his daughter. At this moment Damar was thrust in to becoming the head of the Cardassian Union. Already a heavy drinker his dependency increased as the war went on and looked increasingly as if the Dominion would lose the war. Damar saw his people increasingly becoming cannon fodder, hundreds of thousands of men died waiting for reinforcements that the Dominion never even committed. Then the Dominion welcomed the Breen in to the alliance without even consulting the Cardassian Leader. Damar had enough he stopped drinking and went to work. He used elements loyal to him to destroy vital facilities belonging to the Dominion, thousands of Cardassians were killed in the assault but he proved his point, that the Cardassians wouldn’t become a subservient race to the Dominion, or the Breen. His powerful move bough the Federation time, but he was a conventional leader, unable to think in the terms of a Guerrilla warfighter, so the Federation sent him some help.The Federation sent Bajoran officer and former Guerilla fighter Kira Nerys to provide training and support. The Cardassians and the Bajorans had a long history of poor relations ever since the Cardassians occupied Bajor for resources. Many Bajoran’s were subject to torture and summary execution at the hands of Cardassian officers similar to Damar and his former mentor Gul Dukat who had even been the leader of the occupation forces. Kira helps train them and on a mission a report reaches Damar.Garak: "The Dominion has succeeded in locating Damar's family." Damar: "They're dead. They weren't a part of this rebellion. The Dominion knew that. The Founder knew that. Weyoun knew that. To kill her and my son... the casual brutality of it... the waste of life. What kind of state tolerates the murder of innocent women and children? What kind of people give those orders?" Kira: "Yeah, Damar, what kind of people give those orders?" This hits home, it angers him but he knows she’s right. There’s three different angles to work from here, Damar is devastated at the loss of his family, his sadness is clear he can’t understand why anyone would do this to his family. Then Kira connects it to the occupation of Bajor, ‘what kind of people give those orders’ suddenly becomes answered ‘yours do’. Kira quickly realises that her comment was brutal, decensensitive, ‘that was stupid’. Then Garak, a Cardassian himself and self proclaimed patriot tells her ‘no, it’s what he needs to hear’. It’s powerful, years of Cardassians not understanding the pain they inflicted on Bajor not comes to realisation for Damar. He can’t help but connect the two instances, he can’t oppose it because it’s true and blatant. This is for me one of the saddest scenes it connects so many things and forges the leader Damar wants to be, not the warmonger but the leader of a free Cardassia making up for its crimes and joining the intergalactic community again, without the Obsidian order, without occupations, he will make Cardassia better out of it.But now on to the saddest scene, the Cardassian liberation front disables planetary power severing communications with the fleet engaging a major Federation offensive. The Dominion warn the population by bombarding Lakarian City, killing all 2 million inhabitants. In response the Cardassian fleet turns at a critical moment and breaks the Dominion lines forcing a retreat to Cardassian prime itself, home of the Dominion forces in the Alpha quadrant. In response the Founder orders the mass extinction of the Cardassians as a people.In the hours of bombardment 800 million Cardassians are killed whilst the formidable defences of the which were once themselves manned by Cardassian’s are now being used to prevent anyone from stopping the genocide. In a final act to stop the war Damar leads an assault on the command complex, passing dead Cardassians as he does, even the ones of Dominion puppets no one is being spared. He charged with his men, leading from the front, but Damar gets shot by a Jem’hadar soldier.It’s a quick but painful death, with it goes a man we have watched emerge from a minor job as second in command of a cargo ship to the head of a powerful military alliance, down to terrorist and then back to an inspirational leader who has learned much and is the best hope for a Cardassian future. Most likely Cardassia’s best chance of becoming a great member of the interstellar community is destroyed with him and the loss of his wife and children has even less meaning as the lesson he learned from it now dies with him, on an Alleyway in a bombed out street on a dying planet. With his death Cardassia may be doomed to repeat its own history of a world reliant on its police state and occupation of other worlds, if it can recover at all.

column1: What does it mean when you have a dream of an already dead person redying?
column3: It probably means that you haven’t truly come to terms with losing that person. I’ve often had dreams about friends and have family members who have died. In one dream, I saw a deceased friend and he was alive. I told him he had died and that I went to his funeral. He explained that he had faked his death. I suppose I wasn’t ready to accept that he was truly gone. I was never even that close to this person, but he was my age and we went to school together. That dream was probably more about my own mortality. And I’ve had that particular dream many times. I’ve also had numerous dreams about my grandmother. She’s also alive and I’m so happy to see her. And then I remember. And I realize it’s just a dream. Our minds have a funny way of dealing with loss sometimes.

column1: What person destroyed their entire life by making one simple mistake?
column3: Me! I was 18 years old and came home one morning and found my 21 year old brother dead from suicide. No one else was home, he had hung himself in our garage. Closeby was a handwritren note, several pages of harsh blamestorming towards my Mother, my Father, and me as well, and others. He was heartbroken, and had been deeply in love with a girl in college that my parents disapproved of. This note was so strongly worded that I decided then and there that no one else should ever see it, so I destroyed it and called 911. BIGGEST MISTAKE OF MY LIFE. Police show up and ask about a note. I lied and kept that lie up and subsequently the unanswered questions in each of my family members hearts and minds ate away at relationships and broke apart family relationships as parents, cousins, friends, and myself spent years blaming each other and all sorts of imaginings. I wanted to try to remember exactly what the note said so that I could come clean and “fix” my error, but much time had passed, and I forgot the details he wrote and it was too late. I thought at the time I could be some sort of hero, and save my Mother and others from his angry words. In hindsight, I concealed the very truths they each needed to hear to process his life and his death, and I became a liar and self aggrandized manipulator of The Big Secret that only I (and a few therapists) knew. That was 40 years ago. His birthday was on Valentines Day, and he took his life 2 days after with a broken heart. I have been broken ever since, and will never be whole again in this life. Please learn from my mistake and never conceal the truth, even if it may hurt someone in the short term. Carl in Clearwater FL
column9: First off, please stop shouldering everyone’s grief. You read that letter in a state of, I don’t even know what the word is, pain? I don’t think any word would appropriately describe it. You and you alone found your dead brother. Not only was he dead, I’m sure it wasn’t a pleasant sight. I’m sure you went into a state of shock. Then you read the letter. Of course you burned if. You couldn’t protect your brother. Whom you loved. so you. Without the benefit of clarity of mind burnt the letter. Forgive yourself. You’ve done nothing wrong. Honestly, I would consider telling them, perhaps a “light” version of what the letter said. Whatever you decide please please find peace. You deserve it.

column1: Anytime something major has happened in my life, like a death of someone important to me, I shut down emotionally. When my dad died when I was 12 I felt dead inside. I didn't cry or feel anything and I couldn't talk about it. What's wrong with me?
column3: I was four years old when my mother died. I remember very clearly (or at least think I remember) how it felt, and I remember being aware of a decision being made inside me not to be broken down by this crushing grief. I remember my brother crying for weeks and my father being distant from this point onwards. I didn't want to be broken like this so I didn't cry. I pushed everything down inside me and built up a wall inside myself. I'm not sure how much rational consideration a four year old can make in a situation like this, but this trait of "stepping back" emotionally from these kinds of situations is something which has stayed with me ever since. I now tend to be much less prone to getting carried away with situations, whether in a positive or a negative way. Scroll forward twenty years and my sister died from leukaemia. This time around, as an adult I at least had the ability to observe my thoughts and feelings a more. And although there was still this protective layer inside me stopping me from getting washed away by the surge of grief as everyone else seemed to be, there was a voice inside me saying "this is how people die, I remember this feeling". I was able to acknowledge what was happening, engage with the powerful feelings but not be utterly crushed by them. I was able to cry, to feel loss, to feel the pain but not to feel as if I were going to be destroyed. I think what I'm trying to express above is that there's nothing wrong with you. A situation such as losing a member of your family is a big deal. If you live in a westernised country such as I do, then you also have to content with the fact that death is very much a taboo subject and therefore everyone else around is trying to come to terms with the situation, too - it can be a very lonely place to be. We all have to try and come to terms with life (and death) every day and the way we respond to these situations will always be unique to each of us.

column1: Is there a solution to money-hungry media houses of India who are openly breaking all sensibilities during a national tragedy?
column3: I will start answering this after questioning your short term memory, because people tend to forget. How many of you remember,#GoHomeIndianMedia [1]which was trending during Nepal earthquake insensitive reporting?Erroneous reporting of 2008 Mumbai attack[2]? Do you know they have reported false information concerning the number of attackers, their nationality, their organizational affiliations, origins, and the methods of transport they had used?Jasleen Kaur media trial, where Sarvjeet Singh was portrayed as a ‘pervert’ and ‘molester’. Failure of journalism.[3]Do you know, most of the news is paid[4]? This type of news is typically sponsored by politicians, businessmen, and celebrities in order to improve their public image or accomplish political goals. Often such articles are carried under the name "Special report".There are thousands of examples I can go on with. Recent IAF air strike and Abhinandan’s media coverage was another slap of idiocy on our face. They do not care about individual’s life or country’s security. They all want TRP (Television Rating Point) and they have mastered how to fool their audiences. I agree, you and I are educated people. You don’t believe in media bullshit, but if you open Whatsapp or Facebook you will see thousands of forwarded messages which do nothing, but spread lies. Even educated people forward these things out of emotions. Official statement was yet to come, but Indian media declared that 300 militants were killed in the air strike. Well recently Amit Shah said in one of his rallies that more than 250 terrorists were killed, but we are still waiting for an official statement. Indian media: “Pakistan pe fateh” (Victory over Pakistan). They have made blunders over blunders. Abhinandan was captured in Pakistan where he refused to give any information about him, and these people publicized every data about him. Do they care about the life of Abhinandan?But the question is, what is the solution?Huge number of news channels.According to a report in 2016, there were 892 television channels[5], out of them 403 were news channels. High competition and foolish audiences, what do you expect? Quality? Then stop fooling around. Like I said earlier, you and I are educated who will not believe in these media bullshit, but do you think your father, mother or other family member will have same influence like you have? Let me tell you two small examples of journalism:News Channel 1.We are going to show a report, where India has done air strike on “Jaish-e-Mohammad” camps. We are yet to receive further information, where death toll of militants is unknown, we are waiting for an official statement.News Channel 2.Hold your heart, India has done powerful strike on “Pakistan”, they have avenged the death of our 40 martyred soldiers. More than 400 militants have been killed and from our “sources” Azhar Masood also got killed. Stay connected, we are going to show, how Indian fighters have done it, which planes were used, what was their strategy, who were the pilots, and we will meet their family members. Now tell me honestly, which News Channel you or your family will stick to? Did you see, how they spread lies? 400 channels, fight for TRP, fierce competition, and fight for staying ahead will always lead to spicy, false, and paid news. Solution: Government should decrease the number of news channels.Private Channels which are owned by businessman, politicians etc.These are private channels, not operated by government. But how many times have you questioned the authenticity of their news? Never. Or maybe few times. When you questioned, were they apologetic for their content? Never. Obviously, you will be forced to watch what they want you to believe, but not the truth. Solution: There should be some strict law monitored by a government body when they air some false news to gain TRP. Control over their content, where they shouldn’t compromise with National security or someone’s life.Limitation of Indian mediaWe all know they are TRP hungry people, but few people are aware that there is a root cause behind it. Censorship begins from within.“Most journalists including editors are employed on contracts of three years or less, with an exit clause that permits them to leave or be fired on a notice of between one and three months. As a result, journalists have lost the courage to speak up or write about any issue that owners and managements do not want them to, including the issue of their own unstable working conditions.”[6]Solution: If there is imbalanced work environment, where you don’t know when you will be sacked, you are forced to come up with lies to save your job. Only government can interfere in this matter.These are my two cents, your opinion may differ from mine.Footnotes[1] Indian media facing a backlash in Nepal[2] Erroneous reporting on the 2008 Mumbai attacks - Wikipedia[3] When Media Takes Over Justice: Why The Jasleen Kaur Case Is Journalism's Failure[4] Paid news in India - Wikipedia[5] Total of television channels in India rises to 892, with three cleared in June[6] Selling the Fourth Estate: How Free is Indian Media?

column1: What happens if a pensioner’s death and a family member does not inform the bank and collect a one-month pension?
column3: In Indian Context: when pensioner passes away, the family is suddenly forced to come into terms with his loss. Final rites and mourning period takes a toll on the spouse and close family members. However well educated the departed person was, it is Herculean task for the family to gather the marbles. It is not intention of the family members to cheat the pension disbursing authorities; it may be difficult for the spouse to move out. Searching for PPO, pass book etc would be stressful for the entire family. When the bank gets information finally of the death of Pensioners, do they adjust the excess Pension paid very fast and balance family Pension due to the spouse is disbursed by the bank after a few months. It is a sad reality that Nationalised banks have never covered themselves with glory on this issue because they take minimum three months to make first disbursal of family pension to spouse of the departed pensioner.

column1: How important is it to let go of the people who hurt you badly especially the ones that are close to your heart?
column3: The need to let them go is always incredibly important. If they hurt you so badly while they were close to your heart; do not let them continue to hurt you after they leave. If they can have that much power still it is always them winning, and they don't deserve that. However if we are speaking on coming to terms with the death of a loved one, let it out. Vent, cry, please keep eating, but also talk about it! I've lost so many family members and cousins that had a special place in my heart. It takes time and lots of self healing but no matter the cause of pain I hope you get through it, I have faith in you.

column1: How do I co parent with a BPD ex? How do I tackle her lies during trial? Are they not worried on being found out in court?
column3: How do I co parent with a BPD ex? How do I tackle her lies during trial? Are they not worried on being found out in court? So unfortunately I can answer this question fairly accurately. My preference would be to know nothing about this disorder or dealing with this, but alas, I am here to share with all in the most humane way possible. For the afflicted that will read this, I want you to know that I have a heart for your disorder, the heinous treatment that got you here. Most likely if you are afflicted and you are reading this, you have an interest in getting the hard parts of your disorder in the rear view mirror. If you are diagnosed or have Cluster B traits, treatment is available, and you can live a symptom free life. But it is work. For those of you that have the diagnosis, that wont go to treatment, continue to create a trail of psychologically dead bodies behind you, I truly hope reading this will trigger you into a psychotic episode that gets you professional help. If you are in treatment, THANK YOU for caring about you and caring about the Nons. The key to dealing with the ex in regards to the topic is a little different depending on whether they are male or female. Dont overlook that your ex or ex to be likely also shows up on the Narc scale. Or what I have read and like, the bordernarc scale. Narc’s are very easy to deal with, much like a comorbid female. You win by treating them like a Rattlesnake. Follow me.Do not be aggressive.No sudden moves.Back away slowly.Winning means losing.Let me elaborate. You may or may not have learned that when BPD/Narc splits black the only chance of putting them back together is splitting them white, aka, “ I’m sorry, it’s my fault. I didn’t mean to hurt you, blah blah blah”. So lets break this down. If you are involved in a recent break up, even if a long term marriage, you need to start reading a lot. The first thing you need to learn are the rules of engagement. This is going to sound hard but it comes from a former Marine Corp Colonel who is a lawyer and specializes in helping people divorce borderlines and Narcs. You have to come to terms with the fact that they are never coming back. They don’t love you like a normal adult loves another adult, even in a long term marriage. Their version of love is not nourishing, reciprocal adult love. They have one goal; winning. It is the only way for them to avoid shame and that is all that matters right now. Your job is to allow them to win, just not what they want to win. They are like children so they are extremely easy to manipulate. Part of the disorder is an absolute inability to regulate emotion. This messes with the reasoning/judgment area of the brain. Frontal lobe. As in their brains look different than a non’s. Its from the trauma of maladaptive parenting, hereditary behaviors and trauma. Once you get that through your head, you need to come to terms with what is really at stake and you MUST GET THE RIGHT KIND OF HELP. You need a pro therapist and a savvy lawyer. Their attorney will be coaching your soon to be ex to make you look psychotic. So YOU CANNOT TALK to them, you cannot text them and you cannot email them. You must do all through a third party until the divorce custody issues are settled. The first thing you are going to say is “ I have to at least text about the kids”. USE A THIRD PARTY UNTIL THE FINAL DECREE AND SETTLEMENT. Trust me, you cannot see or read anything from them, it weakens your defenses. If not a lawyer, then a family member. THIS IS A BIG DEAL. Since you are a real person and not a reptile (untreated Cluster B) you are going to be all over the board until you get out of the fog. All that crap you write, say, text etc, that’s on the table physically at trial. My ex had a three ring binder with tabs. It will be lopsided in court. She will have a book of your venting and you will have nothing because she is not grieving or emotionally invested in you, the marriage or the kids. Her only goal is to make you look insane, blame everything on you, deflect and humiliate you. Remember, this person COVETS YOUR DEATH. If your goal is to get the kids, they have to remain in your house, the clothes, school, everything. You cannot talk to the kids or in front of the kids about the ex. You are in a war. Remember, the afflicted have a motto “The person who cares the least controls”. They actually say this shit. Once you get over all the shock and BS, everything you said under duress will be thrown in your face and used to make you look crazy. Remember they do not have this issue because they dont care about you, and they dont care about the kids like a normal parent. They cant, they dont actually have the capacity to love or attach in a normal way so you are way over your ski’s thinking you control anything with them. And remember, they are banging your replacement and getting coaching by someone they have known for five minutes while making you out to be a psycho that abused them for the past bazillion years. So get an infrastructure around you, keep your trap shut, fingers off the keyboard and texts. Because when you cut them off from talking to you, they are going to go berserk. The primary trigger is indifference. This triggers their subconscious pain from mom and dad and they will literally go into melt down mode. Even if they have split black, they will come running back to you. But only to get another shot at discarding you in the most humiliating way they can. You must follow this piece of advice when they come back or want to meet with you or start sending you overtures. I need you to remember a couple of things.This relationship is over, has been over and has never started. This is not a real human being, this is the shell of a human hosting a broken child who is mentally ill that you cannot fix. If you mess this part up, they get a second shot at you and this time they are going to really hurt you. DO NOT BE ALONE WITH THEM UNLESS YOU WANT TO GO TO JAIL.They will have been coached by now that if they can get the cops to arrest you that they will have a better chance at getting the kids. They will have been coached about a ton of stuff by this time. You are divorcing a child in an adults body that reasons like a child and wants to win like a child. They will want things in the divorce that are worth almost nothing but they believe will hurt you to give them up. Fight, but intend to give in. While you are distracting them with a fight (supply) they will take their eye off the ball. Often the kids or bigger assets.They eventually get found out regarding their lie, that is why they seldom keep the kids unless the other parent is a Narc. Narc’s don’t care about kids. There are plenty of stories about BPD’s getting pounded by a judge for lying and losing custody. They don’t want the kids, they just don’t want you to have them. They will eventually come to you.As far as being found out, the problem is they don’t see the difference between truth and lies. They are so used to lying that they don’t even recognize it as lies, everything is rationalized, same as a serial murderer or rapist. Their brain is broken and they simply dont recognize their behavior as bad. God only knows their justification rationale, but they have one.At trial you will want to have written down everything she has said to you or texted you. Make sure the setting on your phone and her phone is saving texts. This is an option with most carriers. Make sure you have the password for both phones, not the afflicted. They will have been texting their replacement or other people not knowing that you are going to print all these texts out on the afflicted persons account. That may contain stuff relating to sex with farm animals or whatever these people do and they likely will cave in to end any dispute with you. I didn’t have the password but said I did and that I had printed all her text with her side piece in case the judge wanted to see them. CAVE!! During the whole affair you have to have a lawyer that has done this before. Their lawyer will find out during the whole deal they represent a BPD or Narc and often bail. Most of these people go through 3 or 4 lawyers because the lawyers hate them and just fire them. My attorney said you have to “pound them to dust” during the divorce and custody hearings. They do not respect nice and they have to be made fearful to even see your name or the lawyers name. Everything that is done with them has to be scorched earth. You will NOT EVER BE FRIENDS with them. You will NEVER have a relationship with them. You will always be hated by them. They will covet your death every morning, cursing the air you breathe. This is the only way they can survive the toxic shame that is the root of these disorders. You will experience the entire affair as a death, the death of the person you loved so dearly. And the hardest part will be when you finally come to terms with the fact that they didn’t love you, not the way normal, non Cluster B folks experience love. Not that they didn’t want to or that you are not loveable, but because they cannot. They lack the capacity to attach normally. They are always trying to attach to mom and dad. Until they work this out with a real therapist, they will be like the cat who is always nursing on everything from being taken off the mother too early. I made so many mistakes, gave years of my life to someone that would not piss in my mouth if my teeth were on fire. Actually said to me, “ just because I don’t want you doesnt mean I want anyone else to have you”. What they are saying is “if you make a relationship work with another person, it means we failed because of me”. And that is the root of toxic shame right there. That is why they secretly would prefer to be the grieving widow or widower, not the ex. Ex’s talk, go on living, have actual normal relationships and are happy. You moving on successfully snaps all the breakers in their breaker panel. SNAP. I will finish up with this. I have a heart for afflicted people. Especially ones that know something is wrong but just cant figure it out. I have a real heart for those in therapy. Those that know they are Cluster B and say “thats just me, take it or leave it”. I strongly suggest you leave it. God Bless.
column9: So many similarities to my mad BPD ex and our divorce. Her lies were found out but after years of legal hell for me. The kids are safe with me and my new partner. Only my our youngest has shared care. Unlike your advice my barrister, in the UK, played it really cool, and we did not use any evidence I had gathered. The whole thing is so unfair but I had to prove I was the stable one, when I look like a bit of a bruiser, while she looks like an angel but is the devil in disguise. column1: Why did King Charles decide to give a new title to Prince William but not Prince Harry?
column3: This MAY have escaped the OP’s notice but Prince Harry resigned from the role of a working royal. In the UK someone who resigns from a job does not get considered for additional recognition, it is a quaint hangover from historical precedents. Harry gave up his work supporting the monarch, as he wanted to become independent of his family and try to make his own way in the world. He went first to Canada, and then settled in California. The working ties with his family have been severed, but that is a consequence of ‘stepping down’ from a job. The king is the head of the family and has the task of assigning tasks and conferring honours to those who are involved in supporting his reign. Prince William is the heir to the king he received the honour of Prince of Wales from his father in the first public announcement the new king gave. Harry having left the ranks of the working royals, and moving to another country, received the kings good wishes for a successful life overseas. it could be summarised as Prince William -> working for the monarch = gets the perks for doing a good job. Prince Harry -> not working for the monarch = no additional perks Recently the king has been diagnosed with cancer, and is reducing his involvement in certain areas of his reign. One such ceremonial duty he has recently transferred to his heir. Prince Harry was not considered as he had resigned from carrying out such duties some years ago. So of the two candidates the OP mentions, one is working to support the monarch in his work and the other left the work to go his own way. The task went to the one who was working for the monarch. update in the UK the system of honours is controlled, the monarch can grant an honour, such as honouring his heir with the title Prince of Wales that is a tradition that goes back to the fourteenth century ( or so) it need not be granted but if a king does grant it it is to the heir apparent. King Charles having vacated that title on becoming king recreated it naming his heir Prince William as the new prince of Wales. Simultaneously the king who had been Duke of Cornwall also vacated that title as it was returned to the crown when he became king. The duchy was set up with an estate to provide for the expenses the heir to the throne would experience in supporting his position in the heart. That change is automatic as Prince William is Charles ‘s older son and his heir so when the old incumbent became king the title became vacant and was filled by Prince William, so Prince William became Duke of Cornwall taking on the duchy from his father he is the kings heir and in the death of King Charles Prince William will in turn become king . So Prince William became Duke of Cornwall as the heir to the throne, the position having been vacated by his father when he became king. King Charles III recreated the title Prince of Wales with Prince William being the recipient of the title. Hopefully this explains the titles Prince William gained when his father became king. Prince Harry resigned from being a supporter of the monarch so as a consequence received no enhancements to his existing titles. There is an issue that whilst understood in the UK may not be understood outside the realms affiliated with the monarch. That of remuneration for the service to the country. In America the head of state is the president, who is paid from federal funds. When they come to the end of their term(s) as president they receive security and a pension funded from the federal budget. In the UK the remuneration for the head of state’s services are funded in a different manner. Two royal duchies have estates attached, the profits from those estates are used by the title owners to fund their expenses incurred on behalf of the state. The estate of the duchy of Lancaster supports the monarch and funds the expenses they incur whilst carrying out their duties on behalf of the country, while the estate of the duchy of cornwall supports the heir and their family in carrying out their duties for the country. The crown estates are property owned by the monarch, but managed by an external organisation who sends the profits directly to the treasury, with a small part being returned to the monarch to fund his work as the country’s head of state. This work is mostly carried out by the monarch’s trusted family members, their expenses while in official duties are funded from the money returned to the monarch from the crown estates payment. When Harry resigned from supporting the monarch he also cut off his access to those funds, a point he mentioned in several of his interviews when he complained that his father cut off his allowance. Prince Charles had been paying Prince Harry an allowance as he had been working for the monarch, which when he said that he would not return to those duties caused the payments to cease. A case of no work, no payment. When his father became king, Harry’s position remained the same, he still did not work for the monarch so did not receive additional honours nor any income. Which is not the case of his elder brother.

column1: Will William wear a certain crown during the coronation of Charles?
column3: Yes and no. William will not wear a crown during the coronation of his father. In the United Kingdom, the term ‘crown’ is reserved only for the headdresses of the sovereign and the (female) consort. Rather, royals and noble peers will wear what is called a coronet. The coronation of a new sovereign is the only time peers and most royals will wear a coronet, and there are different, prescribed styles depending on rank.Coronet of the Prince of Wales There have been different coronets for the Prince of Wales made at different times. In 1728, a coronet was created for Frederick, Prince of Wales (son of George II), although it is unknown if there was ever an opportunity to wear it. According to some sources, this coronet was later worn by his son George III and his grandson George IV when each was Prince of Wales.[1] Another was created for George V to use as Prince of Wales (in the reign of Edward VII). This was the coronet worn by Prince Edward, Prince of Wales at his father’s coronation in 1911.A new coronet was created for Edward for his investiture as Prince of Wales at Caernarfon Castle in July 1911, about one month after his father’s coronation. It was worn (as below) as a circlet rather than with ermine trim and internal velvet cap—it is unknown if this was designed to be fitted with an arch, trim and cap or designed only ever to be worn as a diadem/circlet.After Edward VIII’s abdication, both the George V coronet and Edward’s investiture circlet went with him to France (technically without ownership or permission) and were only returned to the United Kingdom on his death in 1972. This meant another coronet had to be created for Charles for his investiture as Prince of Wales. Charles did not wear any headpiece during the coronation of his mother (being aged 4, that would be considered inappropriate—plus he only attended a short portion of his mother’s coronation). Charles was created Prince of Wales in 1958 and attended his investiture (a ceremonial function only) in 1969. With the absence of the Prince Edward coronet, a new coronet was made for him:Charles’ Prince of Wales coronet was designed following instructions that went back to Charles II—a single arch rather than the two arches of a monarch’s crown. Its most notable feature (often remarked upon) is the very fragile, gold-plated table-tennis ball at the top worn as a “monde” (symbol of the world). We do not know, yet, if this will be the coronet that William will wear at his father’s coronation and/or his own investiture (should he have one). There are other options, including (1) a wholly new coronet—although I think this unlikely as the cost of new jewels of this kind are prohibitive and Charles is known for seeking lower-cost efficiency; (2) wearing the coronet of a son of a king, to which he is also entitled—see below.Coronets of the members of the royal family Although many male members of the royal family are peers, they typically do not wear the coronet that corresponds to their peerage rank but a coronet that signifies their relationship to a monarch (past or present). These include four distinctive coronet styles corresponding to different ranks of relationship:The coronet of a child of the sovereign (a circlet, sometimes with cap and ermine trip, comprised of alternating fleur-de-lis and crosses). Being the highest ‘ranked’ coronet other than any worn by a Prince of Wales, it was also worn by the Duke of Ediburgh as the consort to Elizabeth II at her coronation:The coronet of a child of the heir apparent (a circlet, cap and ermine trime, comprised of crosses, fleur-de-lis and strawberry leaves around the edge). We have not had an instance of a child of an heir apparent (the equivalent Princes George and Louis, and Princess Charlotte) in attendance at a coronation since the advent of photography, so what we know of this coronet is what is ordinarily used in coats-of-arms of a child of an heir apparent.The coronet of a male-line grandchild of the sovereign (comprised of crosses and strawberry leaves alternating around the edge)The coronet of a female-line grandchild of the sovereign (comprised of alternating fleur-de-lis and strawberry leaves)At the coronation of their father, George VI, the then Princesses Elizabeth and Margaret wore specially-made coronets, small enough for their little heads, and worn as circlets rather than coronets. Here we can see the pattern of alternating crosses and fleur-de-lis worn ordinarily by a child of the sovereign.What is notable about the coronets of royal family members is that these are the only coronets allowed in the realm that include either crosses or fleur-de-lis. Those worn by nobles do not include either of these symbolic decorations.Coronets worn by nobles As with royals, there are different prescribed coronets for different ranks of peers (wives of peers wearing a corresponding smaller version of their husbands’). The rules on style were, again, laid down by Charles II after the restoration, some aspects following the styles he encountered in the court of France.Dukes (a gilt—not gold—coronet of eight strawberry leaves)Marquesses (a coronet of four strawberry leaves alternating with four balls)Earls (a coronet of eight strawberry leaves and eight balls raised up on stalks)Viscounts (a coronet of 16 balls, not raised)Barons (a more plain circlet with only six balls, not raised)The different coronets worn by different ranks of peer indicates to the viewer exactly who ranks where at first glance. For example, at the coronation of the Elizabeth II, we can recognise in the below image several earls, viscounts, barons, at least one duke and a marquess.So what will William wear to the coronation? With all this in mind, there are several choices. The final approval will come from the new King, but it is very likely a coronation committee will be formed that will make a series of recommendations and, under the guidance of the Earl Marshall who has traditional responsibility for the organisation of a monarch’s coronation (the Earl Marshall is better known as the Duke of Norfolk, the premier Duke in the United Kingdom). The choices for William include:The coronet of the Prince of Wales as used by Charles at his 1969 investitureThe coronet of George V, now returned to the United KingdomThe coronet of Edward VIII, now returned to the United KingdomAn ordinary coronet of a child of the sovereignA completely new coronet purpose-built for him, either in his role as Prince of Wales or in his role as heir apparent.(Betting on his choice opens November). Thanks Elora for the A2A.Footnotes[1] Investiture of the Prince of Wales
