column1: What is your review of Joker (2019 movie)?
column3: JOKER 2019 REVIEW: Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Gotham.I went into this film with high expectations. Very high expectations.I’ve done this a lot, only to be inevitably disappointed later by over-hyped films. Suicide Squad was one such film. Jared Leto had done so many messed-up things to his co-stars in the name of method acting, so that he could mentally prepare himself for the role of the Joker. Surely his hard work would translate into a masterful performance worthy of his Joker predecessors? 137 minutes and £12 later (plus an extra fiver for the train fare into Glasgow), I left that 2016 cinema theatre cursing myself. Given my disappointment with that and other DC film properties, I don’t know why I allowed myself to hope with Joker. I really don’t. DC has been churning out mediocre (Aquaman, Shazam!) and atrocious (Justice League) movies for years now, after all. They sometimes get things right, like with Wonder Woman, and you have to give them props for the extended cut of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice (or at least what they tried to do with it), but DC has had a rocky time of it as of late. They tried too hard to copy Marvel when Zack Snyder’s Superman-level fetish for Ayn Rand fell through, and DC never really recovered from that. And, to tell the truth, I hadn’t a great deal of faith in Joker until the Venice Film Festival happened. You know the one, where they all praised Joaquin Phoenix’s demented take on the character until they were blue in the face. Five-star reviews poured from Joker’s advance screening like a Biblical flood. Now, I wasn’t always the biggest fan of Jack Nicholson’s Joker (sacrilege!), but I did love Heath Ledger’s, so the question was this: how the hell were they going to top The Dark Knight? The answer: by not trying to.Please note: there are spoilers from this point forward.Joker is wholly isolated in canon, a lone-wolf take on the story of Arthur Fleck, who is constantly trodden on by society. It’s all very reminiscent of Falling Down, wherein the main character William Foster endures slights big and small until he snaps and nearly shoots up his local burger joint. In Joker, Arthur is harassed by teens who beat him up, he’s thrown under the bus by his co-workers, commuters judge him, social services let him down. His mother Penny is of no help, either; he’s the one taking care of her, letting her live with him as he bathes her, cooks her meals, checks the mail for the millionth bloody time for a letter from a Mr Thomas Wayne. That’s about as far as the DC connections go, though. Joker could have easily existed in a narrative vacuum, Arthur Fleck could have just been a wholly original character and it would have worked out just as well. In a sense, the film actually generates an unfair advantage by establishing itself in Gotham City, since we automatically identify its streets as being rife with crime and discord. But this is a minor gripe: while the world-building is lifted clean from other sources, the tale that Joker weaves is entirely self-contained, and it makes careful, loving use of what it borrows from, be that the Batman mythos or Martin Scorsese’s Taxi Driver/The King of Comedy. As for love itself, there’s very little to be found in this film. Arthur’s mother is an insane narcissist who allowed him to be abused as a child, leading to the development of his abrupt, uncontrollable laughter. His boss likes him to a point, but is manipulated by those around him who want rid of Arthur and his laughing fits. His healthcare worker has a passive interest, perhaps, but she doesn’t seem to do anything more for him than is required in her job description. There are no heroes to be found in Joker, and there’s no sense that anyone can solve Arthur’s problems before they get out of hand; indeed, the man promising to save Gotham City from itself in his mayoral campaign calls its biggest demographic a bunch of “clowns”. That goes down about as well as you would expect. And this brings me nicely onto the main story of Joker, the second masterpiece of the production (the primary being Joaquin Phoenix, who’ll get a section devoted to him later). I saw a lot of reviews from smaller papers complaining that Joker is too shallow to really say anything: to this, I say “bullshit”. The reason is precisely that Joker is not trying to say anything at all. At one point, Arthur (in full clown makeup, the mark of the revolution taking place in Gotham at the time) tells Robert de Niro’s character (Murray Franklin) that he doesn’t “believe in anything”, that there’s no politics behind his look, and that he just wants to boost his own act a little. After all, in his own words, he’s not the type of clown who could (intentionally) start a violent uprising! This is the point of Joker: Arthur is only in it for himself, because by the time he’s snapped, he’s grown so sick and tired of people beating him up and knocking him down. So what if his accidental shooting of three boorish city executives spawns a wave of anti-rich sentiment? He’s not aiming for that, he’s really just trying to get himself noticed. A civil war in Gotham, rich against poor, masses versus elites, is only a means to an end in achieving this when his dreams of stand-up comedy fail him. The lack of meaning instead creates a meaning. Nothing matters! As Arthur’s story tells us, it’s a dog-eat-dog world out there, and everything from Thomas Wayne’s callous condescension to the “clowns” he wishes to lead as Mayor to Murray Franklin’s shameless attempt to use Arthur as an interviewee on his show after publicly ridiculing him demonstrates this rather splendidly. Out on the streets of Gotham, most people are just trying to survive meaningless lives in squalid apartments while the rich have it all; indeed, the film does a very good job of showing the divide between the haves and the have-nots while never making it the point of the story. Neither is mental health the real point; note the lengths the script goes to so that the writing does not betray precisely which illnesses Arthur needs seven kinds of medication for! His laughing condition is also described in similarly vague terms, and his stint as a patient in Arkham Asylum is rarely touched upon outside of the odd allusion. The illnesses aren’t the issue, and so Joker smartly relegates them to the sidelines to showcase the true problem: society. Arthur doesn’t hate the Waynes because they’re powerful, he hates them because they (allegedly) abandoned him as their son, which is later revealed to be one of his mother’s delusions. He’s not jealous of their wealth and prestige, all he wants is acknowledgement from somewhere, anywhere, and especially from a father figure. It’s only when Thomas rejects Arthur as family (even as he maintains that his employees at Wayne Enterprises are all one big family), punching him in the face and issuing him with a death threat, that Arthur begin to accept ownership of the mob that protests against the rich fat-cats, blending in with their masks and calling the Waynes out on Murray’s show. What other people do with his personal vendettas means nothing to the central character; they can have their riots, so long as Arthur can bask in the glow of the blazing infernos, having inadvertently stricken the match for their pyre. Gotham City has had problems well before Arthur, it’s having them during Arthur’s time, and they’ll persist long after Arthur is gone. Recognising this, Joker actively (and wisely) chooses to not engage with these problems, creating and discarding story elements whenever they would intrude on showcasing Arthur’s personal struggles. And all he wants is a round of applause while his brief candle still flickers in the shadows; everything else can go to hell. With applause, Arthur is complete, and it doesn’t matter where the applause is coming from. He’s as addicted to attention as he is to his cigarettes. The source of his fix is meaningless, always in the peripheral, and Joker has a genius way of turning a lack of meaning into something incredibly meaningful. Joker is pure Dadaism, the ridiculing of society and all pretensions to meaning, fit for a 21st century audience.Speaking of Arthur, I think it’s time to shine a light on Joker’s not-so-secret weapons: the titular character, and the actor Joaquin Phoenix. When this film was released in America, concerns were raised that Arthur’s story would inspire incels and other violent groups, in part thanks to Phoenix’s incredible turn as the lead. The idea that an incel-esque character could be sympathetic was too much to fathom, because of how we see their antics on the news, in the headlines. Murderers with serious issues and a desperate need to get laid. It’s a miracle that Phoenix could play the story as sympathetically as he could in the current climate of today’s culture. There are very, very persuasive arguments that could have led to Joker’s entire production being shut down or reined in on safety grounds; even in the UK, I saw a couple more attendants in the theatre than I’m accustomed to. I can’t imagine what things must be like in a gun-culture (one British reviewer whose name I fail to recall pointed out that UK viewers will have some difficulty relating to the challenges present in Joker, partially because guns are almost as mythical to us as a wand in a Harry Potter story). But in allowing Phoenix to let loose in his emaciated, haunting performance, the fine folk at DC may have an Oscar on their hands. His laughter, first of all, is phenomenal. He times it just right, falling out of sync with those around him at a stand-up comedy night. His humour is off-kilter, talking about “this bleak world” and that he wants his death to “make more cents than his life”, thinking that the perfect punchline to a “knock-knock” joke is the taking of his own life on live television. His comedy is alienating, setting him at odds with polite society whose members laugh at a constant stream of sex jokes (furthering the idea that meaning is a social construct, with variations in humour nullifying its staying power). One of his first acts in the film is to laugh uncontrollably in tiny little bursts for a good two minutes, and the audience is never sure when he’ll stop. Or even if he’ll be allowed to stop: his condition means that he’s prone to fits of laughter that not only creep the hell out of those around him, but also wrack Arthur’s body with pain. But most cannot see past the discomfort they feel towards him; an angry mother on a bus takes his apologies card and stuffs it into her pocket, even as the writing instructs her to give it back. Gotham City is the embodiment of solipsistic thought, the idea that no-one else really exists apart from the individual whose senses are known to be stimulated. The mother even ignores the fact that her child was giggling at Arthur’s antics and was not bothered by him; in failing to perceive Arthur’s pain through and her son’s delight through her own eyes, the mother’s umwelt has no place for his condition. This is a trait which is shared by the rest of Gotham’s citizenry, and Phoenix is able to deftly convey the intense physical agony alongside the emotional anguish his condition brings upon him. The only person to see past the laughter (Zazie Beetz’s character, Sophie Dumond) is heavily implied to have been a figment of Arthur’s imagination, too. She is real, she lives down the hall in his apartment building, but her presence in Arthur’s life is as a dream, as wish-fulfilment; she’s there whenever he wants sex, affection, comfort in the hospital, and (most important of all) an appreciative audience at his stand-up routine. Her character is never fleshed out beyond this role of a perfectly malleable love interest, furthering the film’s tendency to eschew details that are superfluous to our understanding of Arthur. The incel comparisons that people attach to Joker are never clearer than when we find out that Sophie’s scenes and interactions with Arthur were just a part of his fantasies. Even when Arthur snaps and begins his killing spree, viewers are still able to sympathise with Phoenix’s incredible performance. Make no mistake; this is an art piece and not a comic film, wherein Arthur will start dancing for no reason other than to convey his state of mind. But for all of the strangeness, Phoenix ensures that the viewers are completely enthralled with Arthur Fleck, pouring his entire soul into every little tic of his character. And we must be very clear: Arthur is not a villain because of his mental illness, but because of the treatment he receives at the hands of those around him. Sure, his illness is why he invites such treatment through the aforementioned solipsism, but any sane man would snap after enduring the harms that Arthur has had to endure. I would even argue that Arthur, complete with his illness, handles his life better than most otherwise-healthy people who live in such conditions. We’re told to turn the other cheek, but Arthur’s turned it one too many times; those who say that Joker perpetuates the myth that mental illness creates killers don’t give Arthur (and Phoenix’s portrayal of him) enough credit. Without society beating him up day after day because of their own bigotries and individualistic mindsets, Arthur would go home and be the perfect son to his abusive mother. All he wanted pre-snap was to make people laugh, and in a kinder world, this mentally ill man would be doing just that. Arthur Fleck is not a character that misrepresents people with mental illnesses; if anything, it actually is a very real representation of a human being pushed beyond the point of breaking. Finger pointing at his mental illness betrays a lack of understanding of Joker; the laughing fits may be the inciting incidents that lead to cruel acts being committed against Arthur, but anyone would break with the pressure he is placed under. Most would probably have snapped years ago. As such, we shouldn’t really be behind Arthur as he begins to enact his bloody revenge on society. But there’s that tiny, very wrong part of us that’s oh-so-nearly rooting for him, and that is entirely down to Phoenix’s tragic take on the Joker. Yes, Arthur stabs a co-worker in the eye, but this was the same guy who had lost him his job after he had trusted him (and he allows his other co-worker who had done him no harm to leave unscathed). Yes, he kills Murray Franklin, but the man had made a mockery of his life’s work, his dreams and ambitions, all after Arthur had spent hours idolising him to be a gentle, caring man ever since their (possibly imaginary) first meeting. Yes, he smothers his mother with a pillow as she recovers from a stroke in a hospital bed, but she had given him false hope along with a lifetime of trauma and neglect. And yes, he shoots three executives in a subway carriage who were harassing a woman sitting opposite them (who tellingly tries to look to Arthur for help but denies him any mercy when his laughing fits take over, solipsism again in action), but they had been beating him up like a punching doll. Societal cruelty, not mental illness, is to blame. Everything Arthur does post-snap is objectively wrong, but it is very justifiable. And through all the blood splatters on the walls and subways, Phoenix somehow keeps our sympathies laser-focused on him. This is no mean feat when society is currently on high alert from incel communities and angry white men with weapons and no adequate venting space, but he pulls it off with aplomb. The only similar character I can think of in modern cinema is Star Wars’ sympathetic-if-bratty Kylo Ren, as played by Adam Driver; the little guy who is seduced into villainy through his misdirected anger, leading him begin his own reign of terror through leadership of the tyrannical First Order (previously under Supreme Leader Snoke’s command). Kylo takes his hatred for Luke Skywalker out on the entire cosmos in a temper tantrum, much like Arthur burns Gotham City to the ground after he’s pushed just that little bit too far by a world of solipsistic assholes. Phoenix also acts as the perfect embodiment of Joker’s central motif: the duality of comedy and tragedy, and the weaponisation of the former against the latter. Mark Twain wrote that “against the assault of laughter, nothing can stand”, and he’s absolutely on the money there. Arthur’s laughter causes him pain, both physical and societal. His crying and anguish are often synonymous with these laughing fits; where we would expect to see tears, Arthur fails to suppress the urge to burst into hysterics. His forays into comedy are all based on his gauging of others’ laughter at stand-up nights and plagiarising from other comics’ material (Bob Monkhouse’s “Well, no-one’s laughing now!”, for instance); he only starts to consider his own sense of humour as worthwhile in his subjective profession after he snaps with the world. He is mocked by successful television host Murray Franklin (who gives him his stage name of “Joker”, who calls him “pal” while ridiculing and scorning him) on live television, the final spark for him to begin his new life as a violent criminal. His clown act obscures his negative thoughts, a gun falling out of his pocket at a children’s hospital during a performance, and soon he himself even dons a mask to escape from the police detectives. By the time he appears on Murray’s show, every rioter has donned a fake Joker mask (a perversion in and of itself of Arthur’s own personal mission, furthering the divide between the riot’s agenda and his own: he wore make-up, the rioters wear masks), all phony plastic smiles to convey bubbling resentments. Penny has been suffocated in her bed, Murray Franklin’s mask of kindness has been unveiled, Thomas Wayne’s familial concern for his disgusting employees has been called out by Arthur; for all of the “pal” and “family” references from these two men, precious little empathy can be found in their personas. The faux-polite, solipsistic society has been torn asunder by the riots and looters, and among all the seething laughter and happy faces, Gotham City collapses into utter chaos. With Arthur standing tall upon the police car bonnet as the beloved clown prince of crime, and the centre of attention, at long last. That Phoenix can carry all of that in one performance is outstanding. And the man makes it look easy. Well, as easy as it can be when you’ve just shed 52 pounds (ironically, a standard deck of playing cards excluding jokers comprises 52 cards!) of weight for a role, anyway. So, what do you get when you cross a mentally-ill loner with a society that abandons him and treats him like trash? Sooner or later, what we all deserve, and there’ll be no punchline in sight.I can’t ramble for hours about the cinematography and the music, I fear. Symbolism and narrative are my fortes, and I should leave other praising to people who actually know what they’re talking about. Suffice to say from a layperson’s perspective on these matters that the movie is utterly beautiful to look at, a joy to behold, and I will be replaying Hildur Guðnadóttir’s excellent score a lot. There’s a distinct Viking quality to the music she produces, which plays well into the brutal, unforgiving society of Gotham City (although Gotham is much more psychological a warground than the physical invasions and conquests of Viking days of yore). In equating Viking society (I know they’re really called ‘Norsemen’, shuddup) to Gotham’s own, Guðnadóttir’s music should serve to remind us that the battles against mental illness are just as serious as those which deal with physical maladies; indeed, such battles are worthy of Odin himself. One’s emotional well-being should not be stifled in the way that it often is in favour of addressing more visible injuries and disabilities. Joker serves as a cautionary tale in its reproach of cruel societies that are inhospitable to those with mental health problems, both through its story and through its music. Unfortunately, Gary Glitter, disgraced British paedophile, features in Joker’s soundtrack in the tune Rock and Roll Part II. I could have done without this, but Arthur’s descent as an entertainer who loses his way is the perfect setting to use such music in. The song’s inclusion does make my skin crawl though, especially since Glitter stands to make money from its use, even as he languishes behind bars (EDIT: some comments have brought the recent statement from Snapper Music and Universal to my attention, that Glitter will not receive any royalties, happy day).Joker works on many levels. A meditation on the bleak solipsism of the world, on the divide between rich and poor, on selfish politics and the desperate need to invest in infrastructure and social services. But it is a character study, first and foremost, with nothing to say and everything to say all at once, through Arthur Fleck. You’ll not sleep well after having seen it; you’ll have come face to face with your own hypocrisies, you’ll be reminded of every time you passed a weirdo in the street who was acting a little differently with a disgruntled smirk on your lips, of every time you allowed an “I’ve got mine, you get yours” mentality to prevail when you could have done the right thing. And everyone has those moments, don’t you dare deny it. If this film doesn’t at least get one Oscar, the award will be worthless. Leave your pearls to clutch to at the concession desk, because you’re going to have to reckon with every horrible little thing you’ve ever done in watching Joker. No-one who engages in professional outrage culture is going to survive a screening of this film, with plenty of film-goers leaving the theatres ahead of the ending and calling for Joker to be banned because they can’t take it. If you’re uncomfortable while watching Joker, then that’s very good; you’re not allowed to feel happy with this movie. Don’t expect it to cater to ideals of good and evil, where evil is always vanquished by the forces of good. There are no explosions, no CGI fight sequences, nothing flashy to be found to take your mind off of the things you see. Cinema is often an escape from the world and its troubles, but Joker forces you to face the world and your own faults head-on. And diverting attention to the film’s depiction of the poor, of mental health, of politics, or moaning about the lack of laughs in a film of this nature, is just tone-deaf to its message. Not to mention, it’s highly insincere and disingenuous, and it demonstrates an unwillingness to actually engage with the content. The truth is, we just don’t like to feel called out in our entertainment, but Joker will pull no punches, and will make no apologies for that, whether you’re woke or not. But hey, that’s life!Final Drury rating: 9.5/10 (with a half point deducted for using a Gary Glitter song, though the symbolism of playing music from a disgraced performer during Arthur’s transformation and staircase dance is not lost on me).
column9: This review deserves a standing ovation. The movie is disturbing, tragic and brilliant. If Joaquin Phoenix doesn’t get - at the very LEAST - a nom for best actor, it will be a travesty. My husband and I have seen dozens of films this year, and there’s no other actor we’ve seen who deserves an Academy Award MORE. It’s a master class in acting. He throws himself into the role…he’s fearless, and he completely disappears. He’s riveting. You can’t take your eyes off him.

column1: Do you think K-pop companies need to do more for their artists’ mental health?
column3: Do you think K-pop companies need to do more for their artists’ mental health?From someone who is clearly looking in from the outside, I can only personally deduce that there is a problem that needs to be addressed. Some companies have dealt with this issue and seem to be leading the way. JYPE obviously looks to be working with Mina as delicately as possible as she slowly navigates her way to wellness. She has been sitting out promotions for the last two comebacks.Further…"Health of our artist is our top priority," JYPE added, "so we will do everything possible to provide the best possible measures including medical treatment and sufficient rest for Mina’s recovery."Even in their new Japanese video “Fake and True,” unlike with “Feel Special,” Mina doesn't feature in the choreography. They have already planned for her not appearing onstage. Reports have stated that she was “preparing” for promotions, but none of us really knows what they means until we see how deeply she'll participate. Also, we are not only seeing some companies take a more active role in dealing with these problems but we're also being fed info about idols having them. Straittimes:Also,In May, Goo Ha-ra, 28, a former member of South Korean girl group Kara, was found unconscious in her home and had to be warded. She had posted messages that dwelled on betrayal and self-doubt. She is now back on her feet and promoting her career again.However, the plight of the small company still has it landlocked in underexposure. Yubin of Pink Fantasy is also sidelined due to anxiety disorder, but if you did a random search about her vs. Mina, you'll not see any info about her case. Mina, coming from a large company, gets her situation mentioned at least once.Search for Mina and, even if you weren't aware of her disorder, you'll see something that makes you say “huh? What's going on?” With Yubin, you get a few languages you may not understand and things about group activities. It's an unfair world. But…if you are in the know, you'll know what to look for: That said, from both large and small, you have to wonder exactly what actions are being taken in terms of idol medical treatment. Mina's company can spend treasures on her recovery. How much care will Yeonwoo get? JYP said they were doing “everything possible” for Mina. Yubin's going “on hiatus.” Can her company only afford to give her a vacation? Where? Home to her family? Will any treatment be involved? Nobody knows Mydoll Entertainment. Nobody knows Pink Fantasy. That company may be part of the problem. But it could be the best they can do. But will it be enough? Is it safe for her? How many companies simply can't handle such financial hits and go on hoping for the best as they struggle to simply stay afloat? And how often does this happen? I'd say a lot. There are “Big Three" companies who can pay for these things (but do they? I heard SM and YG sucked) Then there's the rest. Do enough math and we may find that things seem pretty dangerous for idols working for our not-so-rich companies. Fans are fearing that Loona may disband over financial woes right now as I write this. I'm sure there are other mental issues to speak of, but anxiety disorder seems to be the prevailing disease of late. But what is “anxiety disorder?” Let's research.Excessive Worry - Being dissed online, your future, being hungry, not enough comebacks, etc.Sleep Disturbances - The disorder itself may leave one physically exhausted. And then you can't sleep?Panic Attacks - It is said to feel like one is having a heart attack.Nausea/Vomiting - Can affect eating habits and induce weight loss.Muscle Tension - Reactions of “fight or flight" wherein the muscles predict an altercation and “get ready.”Flashbacks - Commonly, memories of what caused all this in the first place surface randomly.Social Anxiety - Emotional closeout. Responses to this could trigger other symptoms.Stage Fright - Ouch.This fear is ranked higher than the fear of flying, bankruptcy, illness and death. Even seasoned actors or musicians may find themselves afflicted with this disorder. ~ ActiveBeatOkay, we have a problem guys. These are serious situations. What might cause these mental and physical failings among idols? Let's talk to a few and see what kinds of problems they're dealing with... “There are many people who debuted with no sense of self yet, and they come to realize later that every move and every word they say is being observed so they become cautious and lose their freedom,” ~ Block B Park Kyung “The last three years have been a dark and long tunnel in my life,” she said. “Music wasn’t interesting anymore.” ~ Younha “Anxiety and loneliness seem to be with me for life…Emotions are so different in every situation and every moment, so I think to agonise every moment is what life is.” ~ Suga “I used to ponder upon a malicious comment written by a netizen in just five seconds with a fleeting thought of ‘I just don’t like this guy’ for the next five hours and five days.” ~ RM “I’m broken from the inside. The depression that has slowly eaten away at me has finally consumed me, and I couldn’t beat it.” ~ Jonghyun The symptoms seem to match the above research. Yet overall, it appears that there's been a longtime reluctance, refusal or inability to really do anything about idol mental hazards. This 2017 petition (that long ago, yes) reached out to companies literally begging them to help their idol charges.“If their idols need therapy; hire personal therapists that can meet one on one with to help them through their problems. If they need medicine; help them find legal medicines they can take to help them.”Medications for depression, natural remedies, muscle relaxers, spiritual retreats, counseling, gradual reintegration into the social spectrum, etc. Resources exist. Yes, but it goes deeper than that. The answer here is treatment. But prevention is the real answer to the answer. The who, what, when, where, why and how. Get to the root of the problem, identify when and how it occurs and eliminate the plagues that grow into something that would need to be treated later. In essence, stop doing the shit that could be potentially killing your idols. Like grueling schedules, cramped living conditions, four comebacks a year. Something needs to be done to stop it from happening, not just dealing with it when it does happen. Kim Byung-soo, a psychiatrist at Asan Medical Center: Thanks for reading.
column9: Great answer! Actually, out of all the K-pop companies I know of, JYP is the only one that hires mental health professionals for their artists. Of course it’s great that they’re doing that, but there are so many other artists out there without the proper treatment or support. JYP can spend millions on healthcare and their organic cafeteria and benefits for employees, but companies that want to do the same can’t and companies that can do the same won’t.

column1: Who is a good psychologist for online counselling from India?
column3: I will suggest an affordable place and experienced psychologist (LISA SHUKLA) where you can take your therapy sessions at 588 rupees only and Manochikitsa online counselling gives this affordable facility.For the last three years, I have been suffering from a severe anxiety-based disorder, named generalized anxiety disorder. I was fed up with my hectic schedule of therapy sessions where I was just wasting both my money and time just for showing up at the clinic for having sessions. I continued taking therapy for three months but after that I quit. I needed therapy badly. It was my requirement to keep my mental health. I had already been suffering from anxiety for so long now that my marriage has started to become damaged just because of me. I was afraid of losing my wife. So, I wanted some professional help and needed to see a therapist who would cure me. I already wasted my two years on therapies where I was not healing at all. When I came across Manochikitsa then nothing seemed better to me than booking therapy sessions at this particular platform. Because I could not be at the same place where my life, family, working life and everything was getting affected. I could not even bear my spouse feeling emotionally unwell because of me and I really used to think for her as she managed the household, me, and our 8 years old daughter. I failed her and my daughter. I lost everything with my business. I love my family very much. So, I have recently connected with online therapy platform, Manochikitsa and started my sessions. The therapist has been of very great assistance to me. A new hope was brought by her in my life since I connected with her via video call session. My anxiousness was destroying me but she was able to control it on time. I am still in the healing process but I am now feeling better than before. I had trouble conveying my feelings and my opinions as it is a part of being a male because generally, they do not share their feelings easily. I would seldom tell anybody what was upsetting me, bothering me, and going on in my head. I never told anyone. During the anxiety period I shared nothing even with my wife in spite of knowing that she was one of those who wanted to assist me and help me but couldn’t because of my unwillingness to speak out. Because of my anxiety, my family was disturbed. My home does not make me feel like I am in my home with my own family members. I felt very relaxed after speaking out everything in front of my therapist and she listened to me carefully. She has given me the exposure of different therapies like cognitive-behavioral therapy and she has taught me coping skills so that I could control my anxiety when I am not in the session. Whenever I open a zoon application for an attending session and see my therapist saying hello to me, I feel positive vibes which actually levels up my morale. After attending a few sessions I started talking to my wife like I never did in the last three years. I saw her happy after a very long time and saw myself smiling with her. It was the greatest moment for me. I am so grateful to her, my therapist, who is not just helping me to cure my anxiety but is also saving my family. I would recommend you to start a therapy session from Manochikitsa for the best results. They will take care of your mental health concerns.

column1: What is your financial planning if you are earning 50 LPA?
column3: It is important to know when the salary or income of Rs.50.00 Lakhs per annum is started. However, if it is before payment of taxes, income minus taxes paid has to be taken into account.If it is at the age of 30, you can choose to save about Rs.25.00 Lakhs in an year, Planning your expenses, which will be about Rs.2.00 Lakhs per month. This could be due to your meeting important officials , which needs expenses as situation demands.You may choose to buy a house in the vicinity of your office, to reduce travel time in moving from office to home.For availing housing loan for a house for , say Rs.2.00 crores, you may require margin for home loan, interiors, any other expenses (like 1% tax payable to corporation for registration etc.), brokerage etc. Keeping an amount of Rs.50.00 Lakhs for these expenses helps getting loan sanctioned, without depending upon bank loan for registration expenses etc., for which banks may charge additional interest/ charges. The interest on loan upto Rs.1.50 Lakhs is eligible for concessions in Tax under sec 80 C. The tax deduction Rs.3.45 Lakhs is available for houses upto Rs.45.00 Lakhs only.Saving in Tax saver deposit Rs.1.50 Lakhs , eligible for tax concessions under sec 80 C, including savings under PF, tax saver deposit, premium for life insurance policies, National Savings scheme, post office savings/term deposit etc., along with Tax saver deposit. After 5 years, Tax saver deposit can be reinvested as Tax saver deposit for that year. (Can be utilised in 6th year, every time it is invested.)Opening Recurring deposit account, for Rs.50000— per month for 120 months gives savings Rs.60.00 Lakhs plus interest at about 6.5% at the end of 120 months. The interest payable on term deposit/recurring deposit, on the date of deposit will not change, irrespective of reduction of interest on next date of deposit. The deposit can be preclosed, in case of urgent expenses or loan can be availed same day. These deposits can be opened online in net banking and accounts opened online can be closed on line. For loan, branch to be visited.Saving under SIP for mutual funds every month can save some amount. However, investment in mutual funds are subject to market fluctuations. Verification of NAV regularly, you will be aware of current value of your savings, exceeding saved amount or less than savings.Arrangements have also to be made for payment of advance tax, if any tax is payable in addition to tax deducted by employer.Planning for holiday , finance for visit to National, international destinations to be done in time. Availing leave could be difficult, which needs planning at right time and also available in times of need, to decide important matters. By saving for holiday, interest payable on loan for holiday can be saved.Preparing plan to save, drawal of amount when necessary, can be done personally or checked what is already prepared by your assistant. Giving necessary instructions, in right time, gives finance at the right time for urgent needs. Paying credit card dues or using only debit card, you can check savings made by lesser purchases, interest/charges levied for loan on credit card.Having personal health insurance policy for Rs.25.00 Lakhs or suitable amount , with parents, spouse, children (male child upto age of 25 years, girl child upto marriage) gives health care to parents, family members. This will be useful, when there is situation, when office group health care insurance not available (when there is gap between changing one job to another or office policy does not cover some diseases).Some amount may be saved for attending national, international seminars,meetings, personality motivation/development programmes, MBA, International Business School, after attending job for about 2 to 5 years etc. It is important to keep you updated on professional, financial, technical issues, to keep you abreast your competitors. It is also important to know latest technology like Artificial intelligence and where it can be profitably employed, before you know your competitors have already installed such technology. (Say car features adopted as per purchaser interest or special addition series).Investment in voluntary PF at the rate of PF, about 8% changed every year, gives freedom to withdraw the amount for expenses, along with loan on PF for designated purposes(For acquiring house, medical expenses etc.)..Investment in land, building , apartment are other options, to get interest exemption upto 3.45 lakhs for house upto Rs.45.00 lakhs, in first year and Rs.1.50 under section C (interest on loan).Investment in company fixed deposits also an option, subject to verification whether the offer is with secured option (to verify securities offered) or in case of losses whether Depisit holders will be treated as unsecured creditors. (Amount will be paid, after all secured creditors are paid and any amount remains).Investment in gold/gold bonds also a choice, as gold rates for 24 karat gold increased by about Rs.1100— On 08 08 19. The rate of gold was about Rs.450— for 8 grams for 22 carat gold in 1977–78 , increased to about 1600 in 1987–88, around Rs.20000— for 10 gr 24 carats, in 2010–11, about Rs.30000— later, but fluctuating. Present rate is Rs.37900—. The rates and years are approx.The important issue in high earning professionals is continuing job tension and important issues, which have to be decided , without affecting colleagues, subordinates, while protecting business interests as well as not to lose business to competitors. This leaves them with less rest, continued tension, pressure from boss, customer demanding completing project with less staff at earliest time. The opposite interests of various groups could not be served , as taking decision may benefit one group, at the same time another group, say employees get dissatisfied etc.It is also necessary to keep savings at high level, due to inflation, to retire early, in the event of uncomfortable job situation (juniors getting good favours, getting in important jobs, deteriorating health) etc. Many young professionals getting disinterested with continued tension and seeking a peaceful life.Investment attracting tax concessions:savings under 80 C section D and 80 G — PF, LIC, 5 year Bank Deposit, ELSS Schemes, Sukanya Samrudhi Schemes in Bank/post office, Post office Deposits, stamp duty and Registration charges for own house, National savings Certificate, Senior Citizen Saving schemes., interest on housing loan instalment/interest Rs.1,50,000—*(maximum amount under 80 c and subsectionsSection 80 ccc savings under Pension Plans, annuity Schemes of insurance companies Rs.150000—*).Section 80CCD contribution to Pension plans of Central Govt Schemes to Individuals.Section 80CCF contribution to central Govt approved infrastructure bond.Section 80CCD contribution to Govt approved equity savings schemes.Section D deduction can be claimed for self, spouse and dependent children Rs.25000— and additional Rs.25000—, if parents are below age 60 and Rs.50000—, if the parents are above age 60.Sections 80 DD and 80 DDB also apply for specific individuals, to be verified, before claiming.Section 80 G donations to institutions having permission from from Income Tax Dept., can be claimed in the tax return. (100% or 50% as the case may be).Following some advices from elders, like,A. not keeping all savings in one investment (either share market or investment in property at one place etc.).b.saving in such a way that your deposit /mutual fund maturity dates are spread like 5 year, 7 year, 10 year, (to invest as per condition of market after 5 years etc.).C. to save from earnings and spend remaining amount only (not to save , after expenses, with exception for emergencies).D.Give importance to maintaining good health, renew health insurance, life insurance, to avoid unforeseen problems.E, Try to save targeted amount, revise targets, when earnings increase, to have hassle-free life.Any Savings option, with nomination facility, gives you freedom to choose to whom you wish to pass on your savings.Bank term deposits, National Savings Scheme, Post office Savings schemes, investment in shares, mutual funds have nomination facility.Writing a will giving your preferences to give your savings, properties to your Son/daughter etc., with 2 witnesses will give validity to will. (A form of Will is available in net or you may contact a reliable lawyer for drafting a will. But a will drafted by you is valid, subject to clarity in thought and expression, including all properties). It becomes a document, on death of person writing the will. It can be kept in your bank locker, without knowledge of your family members, if you opine that your options may land you in differences with your family members. It can also be given to local sub-registrar with acknowledgement. The information about will in locker or with sub-registrar should be available with one or two of your well wishers. The will reduces chances of any conflicts between family members or few of them going to court Reg rights on property.A will can be changed at a later date, with changes , if any and state at the end that it is last will and written while you are in good health and mental condition.The option to register property in family members name, gift also options, but their refusing to give you benefits , after parting with rights on property (though you may stay, can be sent out) may land you in problems. Opening account with joint account (operated by both), either or survivor, former or survivor ( can be closed/operated by survivor/survivors on expiry of former ) are other options. Having joint account with spouse is an option, Which ensures family members take care of spouse, in case of death of husband/wife having Deposit/property. In case of unfortunate death of survivor or second named party, the name can be changed in SB account, term Deposit, NSC, demat account for shares, subject to conditions laid down for each category. You may get necessary forms from concerned authorities, for use at appropriate time.

column1: What should we make of the results so far for Super Tuesday 2024?
column3: This is what I make of the results of Super Tuesday 2024… First, we are seeing how incredibly weak Donald Trump is within his own party as he goes “full fascist” and sounds increasingly like Mussolini in his vile, bombastic, incoherent, lie-filled speeches.Trump would be Mussolini’s twin if not for that bizarre wig or whatever it is. The chin tilt is the same, the perpetual scowl is the same, the inflammatory rhetoric is the same, the insanity is the same.Like Mussolini, Trump is a pig of a human being and loves to wallow in slop. Nikki Haley, who has no chance of winning the Republican nomination for president, was victorious in her second primary and now has 89 delegates. She won in Washington DC and Vermont, and has made strong showings in other states as well. Thus, there is clearly dissatisfaction with Trump within the GOP. It turns out that many Republicans are not in favor of destroying American democracy and junking the Constitution in order to appoint an evil, doddering idiot the first American dictator-for-life. Second, Trump is increasingly disoriented, is having trouble pronouncing simple words, is having more and more “grandpa” moments, and most disturbingly is replacing simple words with non-words. Substituting non-words for real words is a strong indicator of advanced dementia according to mental health experts. For instance, when Trump was trying to say “later” and his deteriorating mind came up with “three years lady, lady, lady.” As Dr. John Gartner has pointed out, no one with a normal brain does that. Forgetting or confusing names and dates is not all that unusual. Babbling nonsense is, and Trump does it all the time now. Trump is not well and is deteriorating rapidly but MAGA doesn’t care and would vote for him in a padded cell. (The ambiguity is intentional.) As Nikki Haley told NBC recently, Trump is “diminished” and “unhinged.” Haley explained away her past support for Trump by saying bluntly that “he is not the same person he was in 2016.” She also observed that “We have to see this for what it is. This is a fact: He is now saying things that don’t make sense.” Third, both Joe Biden and Donald Trump will coast to their parties’ respective nominations. Once American voters understand that their only electable choice is between the 80-year-old Biden and the demented 77-year-old Trump, the question will become which of the two is more competent to be president of the United States. Joe Biden has his occasional gaffes, but Trump is literally falling apart before our eyes. He has gone from merely evil, devious and moronic, to evil, devious, moronic, deluded and lacking a functioning brain. Hopefully, Americans will make the only sane choice and vote for Joe Biden for president. To do otherwise is to court disaster with a demented “president” whose demented dream is to become the first American dictator, the American Putin. MAGA will come out to vote for Donnie Dementia, so it’s up to us to do our patriotic duty and vote for someone sane. TRUMP IS FALLING APART BEFORE OUR EYES According to psychologist Dr. John Gartner, a professor for 28 years at Johns Hopkins University Medical School, Trump's mispronunciations of simple words and his inability to formulate complete sentences appears to be a sign of growing dementia. And Dr. Gartner is by no means the Lone Ranger. Over 700 mental health experts submitted a petition to Congress warning of Trump’s declining mental health. In an interview with Chauncey DeVega of Salon, Dr. Gartner observed that Trump is showing “gross signs of dementia” and is “dangerously demented.” It bears noting that Trump’s father, Fred Trump, died with severe dementia and could not identify members of his own family. Dr. Gartner told DeVega that Joe Biden's occasional gaffes “are well within the normal limits of aging.” Trump, however, appears to be showing gross signs of dementia. “This is a tale of two brains. Biden's brain is aging. Trump's brain is dementing.” This is what Dr. Gartner told DeVega, verbatim:I had to speak out now because the 2024 election might turn on this issue of who is cognitively capable: Biden or Trump? It's a major issue that will affect some people's votes. Not enough people are sounding the alarm, that based on his behavior, and in my opinion, Donald Trump is dangerously demented. In fact, we are seeing the opposite among too many in the news media, the political leaders and among the public. There is also this focus on Biden's gaffes or other things that are well within the normal limits of aging. By comparison, Trump appears to be showing gross signs of dementia. This is a tale of two brains. Biden's brain is aging. Trump's brain is dementing.DeVega said Dr. Gartner advised him that, based on Trump's speech, memory, recall, and other behaviors, he appears to be “hypomanic” and “cognitively deteriorating at a rapid rate.” Dr. Gartner also told DeVega that “the diagnostic signs are not subtle” and would be obvious to laypeople. In interviews Dr. Gartner has noted that during his speeches Trump appears to be spiraling into "phonemic paraphasias" which means "the substitution of non-words for words that sound similar.” Such symptoms “are not normally seen until a patient enters the moderate to severe stages of Alzheimer’s." In an interview with John Iadarola of The Damage Report, viewable on YouTube, Dr. Gartner noted that phonemic paraphasias is always evidence of brain damage. ALWAYS. In an interview on the David Pakman Show, Dr. Gartner said that he consulted other mental health experts and they all agreed that no one commits such “phonemic paraphrases” without brain damage. When he asked other experts if they ever saw such non-word pronunciations in people without brain damage, “They said ‘no.’” Dr. Gartner called Trump’s inability to pronounce simple words or to complete coherent sentences a “neurological smoking gun” and a “real breakdown in the capacity to think and use language.” Such symptoms, according to Dr. Gartner, are “formal evidence of dementia.” In his interview with David Pakman, Dr. Gartner called what Trump is experiencing a “basic breakdown” in his ability to use language to express his thoughts. Dr. Gartner also described an “enormous regression” in Trump’s ability to express himself. Dr. Gartner also noted that Trump’s repeated used of superlatives is a sign of dementia, an indication of his “impoverished vocabulary.” Rather than finding more appropriate adjectives, Trump’s malfunctioning brain keeps coming up with “wonderful” and “beautiful” even when such terms are completely inappropriate. For instance, Trump called Vladimir Putin’s excuse for invading Ukraine and mass-murdering Ukrainian children and their mothers “wonderful.” This is how Dr. Gartner described what happens when Trump can’t remember a simple word:When Trump can't find a word his whole demeanor changes. It’s almost like someone pulled the metaphorical plug. Trump looks blank, stops in mid-sentence (or mid-word), his jaw goes a little slack, and when he starts to talk again, he slurs, speaks haltingly, and often looks confused. Trying to get the word out, he shifts to a non-word that is easier to pronounce. When people are losing their ability to use language they use non-words. They start with the stem of the real word, and then they improvise from there.Dr. Gartner noted that Trump also exhibits “semantic paraphasia” which involves choosing the incorrect words, such as Trump saying, “I hope they now go and take a look at the oranges of that investigation.” Another sign of dementia, according to Dr. Gartner, goes beyond forgetting and mixing up names, to mixing up “generations.”The Dementia Care Society says “mixing up people and generations” is a sign of dementia.We have seen this repeatedly with Trump:When he said there were “airports” during the Revolutionary War.When he said we are in danger of World War II.When Trump said seven times that he ran against Barack Obama in 2016, or is running against him in 2024. And when he said that Putin doesn’t respect Obama and is starting to talk “nuclear” as a Virginia audience fell silent in disbelief. While Don the Con claims that such gaffes are “intentional,” we know that he’s lying because during a speech in North Carolina on Saturday, 3/2/2024, Trump caught his mistake and corrected it. After saying that he beat Obama in 2016, in “an election that everyone said couldn’t be won,” Don the Con paused, then provided the correct name, saying, “We beat Hillary Clinton.” Thus his claim to be “intentionally” citing the wrong name is just another Trumpian lie. I suspect that Trump’s handlers have cautioned him about not seeming to know the current president and not knowing who he ran against in 2016, but he remembered too late in the NC speech.When he said that his father was born in Germany when it was his grandfather.Michael Wolff observed that Trump frequently didn’t recognize old friends of his. That is a far cry from just forgetting or confusing their names.When he said four times that Nikki Haley was in charge of security on Jan 6., although in reality she had never been in charge of any kind of security outside South Carolina when she was governor there nearly a decade ago. Nor had Nancy Pelosi ever been in charge of Capitol Hill security, if that was who Trump meant. Apparently, Trump has forgotten that he was still president on Jan 6., and was thus in charge of all branches of the U.S. military, including the National Guard.Trump has said, more that once, that he is running against the person who was in charge of security at the Capitol. But he is running against Nikki Haley and Joe Biden, neither of whom were in charge of the Capitol on Jan. 6. Nor was Nancy Pelosi. It is very hard to understand what is going on inside Trump’s confused and deteriorating brain. He hasn’t just confused names, and hasn’t just confused people and generations, but he has confused his lies with reality, creating “alternate” people who never really existed, like an insane person believing he had a relationship with Cleopatra.When my elderly mother suffered with dementia, at one point she didn’t recognize me, her eldest son. That was a flooring realization for me, a hammer blow. In my opinion, while being a layperson in this regard, the single biggest sign of dementia is not forgetting or confusing names, but having a loved one or close acquaintance replaced by a blank. And there are many such blanks in Trump’s rapidly deteriorating brain. As Dr. Gartner pointed out in his interview with The Damage Report, a person not knowing the identity of the current president is a sign of dementia or extreme disorientation. If you were in an emergency room and couldn’t identify the current president, that would be a “very serious indicator” that something was seriously wrong with your brain. Trump’s “explanation” that he says Obama when means Biden “on purpose” does not explain why he thinks his father was born in Germany, or why he thinks World War II is in the future, or why he thinks there were “airports” during the Revolutionary War. Furthermore, Trump has repeatedly confused people he knows well, some intimately:Melania became ‘Mercedes’ after Trump paused and apparently struggled to remember his wife’s name, then failed and came back with an approximation.In a speech Trump said, “Secretary Pompeo is here,” then corrected himself, “Secretary of State,” but immediately got the next name wrong, “Mike Bolton, John Bolton is here.”Trump said Jeb Bush, who was never president, got the US into its war with Iraq. I don’t know anyone who thinks Jeb Bush was president. He never came close. Trump shared debate platforms with Jeb Bush and knew very well who he was at one time.After once again praising the dictators Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Kim Jong-un during a November 8 rally in Florida, Trump said Kim Jong-un leads a country of 1.4 billion people. North Korea has a population of just 26 million. Apparently, Donnie Dementia thinks Kim Jong-un is the powerful dictator of China!Trump called Argentina a "great guy."There seems to be a very clear trend at work here, and that trend suggests a mind that is no longer functioning on all cylinders. These are examples of Trump’s non-words:In a speech Trump said “Last year alone ICE ‘offices’ removed 10,000 ‘suspesdig’ gang members.”Later became ‘lady.’ — This is a glaring example because both words are very simple, easy to pronounce, and have nothing to do with each other. Trump saying “Three years lady lady lady” when he meant “later” and getting the word wrong three times, is not normal, even to a layman like me. Again, Dr. Gartner, an expert, said phonemic paraphasias is always evidence of brain damage. ALWAYS.Trump sometimes creates strings of non-words: “Americans of all walks of ‘lice’ ‘rofe up’ … rose up.”Stock market became ‘slock rocket.’ During this speech Trump paused, then came back with the correct term. So at times he catches his mistakes and corrects them, but usually not.Beneficiaries became 'benefishers.'Bipartisan solutions became ‘bipartis solushus.’“As bad as it is” became “azzbadidtizz.’Armed forces became ‘forcive’ and ‘forshuh.’Trump particularly struggles with Venezuela, which at various times became:‘Ven-esh-wail-uh’‘Ven-ez-wail-lass’‘Ven-ez-wellzso’‘Ven-ez-wellez’or just “Venez-’ followed by silence.Applicable became ‘appliculbulls.’Renovations became 'renoversh.'Pivotal became 'pivvittable.'Lawmakers became ‘lawmarkers’ more than once.Obama became 'obamna.'FDR became “Franklin ‘De-lay-no’ Roosevelt.”Missiles became 'mishiz.'China’s supply chain became ‘supply chern.’Christmas became 'Crissus' and “the ‘eastwisemen’ traveled (pause as if recognizing his mistake) far, far (pause) afield.”Sometimes it’s impossible to understand what Trump is trying to say:“Enen they announced there was no by yesno.” (Some sort of vote?)“Our army man the amp, it ‘ranned’ the ramparts, it took over the airports, it did everything!” (During the Revolutionary War, our army took over nonexistent airports, manned the amp (amplifier?), and did something, who knows what, to the ramparts.)Bipartisan became 'bipars.'According to Dr. Gartner, “This is a fundamental breakdown in the ability to use language. If you were talking to your father on the phone and he did this you would think he is having a stroke. There is no healthy older person who speaks that way." In his Pakman interview, Dr. Gartner said such mispronunciations, in which the stem of the word is used, but the demented mind comes up with a nonsensical non-word ending, is “hard clinical evidence of brain damage.” There is no guesswork involved. Trump has brain damage, and it’s getting worse, rapidly. In the comments Paul Peterson noted:Good update. Yes, this also supports Wernicke-Korsakoff “Frontotemporal dementia”, with “confabulation" endings to sentences, where “angry bird" words are filled in, from Amygdala cache memory.Another symptom of dementia is tangential speech, or confabulation, and no one in my experience has ever been more tangential, or more “rambling” in incoherent ways, than Trump. An example, one of many, of Trump’s rambling confabulations, is his rant about magnets. Trump ranted that the Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier should have used “John Deere” hydraulics rather than electromagnetic elevators and catapults. Trump concluded his confabulated rant by saying: “Think of it, magnets. Now all I know about magnets is this, give me a glass of water, let me drop it on the magnets, that’s the end of the magnets. Why didn’t they use John Deere? Why didn’t they bring in the John Deere people? Do you like John Deere? I like John Deere.” Of course water does not destroy magnets or demagnetize them. Magnets can be used underwater. I am unaware of John Deere having anything to do with aircraft carrier elevators or catapults. I rather doubt that an ultra-sophisticated American aircraft carrier is going to use tractors to haul ultra-expensive jets from storage to the flight deck. Trump makes less sense than any elderly person in my personal experience. Trump instances of phonemic paraphasias, semantic paraphasia, tangential speech and other “doddering grandpa moments” include:Trump says things that make no sense, like “We’re going to defend pro god…” then stops speaking, his face grows blank, his jaw goes slack, he looks around as if at a loss for what to say, then comes back with something completely unrelated, like “Context and content!”Such nonsensical “word salads” are increasingly common in Trump’s speeches. He seems to slip into, then back out of, coherence. And he’s more out that in, these days.Origins became ‘oranges.’Trump can no longer say the name of the country he once presidented: United States became ‘United Shersh’ and ‘United Stage.’Crooked Joe became ‘Cricket Joe.”Trump said a soldier was awarded the ‘combat infantroopen badge.’Evangelist became ‘evangelish.’Anonymous became ‘enenamas.’Hamas became ‘huh-maas.’Yosemite became ‘YO-se-min-NIGHT.’NAFTA became ‘Nasta.’Prison became ‘privit.’Overdose became ‘overdoth.’Neonatal became ‘neonetical.’The Harvard-Harris poll became the ‘Harvard-Harris bill.’Trump said there were airports during the Revolutionary War.Trump during a meeting with Justin Trudeau accused Canada of burning down the White House in 1812. Of course it was the British who burned Washington in 1814.Trump claimed more than once that F-35s are invisible and can’t be seen: “Even if it [the enemy] is right next to it, it can’t see it.” Trump apparently doesn’t understand a plane being invisible to radar but visible to human eyes.Trump said “windmills” kill whales and their noise causes cancer.Trump said injecting disinfectants into the lungs would “knock out” the coronavirus “in a minute, one minute” and that it would be “almost like a cleaning.” No, dumbass, it would be more like instant death.Trump said Hungary shares a “front” with Russia, but Hungary has no border with Russia.During a 2019 cabinet meeting Wednesday, Trump argued that the Soviet Union “was right” to invade Afghanistan in 1979 because “terrorists were going into Russia,” an argument that is historically inaccurate. The Wall Street Journal editorial board reacted strongly to Trump’s comments in an op-ed: “Right to be there? We cannot recall a more absurd misstatement of history by an American President. The Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan with three divisions in December 1979 to prop up a fellow communist government.”Trump said, “Russia used to be the Soviet Union. Afghanistan made it Russia because they went bankrupt fighting in Afghanistan.” That, too, is historically inaccurate. There were many reasons for the collapse of the Soviet Union and it didn’t go “bankrupt.”Trump told reporters that China respects him for his “very, very large brain.”Proving that his brain is not incredibly large, Trump said Puerto Rico is surrounded by “water, big water, ocean water.” And he once helpfully explained that “water is wet, from the standpoint of water.”Trump called Hurricane Florence “one of the wettest we've ever seen from the standpoint of water.”Trump wanted to nuke hurricanes and has apparently never heard of nuclear fallout.In a speech Trump claimed, “We’ve ended the war on beautiful clean coal.” Trump went on to say that a new coal mine was opening where the miners would take out “clean coal” which he explained meant that the miners were going to clean the coal. Like washing dirty dishes, presumably. Of course there is no such thing as “clean coal.”Trump has said repeatedly that he defeated Barack Obama for the presidency in 2016.Trump said he won all 50 states, when he didn’t win his home state, New York, or the state with the largest population, California. Trump lost resoundingly in two of the highest population states. It wasn’t even close.Trump claims he has been “treated worse” than Abraham Lincoln. The confederate states seceded from the Union after Lincoln was elected, and when the South lost the war, Lincoln was assassinated. Trump has been treated very mildly compared to Lincoln.Trump has repeatedly claimed to have “aced” a “very difficult” test for cognitive impairment that any normal person can pass easily. There is nothing at all “difficult” about the test, suggesting that either Trump didn’t take it or didn’t pass it and is lying. Only the mentally impaired would consider the test “difficult.” Trump has claimed that “no one” gets “person, woman, man, camera, TV” in the correct order. Only Trump can remember five words in the proper order. According to Trump, the astonished doctors said, “That's amazing. How did you do that?” But in the interview where Trump demonstrated his amazing one-of-a-kind ability, within less than a minute he got the order wrong, reversing the order to “man, woman.”Dr. Gartner noted several symptoms of dementia in a single Trump speech, the one before CPAC:This weekend, Trump showed more evidence of his accelerating dementia. Trump named the wrong month for the primary, said that Putin would rather see Biden as president and he [Trump] agreed with him, and that he made Israel the capital of Israel. But most important are the fundamental breakdowns in his ability to use language. Once you become aware of a symptom, you start to notice it, whereas before you might have overlooked it.Indeed, the symptom’s of Trump’s dementia are everywhere, in his speeches, interviews and tweets. In an interview with David Pakman, Dr. Gartner said these are "clear signs of dementia" and very different from Joe Biden confusing names and dates. Gartner pointed out that at age 66 he too sometimes confuses names and dates, yet is a much better psychologist at age 66 than he was 20 years ago.Trump is evidencing formal thought disorder, where his basic ability to use language is breaking down.Trump also has physical symptoms according to Dr. Gartner:These physical symptoms include a wide base to his gait, his leaning posture, and his loss of fine motor control. … In my opinion, Trump is showing a level of symptoms where no real expert would think that there is not something seriously wrong with his mind and brain.Even before Trump began exhibiting symptoms of advanced cognitive decline, numerous mental health experts observed that he exhibited symptoms of being a malignant narcissist, psychopath and/or sociopath, such as a lack of empathy and wildly inflated ego. For instance, Trump has bragged repeatedly about “acing” a very simple test for cognitive decline.Trump is bragging about passing the MOCA, a screening test for dementia, as if it made him MENSA, when it’s a test any kindergartener should pass.Trump has a stunning lack of awareness of his limitations. These are things he said “nobody knows” except for Trump, which means he assumes that if Trump didn’t know something, no one else could either:“Nobody knew that healthcare could be so complicated.”“Few people have ever heard of a Category 5 [hurricane].”“Nobody ever heard of a caravan.”“Nobody heard of Osama bin Laden until the World Trade Center.”“Nobody heard the word ‘trillion’ until 10 years ago.”“Nobody had even heard of Ebola” in 2012 or 2014.Other examples of Trump’s lack of awareness and/or outright dishonesty:Trump has claimed that he “built the greatest economy in the history of the world” and was “the greatest jobs president God ever created.” In reality, Trump presided over the greatest American job loss since the Great Depression.Trump repeatedly lied about the coronavirus while 400,000 Americans went to their graves on his watch. Trump’s lies included that the coronavirus was a hoax, just the flu, limited to a handful of people and completely under control, sure to vanish with the spring heat, etc.Trump lied when he told journalists he knew nothing about $130,000 in hush money paid to porn star Stormy Daniels. In reality, Trump had already reimbursed Michael Cohen, his personal lawyer and “fixer,” and had set up a Delaware cover company to keep the payment secret.Trump repeatedly said that a bigger, better healthcare plan was coming “in two weeks” when in reality there never was a Trump healthcare plan. Rather, Trump tried to wreck Obamacare without having a replacement plan for all the Americans he would have killed, if he had succeeded with his evil plot.Trump claimed over 150 times that he got the Veterans Choice program passed after other presidents had tried and failed for years. But in reality the Veterans Choice program was passed during the presidency of Barack Obama in 2014.Trump falsely claimed multiple times to have been named Michigan’s Man of the Year, when he never lived in Michigan to be eligible for the award.Trump’s biggest lie is called the BIG LIE — that he won the 2020 election when in reality he lost in a Biden landslide by more than 7 million popular votes and by a 306-232 margin in the electoral college.Trump’s lack of awareness of what is happening to him mentally is a big part of the problem:One of the things that's most notable is Trump's lack of awareness when he makes these mistakes. He very rarely corrects himself or goes back, typical for someone with this kind of organic decline. Ironically, Trump boasted that “If I were cognitively impaired, I’d know it,” but actually he wouldn’t, and he doesn’t. Sometimes a patient with organic brain damage will have what we call a "catastrophic reaction," where they suddenly realize "Oh, my God, I can't think!" They'll then have an anxiety attack or begin weeping because their denial has been broken through and suddenly, they realize just how serious their condition is.MAGA is a big part of the problem, by applauding and cheering Trump’s deeply disturbed and disturbing behavior:As for Trump's MAGA people and other supporters, in a healthy relationship, they would become concerned for Trump and realize that what appears to be his worsening cognition and other behavior actually makes him not qualified for the presidency and that he should seek help. Instead, the worse Trump's behavior becomes the more they seem to adore him. This is textbook collective pathology.As a translator, editor and publisher of poems about the Holocaust, I must note that the collective pathology of Nazi Germany, in which Hitler expressed similar pathologies and received wild applause and adulation in return, led to the destruction of Germany. Ditto for Mussolini and Italy. Ditto for Hirohito and Japan. Ditto for Putin, who is in the process of destroying Russia with his murderous invasion of Ukraine. There is invariably a severe price to be paid, for adulating a psychopathic leader. And things are only going to get worse, where Trump is concerned:Whatever personality disorder someone has, it gets dramatically worse as their cognitive functions decline. All of Trump's viciousness, hostility, and unpredictable and other pathological behavior is only going to get worse. In the end, Trump and the MAGA movement are a cult, and he is the leader.But MAGA is not the only problem. The so-called “mainstream media” with its false equivalence of a mild Joe Biden gaffe to a Trump meltdown, is a big part of the problem:I don’t want to say the mainstream media is covering up Trump’s cognitive disability, but they certainly aren’t covering it like the five-alarm fire it is. The media will show Trump being combative and saying something outrageous and his audience reacting to it — but they are consistently not showing the parts of Trump’s speeches and interviews where his eyes go blank, his jaw goes slack, he looks confused, and slurs words, uses non-words, can't finish a sentence, rambles, perseverates, confabulates and babbles incoherently. That’s what should make the 6 o’clock news. Doesn’t the media have a duty to warn the public that the man who wants the nuclear codes back (not including the ones he probably stole) is publicly displaying unimpeachable evidence of a broken and deteriorating brain?Yes, and a brain that was sociopathic and psychopathic to begin with, and is now getting worse and worse. Much worse. A third critical problem is the people who will take advantage of Trump’s rapid mental decline, such as Stephen Miller and Steve Bannon.The obvious comparison here is Ronald Reagan. I am no fan of Reagan and do not understand the worship of that man. We now have confirmation that towards the end of his presidency that he was basically senile. The United States and the world were very lucky that Reagan was surrounded, mostly, by very serious people who were institutionalists. By comparison, Donald Trump is surrounded by fascists, white supremacists, Christian nationalists, plutocrats, corporatists, and other malign actors who are going to take advantage of the situation to get what they want. That possibility — if not outright certainty — should terrify any reasonable thinking person. There will be no guardrails to Trump's absolute most primitive, impulsive, destructive, and insane actions. There will be no pushback from within his inner circle and regime. I have no reason to. If anything it might make people more aware. Before I've written briefly about having a family member addicted to drugs. That person is my older brother, my only sibling, really. Outside of this we were close growing up, the family bond was strong with us and unfortunately he also had to act a bit like a parent to me to help my mother. Our age gap is 8 years [a middle child was born with complications and died shortly after birth] and I am the youngest. The last one born before my parents split up and divorced. My brother has a lot of health problems. Mainly mentally. , there is the family history. In that history is depression (whether chemical, situational, regular or maniac), Schizophrenia, anxiety, addiction and some physical health problems such as the heart and a bad back. Growing up as a kid, I heard about this. My (Mum's sister) Aunt had it(4). We've never been sure what he's had but.. He's had a few breakdowns. The earliest I remember being scared on an extreme anger burst wasn't even directed at me and might have been a reaction to something my mother did to him. i.e. kicking her 15 year old son out. Because I was so young at the time, I cannot be completely sure what happened between my mother and my brother(1). I was also semi the golden child. Not completely but enough compared to him. I attribute this to me being female AND being the “baby,” of the family, let alone the miracle baby given my mother's problems with having them. It could have also been because of what my mum was like, I won't go into it too much; read my answer to “What's the saddest secret your father has ever confided in you?” If you're curious. The police were called for that instance. The next instance is blurry a bit because I was around 14–15. This was around 8 years ago. Something happened that caused me to me taken from my mother, even though me keeping a bread knife with me was because of my own mental health (depression/anxiety and idealation of self harm) and not hers. Sorry, but I'm not naive enough to believe parents can have the all seeing eye of God and know everything about their children every minute of the day. -PART 1- Moving on.. because of that I lived with my brother [Let's call him Jim] and his long standing girlfriend for 6 months. It was a mix of fun times as I was super close to school and could walk there! I lost a lot of weight and found a group of friends that were in walking distance. I had a fun social life and even found a girlfriend myself eventually. The downside? My brother's relationship with his girlfriend ended. I do not begrudge him this, from what I found out they did not seem like a good fit. HOWEVER, that relationship had gone for about 4 years and nearly 9 months. To say he had a breakdown was an understatement. This is the true beginning of my story.. Because of the stress from being with her and dealing and the financial repercussions of her spending habits (and others) plus his habit of anger and stuff and then the relationship ending… Jim started going down hill. I found out later he'd started taking drugs.* What I remember from it: I was yelled at serverely for small things. Crumbs in the butter, if I closed or “slammed,” the door. Whether it was on purpose or not. We also started to not have a lot of food in the fridge at the end of my stay. And I wasn't allowed to go see my mother for her 50th either (no one could take me or find a way to get me there). That killed me inside. But because it was so long ago I cannot remember everything he yelled at me for, only the feelings. And how much my anxiety disorder was set off. He would never, ever hit me. He and I both know that but… Well, you'll see in next part. -PART 2- Fast forward to about a couple of years ago, perhaps 2017–2018. My brother, Jim, had been working as an apprentice at a steel place. It had been going good. He was close to finishing it too. But.. The business went in to debt. It closed down. His boss have him notice so he could find work because he knew it would be harder for my brother. That was good. But for my brother, it didn't end well. We're not sure exactly what got him on the line of thought other than him losing a job he loved and how hard it can be to find work but he went back to drugs. This time was worst. About 10 pm on a coldish night, he turns up at my door. I answer and he asks if he can come in and stay the night, he's wearing just a t-shirt and thin clothing. I say yes. That was my mistake. What happens from there is nearly two days of torture and him yelling at walls to me, my dad, my mum. He starts cleaning up my place when I never asked him to. Granted it needed it badly but I never asked him to do that. That will become important in a bit Now as I'm trying to sleep I hear his ranting and raving through the walls. Hate towards mum and dad. The other stuff he said was probably worse when he didn't know I could hear. Possibly stuff like “how can she sleep?” Said with a lot of negative emotions and some other stuff.
