column1: What, if anything, do you hate the most about being Indian or being from India?
column3: To begin, hate is a very strong word. I am simply going to use this question as an outlet to vent out all the frustrations I have against Indian culture that I cannot share with my family members. I was not raised in India but being Indian I can identify with certain aspects of the culture I have issues with and make me question where I come from. So, here it is in no particular order: 1. Too much emphasis on Physical Aspects: Why do I have a problem with emphasis on good skin?As a girl, if you don't have good skin, hair or a figure, be ready to fall prey to mother's daily recommendations on what to do for your skin, hair or body. Not only does she take immense pride in always giving you advice on what's good for you, she also justifies making constant comments about your physical being be knowing what's good for you. Mommy knows best girls! Trust me, this starts as soon as a girl becomes 13. Every time, I get a few pimples on my cheek, before even saying good morning, both my parents are just shocked. They ask, "What happened to your face?". This sentence not only makes me completely lose my cool completely but it hurts more than a slap. Even a slap would feel better. Growing up listening to this comment, I learned to gradually ignore my parents because I realised that I had a choice. That choice was for me to accept my parent's being overly critical or just accept myself for who I am. A few pimples on my face don't have anything on how I approach people, how I think or who can be my friend. I am now 23 and have stopped caring about what my parents say about my face. Inspite of clearly telling them how I feel when they say such things, my voice has been ignored. For 10 years.The obsession with fairness.Just this morning, I had used a face mask of pure honey on my face. My mom was happy that I was trying to take care of my skin, but she then proceeded to pester me to use lemon juice with the honey. I told her, that she has been saying this from the last year and I tried lemon and it dried out my skin. What's worse is that my skin is already dry. She once again, paid no attention to my words and then proceeded to tell me all about this one lady who supposedly applied Olive Oil and Brandy face mask to her new born daughter's skin and from being dark she became fair. Good skin is for our health but it is completely natural for pimples to appear from time to time. I have a bigger problem with criticism of any imperfections on our skin but with not accepting the skin for what it is. 2. An impossible pressure to be married. Why should a girl be pressured into marrying when she is 21 but a boy should not? I have a question to other Indian boys, have you been asked to "start looking" for a girl when you turned 21? Or did your mother simply allow you to grow up? Find a job for yourself and give yourself a few years to become financially stable. I also don't understand why should a boy always have to be 2-3 years older than a girl when it comes to "looking for a partner". 3. Stigma towards people with learning disabilities and being mentally disabled. Do take note that these are two very different things. Having a learning disability means that you have cognitive ability but it is simply slower than the normal person. Being mentally disabled means that there is a defect in your hormones or sometimes in your brain structure and this affects day to day life much more significantly. These individuals struggle with basic functions such as eating, showering, sleeping on time and add learning in school. My blood really boils when I hear other parents making insensitive comments about somebody else's disabled child. It's either that or complete sympathy but no empathy. People need to have enough sense to differentiate between empathy and sympathy. Nature is not "cruel" to some individuals in society and also stop using these individuals as inspiration porn. Get with it you Educated people! I once heard my uncle tell my mother that a So-And-So's three old child might be mentally disabled and there are talks going in society. Apparently she cannot talk or walk "as per the standard". Families who have maybe a disabled child or a relative will of course be more understanding towards disability. My problem is with the reaction of the general public when they see a disabled child in public places like a mall, park or swimming pool. I have volunteered with special needs children for a very long time and have been a sad witness to these reactions. 4. Representation of " Indian Values" on Television Almost every TV serial, shows women to almost always be house wives. If not, then the more career oriented woman is "bossy". The shows also demean women by constantly showing them as subjects to emotional manipulation. 5. It is okay for Indian men to do whatever they want but not the same for a girl. Even though, this might be part of anothe answer on this thread, I will let out the couple of questions that have been swirling in my brain like an angry swarm of bees. Why can't a girl date a guy? Why can't a girl have a glass of wine? Why can't a girl be allowed to speak her mind on what is blatantly wrong? Why can't she form an opinion? Why can't she form her own thoughts and perspectives? Why can't she find work? Why does she have to be pressurized into being married young but not the guy? And lastly, why is she constantly criticized for physical aspects but not the guy? So a guy can drink, go out to parties, stay out late, visit friends and even mabe have more than one relationship in his twenties but it's wrong for a girl to do the same. 6. No respect for servants or maids. I have seen people actually pay their servants or maids very less for all the housework they do, and also give them lesser food. What's even more pathetic is that the person cooks all the food. All three meals are made by this person and they barely even get two meals a day. Why is it against anything for the person who cooked 3 meals for somebody to not have their share? I am talking about full time maids or servants who go through this issue. I grew up with a maid myself and she is has played an equally important role in raising me just like my parents. I am simply disgusted when I see some helpers treated badly.When I was in India, this one time, my parents had gotten a helper from family friends to assist with lifting the luggage and placing it into the taxi. I was completely horrified and disgusted when I noticed that the helper was as old as my grandfather. In the same culture, where we are always told to "respect our elders", how is it ever appropriate to ask somebody that old and frail to lift suitcases? Luckily we only had two suitcases and I carried both of them by myself down the stairs. My parents were too shocked to say anything. A family friend casually remarked that I should grow a mustache, muscles and call myself a man. Disclaimer: This is not intended to paint my parents or the culture in bad light. I have had numerous debates with my own parents and am thankful to them for giving me the space to ask questions and have an opinion. I want to see India change for the better just as anybody else.

column1: What causes some people with borderline personality disorder to seem happy even though they suffer greatly emotionally and mentally?
column3: There are two factors to this:1) OUR CHILDHOOD(Britney Spears, famous borderline and scapegoat child) BPD is driven by childhood trauma. Most of us were scapegoat children in the toxic narcissistic family structure, as opposed to golden children or invisible children. That meant, for the narcissists in our family, we were born as someone to abuse, someone to blame, a place for people who cannot process shame to project their shame and self loathing. Being children, we do not understand we are being abused or that our parents are mentally ill. We believe our parents are just as perfect and grandiose as they say they are. And we are just as worthless as they say we are. We believe we were born all bad, as we are told, and if we want to earn love then we must meet standards of unreachable perfection.These standards include:Being cute/beautifulGender conformity and performanceBeing politeFollowing all the rulesGetting perfect gradesPerforming for our parents for entertainmentPerforming household laborServicing our parents: back massages, foot massages—it can even be sexual and often isEnduring beatings and emotional and psychological abuseEnduring bullying, mockery, and humiliationCatering to our parents’ and siblings’ emotional needs when they are emotionalHaving no emotional needs of our ownDealing with our grief and trauma aloneAgreeing with our parents and siblings who say our abuse was deservedSo, imagine you are enduring daily beatings and/or sexual abuse as a child for unjust punishments you can’t understand… …and you are absolutely terrified of doing something wrong at school and losing YOUR TEACHER’S LOVE, which is the only reprieve you have from abuse. …And also absolutely terrified that you will upset your parents and get more abuse if you do anything wrong. …And also feeling like, maybe, just maybe, if you can be the PERFECT child, you’ll finally be lovable and worthy. …And also having family pressure to be exceptional, because your goodness helps to SECURE THEIR MASKS. …And also watching your siblings get lovebombed and spoiled and wanting to be loved like that. ….Well, you’re going to “be daddy’s strong little soldier,” as Britney Spears described it, and you’re going to PERFORM.You’re going to try to be the sweetest, happiest child with no emotional needs who is not a burden and pray that this is the escape route from your internal confusion and suffering. To get a release from the pain and shame we internalize, we begin to self harm. I first attempted suicide at 8, began burning and cutting shortly after, bulimia by my teen years, and smoking by my 20s. Yet I had a 4.0 GPA and a smile always. Also by my teen years, I developed a sex addiction, desperate for human touch. To narcissists like my family.And because narcissists live in fantasy and also have sex addiction and codependency on supply, we learn how to become people’s sexual fantasy in attempts to secure love. We master the arts of seduction.(Famous borderline). It never makes anyone stay. We become more and more abused.(Announcing her divorce from Joe DiMaggio after enduring domestic violence). WHILE NARCISSISTS MASK THEIR REAL IDENTITY, BORDERLINES MASK THEIR REAL EMOTIONAL STATE. I always knew I had mental health problems. My parents always said I was crazy and/or I was retarded. I asked for mental health care but was told psychologists were crazy. I always read books about suicidal, mentally ill girls, trying to feel less alone and heal. This is why I ultimately got my degrees in psychology: I didn’t want to be a psychologist: I wanted to be a writer (got an MFA in poetry too). The psychology degrees were to try to heal, to understand people, to find the answers denied to me. Because we were socialized to take blame for everything, even things we didn’t do, we become pretty shameless, which also aggravates narcissists, who are working overtime to hide and never admit shame. We process what they can only project.We then learn to have high levels of performance and even give much to the emotional needs of others while neglecting and suppressing mountains of our own grief. We grow up to be empaths, and this childhood trauma becomes a source of our resilience and ability to perform and work and give healing to others who are suffering—doing so with a smile through the darkest pains.Notice her last line… But despite our smiles, we are deeply susceptible to trauma bonding, being stuck in violent and/or abusive relationships, addiction, and suicide, unless we have a chance to fully grieve and resolve that childhood trauma, which takes many years, and many borderlines never get accurately diagnosed or have access to help or safe places and people to process with.2) WE ARE EASILY MADE HAPPYI believe this is the trait about me that narcissists and sociopaths have resented most. Because I’ve never known someone with NPD or ASPD who wasn’t constantly complaining, constantly jealous and judgmental, and constantly unhappy. Only abuse gave them relief. Whereas, borderlines have a childhood innocence due to our childhood trauma. (We often attract pedophiles as children or even adults due to this). People have always told me I seem childlike, and every borderline I know does too. Again, Britney’s posts are a great example.In one sense, when unhealed, we can be very naieve. We love everyone and give everyone the benefit of the doubt, and we get burned and blindsided a lot due to this. Because people with the most shames will cling to people with our disability, just as they will also cling to children, the autistic, the elderly, and other mental handicaps. They see this as easy supply: easy prey. They can relish feeling the fantasy of having power over us and engaging in duper’s delight with us. But in the other sense, it is really not hard to make us happy. We didn’t have lovebombs, or love, in our childhood, so just a little bit always feels like A WHOLE LOT for us.I feel happy on a beautiful day, during a stunning lightning storm, drinking a delicious cup of coffee, reading a good book, enjoying some lovely art, making art, being in my home and taking stock of my blessings. If someone gives me a simple card, I will burst into tears of gratitude. Gifts make me beside myself in shock. Borderlines often love and bond strongly to animals. But our ease of happiness is also why we can trauma bond to narcissists for so long. We are susceptible to lovebombing manipulation. We’ll internalize abuses as our fault and be satisfied with simple breadcrumbs of affection, while we give consistent love until the abuse or betrayal becomes a threat and we collapse and see our loved ones as predators. These collapses can be shocking and they are traumatic. Imagine thinking you had the love of your life for years, only to get cheated on a million times, to try couple’s therapy and personal therapy because your love says it’s your fault, and then need to get a restraining order after your home is broken into and destroyed, and then finding out in court that the love of your life is actually a registered sex offender. (True story). It is a shocking collapse, and it hurts.While narcissists split for no reason and stay stuck in devaluation; borderlines stay stuck in idealization for no reason and then split in pure shock when the abuser’s mask comes off. Then we revert to all the toxic fighting tactics we learned in childhood. And abusers are very sensitive, so they respond badly to it. It triggers their complex PTSD.It’s why they smear and bully borderlines and empaths so badly online. However, even in the worst moments, we have been self healing by finding ways to self soothe and finding joy where we can, so we can find happiness when suffering. It can cause our emotions to seesaw dramatically. Just look at Britney, dancing, just days after her divorce announcement.Very typical borderline. You cannot deny her light. It is why she is so hated. It is why it took a mass movement to fight for her freedom from enslavement with her father. In fact, when we leave abusers, we tend to start doing better. Our physical health issues go away, our skin clears, we find mental clarity, we find peace and quiet, we get wiser, and this agitates narcissists even more. They want the power to break us and make us permanently sad. They want to break our light and our ability to love like they are broken. They don’t want anyone else to have us or love us or be happy for us or because of us. They can become very obsessed with us for that reason. They never emotionally attach to us, but they want to own and control us. Not having that can trigger them to the most dangerous mental states.However, that hole in our hearts that says we are unlovable and everyone we love will abandon us or betray us and we can never be perfect enough remains. UNTIL WE GRIEVE OUR CHILDHOODS FULLY, AWAKEN TO OUR PATTERNS, LEARN TO RECOGNIZE ABUSERS, AND BECOME ENLIGHTENED EMPATHS. This can set us on a healing journey for ourselves and others. We usually have many spiritual gifts, from lucid dreaming to premonitions. I wish the same healing for our narcissist siblings, family members, and lovers, but, as every borderline knows, healing is long term work you must commit to and want independently. We can’t always be responsible for regulating others’ emotions. I pray for them, and I know I cannot enmesh with them, or anyone, anymore for my own health and freedom. However, many borderlines never make it that far to healing. Our life is expectancy is 39, and many of us die tragically. May the borderline reading this be the Phoenix and rise from the fire of the pain that made them: leave what doesn’t serve you behind in a pile of ash. Find what makes you smile and don’t ever apologize for smiling.

column1: Do you feel like the mental health of you or people around you have been affected by all the negative in 2020?
column3: Yes, definitely, all of us, everyone I know has struggled in some way. The uncertainty, losing jobs, being cooped up at home, changes in the way we do things, depression, anxiety, feeling overwhelmed. I had a couple months of anxiety that made me go to the doctor to try to find some kind of medication to help, I was losing it, in a constant state of panic. A lot of people I know are struggling because their friends and family are divided over politics and all the other issues in the country, to the point they’re disowning family members. That’s all extremely stressful but humans are adaptable and we will learn how to deal with everything. Hopefully we won’t have too many more crazy things happen this year, but I kind of doubt it because this year is going to wake everyone up in some way, and it isn’t easy to look at ourselves and change. I hope you are doing well and not struggling too much, but if you are, please be kind to yourself, try not to take everything too seriously or spend too much time looking at the news or the internet because the nature of it really messes with us, trying to create fear. Turn it all off and go outside, read a book, nap, exercise, do something good for yourself and let it go for a little while.

column1: Should I stop pleasing people even if it means losing all of them?
column3: This question doesn’t necessarily have a size-fits-all answer. However, evaluating the situation, the people that surround your inner circle (friends, close family members, coworkers), and which context of people pleasing affects your mental and physical health. If it is more negative than positive, carefully evaluate who you believe it is most necessary to help. Most of the time, you’ll find yourself in the most need of self-preservation. It’s the psychological equivalent of putting your oxygen mask on first, so you can help others.

column1: What is it like to be a flight attendant right now in 2020?
column3: This is my personal experience and views about being a cabin crew right now. I feel flying right now, is all about anxiety, stress, discomfort, and worries. These days I feel things are much more difficult and negative compared to pre- Covid-19 days. Which is understandable. It is the same in all jobs and companies right now.Job security. You no longer know if you will have your job tomorrow or not. Airlines are laying off staff, you never know what tomorrow brings. That is the most negative with having this job right now. Living each day in fear that you will lose your job. When will I lose my job? Who knows. Perhaps tomorrow or next week.Unhealthy working environment. You are working in a job where you can end up getting dead or seriously ill. The working environment is no longer optimal or safe. You meet so many people onboard, and you never know if you will end up getting sick or not. It is extremely uncomfortable to work during these times. To have the mask, gloves, and protective stuff on. Especially now during summertime. It is so hot and you sweat all the time. It is truly so uncomfortable. A co-worker fainted onboard a few days ago. Because of all the protective gear that she was wearing and it was very hot onboard.Layover. In some destinations, we are not allowed to leave the hotel. In other destinations we can for example go to the nearest grocery store etc. But we are not allowed to enjoy the layovers like we used to. Not allowed to sightsee etc. In some destinations, they removed the layovers, and made the flight a turnaround. We get to rest onboard instead. Sometimes we operate the flight with two sets of teams. One team operates the flight and on our way back, they rest. Then the next team takes over etc.Salary/benefits. Things are slowly changing. The benefits and salary we used to have, have changed. The airlines want to save as much as possible now. For example, we used to have discounts in various places, but now slowly one by one they are removing those. We no longer have the same benefits etc. They reduced our salaries temporarily. But who knows, once the Pandemic if over, they might reduce our salaries permanently. Or reduce it for a fixed period, to a different number than what we had pre-Covid. I am no longer flying as much as I used to, this has resulted in not getting a lot each month.Customer service. We have removed various items from the normal meal service. The passengers isn't getting excellent service like before. We no longer have the same interaction that we used to with the passengers. It is strange to not be able to do your job properly as you are used to. Of course, this is temporary. Once the Pandemic is over, we will get back to the excellent customer service. But I wonder if certain changes will remain forever because of Covid-19.Work-life balance. I am not seeing people as often as I used to anymore. I am not going out and trying to social distance etc. Because of Covid-19, it has mostly been ''Work and home'' on repeat. I don't meet anyone anymore. Especially with the job that I have, meeting so many people onboard. I am being responsible and have been trying to self isolate when I am not working. This has resulted in me not having much of a work-life balance. Although I know this is normal and everyone is experiencing this.Co-workers. You try to not get too attached to your co-workers these days. You never know, one day they will fly with you, and the next day they are laid off and moved away. It has become a sad thing. Most of my co-workers are not in their best moods these days. You can sense the energy onboard among us crew members. The excellent teamwork we used to have, isn't as excellent anymore. We have masks onboard and this means that we can not see the expressions on each other's faces. It is difficult to work onboard looking like robots. Acting like robots too. I used to smile all the time when talking to my co-workers onboard. The same with passengers. Now that we are not able to see emotions because of the masks, I feel the environment has become very cold.Rules and regulations. I am confused whenever I have a flight. The rules and regulations change daily. One day they tell us to do this, the next it has changed. We need to keep up with all the new changes onboard. It is confusing with all the new changes that happens daily. There are more rules and regulations now. My head spins when I read memos that we get about the changes.Hotels. We used to stay in amazing 4–5 star hotels during our layovers. Now that the airlines are trying to save money, they have changed a lot of those hotels to 3–4 stars. We still have some 4–5 star hotels left. But I assume they will remove those as well. A lot of those hotels are now close to the airport. Before they used to be close to the airport as well, but now more of them are. It used to be a cool thing visiting these hotels during my layovers. Now everything is closed and you can't experience those hotels like you did before.Personal health. My mental health isn't the best. You are worried, feeling anxious, stressed, scared, and depressed. You feel affected because of Covid-19, your job security, your economy, and that you are not able to meet your friends and family. Of course, I have good days too, but overall this situation has brought a dark cloud over my head. Again this is something most of us are feeling and going through.Changes. There are a lot of changes happening right now. For example, the contract I have will most probably change in the near future. The new joiners that will join the airline in the future, will most probably get a new contract. Changes in salary, flying hours, benefits and health insurance, etc. Changes that will benefit the airlines and not us crew members. A lot of changes so that the airlines can save money.Manager and employee. The relationship between my managers, and I, have changed. It was never a good relationship, to begin with, but now more than ever I feel replaceable and invisible in the company. The airlines are looking after themselves and not us. It is of course understandable that companies during these times want to do everything they can to survive. Including laying off their best staff. But when discussing the relationship between us, it is an all-time low right now. Covid-19 has truly messed up everything. Covid-19 has created a huge rift between me and my managers/airline.These are my personal views and what I am experiencing right now, with the airline that I work for. I did not mean for this answer to be so negative. But this is the reality. I don't want to sugar coat it and say it is amazing to be a cabin crew right now. Yes, I do have fun days too, but the bad days and the negative stuff are much more heavier and more visible these days.

column1: Why does a friend walk out of another friend’s life?
column3: This behaviour about walking out from a friend’s life can be explained. Psychology says there are multiple causes of a single behaviour. Because the conditions vary under which a particular behaviour is observed. Let us say there is a condition that your friend is migrating to another city. Now we are interested in knowing what occurs with this friendship. There can be two explanations to this behaviour. Two phrases namely Out of sight, out of mind and Distance makes the heart grow fonder briefly describe the explanations. But both of the statements contradict each other. So one of them should persist in such a case. It will depend on what happens in your life once your friend has left. If you manage to find another friend as a replacement your attraction and connectivity will diminish. And the former one is most likely to be true on this situation. The other way around you will be continuing this friendship no matter of distance and so the latter one is applicable then. According to a research for a friendship to last forever it needs to complete seven years. We meet many people in life. Not all remain in touch. When we complete school and graduation we all have different paths to follow leading to different directions. Those remaining in touch must be ones sharing the same wavelength, interests and passions. Often beliefs contradict and friendships are officially or unofficially broken. What should be the right way is to allow each other to express but not to judge or criticise directly. However, we all have different perspectives. But most of the times distance is created for this misunderstanding which starts from not even listening to each other and keeping grudges. column1: What is it like living with mental disorders? How does it affect your everyday life?
column3: It is….mostly really, really hard. Often unbearable. Incredibly frustrating. Isolating. Not only do we endure torture inflicted by our own brains, but the symptoms of our illnesses are misunderstood by our friends and family. Our relationships suffer simply because we are sick. When our illnesses rear their ugly heads, we are often blamed for the crisis. We are told we have no willpower, that we just need to “snap out of it”, that our illnesses render us incapable of functioning in society. At the same time, we are accused of malingering, of being lazy, of being antisocial. Buck up. Think positive. “Everyone feels like that sometimes”. No, not everyone seriously considers suicide to be the blissful end to the torture their brain subjects them to. Not everyone has to wonder whether their emotions are “real” or a symptom of their illness. Not everyone is shunned just because they are sick. Not everyone is told that taking medication for their illness is a sign of weak character. Not everyone risks losing friends family and jobs if they choose to disclose their illness to their friends, family members or coworkers/employers. Day to day I either work extremely hard to keep from hurting myself, to keep my head above the rising floodwaters in my mind, or I try to enjoy the relative peace that stability brings without worrying about the inevitable next episode or crisis. It's exhausting and it takes so much work. Some weeks getting out of bed takes so much effort that I can't find the energy or motivation to even shower or eat. Some weeks I can be thankful that the turmoil in my brain had died down. Stress is almost sure to trigger an episode, and it doesn't have to be that much stress: getting a cold or the flu, working for too long (for me more than 16 hours a week or 4 hours a day), prolonged or chronic physical pain. In short, my illnesses take every bit of energy I have, even when I'm stable. EDIT: I realize that some of the language in this post is disturbing. I am not currently suicidal, and I do not mean to encourage those who are to act. If you are feeling suicidal, please contact your mental health team, a crisis hotline in your area, or your local emergency department. It does get better. You will get through this. You will be stronger for it.

column1: What are some K-Tube trends that need to exit in 2023?
column3: There are multiple that I would love to get rid of. So buckle up buttercup, because you’re in for a ride.Save one/Drop oneI don’t think this needs to be explained. But for those wondering why I think this needs to be left in the past, allow me to present this idea. Imagine you’re a k-pop idol. You worked for years to audition, dreaming about the day you’ll get to debut with a group of guys/girls chasing their dreams just like you. The day comes and you strut your stuff. To your surprise, you get accepted. Then you’re forced to do daily weigh ins, watch your weight, exercise, and dance for hours on end, losing sleep, all of that. You don’t get to debut until the company decides you can. And the day comes where you can debut. You’re ecstatic. Finally! You’re debuting. And let’s say for good measure, you’re group is fairly successful. You’re not super big, but you’re working your way up. how do you think idols would feel if they were on YouTube, and they saw their name in a drop/save one. It’s purely disgusting and utterly disrespectful to the idols themselves. They lose their freedom in order to chase their dream. “But they knew..” it doesn’t matter. Just because you like one idol more than another does not mean you, or anyone, have the right to decide who ought to stay in the group/industry. Grow up. all idols work equally hard for our entertainment, and face mental health challenges as their contracts continue. Foreign idols don’t get to go back home much, and when they do it’s only for a spell. Can you imagine seeing that and knowing you aren’t wanted? I can’t.Dating issuesobviously, I don’t care if my faves date. I sincerely hope they do find someone who’s right for them, and who can be by their side through it all. But the amount of hate the idol and their significant other get is ridiculous. Why CANT they date? Why can’t they have a relationship just like us? Why CANT they dream of starting a family? They won’t be around forever. They won’t get any younger. They won’t be able to stay around in the industry forever. And that’s okay. Because we, as fans, should be the ones rooting for them. Not tearing them downDebuting minorsMaybe you’ve all heard about YG’s new girl group, BaeMon. Supposedly, the youngest is 13. I don’t know if it’s true. Nobody does, as all sites are saying something different. So what’s the problem between debuting people who are young? A lot of things, honestly. I get it. It’s part of the marketing strategy. I must say it’s smart. Young/fresh faces that are attractive will catch our eye. And that means they won’t age as quickly. the downside is the toll it’ll take on mental health, as well physical. I can’t imagine how it would affect their world knowledge, and how it would affect their family members. Even if they are from Korea, I can only imagine how often parents get to see their children. It would probably affect their social skills and cognitive skills as well. So… yeah.

column1: Did quarantine work? Obviously it helped against the spread of Covid-19, but was it worth it?
column3: I would say no. Some countries did not use lockdowns and quarantines, and from what I’ve seen, they did about as well as anyone else. The only people that should have been quarantined were those with serious medical problems which made the virus much worse for them. IMO the mental health of a lot of people, especially children, was badly affected by the lockdowns, and I don’t know anyone who thinks that their children got as good an education during the lockdown years as they would have if they’d been physically in school. Also, there are 5 million people in the US in nursing homes, and we didn’t lose anything near 5 million people. Even most of the people in nursing homes survived. That’s not to dismiss the grief of those who lost family members because that was very sad, but in a macro sense, I personally don’t think the quarantines helped compared to the damage they did including jobs lost.

column1: To anyone who has caught COVID-19, or knows someone who has, how bad are the symptoms?
column3: I tested COVID Positive today. I think I qualify enough to answer this question. Let's start from the beginning. My father was hospitalized for serious health conditions in NCR- Delhi. I had to urgently rush from Lucknow to Delhi to see him. My husband and I went through flight. My father was COVID negative. He had other health conditions. I stayed there for a week. And came back to Lucknow (again by flight) on the 13th August, 2020. Here starts my journey. 13th August- I felt a little discomfort in my throat. The food I ate was a little off too. I somehow had a premonition of having acquired the virus, either in transit or at hospital when I regularly visited my father there. Perhaps my symptoms showed later. 14th-15th August- I felt extremely cold at night. I was shivering. I had running nose and cough too. On 14th I started my homeopathic medicines to control fever. And, I also took paracetamol for two days. I haven't gotten any fever since then. I also isolated myself completely and started with my home remedies of hot water, steam, kaadhaa and turmeric milk. I stopped taking normal water completely. Only and only hot beverages. 16th-17th August- I felt a little uneasy. I was making a lot of efforts for a good breath. My breathing wasn't normal. Air wasn't going into my lungs and I could feel it. I got exhausted too soon. My chest felt constricted, like there was some pressure on it. My nose felt wierd. 18th August- I visited a doctor in emergency at the nearby hospital. He asked me a lot of questions. There was a 1.5 hours counseling too. My saturation and oxygen level were fine. All vitals were perfectly okay. Yet, the doctor said that all my symptoms were that of corona, but they would start with flu medicines initially. If the symptoms did not suppress, they would get me tested. Most importantly, he counselled me to steer clear of any kind of stress or anxiety because this is too harmful for immunity. 19th August- I stopped working because apparently mental exhaustion was making things a little worse for me. I continued to feel discomfort in breathing. In the noon, I realized that my sense of smell has completely vanished. I was sanitizing my hands and couldn't feel it's smell. I jumped from my chair and put lots of deodorant and perfume on my hand and sniffed it. Nothing. My sense of smell is completely muted even now. My nose wasn't blocked. My throat was clear. I was just sure that it isn't a symptom of normal flu. It's a classic corona symptom. I started reading the Oxford research papers frantically. That was the time, I panicked for the first and only time. When you feel loss of smell and taste in flu, you still have some senses. In COVID, they are completely muted as if someone has unplugged that wire from your brain. So, COVID affects the brain too, apart from lungs. The virus mutes certain nerve in the brain. It will take 3–4 weeks to regain these senses back. 20th August- I went to the chest specialist in emergency again. My vitals were again normal. BP, sugar, Oxygen, pulse- all normal. But I was sure I was COVID positive. I was having strong gut feeling. When I have intuition, it's NEVER wrong. The doctor wrote COVID test for me. He said that since I took early precautions of self isolation and hot beverages and steam, I managed my disease at an early stage itself. The same day, I went to SGPGI to get my COVID test. Thankfully there was no crowd there. This was a special Corona Hospital (Trauma Center, SGPGI Lucknow).The white door is where I had to go for swab test after they called my name. God, they were quick! In less than 10 seconds, they took a sample from my nose and throat. The report had to come today, on 21st August. I knew it would be positive. 21st August- At around 4.30 p.m., my husband had called me twice on my phone. I was sleeping. I woke up. I called him back and said, “positive na?” He said, “yes.” He asked me if I was tensed or worried or panicked. I wasn't. It didn't come as a surprise to me at all. I knew all along. I wasn't treating it as a regular flu. I had started my treatment as a corona patient only.So, today I feel fine.I have no fever.I have no cold or cough.I have no body ache.I have no headache.My vitals are fine. Since I have a little breathlessness, I'm supposed to check my oxygen every half hour, or when I'm short of breath.My sense of smell is still completely lost. I cannot smell a thing! You may fart, I wouldn't know! My sense of taste is also muted. Albeit I ate two green chilies to test today. It felt a little hot. For salt and sugar and most of the food, the taste buds are unconscious. I can't differentiate between sugar and salt. That is all. My homeopathic medicines include- Aconite, Belladona, Eupatorium Perf, Bryonia. (My FIL is a homeo-specialist. I'm taking all these medicines as suggested and guided by him, in doses and power explained to me.) My ayurvedic treatment/ home remedies include-Kaadhaa (my MIL is giving it to me 3 times a day)Turmeric milk (once at night)Hot beveragesSteam with eucalyptus oil (as suggested by my SIL) (3–4 times a day. I will increase it further from tomorrow. This will repair lungs faster.)Immunity boosting fruits- Papaya, Orange, Lemon in hot waterProtein diet- Moong daal, garlic, chick peas (chana/chhole), kidney beans (rajma), cottage cheese (paneer- 3 to 4 times a day- raw or roasted).My other medicines include-Vitamic CVitamin DMultivitaminsOne antibioticCough syrupMost important thing- Strong will power/ Fighting spirit. I have to fight this off for a lot of people in my life, but for the most important person- my husband. He isn't at peace since I've fallen sick. He calls me from the other room every half an hour. He chats with me on whatsapp to know the status. He is my alarm clock for pranayam. He video calls me and tells me to practice breathing exercises in front of him. He sits at the good enough distance to talk with me. So these days, he is at the kitchen door and I'm at the door of my room. That's how we talk. Today, I called him in the garden to talk. So he was standing in the garden and I was at the end of my bed. (I had an Amazon COD. I told him to collect that! Haha)Very very important message-As soon as you see the first ever sign or symptom, start treating it like corona and not a normal flu. Only then, you can keep your symptoms under control and manageable.ISOLATE immediately. Don't wait for other family members to show symptoms. Use a separate washroom. Before flushing, close the lid of seat. If possible, spray the sanitizer on seat and flush knob after use. Also spray the sanitizer on taps and knobs of doors you've touched. Steer clear of everyone else. Keep your utensils seperate. Wash them on your own. Keep a seperate dustbin too. Behave like you are all by yourself.Don't ignore the gut feeling. If you feel something off, pay attention and act fast.Stay positive after you've tested positive. You've just lost your sense of smell and taste. Don't lose your sense of humor.Fight. Fight. And, fight. Don't let this virus get to your mind. Fight it. Leave the rest to God. Whatever he has decided, will happen. But for now, keep fighting.Hot beverages only. Stay away from cold water or cold drinks. Just consume hot water.Laugh and make others laugh too. It's just corona. Don't panic. It's just a bloody monster trying to eat you from inside. Kill it in your throat before it reaches to the lungs.Go in reverse and find out- where did you make a mistake? I think I touched my eyes. I do that a lot.Once negative, stay on alert mode. The virus can get you second time too.Keep a check on anxiety. Don't be too psyched or paranoid about the whole situation.P.S. I will get my second test next week perhaps. Till then, have a great time reading! Eat. Pray. Love. Drink (healthy and hot). Edit 1- Thank you for your good wishes. You guys are great! God bless each one of you. Thanks for connecting through comments and messages. P.S. I forgot to mention one of the most important things- DO NOT SIT IN A CLOSED AC ROOM. The same air circulation will make things worse. OPEN THE WINDOWS AND LET THE FRESH OXYGEN BLOW IN. Much, much required. If it feels too hot, turn on the AC, but keep the temperature 27 or 28 and keep the door open. DO NOT SIT IN A CLOSED ROOM. Edit 2- These are the homeopathic medicines I'm taking. Your antibiotics- allopathic medicines and homeopathic ones must have at least one hour gap. Do not mix them. For fever, cold & cough- Aconite- Belladona- Eupatorium Perf 30C (5–6 drops directly after every 2 hours. For example, at 10a.m. if I'm taking Aconite, at 12 I would take Belladona, at 2 Eupatorium Perf and the cycle would continue) For breathlessness- Bryonia 30C (5–6 drops) I was taking it 4 times a day. Yesterday I took Bryonia 200C (200 power) once a day. Don't take 30 power if you have taken 200 power once a day. For Steam- Put 3– 4 drops of eucalyptus oil in water. Steam will repair lungs and improve breathing. Pranayam and breathing exercises. Gargle with hot salt water, or betadine gargle to remove infection fast. For kaadhaa- 6–7 Tulsi leaves, 4–5 laung, 4–5 kaali mirch, 2–3 badi elaichi, a little cinnamon stick (dalcheeni)- all to be boiled in 2 glasses of water unless it reduces to 1 glass. Drink twice or maximum thrice a day. Don't overdo this. P.S. - Please refer to an expert for following medicines. This is my regime. Although it's all safe and home-remedic, I would still suggest that you consult a doctor first. Update 1- 23rd August- I got my taste back. I was able to taste lemon, salt and sugar- all three things. To test, I sprayed perfume in my hand and was able to smell it. I'm really happy. I have a little headache and cold and cough today, but that's because my body is rigorously putting up a fight now. Nothing to panic. Thanks to each one of you for blessings and good wishes. Update 2- 2nd September- I'm finally COVID-free. I tested negative today. I wholeheartedly thank everyone for sending across their best wishes through messages and comments, and reaching out to me. P.S.- This answer is finally closed for further updates and edits.
