column1: How do people discover their BPD?
column3: High functioning people with BPD primarily discover the BPD though the sudden idealizations and devaluations where they can begin to notice that a problem exists. Also if someone knows exact how BPD affects people it is super easy to spot. Below I am attaching a good summary of BPD behaviors. I hope it helps. Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) is a hereditary, genetic condition that significantly affects emotions, sense of self, memory and interpersonal relationships. Studies reveal extensive differences in brain structure and function. BPD is often triggered from the interplay of genetics with trauma during childhood. It is suspected that during early childhood, increased levels of cortisol caused by stress (trauma) permanently change the brain structure and function of those genetically predisposed to it (such as increased gray matter in the amygdala area, among other things), causing BPD. While there is no cure, BPD is very treatable with Dialectical Behavior Therapy that was specifically designed for people with BPD (by a person with BPD) and can give someone the tools to recognize and manage the symptoms. BPD is a disorder of Dysregulation made up by Emotion Dysregulation (the core of BPD), as well as, Interpersonal, Identity, Behavioral, and Cognitive Dysregulation. More specifically, BPD causes intense emotions that are difficult to control and manage (i.e. “Emotion Dysregulation”) including unreasonable Fear of Abandonment which is central to BPD. BPD is primarily noticed through interpersonal relationships (“Interpersonal Dysregulation”): Persons with BPD (PBPD) feel all emotions intensely, therefore, when they like someone (either in friendship or romantically) PBPDs will love that person intensely. If the other person reciprocates then they will both be enmeshed in a very intense and personal relationship. PBPDs see the world through Black and White Thinking. Themselves and others are viewed as either “good” or “bad”. There are very few gray areas, if any. For example, it is difficult for a PBPD to be angry at a loved one and recognize that - while the PBPD is angry at them - the PBPD still loves them. Conversely, if a loved one is angry at the PBPD then the PBPD will view either themselves or the loved one as “Bad”, because for them, someone who is “good” would never criticize or make them feel sad. Thinking is generally Black and White or Good vs Bad. When a PBPD loves you, they will make you the center of their lives. This phase is called “Idealization” and the loved one is viewed as “all good”. PBPDs also feel intense fear of abandonment - and in order to avoid the possibility that a genuine loved one will abandon them - they will unconsciously suddenly start to hate (“Devalue”) their loved ones in a process called Splitting (which will also completely change their memories of such a person). In addition to Fear of Abandonment, many PBPDs experience “Fear of Engulfment”. As mentioned above, close relationships for PBPDs are very emotionally intense, and because PBPDs are afraid that their loved ones will Abandon them, they are also afraid of getting very close to such loved ones in the first place. If you are in a close relationship with someone with BPD, it may feel like they are pulling you closer with one hand, while at the same time pushing you away with their other hand. BPD relationships are often a balancing act between Fear of Abandonment and Fear of Engulfment. It is due to those fears that Splitting and Devaluation occurs. Splitting occurs primarily against those people PBPDs feel like “they cannot live without”. At the suspicion of real or imagined abandonment, suddenly (overnight), the loved one will be viewed as “all bad” and all their behaviors become suspect with malevolent ulterior motives. The entire relationship is completely forgotten and replaced with an alternate reality where the former loved one was always “all bad” and the two were never enmeshed in an intense, loving and personal relationship. This phase is called “Devaluation”. PBPDs also Devalue people they feel threatened by or who make them feel insecure. It is important to note that BPD causes fragmentation of memory including, lack of object constancy, lack of whole object relations, “emotional amnesia” as well as outright False Memories (things that never quite happened, but feel as true to PBPDs as anything else). This peculiar problem with memory means that PBPDs only remember others based on their last encounter and continuously color the entire relationship based on each last encounter (i.e. they are unable to link the past with the present. Because of the lack of object constancy, they can only live in the present). Because PBPDs memories are fragmented, it becomes exceedingly difficult to trust others. PBPDs experience difficulty intergrading what they know about someone into a cohesive image. It is not uncommon for PBPDs to believe that loved ones, will betray them at any moment. For reasons that are not yet fully understood, the PBPD’s mind cannot integrate a consistent perception of others based on past experience. The past cannot be integrated with the present. For a PBPD, given the opportunity, anyone may do anything, no matter how absurd under the circumstances or how out of character it would be. As such, PBPDs are unable to exhibit normal levels of trust. PBPD memories are based on their present feelings and not the actual past (i.e. for PBPDs, their emotions and feelings dictate their reality, instead of facts.). A distorted view and understanding of reality is one of the major issues of BPD. Without treatment, PBPDs are generally unaware that their memories and perception of reality are distorted. If a PBPD Devalues you, then you will be remembered as always having been an unworthy person who they don’t particularly like (even though up until yesterday you were the center on their lives and could do no wrong). Any attempt to remind an untreated PBPD of the past will cause them confusion and cognitive dissonance. Untreated PBPDs will ultimately rationalize their behavior even against overwhelming facts. For PBPDs, how they presently feel about something, makes it the absolute and only truth. In short, when a PBPD loves someone intensely, the fear of abandonment will be so overwhelming and all-consuming that the mind, in order to protect itself from those overwhelming emotions, will suddenly “flip a switch” and cause to PBPD to suddenly feel nothing for loved one, hate them and lose all their memories of ever loving them. Sadly, unless treated, the effects of BPD on a PBPD can only be called tragic. There is a relevant and well-known quote by a certain Dr. Thomas Sydenham that accurately describes the unfortunate effects that BPD has on the sufferers: “They love without measure those they will soon hate without reason”. Once Devalued, the loved one will notice a very drastic, sudden change in the PBPD’s behavior towards them– the person who was extremely loving yesterday and the two of you were inseparable, now treats you like a persona non grata for no apparent reason while denying anything is different. The Devaluation phase completely erases the loving and close relationship. The PBPD will be unable to remember that they once had strong feelings for you. For those close to a PBPD (such as close friends, life partners, family members etc.) it may feel as the PBPD has two personas, a Dr. Jekyll and a Mr. Hyde, where neither the Dr. Jekyll nor the Mr. Hyde persona is aware that the other persona exists. When the Mr. Hyde persona (i.e. the persona with BPD) comes out, the PBPD loses all recollection that the loved one is actually a genuine love one. Again, the loved one is instead viewed as having always been an unworthy and manipulative person who the PBPD never really cared for. From a loved one’s perspective, the two distinct personalities appear as two very different people (and they might as well be), each with their own separate memories and behaviors. In fact, the two personalities view reality itself very differently. It is important for loved ones to become familiar with the behaviors of each personality and know which personality they are dealing with at all times. At the exact moment of Devaluation, PBPDs may start planning and implementing their exit strategy from the relationship (since they now hate/dislike the other person). The PBPD may unconsciously create a false and negative narrative regarding the former loved one, justifying any actions the PBPD takes. Typically, this involves a lot of rationalization as well as the elaborate manipulation and gaslighting of the former loved one that PBPDs are known for. Rationalization, manipulation, distortions and gaslighting are not done consciously or with malice, but are simply the result of whatever the PBPD feels is true at the time. As mentioned previously, PBPD perception of reality is based on present feelings (and during Devaluation, they will believe, beyond any doubt, that the former loved one is a person with little to no worth). This is as part of the famous “I hate you, don’t leave me” phase. In this phase the PBPD will be emotionally distant and very mean to the former loved one (“I hate you”), but at the same time, due to the Fear of Abandonment, they will also take steps to convince the former loved one not to disappear from their life (“don’t leave me”). Needless to say this is a very toxic phase. Alternatively, a PBPD may suddenly disappear from the former loved one’s life completely (they now want nothing to do with the devalued loved one) while the Fear of Abandonment may cause them reappear later. It’s possible for the PBPD to slowly love the devalued person again (after all, the person they liked initially is still the same person), starting the cycle of idealization and devaluation all over again. Until the PBPD receives treatment, devaluation of loved ones is inevitable and at some point, this cycle will break into permanent devaluation. To those familiar with Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD), this repeating cycle similar to the famous NPD cycle (popularly known as the “Idealization, Devaluation, Discard, Hoover” cycle), but it is rooted in completely different reasons (as explained above). The Broccoli allegory: A silly, but easy to explain way of how BPD works in relationships is this following allegory involving delicious broccoli: Imagine that you really like broccoli, and you want it to be a healthy part of your life. If you have BPD, the disorder will cause you to fear that broccoli will disappear from your life forever and you will no longer be able to have it: “I am sure the broccoli market will collapse and I will not longer be able to get it from anywhere!” The fear is overwhelming and you start to hate and devalue broccoli rather than lose it: “You know what? I never really liked broccoli and I don’t care if I will not be able to have it in the future anymore. It tastes terrible and I am sure it’s bad for me. I want nothing to do with broccoli and I am cutting out of my life.” BPD will also cause you to forget that you ever liked broccoli, and create false memories and false rationalizations of the past: “Why was I eating broccoli until now? I am sure there is a reason. Maybe I was eating broccoli because my roommate always brought some home, and I only ate broccoli because I used it with that sauce that I like. I only liked the sauce, not the broccoli! Yeah, I am sure that was the only reason. After all, broccoli sucks and I would never genuine like it. In fact, now that I think about it, I was not really eating broccoli all that often anyways, and the very few times I was, I certainly never cared for it”. Then, you may stop eating broccoli altogether: “Good thing I no longer have to deal with that disgusting broccoli”. With that said, fear of abandonment is central to BPD and it does not go away: “Maybe I should not cut broccoli completely out of my life. I think I will keep it around a bit - even though I certainly don’t like it and will treat it with the contempt it deserves”. Then, because you actually like broccoli, you may start warming up to it again: “Oh hey, this broccoli does not taste bad! It really should be part of my life!” At that point, the Cycle begins all over again until the circumstances are such that you permanently devalue broccoli forever (even though, if not for BPD, there would be no reason you would not be enjoying broccoli for the rest of your life). Again, this allegory is a bit silly, but hopefully it makes a good point. Another important aspect to remember which is common with many PBPDs is that the Black and White Thinking causes PBPDs to Project their own flaws or bad behaviors on others. This type of thinking is the reason why many PBPDs find it difficult to admit fault even against overwhelming evidence. For a PBPD, admitting fault in anything would, in the PBDP’s mind, mean that the he/she is “bad”. Therefore, the “bad” actions or behaviors are often Projected on others. BPD may also cause “Unstable of a Sense of Self”. PBPDs find it difficult to form a coherent image of themselves and their likes/dislikes. As such, when PBPDs Idealize someone, they will often change their personality to match that person’s (as there are unsure of what their own personality is). This “chameleon effect” can occur both consciously and unconsciously. There are many stories of previously idealized persons, reconnecting with their PBPD former loved ones, and being very surprised that the PBPD now has a very different personality than the one they were familiar with. There is also a distinction in behavior between Traditional and Quiet BPD. A person with “Traditional BPD” will express intense bouts of anger and rage towards the former loved one, while a person with “Quiet BPD” will simply become cold and distant. (Note: Quiet PBPDs experience the same intense anger as Traditional PBPDs, but instead of expressing those feelings outwards, they are internalized). It is important to note that PBPD s Idealize and Devalue themselves as well as others. They may confident and proud in themselves one moment, but the next moment see themselves as terrible persons who do not deserve love, friendships or success in life. BPD can cause a host of other symptoms, such as: Getting angry or upset very easily and finding it difficult to calm down (“Emotion Dysregulation”); unstable sense of self (due to the intense emotionality, PBPDs have a hard time knowing who they are or what they like and dislike) as well as strong feelings of emptiness ( “Identity Dysregulation”); impulsivity, drug use, promiscuity, binge-eating or shopping due to the intense emotions and feelings of emptiness; self-destructive behaviors such as sabotaging close relationships or even self-harm (the self destructive behaviors are called “Behavioral Dysregulation”); difficulty to admit fault and “projection” of fault to others; disassociation from reality under stress (and/or hallucinations) as well as incorrect perception of reality (“delusions”) (called “Cognitive Dysregulation”) ; and ultimately an extremely high rate of suicide (up to 70% of PBPDs will attempt suicide and 1 in 10 will commit suicide). BPD can range from Mild (people with Mild BPD are considered “high-functioning”) to Severe (people with Severe BPD have trouble functioning, i.e. holding doing a job, taking care of themselves etc.). Not all PBPDs exhibit the same symptoms and in fact, there is great variation of how BPD manifests in different people. BPD is a serious and dangerous condition and one of the four “Cluster B” Personality Disorders (Antisocial, Narcissistic, Borderline, and Histrionic) that are characterized by dramatic, overly emotional or unpredictable thinking or behavior. It is imperative that PBPDs receive professional treatment. Unfortunately, many psychologists appear to lack to skills to properly diagnose BPD and it is often misdiagnosed or even left undiagnosed. To make matters worse, because of Interpersonal Dysregulation (PBPDs will hate those they trust and depend on), PBPDs have a reputation of being notoriously difficult patients and many psychologists outright refuse to treat them, so it can be difficult to find a treating psychologist. Besides Dialectical Behavior Therapy which is absolutely necessary, it is said that yoga, meditation and breath-work can help manage the intensity of the BPD emotions. The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM–5) lists 9 easy to spot BPD behaviors. A psychologist will diagnose someone with BPD if at least 5 of those 9 behaviors are spotted. Laypersons should not use the DSM-5 in attempting to understand BPD; it is a tool for professionals used for the limited purpose of diagnosis and NOT a full description of BPD. Furthermore, there have been several recommendations in updating the DSM in regards to BPD based on our updated understanding of BPD. It is also important for the loved ones and former loved ones of PBPDs to seek help for themselves. The trauma of suddenly being treated in a horrible way by a loved one and losing them for no apparent reason often causes PTSD and/or other mental health issues. For this reason, people who have been through a relationship with a PBPD are often called BPD survivors. Once someone is aware of what BPD is, it is relative easy to spot due to the intensity of the interpersonal relationships and the sudden devaluations that follow. It is through these interpersonal relationships that high functioning PBPDs often realize that a problem exists.
column9: I suffer from “quiet” or “mild” BPD- I’m 40 yrs old and covered with self-inflicted scars but have survived multiple suicide attempts. Thank you for your very clear and accurate desciption of this tragic disorder that is HELL to live with. I am high-functioning though, and through years of therapy and trial & error, I have learned to recognize and stop/prevent/change my behavior. I have also learned to admit my faults/manipulations and am fully self-aware and cautious of how I treat others. However, due to extreme trauma I also have severe PTSD (and am bi-polar), which exacerbate and make my symptroms confusing to figure out. I have never had a healthy realtionship, esp. romantic, and at this point have given up on anything but tentatively and fearfully trying to form platonic relationships with other women (my greatest difficulty). It is sad as I am a very loving, giving, affectionate person; but I wouldn’t want to put any man through the hell of trying to figure me out and understand me, esp. incl. my issues with men from past trauma. I trust no one after what I’ve been through. And I suffer from bouts of paranoia and delusions so I always have to bounce my perceptions of reality off someone else to keep myself in check. I appreciate the information about memory issues, because I thought mine were just from dissociation due to my PTSD and depression. I have lost at least the last 10–15 years of memories-the good with the bad. This really sucks as I have 5 children regarding whom I would really like to have the good memories back. And yet I have horrible memory flashbacks that haunt me every day! But for years I have believed my ex said a couple really wrong things to me but he swears he never said them. This infuriates me because I do not have auditory hallucinations (or so I thought). But perhaps I am actually having “false memories”!!!…this new insight is making it even harder for me to trust myself now! What a confusing mess I am.!!! I would like to say that I no longer engage in manipulation or “gas-lighting”…my Narcissist ex does all that for me. I have come a long way in disengaging from this last toxic relationship, but he uses our son as a pawn so it is proving very difficult to “disengage”. But thanks once again for your insightful information- it encourages me to read more on the ‘splitting” and memory issues esp. Good job being objective and including the fact that not all of us are completely lost causes. I wish people could understand that being Borderline does not make us bad people. The easiest and most accurate description I have come across is that we suffer from an “emotional hemophilia”- meaning we feel EVERYTHING so intensely and we have no natural mechanism to keep these emotions in check- so basically we bleed to death emotionally. I cannot convey in words the depths of emotional agony and pain I have endured, largely due to extreme fear of abandonment and lost sense of self. I know I was biologically predisposed to this disorder, and early trauma and separation from my parents triggered it. Years of abuse and the subconscious “recapitulation of abuse” have only made it worse; yet I have read and know that due to my intelligence and level of self-insight I have survived, and am actually getting better and slowly, slowly healing. I could not reconcile myself with myself until one therapist pointed out to me that aren’t emotions what make us human?! Wow! So really, I am just a deeply sensitive and deeply emotional and deeply wounded person. But at least I CAN feel and am not numb or callous or hardened. Indeed, I am FULLY human!!!😊 And very much an empath.

column1: What was a choice you made that completely changed your life?
column3: I wrote about my Aunt Jackie in a previous post, My Aunt Jackie was mentally ill. she was discharging herself from the hospital. she would refuse to listen to the doctors. I was only 21 years old when I lost her. I didn’t have anyone looking after me. I was high functioning autism anyway, I met this family through a taxi service. I was working at Safeway during the time and I was leaving work early to go see Aunt Jackie while she was in the hospital around early 2022. Anyway a nice young doctor who was probably in his 30s told me, I’ll call him Wilson to protect his privacy. Well ‘’Wilson’’ told me there was nothing left he could do for Aunt Jackie, he told me that she was intubated. her body was shutting down, she was a chronic alcoholic. At the same time, I was losing my home. my home was being foreclosed upon. I met this family anyway through a taxi service, the grandmother who I’ll call Debra for her privacy as well, Was giving me rides back and forth to the hospital. they were gonna take my Aunt Jackie off the intubator as she was skinny. The machine was pumping oxygen into her. at that point your basically brain dead. Well this family that owned this taxi service was the only people who were in that hospital room with me, when I lost my Aunt Jackie. they held onto me and let me cry. I’lll never forget the day Aunt Jackie died I said ‘’IF you need to go, I understand’’. She immediately passed away. I do believe in the spirutual life and the afterlife. She died after I said those words. The nurse pulled back the curtain and said ‘’She passed’’. I immediately broke down and hugged her body holding her in my hands. nobody should be planning for a family member or anything. I was in a mess. I wasn’t taking care of myself and 2022 was the hardest year of my life. I had to start living. I didn’t want to eat, nothing. I was wanting to drown my sorrows in alcohol and I remember that being the toughest year of my life. As for the house, Well I had to file bankruptcy. No kid at 21 years old that has autism, will likely be filing bankruptcy but I had no choice. I started teaching myself how to fend for myself and the family did help me out. It felt weird like I was living a normal life. I was used to anarchy and abuse from my Aunt Jackie for years. she was mentally and emotionally abusive. She would not let me go to my own high school graduation because she was paranoid someone would kill her. Yes she was that bad. I learned to undo a lot of what she did. She would constantly start fights with the neighbors, the cops would get involved. it was a really toxic relationship, it wasn’t until she passed away that I knew how I was living wasn’t normal. I was paranoid pushing people away. The family that I met through the taxi service we would have our own disagreements, it was like I had my own brothers finally after being an only child. I lost touch with the family after I moved away. We didn’t get along, I was dealing with my own mental health issues. How I came into the world was My Aunt Jackie lost her two year old son billy in a drowning. she let the backdoor be open, he wandered out and drowned. they put him on life support. she tried killing herself, after Billy died. She wanted another chance at being a mother. She approached my biological parents and they planned me for her. They thought Jackie was a woman of God, a decent woman who would go to church and they realized it was a mistake. Jackie was a chronic alcholic. I would go to meetings with her at 11 years old. My life could be like a book considering everything I went through. I’m still alive and I’m tough years later. anyway They planned me for her and gave me to her. I’m the only child my biological parents ever planned. I know who my biological siblings and I have reconnected with my biological mom and dad. and my brother. What I will say the moment that changed my life forever was my Aunt Jackie dying. I’m incredibly grateful for Billy for giving me a chance to live. I hope him and Jackie are up there in peace. We all learn and live. Who would of thought a kid with high functioning autism would go through all that, and still tell the tale. I’m still alive and kicking. Anyway I left the house behind because I couldn’t afford the mortgage on a three bedroom home anyway I was only 21 years old. I got on a greyhound bus, packed two luggages and went halfway across the country to restart my life. I was only 22 years old on a bus with complete strangers. As I type this, I realize how far I’ve come and anything is possible. it doesn’t matter the circumstances of your life and what the cards you’ve dealt with. it’s how you deal with it and live that matters.
column9: But you came through it all and that proves that you’re a survivor, and a damn good one.

column1: What can we learn about the Nodes or Rahu/Ketu and their dasha results through mythology?
column3: Since there have been so many questions on Rahu/Ketu and their dasha effects, I thought that maybe we can try to understand these nodes better by understanding the mythological story behind their origin. The origin of Rahu-Ketu or North Node/South Node of Moon beings with the great “Samudra Manthan” or “Churning of Ocean of Milk”. Now I can’t really figure out what the “ocean of milk” refers to but it is possible that it might be referring to the primeval cosmic ocean or the dark matter field in the universe that we can’t see or feel but constitutes a great portion of the invisible universe as per Western cosmology. Interpretation: The story for Rahu-Ketu origin is set in the dark matter of the universe or a force field which we can’t grasp with our senses or mental comprehension. So, the effects of Rahu-Ketu originate in the hidden subconscious field of our mind which we can’t see or feel but that produces all habits, inclinations, pain, happiness etc. It is said that the subconscious constitutes almost 90-95% of our mental universe. It is the sub-conscious where karmic effects from the astral universe start taking shape before they come in our field of conscious mind. The events leading to Samudra Manthan * Indra – The King of Heavens while riding his divine elephant Airavata came across Sage Durvasa (known for his ascetic powers and anger) who gave him a special garland as a gift from heavenly nymph. * Indra placed the garland on Airavata’s trunk which attracted swarm of bees due to the strong smell of the divine flowers. * Out of irritation, the elephant threw the garland on the ground which enraged Sage Durvasa who considered the garland to be a symbol of fortune and something to be respected and worshipped. * He cursed Indra and the Gods (Devas) to be devoid of all strength and fortune. * As a consequence of this, the Gods lost all their battles with Asuras or Demons who slowly gained full control of the entire universe. * The Gods turned to Lord Vishnu for help who advised them to form an alliance with the demons to churn the primeval cosmic ocean for the nectar of immortality (Amrit) and promised them to deliver the nectar to make them powerful and immortal. Interpretation: * Indra means – King of senses (indriyas) and it’s the Mind that controls the senses. * The Gods Agni, Vayu, Varun, Dyaus, Prithvi represent the 5 elements Fire, Air, Water, Sky, Earth which are responsible for Sight, Smell, Taste, Sound and Touch respectively. * Indra along with the gods getting cursed for not respecting the divine garland indicates the karmic payback that we have to give because our mind and senses in a rush to fulfill our desires constantly ignores the universal laws and the divine inner calling. * The gods getting defeated to Asura reminds us of our suffering and pain that surrounds us like demons and elicits all negative reactions out of us like frustrations, anger, despair etc. and can even compel us to take refuge in alcohol, intoxication or other negative karma (all Asura or demonic activities). * Indra and the gods turning to Vishnu for help relates to our turning to the almighty in times of suffering. The nectar of immortality refers to the realization of our own immortal soul after going through inner churning The ‘Samudra Manthan’ process * Both the gods (Deva) and demons (Asura) formed a pact to churn the cosmic ocean using Mount Mandara as the churning rod and Vasuki (serpent king) as the rope. * To avoid being in the firing line of the poisonous flames that will emit from Vasuki’s mouth while churning, Indra played a trick on the demons asking them to hold the lower part of the snake in the process. * He knew that the demons will find it offensive to hold the impure lower part of a reptile and insist on holding the upper part of Vasuki. * This is what happened and the demons had to face the poisonous flames of Vasuki while pulling it. * While churning, the mountain used to sink down and so Lord Vishnu agreed to take the form of a giant tortoise to support Mount Mandara and give it stability Interpretation * The churning of the cosmic ocean reminds us of our own inner churning during suffering or an intense struggle period that every soul goes through on this earthly realm. * The Deva and Asura represent the good and bad, the hope and despair, the faith and mistrust, surrender and false pride, good karma with sincerity and the shortcut path of lawlessness. We are constantly being pulled between the two as if churned from inside. * Vasuki – the serpent god represents our reptilian brain which fights for survival and controls our primal self-preserving behaviour. * The poisonous flames coming out of Vasuki’s mouth represents our distress and frustrations coming out during the inner churning process and struggle. * The demons insisting on holding the head side of Vasuki the reptile indicates the difficulties and negativity catching hold of our reptilian brain and forcing us to confront our survival issues head-on. * Mount Mandara represents our inner determination and rock like rigidity of purpose that keeps us going during the inner churning but at times, this can also sink during immense struggle or pressure of circumstances. * We then have to turn towards our innermost divine core in utmost silence and stillness which gives us strength like Lord Vishnu in the form of a tortoise which stood still under Mount Mandara After-effects of Samudra Manthan or Churning of Cosmic Ocean * The churning of the cosmic ocean initially produced a massive amount of poison called “halahal” that had the potential to destroy the entire universe. * Lord Shiva on the request of the gods drank the poison which turned his throat blue and came to be known as “Neelkantha” * The churning also produced various divine gems (ratna), goddess of fortune “Lakshmi” , wish fulfilling cow called Kamdhenu, wish fulfilling tree called Kalpavriksh, many divine animals etc. * Finally, the churning produced the immortality nectar called “Amrita” Interpretation * Our inner churning during times of confusion and struggle always brings forth the poison of uncertainty, frustration, low self-esteem, self-doubts etc. * The “blue” colour in the poison refers to Saturn and its hard taskmaster role in putting us under pressure. * The blue throat of Lord Shiva refers to the Vishuddi Chakra which gives us inner strength and purity * Our struggles also produces the good results of our persistent efforts in the material domain in the form of success, fortune and desire fulfillment * In the spiritual domain, our efforts in purifying our inner self finally leads to enlightenment and realizing the inner immortal soul Rahu / Swarnabhanu * Ra/Ke’s original mythological name was Swarbhanu. He was the son of Viprachitti – a powerful demon king and Simhika – daughter of Sage Kasyapa and Danu (mother of all demons, also called Diti) * The name ‘Swarbhanu’ translates into ‘Radiant Splendor’ * During the distribution of nectar of immortality (amrita), a fight broke out between the gods and demons. The gods approached Lord Vishnu and urged him to take care of the distribution so as to avoid the nectar falling into the hands of the Asuras or demons * Lord Vishnu took the form of a beautiful enchantress Mohini who distracted the lusty Asuras and started distributing amrita to the Deva * Swarbhanu observed everything without any distractions and realized Mohini’s illusion. He disguised himself as a god and got himself a drop of the amrita * His fraud was caught by Sun and Moon gods who informed Mohini. * Lord Vishnu immediately severed his head with his Sudarshan Chakra but Swarbhanu became immortal as Rahu – The Head and Ketu – The Body * Rahu promised to take revenge from Sun and Moon by periodically eclipsing their glow and radiance Interpretations Nature and disposition of Rahu Swarbhanu was the son of demon king Viprachitti and Simhika (who carried both Deva and Asura qualities as the daughter of Sage Kasyapa and Diti). His name translates into “Radiant Splendor”. * The fact that Rahu’s mother has both Deva and Asura lineage indicates that Rahu is not only a tamasic materialistic energy as portrayed by astrologers but also carries some sattvic godly energy as well. * The proportion of demonic qualities is obviously higher but because of his maternal grandfather being the exalted Sage Kasyapa, Rahu carries tremendous intelligence, ability to understand mysteries and higher knowledge and ability to move into a realm of higher consciousness. * This is obviously very difficult in today’s materialistic Kaliyuga but if Rahu gets associated with a well-placed 9th lord, well placed Jupiter or in Jupiter’s nakshatra, then Rahu can help a person in his or her spiritual journey also contrary to belief Asura * As per ancient texts Asuras are great builders, are full of lust, greed and aversions, are power hungry, are argumentative and arrogant, have the know how to create illusions etc. * Many scholars describe Asuras to be "lords" with different specialized knowledge, magical powers and special abilities, which they choose to deploy either for good, constructive reasons or for evil, destructive reasons. The former become known as Asura in the sense of Devas/Gods, the later as Asura in the sense of Asuras/Demons * Rahu as the “head” of Swarnabhanu, carries all the Asura qualities mentioned above. Rahu can bring forward immense arrogance, aggression, pride, ego, lust and uncontrolled hidden desires to the forefront * But under right benefic influences, Rahu gives the power to imagine and build things, gives great mathematical ability and ability to understand the workings of the universe. All the great inventions of modern world like supercomputers, tunnel boring machines, fighter jets, mega engines, semi-conductor chips etc. are the gift of Rahu * Swarbhanu’s radiance implies that Rahu carries a certain glamour factor in it. However, this radiance is artificial compared to the natural luminosity of the Sun. This is why Rahu rules all sorts of artificial lighting like neon lights etc. which provide radiance in the night. * Rahu also rules the artificial glamour and radiance of celebrities which are just normal human beings in real life but seem to exude charisma on screen because of photographic effects and artificial lighting Rahu’s struggle Swarbhanu also participated in the arduous Samudra Manthan or churning of the cosmic ocean and would have definitely inhaled the poisonous flames being emitted by Vasuki – The Serpent * Normally astrologers while writing about Rahu talk only about the short-cuts that Rahu loves to take on the path to success as evident by the fact that he disguised himself as a God to get the Nectar. Fair enough! But the question that come up are – * * Didn’t he and other Asuras deserve the nectar on the basis of the struggle they went through along with the Devas? * Didn’t Swarbhanu deserve a reward for not falling under the illusion and lust of Mohini? * Wasn’t it Lord Krishna’s divine plan only to involve the Asuras in Samudra Manthan? Was it his plan all the way to give birth to Rahu and Ketu? * Rightly, Swarbhanu did get his reward in the form of an immortal god and ability to give the rewards of a person’s karma but he also paid the price of his short-cut and treachery by getting his head severed and is in perennial search for his torso (Ketu) to achieve completion Lessons from Rahu’s initial struggle * Contrary to belief, Rahu is well known for making a person toil and struggle hard especially in its dasha * There could be beneficial short-cuts only if the person has put in the required effort * Any sudden benefit that one can see in Rahu dasha like lottery, winning a contest etc. can be attributed to efforts of many past lives by that soul which we are unaware of * Any short-cut without efforts will ultimately bring a massive downfall for the person in the long run * Be prepared to pay a heavy price for all the materialistic desires that Rahu can fulfill in its dasha period. * For every career success or new position, it can create heavy stress and lack of mental peace, for every beautiful woman or powerful man you become crazy for, there might be lot of strings attached, for every luxury possession one struggles for, it can bring in a constant fear of theft or loss * There is a certain “boundary crashing” quality of Rahu which it imparts to the native in its dasha * * 1st house – Can go for weird looking hairstyles, clothes or self-declaration of greatness * 2nd house – Values will be influenced by foreign cultures, family might be unorthodox or non-traditional * 3rd house – Can acquire skills that are normally not common, communication style will be out of the ordinary * 4th house – Vehicles owned might be uncommon among community members, house will have exotic and non-traditional items * 5th house – Literary skills will be unorthodox, can write something which can be usually unacceptable, children will be unorthodox, might bring his or her own unique brand of creativity. Example:- JK Rowling created the unorthodox Harry Potter fantasy series * 6th house – Non-traditional approach to competition, can woo over enemies with guile and charm, preference for unorthodox health treatments * 7th house – Non-traditional approach to partnership, marriage or business * 8th house – Unorthodox sexual or occult experiences, risk taking approach to life or other people’s resources * 9th house – Non-traditional approach to religion and higher knowledge, foreign influence in belief systems and gurus * 10th house – Unorthodox career or approach to leadership positions * 11th house – Network circle or friend groups might consist of “weird” people or people who are outcasts * 12th house – Non-traditional approach to secrets, behind the scenes work or relaxation periods * Rahu dasha can be well known for “cutting off” one’s head after reaching the pinnacle. This can mean loss of position or loss of ego. Famous example: Bollywood superstar Rajesh Khanna Rahu’s burning ambition and desire * As per ancient texts, Asura can reach the level of gods or Devas through years of intense penance and meditation through which they are able to move beyond their negativity into light * However, Swarnabhanu was more interested in becoming a God through whatever means possible and not wait for time. Hence, he remained totally alert and aware through Mohini’s deceptions, changed his form and personality and got what he wanted but at a cost Lessons * Rahu gives a burning desire related to the house it sits in. It can be one aspect of the house or all aspects. * The person can even think of multiple ways to quickly fulfill that desire irrespective of the feasibility and sustainability * For houses: * * 1st – Burning desire to be respected and recognized as an important personality * 2nd – Desire for wealth, knowledge and display values or opinions * 3rd – Desire for communication and selling one’s abilities or story * 4th – Desire for patriotism, vehicles and emotional fulfillment through family * 5th – Desire for creative output, kids, romance and individuality * 6th – Desire for winning conflicts and competitions * 7th – Desire for the ‘other’ – relationships or partnerships * 8th – Desire for sex, other’s possessions and legacies * 9th – Desire for religion, preaching and teaching, travelling * 10th – Desire for leadership, power and control * 11th – Desire for rewards, awards and network circles * 12th – Desire for retreats, aloneness, private activities and secrets * The goal achieved through such a short-cut can give riches or fame but can be short-lived. Struggle is important to endure if Rahu brings it because the gains will be sustainable in the long run * It is very important to generate that awareness and alertness in Rahu’s dasha so that one is able to navigate through the temptations and material illusions * Rahu’s ability to change form into a God implies that one gains the ability to move from one level or form to another in its dasha. This level or form can be knowledge, beauty, status, wealth, identity, skills, intelligence, personality etc. * Rahu can also bring in tricksters and fraudsters disguised as friendly figures. Alertness is the key as displayed by Sun and Moon gods in catching hold of Swarnabhanu’s fraud * Since Swarnabhanu’s deceit was caught by Sun and Moon – implies that one’s inner voice and alertness of the mind can help in dealing with the uncertainties of Rahu dasha Rahu – The Head VS Ketu – The Torso * Rahu being only the head implies that it can control and affect intelligence, senses, emotions, power to think, ability to react or act as per external stimuli * Without the body, Rahu can absorb as much external information as possible without feeling saturated and also find it difficult to digest things that go inside. This means that Rahu in its dasha can grant the ability to gain as much knowledge, money, fame, power, possessions as possible without ever feeling contented. This can also lead to confusions, greediness and situations where the person might be taken for a ride by others and losing control * It is essential that the dispositor is in a good shape and Rahu preferably receives Jupiter’s aspect to be able to better synthesize the incoming information * Rahu being the head has the ability to manipulate information, intellect and emotions. It represents “the preacher” who can brainwash others into following a particular ideology and make terrorists out of them. It also represents the scientist or researcher who can decipher meanings out of phenomena * Ketu being only the torso implies that it can’t feel anything, any emotions, any external stimuli or information coming in * Without the head consisting of the senses, Ketu is just like nothingness and open to everything coming in without the ability to react. Hence Ketu is associated with meditation where the senses are turned inwards and the body is sitting still with nothing to process and just watching the thoughts and emotions pass by without reacting * Since Ketu has no head, it cannot imagine any future but only carries the impressions of the past. Hence it can act under bodily compulsions and if misguided by Rahu led people, can cause immense suffering The Push-Pull churning of Rahu-Ketu axis in the horoscope The “Samudra Manthan” or “Churning of Cosmic Ocean” can be compared to the Rahu-Ketu axis in our horoscopes. This is just a thought process and any comments are welcome * Rahu is constantly pushing us towards the future that represents our pending karma whereas Ketu is pulling us towards the past inclinations and behaviors * This Ra-Ke axis needs the balance of a Mount Mandara to be able to properly balance our past and future. This balance is provided by the houses lying exactly in the middle of the axis. We will have to focus on these 2 houses so that our Ra-Ke axis operates properly * The houses that can struggle because of the Ra-Ke axis are in the 6th, 8th and 12th from either Rahu or Ketu. This can be the poison generated from the churning * The houses that can benefit from the churning are in the 5th and 9th position from either Rahu or Ketu Let’s see the above points for each Ra-Ke axis: 1/7 axis * Rahu in 1st pushes the person towards self focus, self identity, personality focus, narcissism, fame, individuality whereas Ketu in 7th pulls the person towards life partner, compromise, balance and other people. The opposite is true for Rahu in 7th and Ketu in 1st * The balance for this axis is provided by the 4–10 houses. Rahu in 1st needs the support of the public and career in 10th to develop its identity and personality. Ketu in 7th needs the person to focus on 4th house of emotions to better connect with life partner and others. Same is true for opposite polarities * The houses that can suffer in some dimensions are 2,6,8 and 12 because they fall in 6th, 8th or 12th from either Ra-Ke polarity. Ketu or Rahu in 7th when neglected can spoil the family relations in 2nd and drain the wealth. This can also create legal tussles, divorce etc in 6th house. Rahu in 1st when misused can destroy peace and meditation of 12th house. Ego can be very high thus affecting 12th house of higher surrender to god. Ketu in 1st when misused can affect the body or health in 8th house. 8th house is also in-laws and spousal money which can get affected because of Rahu/Ketu misuse in 7th house of spouse * The houses that can benefit are 3,5,9,11. Rahu in 1st when operating properly can improve the personal selling skills and communication power of 3rd and give you gains of 11th house. It can boost your individual creative power of 5th. 3rd is also 9th or fortune of spouse in 7th. Ra-Ke when operating properly in 7th can get you gains from spouse in 5th and 11th (5th from 7th) houses. Ketu in 1st can make you spiritual and religious in 9th house 2/8 axis * Rahu in 2nd pushes an individual towards birth family, own values, opinions and decisions, knowledge and developing skills to earn self made money, valuing money and possessions. Ketu in 8th pulls a person towards spirituality, crisis situations, valuing other person’s opinions, money and resources, in-laws etc. The opposite is true for Rahu in 8th house * The balance for this axis is provided by the 5–11 houses. column1: I'm 21, my parents have fights on alternate days and compare me with other kids and themselves at my age. They don't think it affects me but I’ve suffered from serious anxiety & depression recently. What do I do?
column3: I'm a 26 year old and I face similar problem at my home. Only difference is I'm a girl. Growing up seeing them fight every moment of their life has made me lose interest in my own life. On top of that they see and treat me like I'm an unwanted member in the family. I was at home till high school but left to another city for Uni. Then I got job and moved to different cities. That was when I understood I had depression. The childhood trauma affected my early adulthood very badly. I was overly sensitive. I was insecure about life. I trusted people blindly. I cried, cried and cried alot for everything. I suffered a lot emotionally. It took so much time for me to balance life with depression. When I realised that my life is not hopeless just because my parents didn't see any hope in theirs I went to a therapist. He helped me with some medications which kept me sane. But after a point it became like a habit and without med I couldn't be happy. So I slowly stopped taking anti depressants and focused on my hobbies and tried to keep myself busy. I started to feel alive and started to see the world from a whole new perspective. Life seemed very beautiful for the first time and one-day suddenly due to some unavoidable reasons I had to come back home. It's been almost a year and now everything is back to square one. How much ever I try to live life in a positive way, my parents make me feel worthless over and over again. Being at home is happiness to many. But to me not even a day goes without crying. I'm a healer so I'm trying to heal myself everyday in order to protect my mental health. I try guided meditation. Exercising, watching a favourite show, reading a book, painting or even listening to my favourite song helps me alot. All that I'm focused in life right now is to get a full time job and move to another city or country to keep myself safe from the negativities of my family. So for you too, I'd suggest you to live away from your home temporarily. Maintain a safe distance between you and your parents as it's good for both of your mental health. When you get out of home focus on your passion and hobbies. Focus on yourself first and with time you'll be out of your depression. Surrounding yourself with positive people and those who motivate and encourage you helps. And try seeing a therapist who can guide you through your journey to a depression free life. I'd suggest you not to take too many medicines as it'll become addictive. Living with depression is not an easy thing. I'm still fighting it. But I'm confident and hopeful to overcome this soon. Likewise I want you to be confident first. Engage yourself with a hobby, do things that makes you happy. Try to distance yourself from situation that makes you feel demotivated. Try guided meditation. Even if you can do it for 5 mins it's completely alright. As you practice, you'll be able to focus for a longer duration. Meditation helps you to free your mind. It's undoubtedly a great way to relieve yourself completely from depression and anxiety. And hey, prayer also helps me alot. If you believe in the superior power above you, try to spend some time for prayers. It gives you strength and confidence. After all, life is very beautiful. I wish you a great life ahead. Stay blessed and be wel! Thanks to all those who read♥️ And special thanks to those who have upvoted my answer ♥️♥️

column1: Are schizophrenics aware of the impact their disorder has on their family?
column3: Oftentimes in my experience. My uncle-in-law had paranoid schizophrenia. He was a good hearted man, but off his meds he was extremely paranoid and out of control. When he was first confronted by family members about his possible mental illness, he realized he had problems and he agreed without hesitation to a medication regimen. He was very good about taking his medication so that he was able to function in society. He knew that it affected others, particularly his mother who cared for him. He was devastated when she died, but he learned to become more self-sufficient. His family continued to emotionally support him until his death, although he would have some outbursts occasionally. He would always apologize and knew he was in the wrong for calling other people names or yelling at them. Fortunately these incidents did not happen often. But my uncle-in-law was acutely aware of his paranoid schizophrenia and that it did affect his family. He began taking medication as soon as the family and he were aware that he had a serious mental illness. As a professional in the mental health field, I personally found that people with schizophrenia were very often aware of their condition and usually complied with their medication so that they were able to function. Many times they were able to talk to me about their hallucinations and how it affected them. However medication often has to be adjusted as people become used to their medication so it loses their effect. Those with schizophrenia usually cannot function in society without medication so they tend to be pretty good about taking their meds. Otherwise they end up in the hospital where they are again prescribed medication. Keep in mind that although they have visual and auditory hallucinations, they are usually not violent towards others. On the other hand, I found that people who were diagnosed with bipolar were the opposite. Often times they refused to admit their mental illness and often refused to take medication as they like the manic phase of bipolar which has been likened to a methamphetamine high. They tend to be more self-obsessed and don’t realize how badly this affects their family.

column1: What is the coldest, hard truth you've learned in life?
column3: Life is filled with cold hard truths. It only depends on what subject. As above so below, they say. And as cold as the truth may be- there are warm truths too. So don’t forget about those when reading this.Everyone around you is going to die. Keep this in mind with older relatives, family members, and older friends. People who are prone to high blood pressure, those who can’t stop drinking alcohol, & those who are simply of old age. Treat everyone as if it were the last time you are seeing them.Dating in your 20s is painful. You might as well wait until you approach your 30s and remain single in your 20s. The amount of time wasted in relationships could be that degree/certificate on the counter. It’s not pointless, so as much as you learn the lesson. Invest in yourself.Success is consistency. You cannot have one without the other. If you build habits easily, form routines, carry out important tasks in the beginning of the day, you’re doing good. But you must KEEP UP & not lose sight. Consistency is right there with persistance. You need to commit all of your energy on what you want.Make-up, tanning, nicotine, steroids, all of these things harm your body and speed up your age process. Be natural, it’s in. Work on skin care & other beneficial ways to live the best life.Reading makes you smarter, social media makes you crazy.When things don’t work out- complaining and dwelling makes it 10 times worse. The brain will keep releasing adrenaline and then you will bring it up again hours later, that same feeling will return, like a gun shot wound. Your brain makes these associations, so Put it to bed and move on.If you don’t have a pet, you’re more prone to a heart attack. Cats are easy & inexpensive. Go save one.Getting too attached to people will hurt you, obviously. Buddhists and Monks have a zen mindset and don’t hold expectations or attachments when it comes to other people. Desire isn’t a word in their vocabulary. Let the energy be what it is. Learn to meditate and not be so dependent.Stop trying to people-please! No one really gives a hoot. Sure we all have our family, best friends, and significant others- but other than that no one gives a crap. If a co-worker is talking about you in the corner, it’s only because they have no imagination, and are only capable of making amusements out of the people around. Small minds discuss people. In real life, they don’t truly care about you. Don’t bother trying to befriend these folks.Time spent scrolling on Facebook is unproductive and acts as a drug. We search for external validation so much, whether through Instagram or FB likes- we forget that internal wisdom is our priority. Under settings on Facebook, it’ll tell you how many hours a week your on Facebook. Take it with a grain of salt. If you are scrolling mindlessly, go for a walk. Leave the phone at home. Journal. Call a friend. Do anything else but scroll. Plus, the light is bad for the brain.Psychologically, we all have issues. There is no perfect person. Celebrities even have mental health issues. It’s becoming noticed more & more. People tend to feel shameful towards their inner demons, they project isolation and dwell in anxiety, stop doing that! Everyone has their issues, whether it’s mental ocd, hyperactivity, trauma, ADHD, depression. Don’t let shame run your life. Everyone is painting a picture of their ego.Learn to be happy BY yourself, one day you will be alone. I know this sounds grim, but it’s better to achieve self- wholeness as a young person. Many elderly people turn bitter and depressed, whether they are widowed or separated, they are alone and unhappy with themselves. They didn’t spend much time with their selves in life, because they were always in company with another. Master yourself.Your thoughts control your life, more than anything. If you wake up and you’re dreading the day, congrats, your day is going to suck. Associate thoughts with positivity and learn to live in the moment. Learn to be spontaneous. The more complaining, the worse the outcome. People underestimate the power of their own self-talk and voice. If you keep calling yourself an idiot and being negative, you will automatically operate on a lower frequency.Birds of a Feather flock Together. Separate yourself from the herd of haters & move on. Misery loves company, toxicity loves poison. Get away.Many people aren’t honest to your face. Exactly how it sounds. not sure if someone’s listening to you? Say something completely random and ask their opinion right after. And oh, if they are on their phone, this exercise doesn’t count. Keep in mind though, some people have bad days, & it is hard sometimes.Everyone is prone to cancer & You are what you eat. If you’re consuming donuts and milk for breakfast, meat and coffee for brunch- yeah your body isn’t going to be happy with you. You’ll be able to tell by just going to the bathroom. Your skin will tell you. Metabolism only goes so far, and then age kicks in. Try to consume as much water as possible.Life will teach you the same lesson over and over until you get the message. If you keep dating crappy guys, you’ll keep getting the same results. Try dating yourself. Be your own best friend & lover. This could apply to bad luck, friends, car problems, complaining, etc. it’s in the air and it manifests.There are millions of homeless people dying. So next time Jenna from D&D makes your coffee wrong, stop being so selfish. Forgiveness is important.The most crooked people are Millionaires. They know someone, who knows someone.. Some are movie stars, some politicians. Sociopaths excell in business & feeding off the people under them, and the empathetic.Everyone has debt. Money doesn’t buy happiness: it just is a TOOL. The real wealth comes from inside.Even with the internet, people still make descisions based on popularity. People are concerned with what’s “in” and what’s “cool”. Even with technology in our very hands, your fellow pupil won’t dedicate time to research. Keep that in mind next time you’re having an in depth conversation with someone.It takes nearly 3 weeks to form a habit. This is a hard truth because commitment is hard.
