column1: In what ways will your life never be the same after the end of covid-19 sheltering-in-place/quarantine?
column3: For me I took my wife to the Emergency room on January 15th, 2020 and was sent home because they were going to Transfer her to another hospital. The next day I was told she was missing. I filed a missing persons report and on February 8th, the sheriff came to my home and told my son & I she was dead. After 3 weeks of grief, before a childhood friend suggested I shold move out West and they'd help me establish my life over again. To go there and stay with his wife & him, would allow me to save money to find a new home for my son & I. Still numb with pain of memories, not eating or sleeping much in past 2 months, I began a journey of driving more than 2,800 miles. Across 9 States facing many unforeseen problems, including weather. The 3 days of estimated travel turned into 10 days. In all this time I was never aware of the virus even going on in the world until the 7th day of traveling. Then I began to experience the impact of my of surroundings that the virus now played a part of slowing my progress as I drove each day. Upon my arrival, the plans I had made prior to leaving began to disintegrate with lockdown measures in place, that I had no control over. Everything changed into a nightmare of turmoil and more despair. I was told I'd now have to isolate with my son in a tent on my friend's property with temperatures close to freezing. Hotel/motels now closed, churches, State parks and many agencies had closed too. This left us no where to turn to for help. Then suddenly after being here less than 30 days, my friend tells me, “I'm sorry but you need to leave and find another place to go, as I can no longer help you anymore. " With nowhere to go, no family members to help, we have been cut off and face new challenge of being homeless. To me it is like losing everything for a second time all over, only I have still have a child who depends on me. I have absolutely nowhere to turn to now. How does this change affect me? It's like, does the virus take us or circumstances destroy us? I don't think we will ever be the same again and humanity has went out the window, is how I really feel this crisis has now become to me. To me personally I feel like a slow death is overcoming me. It leaves me with no feelings left inside except the shock of helplessness .UPDATE November 2020: Apparently I wrote this at a time of despair and had no idea what was in Store for me next! My son & I slept in a ride/share commuter parking lot one night in our truck. A woman knocked on our window and wanted to know if we were okay. She took my phone number and promised to call the next day. When she called, she gave me directions to meet another woman at a church, who in turn loaded the back of my truck with food. Then gave me 2 $50 gas cards.A few hours later another woman calls and gives me directions to a motel in another city to get out of the cold for a night and take a shower. When we arrived, we found it had a microwave and mini-fridge and a Meal Coupon for 2 Hot dinners! (And we found a receipt that the motel was paid for an entire week, not just a night!). The next day a Stimulus check posted to my bank account and I woke up and told my son I had a strange dream we were living on a boat. So I went on Facebook Marketplace and started looking for a boat, which I thought we could live on dock, have electricity, showers, toilet and still access my truck on land to get around. And so I got into a week long discussion on getting this boat for sale for $1,000. I was told that because this boat was completely stripped bare, I'd need to buy an outboard motor, a dinghy to get to and from the boat and a generator before we could even come aboard. So I ran around buying each of these things, boat still unseen until the day we checked out of the motel and went to a place I'd never been to take possession of my first ever sailboat to live on. The owner went with me to Transfer the title of the boat and at the counter he sold it to me for $100!!! He also decided to stay with us for 2 weeks teaching us about boating.On the third day of hanging out together, we were driving to go get supplies we needed to be more comfortable in living on a boat, like a porta-potty and a gas camp stove. While I was driving my cell phone went off and it displayed my Wife's Phone Number! With shaking hands I answered the phone and heard my wife's voice in tears. She asked why did I leave her? She seemed very confused and said she thought I never wanted to speak to her and left her alone. (Long story short is I got her on a train from Ohio to Seattle, it turned out to be the very last train before Amtrak shut down due to COVID-19). So when she arrived and I took her across Puget Sound on the ferry, she told me how she had stopped taking her medications for Bipolar for almost a month before I had taken her to the ER. She was taken by a social worker to another city and to a different Hospital to be checked out, during this time she was sick with the flu and later determined to be COVID-19. She remembered coming out and being placed in a shelter and was in a Fog. When she started to remember things like family and home. So we began on an adventure living in a sailboat and sheltering in place. We sailed to new places and learned many things during the lock down, all Marinas were closed, nobody answered phones at any agencies I called for help. So we celebrated Mother's Day, Memorial, Father's Day, July 4th, birthdays and Labor Day sailing all over as a family of 3 with our dog. I have truly been blessed in more ways than my shortened version I just gave account of, so I will have to find time to really share more parts to this story than time allows for now. I thank God for his hand in this.
column9: That is a very sad story but in all this you never mentioned contact with a social worker. It sounds like you need one to get things sorted out. A childhood friend is not enough. There are work and financial issues. You have a right to ask for professional help and should not hesitate to ask.

column1: What did I do to deserve this suffering? I grew up w/ 4 narcissistic family members. As a result my romantic & some friends had NPD. I am certain as I use the DSM in my job. It does not get better. You end up alone while they are w/ the next supply.
column3: The only option is to make meaning of your pain. Or let it swallow you.I’ve asked myself this question often. I cry it as an unending refrain. I look at photos of myself as a child and ask: How could they all hate her?I think of how deeply and unconditionally I’ve loved my whole family, and I feel truly bereft that there’s none of that for me. In all my life, only narcissists have ever been physically or romantically attracted to me, which makes me feel as if something is fundamentally wrong with me, if I’m unlovable. I had two Npd/ASPD parents, an NPD sister, An NPD aunt who had two goldens and an invisible, so my cousins also had NPD, with one with HPD. On my mother’s side, the family is full of felons. In my worst moments, I question if there’s anyone on this earth with love in their heart at all or if I’m an alien. I’ve done extensive healing work and education. But I’m seven years celibate. The last time I had sex was when my NPD/ASPD maintenance man drugged me and raped me for three weeks 8 months ago: that happened despite me knowing all about NPD and trauma bonding and how to spot and avoid it. I’m targeted at my jobs; I’ve had to sue for things narcissists did to me. I truly feel my very existence makes people enraged, no matter how kind I am to them. IT’S TRUE: IT DOESN’T GET BETTER. It really doesn’t. I have never in my life experienced the feeling of loving someone romantically and being genuinely loved back. I do not think I ever will.So, what now? As a BPD, I don’t think I can ever rule out that suicide could be my fate. It is something I battle often. The classic theory of the five stages of grief areDENIALANGERBARGAININGDEPRESSIONACCEPTANCEIf you were born to a cluster b family, you entered these stages in early childhood……when you lost the love of your parents. The BPD child, the scapegoat, enters this AT BIRTH, when they are born to a predator, and the immediate energy they receive is not one of warmth, but that of hate. But a child needs love to survive… They need this predator to get their basic needs met… So, the infant brain enters into DENIAL.As they grow cognitively in this state of denial, they must then internalize the abuse. They must believe they deserve it, and love can be earned. Over time, the goalposts keep moving, nothing is ever enough, and we begin to enter the other stages in early childhood: anger, bargaining, and depression. WE CYCLE THROUGH THESE REPEATEDLY, never getting to acceptance, because it’s so hard to face the truth: that our caretakers never loved us and never will. In fact, they hate us and want us dead.Instead of reaching acceptance, we find surrogates. People who feel familiar, who lovebomb us, who mirror us, whose love we believe we can earn, and we repeat the trauma of our childhood until it nearly kills us…or succeeds.I was watching I Am a Killer last night, and one of the cases was an ASPD man who shot his wife, shot himself in the head, and survived. One stunning detail: the wife’s father killed her mother when she was a child, and then he killed himself. She watched it happen. She died the exact same way. It’s because we cycle through the stages of grief, over and over and over, never reaching acceptance…..This is also why cluster b’s have problems with substance abuse: the most bearable stage for us is DENIAL.The last person I unmasked in my family was my sister, and it was so incredibly painful to break that trauma bond that I swear I could feel cancer taking root in my body. THIS LOSS, I thought, I WILL NOT SURVIVE. But unmasking her took me to the final stage: acceptance. I’m an orphan. I always was. I’ve raised myself and I survived by myself. A child amongst wolves.But what now? This acceptance is not peaceful.BPDs often have visions, predictive dreams, and lucid dreaming, and that’s been true in my life and something precious about my disorder that I wouldn’t change. I had a vision in meditation shortly before I unmasked my sister. I was walking through a fog, and I could see that it was lifting. I was eager to see what was behind it. I expected a field of wildflowers, the sun, a glittering stream.It was a barren, grey, apocalyptic city landscape. All the buildings were rubble, and I was alone. It was THE TRUTH. It was what happened to my bloodline. It was the grief I’ve carried, buried, tried to deny. So, this is what acceptance looked like? When I finally unmasked my sister, it was as if I lost a limb… As if I’d fought a bloody war with my most trusted friend and soldier by my side in a ditch, and one day I woke up and her brains were in my lap. Suicide never felt more alluring. I could lose every mediocre narcissist man, I could lose my narcissist favorite people, I could lose my parents, but my sister…. …I BLED WITH HER. I mean that literally. WE WERE ABUSED, AND WE BLED TOGETHER. WE ESCAPED TOGETHER. Except, what I didn’t understand: she didn’t escape.Because the NPD child doesn’t cycle through the stages in the same way. THE NPD CHILD IS STUCK IN A LOOP OF ONLY TWO STAGES: DENIAL/ANGER/DENIAL/ANGER/DENIAL/ANGER They enter these stages in toddler years, when the NPD parent splits them to black and begins abusing them. This is when they have their first mental collapses. IN THE NARCISSIST COLLAPSE, THEY MEET THE OTHER TWO STAGES, BARGAINING AND DEPRESSION.In bargaining, a person bargains to God. In a cluster b family, God is the NPD parent. The golden child begs and pleads to their God: please don’t abandon me! I’m innocent! I’m a good child! I’m your child! AND GOD CASTS THEM OFF. They face depression. And THEY DIE THERE.Spiritually, they die. TO BE CAST OFF FROM GOD IS TO HAVE YOUR WHOLE IDENTITY ERASED. To go into the pit of hell. And turn demon.When the suffering of the collapse ends, when the NPD parent returns to the golden child with a breadcrumb, they go back to DENIAL.They go back to being the golden child: perfect, innocent, in a world that will be full of toys and happiness. BUT THEY ARE ALREADY A GHOST AT THAT POINT. They just don’t know it. They can’t face that truth. It’s unbearable. DENIAL/ANGER/DENIAL/ANGERRecently, psychological theorists have proposed that there is a 6th STAGE OF GRIEF:MEANINGVictor Frankl is a psychologist who endured horrific brutalities in a Nazi concentration camp. After surviving, he went on to write the bestselling book Man’s Search for Meaning. Frankl asserts that if life has any meaning, then suffering must have meaning. If we all must die to complete our life, that means, we all must suffer. So, the test of life is how we respond to our suffering. Frankl said we can discover meaning in three ways:By creating works or doing deedsBy experiencing other peopleBy the attitude we take towards sufferingFrankl’s meaning, he felt, was his book: turning his pain into art and into philosophy. THE BOOK SOLD OVER TEN MILLION COPIES. He reached almost as many people that died in the Holocaust. That’s just one man’s suffering…but look at the POWER of its LIGHT.I’ve suffered a lot in my life, but I’ve not had to experience the Holocaust. There are people, many millions of them, who were born and died in slavery, in the most brutal conditions. And those people were victims of sociopaths too: the horrors of the world happen at the hands of people with this disorder. We have much art and many lessons from the Holocaust and slavery, but we still haven’t stopped electing sociopaths, or allowing greed, war, colonialism, and genocide to ravage innocent people. We leave us all at the whim of broken people cycling through only two stages of grief. They can’t reach acceptance, because they CANNOT ACCEPT THE SHAME OF THEIR TRUTH. They can’t accept they are a haunting: returning over and over to reenact the same wound that took them out. NPD and ASPD grow every generation, and the reality of our world shows its cancer that threatens our whole species. Most people see no urgency in this problem. So, really, what’s the point??? WHAT MEANING COULD THERE POSSIBLY BE?THE MEANING IS ENTIRELY UP TO YOU. It is the one place in this rotten life in which you are free. YOU HAVE CONTROL. And you can choose for it to mean nothing, or you can make it mean something.I believe I’ve made meaning from my traumas. And I hope to make more. After I was raped by my apartment maintenance man, I saw myself in a dream as a mermaid swimming by a shipwreck. I heard a voice: “There’s so much to discover in a wreckage, treasures worth more than gold, ghosts with secrets to tell you.”This is how I imagine myself now, as I retrace my memories, write my poems and memoir, write these posts. The reason I have the knowledge of sociopaths that I do is because I had to be intimate with his pain and the true horror of it when he raped me repeatedly. He was a stalker, and, against my will, we were fully enmeshed. I don’t ever want to see him again, and the memories are deeply traumatic, but I think he is the most important thing to ever happen to me. He woke me up; he illuminated everything. He connected all the dots. Being forced to understand him to survive him and being able to feel his feelings made my whole childhood make sense. He woke me up from my denial: I stopped thinking there was anything I could do to earn people’s love. Now I live in reality. Now I pick up pieces of his wreckage and that of everyone I’ve loved, and I try to make them into something beautiful. I bring them back to land with me: I offer them to the living.The dead still surround me everywhere I go. But my treasure is hidden from them, because it exists in the one place they have not been able to defile: MY SOUL. What humanity can be salvaged from the stories of the dead, from the love I had for them, I polish, and seek to refurbish. I hope to help others see the ways they suffer which they can’t even see themselves in their cycle of grief. Denial/anger/denial/anger. In this way, I’m still their family, and still loyal to the inner children in them that I fell in love with. In this way, I honor and memorialize my dead.I hope I pass before my sister, only so that my spirit can be there when she finally is freed from the prison of her body, so I can scoop her in my arms and hold her like I did as a baby in her collapses. So I can usher her to the other side, take her somewhere safe, where there’s light, and love, and no more fear. So she can feel, finally, unconditional love.Pain is energy, and energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be TRANSMUTED. The narcissist deals with the energy of pain by giving it to someone else. ABUSE IS AN ENERGY EXCHANGE. What you feel when they abuse you are the shames that they aren’t strong enough to face. Shames they cannot survive. So, you must take that pain and transmute it somehow. I see myself as a vessel, holding the vulnerabilities and pains of all my family, my friends, my lovers, and even my rapist. I feel the things they can’t survive feeling without killing themselves. Everything I hold is toxic and a serious threat to my life. With all the magic I can muster, I take the poison to my tongue and transform it into nectar. I make it art.I heal myself and I heal the pain this way, and I hope THIS ENERGY brings people healing or clarity. Even if one lonely soul out there decides to live, that means everything to a girl whose first love killed himself at 15. That’s transmuted his pain that I carry.I’ve found reading a variety of religions and spiritualities have comforted me when I felt alien and alone. Spiritually, there are many ideas that align with this type of role of suffering:Generational curse breakerEmpathFae/FairyStarseed/LightworkerEarth AngelChosen OneI tend to think of my rapist, who was the catalyst that awakened me to my sister, as a vampire who turned me, and as my maker, and therefore as a part of my family as well.(This is his favorite fictional character 👆🏼Vampire Lestat). Because, after the trauma of him, I had powers and gratitude beyond anything I’ve known. I had the ability to finally reach acceptance. I lost my fear of death, and I realized all fear is an illusion. I grew closer to God. I became God’s daughter, not an orphan at all. Every day became a gift, a blessing. To survive him, I had to become nothing short of SUPERNATURAL.I learned my worth: my intelligence and my strength. Because it took a Herceulean effort to escape him while drugged and to endure the continued stalking while withdrawing. The only reason someone like him would attack me is because I am a threat to their grandiosity. I have worth. I genuinely didn’t know that. I also understand that he was exceptionally horrific because his inner child was exceptionally harmed and abandoned. I hope someday his spirit can reunite with that child that died, and every day, I pray for his peace, so that others will not be burned by the anger of his grief. I do not fear him and I do not hate him and I do not wish for revenge. HIS WHOLE LIFE IS HIS KARMA. And it’s one he never even deserved to begin with: he was just a baby. We all were. I see him as my father, my son, my brother all in one. Every day, I find his pain—a tiny, snarling, baby wolf nestled somewhere in fear in my ribcage.I pick him up by his scruff and look at him as he snarls and snaps. How did you get out again? I ask. Come, ghost pup, let me take you back to the family mausoleum.Most people think it’s crazy that I think this way. People tell me he deserves death. But it’s not their PTSD and Stockholm Syndrome to make meaning of: it is mine. This is my trauma, my heart, my soul, my survival, and my meaning. I don’t want to return to the stage of anger. This is the meaning that allows me to leave the cycle of grief and work on healing.Yours will look however you want it to. Narcissists survive on a fantasy of lies. We should be able to survive on the beauty of our truths. Wishing you gentle days, gentle people, and meaning. ❤️‍🩹 From ash, all things are created.

column1: What is the most psychologically damaging thing you can say to a child?
column3: Some phone calls growing up were relatives telling my parents another family member died, my parents and I didn’t attend the funeral, and their memories would often barely register in my mind. I lost another part of me that had grown apart from me and died before I could know them. It felt like losing an imaginary friend and the more I lost, the more of my childhood, and innocence died with them. I played the memory of my grandmother being murdered in our home a million times, because she was the only relative that had died that I had known, that I could remember holding, I could remember her moving and living. And she was real, she was SO REAL. I remember that skin when it was pulsating and when it was unmoving ice under warm tropical nightfall. I remember sleeping next to her corpse because there was nowhere to go, and sometimes during dark moments I still feel like there’s nowhere for me. Her life and death were real to me, while other relatives were ghosts. I could never leave to visit or attend a funeral because I was young and undocumented and it would mean a mandatory 10 year ban would be placed on me. I never saw my family back home after the age of 6, they were so distant in my mind they didn’t feel real. I didn’t know them enough to know what I had lost when they died. A breakdown during a field trip from a friend because her grandfather died, another friend losing their dad, a brother, a niece, an uncle, I would look on feeling often numb, or even annoyed at their tearful breakdowns, their confidence that it was the first death they had experienced when I had already experienced several. They were in their teens, or adults and I could feel apathy and frustration at my core that I was working to suppress while trying to share in their grief. Didn’t they know? Family dying is normal, why be so dramatic? What was taking them so long to move on? Couldn’t they understand that the world didn’t owe us anything, that none of us, or our silly human connections mattered? That our lives were simply meant to be taken and forgotten, stuffed into memories for the weak who carried on remembering to feel a bit of love in an uncaring world. I struggled to feel human at times. I struggled to feel that I, or anyone was entitled to safety and a loving family. Being told by news articles and speakers on TV that I deserved no pity for any hardship I ever had could do that. It’s a popular argument, one I grew up with as a first grader to early adulthood, that our stories are worthless and shouldn’t even be taken into consideration because they were “emotional appeals”, not facts. That our sadness, and pain, and tears were just us manipulating citizens into mercy we didn’t deserve. That my existence was taking up resources that didn’t belong to me, I was “stealing” by going to school and eating. Our parents and siblings being taken from us and even dying in detention centers, around the border, or in another country weren’t “facts”, the crippling of our mentality driven by the stigma, medias portrayals of us, and the system that leaves us in fear of our lives weren’t “facts”, the wars the US fights in our backyards aren’t “facts”, they’re “emotional stories” meant to fuel empathy in citizens and trick them into maybe loosening up all the obstacles they placed to ensure the playing field was never equal. We didn’t deserve empathy, we were criminals even if we weren’t convicted, even if we paid taxes, even if the government gave us temporary rights to work and stay temporary. Illegal means illegal, and it means you are a criminal, you have no rights, and you aren’t human. Any attempt made by me to show my humanity or capability to feel and experience horrors was met with laughs from regulars in mass media that frequently spoke on immigration. “Oh their daughter or father was deported, well… GOOD!!! Hahahaha justice prevails!” Confetti was thrown and cheers were heard from crew members. “This Illegal died working, serves him right for breaking the LAW! They can’t be crazy enough to expect sympathy right? They’re nothing but criminals.” As a child the way I fought back internally was by developing tough skin. I let racial slurs, and words calling me a parasite, criminal, illegal flash by my face during study sessions as if they were nothing. They became part of my identity, words that were used to talk about children like me who didn’t deserve anything. I accepted that I could never get a handout, help, nor should I expect empathy. Living with constant uncertainty meant living on hope alone. And I hoped that one day I would be worth something if I worked hard enough to prove my worth to citizens. I dreamed of the day when citizens and the government would have no choice but to recognize my humanity. That dream died in my teens. Accepting what I saw so frequently, meant accepting that I was worthless by default and would need to be extraordinary to gain any kind of acceptance. I couldn’t just be me and be an average person – that would be deemed unworthy and undesirable. It meant accepting the belief that my family and my connections and contributions to the US and the world were meaningless at best, harmful at worst. Accepting what these people thought about people like me would mean viewing the very worst in humanity, complete dehumanization to the point of apathy to their death. I didn’t want to be like them. I wanted to feel. I wanted to stop being numb because I was killing my humanity by allowing their ideas of me to destroy the reality of myself that I knew. I wanted to see all of life as meaningful, and death of a person as a loss to the world. I wanted to experience the reality, the facts of life. The fact that we’re social animals, and our ability to care about others is what makes civilization, our very support networks, and our ability to grow and live rests on others caring enough about us. I couldn’t accept that apathy and dehumanization was rational, objective, and a sign of a skeptical person. I saw it as a serious mental disorder, as the inability of a person to see another person as human as they are. That’s why I stayed when my friends broke down and tried to feel the pain in the back of my throat again from the first death I truly felt. I needed to grow my love and empathy because I would be damned if I grow up to become one of the monsters I saw in the media.

column1: Have your parents ever completely disowned you?
column3: Yes. It just happened on the way to a funeral for someone in another side of my family. My aunt hss a history of taking several years to deal with a perceived slight. She demands loyalty to the endth degree regardless of whether you agree with her or not. Many years ago, one of my aunts brought a serious boyfriend home for Christmas. My grandmother was a widow (and a snob) so she asked him about his plans to keep her daughter in a satisfactory (to her) way throughout their life. My uncle didn't appreciate the invasive questions and he let her know it wasn't her business. My other aunt was outraged and went ahead with telling her own sister she wasn't welcome at home for Christmas because he was “rude" to my grandmother. My grandmother didn't want to say anything herself but my other aunt just decided to do this and no one stopped her. Not long after that my temporarily disowned aunt got married, and the reception was in my grandmother's back yard. I assume that the big dramatic uproar was resolved to some extent. When my great grandmother died there was a huge argument and subsequent rift that lasted for several years over some material objects that my dad took away from my great grandmother's house when her grandchildren met there to divide her personal effects. After that I recall a Christmas or two where we were not allowed to speak to my dad's side of the family. When I left home at a young age my father stopped speaking to one of my aunts because she gave me a place to live for a year. Several years later my grandmother died. Her estate had some sort of legal issue because paperwork proving a loan to her business by another industry related business was either lost, not recorded correctly or something. I don't know what actually happened because it wasn't part of my life. Somehow I got dragged into communications between my aunt and my dad as the court case moved through. I relayed information from my father to my aunt that she really didn't like (not even sure what was said) and she told me to tell him that she said “I'll see him in hell!” Then she slammed the phone down. Ten years after this she went through treatment for a fairly advanced cancer. Suddenly my aunt had an epiphany and she took my dad to lunch and pretty much insisted that he speak to her again. All of a sudden we were allowed to speak to my aunt again. Whenever we got together with my dad and his siblings it always struck me as odd that he barely spoke when they were around but I didn't connect the dots between the pieces I knew and my dad deliberately keeping quiet with his own siblings. About five or so years later, my father died suddenly. My aunt was helpful to me and my siblings to an extent but then she and my mother whom I had not spoken to because she refusrd to acknowledge the child abuse she inflicted on me, and one other sibling. I'm talking about beatings with objects, throwing children down stairs, near drownings, and constant screaming and threats to be thrown out of the house for my childhood. My aunt was fueling the fire from behind the scenes with me and my mother fueled the hate against me and my aunt. Dad's estate was in total disarray with debts and leins on his home. My mother and aunt (dad's sister) essentially used me and my siblings as pawns in their battle. My mother told me that I was being manipulated by my aunt but I was so far gone with grief over my dad in addition to our own estrangement that I wouldn't listen to her. Another aunt didn't do as she was told over another family crisis and my aunt told me I was not allowed to speak to her because of it. I tried to reason with her but she became hysterical and screamed at me that I had to alienate my other aunt. At first I obeyed but then someone in the family was gravely ill and I called the person she forbade me to contact. I couldn't imagine this other person dying and no one telling her. One of my aunts is not in the best of health. She underwent surgery to improve her mobility. On the way to visit her I bought a box of high quality chocolates. I was very careful to pick chocolates that didn't take a lot of strength to unwrap. I arrived in my recovering aunt's room and presented the chocolates. My other aunt was in a huff about something and she grabbed the box out of my hands, said my aunt had been “rude to the nurses and bad" so she was giving them to the nurses. I was shocked and (I'm ashamed to admit) I was scared to say a word in disagreement. I have been struggling with depression and anxiety disorders since having a number of serious incidents in a one year period (job loss, car accident, and the loss of another important family member) that I was really having a hard time getting through each day. My aunt said I was fine and to “stop whining and playing the victim”. I got worse for a while because I couldn't afford proper mental health treatment. I tried hard to both keep my distance and keep in touch for fear of losing her. Over the past 4 years things between us became more and more strained. She decided to disown me just a week ago as I traveled to a funeral for someone unrelated to her who was important to me. Sitting in the chapel at that funeral was very difficult and she enlisted my siblings to make sure to let me know they also no longer thought of me as family. By the end of the service it was obvious that my presence at the internment and wake was unwelcome so I went home in order to avoid further humiliation for myself and to avoid an ugly confrontation in front of the other folks on this other side of my family. I wanted to kill myself because it felt like I had just lost one of the most important living people in my life. My spouse is furious and he gave my aunt a piece of his mind. The thing is that when I thought about the whole sordid, embarrassing, ugly mess I realized that my aunt is at the root of all of these problems. Over the past 15 years my aunt has changed her will cutting first, making me the executor of her estate without telling her former executor (her own sister) that she had done so. Then she cut two of my siblings out because she didn't like the way they behaved after my dad died. I am sure she has already been to see her lawyer about removing me from her estate entirely. I just don't think it's right to hurt people you're supposed to love with such extreme measures so often. There has been a great deal of loss in my life which makes this disowned status particularly difficult to handle but I have to accept this new situation and move on. Don't mistake me for believing that I feel I am perfect. I am a deeply flawed person but also a work in progress. I just don't believe anyone has the right to take so much control in a family much less being so destructive to all. It's extremely painful to be disowned but I think it might be better for me than to “obey" any longer. It's going to take quite a while to heal from this as it triggers abandonment issues deep in me but I have to heal because I'm not going to end my life just because someone is hateful and doesn't love me anymore. To those out there who are facing this same situation, remember its not you they're rejecting. They don't really know you. Reach out to your friends, other unrelated family members for support. If you feel lost find a therapist. Just do not give up on yourself and do not let anyone tell you your value. My aunt does not know what love is and I'm not about to stick around to show her. It's not worth ir, she's not listening.

column1: I feel empty, I never feel satisfaction in anything and I don't understand why. I'm not depressed because I don't feel sadness. What does it mean?
column3: I understand EXACTLY how you feel. I have been in depression for about 9 years now and I think I can contribute to your question. Just for the sake of relatability I will tell you the details. My mother and younger sister committed suicide on my 21st birthday, I will be 29 on this 1st of May. Following that event, I have seen everyone look down on me and hating my guts since I had been a very confident and smart kid but very laid back and lazy, with a very short temper so I never shied away from telling things as they were (mostly in a condescending manner), although I have always been a very reliable friend who would give my life for someone I know if they need me but yah, people could not win an argument with me. Not saying I was always right but sometimes when I was wrong I would not admit it since people always looked for an excuse to put me down. Also maybe because I used to get bullied as kid when I was kind and spoke very little since I was very fat and dressed and had a haircut that my mother always picked for me even though all the kids around me were showing off. So starting puberty I followed the wave too to gain friends although in the core I was who I had always been but I would not shy away from hurting other people with my words if that was the raw truth. (I know better now) So, needless to say that in my weakest time everyone started looking down on me and with that I got more bitter and became a loner and I still live alone with my 4 dogs although I am not bitter anymore. Please bear with me while I babble a little more for the sake of context. People and their behavior only made me angry and betrayed but not sad but the thing that really made me grieve was my family’s death since my mother raised us all by herself and it was just us growing up and I had a wonderful childhood thanks to my mother and the loving atmosphere of the house. Now that was all gone. I loved my sister and mother the most, now they were gone. I did not have any desire to do anything, no reason, no excuse. Only overwhelming grief for which I was too foolishly tough to actually grieve. I was only angry and since I always picked fights with anyone and everyone who tried to bully me from 7th grade, I had no problem making enemies and by then I was also a good amateur boxer. Not very strong, I was lazy but very stubborn and very angry and I would not mind getting hurt to prove I am not what they think I am. So, I did not grieve, I could not grieve. Since I was always a very curious kid growing up, I always enjoyed finding questions and answering them. No time better than the information age for someone like that. I could not grieve and instead I channeled all my thoughts to answer any and every question that bugged me. From conspiracy theories to facts to history and quantum physics and so on. But the goal was only to find the answer and look for something else to keep my mind occupied. I LOVED video games as a kid. My mom let us watch all the movie, cartoons and play all the video games we wanted which greatly contributed to my creativity. I was not playing a game, I was in there living it. I was in the cartoons, in the movies I watched. It was all so real. And all so great. But now I was only did things to keep my mind occupied so that I would not have thoughts about what happened. And now it was not the same. I could not FEEL anything. I could not live the games I played, could not enjoy anything. Although I had a very critical view of things, I noticed it all but never felt it. The blue sky, the cold nights, the colorful games, I saw them all, they all registered with my brain but not my senses. I played games all the time, watched movies all the time, ate what I felt like eating since I had always loved eating what my mother cooked and that is why I was fat. But now nothing felt like anything. I ate and ate till I could hardly breathe and had to throw up eventually. Since I was living alone with my dogs, there was no one to tell me to stop and by this point I had stopped listening to what anyone had to say. They did not say it because they cared, they said it because they could point something wrong about me and I hated that so I did the opposite as I willed. I was always a capable guy, had good education, my teachers called me a brilliant kid but always added that I was over confident too. Since I was always a smart kid at school, my mom did not force me to do anything like study harder or so on since I was the only one among my siblings who aced all subjects without even trying. That fed the fire of my arrogance and ego. I was not arrogant right off the bat, I was kind, well spoken and a funny guy who did not mind making a fool of himself to make people laugh but if there was a discussion where I felt like someone else is acting foolishly or arrogantly, I would be more arrogant and rude with my words and beat that at the discussion and people seemed to enjoy that. I did not mind insulting people on their face but I only did it on their faces even if they were my teachers, elders or peers. So, its not hard to see why people found it hard to digest me. But apart from that I was very funny and fun to be around, very helpful and never said NO to anything someone asked no matter what price I had to pay for myself. I loved being able to help. And one thing about people is they forget the 100 good things u do if you piss them off just once. And now they all had a excuse to point fingers toward me. I hated it, I hated everyone and that was the only thing I felt if I ever felt anything. During all other activities I was empty. I could not tell which day it was, whether I had lunch a few hours ago or the last day and years passed by without notice. I could not feel anything, I could not enjoy the things I used to love but I always kept chasing them telling myself that I am doing what makes me happy. It never did. There was not motivation and despite me trying to force objectives and goals upon myself, it never came from the inside and everything fell apart soon after. It did not bother me either. Until………. I mentioned I have 4 dogs, dogs have been in my family for about 18 years now. My mom loved animals as she loved us and she loved us immensely. She had a very troubled life full of suffering, betrayal and negligence and had attempted suicide before we were born and failed with major injuries. And raising us, she found a will to live and that magnified with our dogs. She loved animals, everyone of them. We had 4 dogs indoors and she fed and took care of all the strays of our neighborhood and visited shelters and animal welfare organizations and helped generously. When she left, she left me with Annie, a female Japanese Spitz who was birthed by Jenny, a female spitz we had bought from a puppy mill. She was the apple of their eyes, both my mother and sister. You could not tell that they were animals or pets if you saw how my mom and sister treated her. She was their daughter and she was immensely intelligent. They left her in my care and wrote in their suicide note to take good care of my little sister Annie. When they left me I had 5 dogs, soon I buried them one after another, I fed them and everything but I could not love and care for them like my mother and sister wanted me to. Sure, they ate what I ate, they slept on the same bed with me but I was lost in my own head for far too long. After 8 years, I lost Annie on the 1st of July last year. I loved her and she loved me more than I could ever love her. I remember laying on bed for 18 hours straight, thinking, dreaming, and she woke me up. Not for food or water, but to keep me with her, I would have rotted on my bed long ago if I did not have to get up for her. I buried all my other four legged family members one after another, even adopted a lot of sick strays who did not seem like they would make it on the streets much longer. Only to give them the last few days of love and a warm bed. But that's all I could offer them, not love, because I had none left in me and I did not love myself either. My health was deteriorating, Either I was eating like a mad man or did not eat at all. I was on my computer all the time. I worked as a freelance writer and did game reviews for papers. My brain worked fine but I could not feel anything. I always kept myself occupied with anything and did not play or pay much attention to my dogs. But if they got sick its like it would wake me up, the fear of losing them. And after they were fine I was back to the same useless distance self. It was when I lost Annie that I cried after 9 years, I could not cry when I saw my mother and sister hanging from the ceiling but when Annie left me I cried like a child. For 32 days straight, I cried every day like a child, two or three times a day every time I thought about it. And now since I have suffered some more losses after Annie I am getting back into being a responsible sane person. The point I am trying to make is, I used to feel empty, like there was nothing inside me despite trying so hard to find it. I could not. But then I suffered the unimaginable loss that I never thought I would. Then I realized there was so much for me to lose and I was convinced that I had lost it all. Now I have 4 dogs that remind me that time is ticking. Soon their time with come or mine. And when that day comes, I do not want to grieve thinking what could have been if I had more time with them. I want to spend every day with them making them feel loved and keep them happy. Because they are the ones who love me, and we owe our life to the ones who love us. So, unless we realize how much love we are surrounded by, we will continue feeling empty, like there is nothing, when in reality there is always someone is counting on you, who will miss you when you are gone, and to whom you owe your happiness. So, if I think about the ways of keeping the ones who love me and whom I love happy and make them feel loved, that fills the emptiness inside me with resolve. Then nothing seems impossible or unattainable. There is no EGO on the way because the only thing that matters is them and their love which makes me feel alive. Those who rely on me and those who will bask in the joy of my success. So there is always something to live for, When this realization comes from deep within, then only do we truly feel alive and achieve our best self. No problem is unsolvable, we can do what needs to be done. I did not feel the same even after I answered all my questions. YES! I found the answers to everything I was looking for about a year back before losing my beloved Annie and even though I had thought that it was the answers that I was missing, I realized that I was only chasing them because I needed something to chase. They did not matter. Now, I know how everything works, I have answered my questions which I KNOW have been answered, but it does not matter. What matters is HERE AND NOW and the ones who love us. This has given me the energy to wake up early, cook proper meals, meditate for a sound mental and physical health and succeed in worldly terms all the while fulfilling my purpose and FEELING ALIVE. I am starting to get a sense of being in the videogame, being in the movie or a book that I am reading. When I walk on the streets, I know I am there and what time it is and what I am there to do and whatever may come next, I shall get it done. No plans, no waiting for something to happen, just doing it and getting it done, because they need to get done so that I can spend blissful evenings with my dogs and understand them and know them better in order to provide them with the happiness in return for the unconditional love. I know that there are a few friends of mine who would mourn if something unfortunate were to happen to me and who would joy in my success. That's all that matters. Not money, not aliens, not the Gods or religions, nor the politics or world peace. All we have to do is relate with the suffering and it will help us grow. I still help people and my friends but I do not feel hurt if they do not do so. I do not feel bitter if someone says something or gives me ‘that’ look. Because I know what matters, and its love. :) Forgive me if I babbled for too long. If there is even a single line or word that resonated with you, I am glad, and grateful. thank you very much for the question. Answering it gave me a clearer perspective on myself too. There is no cure to depression, its not a disease or illness. Its a state of mind, a pattern of thinking and the perception of the world and situations we are surrounded by that creates one’s reality. If we can understand our own mind, we can fix what needs to be fixed but only as long as we do it every living moment, every single day. There are people who tough it out every moment and they have been dealt the worst cards possible. We can only be grateful for having so much.

column1: What’s a time in your life when you realized something like that would happen for the last time?
column3: “What’s a time in your life when you realized something like that would happen for the last time?” When I heard the words on the telephone “You’re not my real dad. I never want to see you again. Don’t call me anymore. K___ (my best friend from childhood) is my dad now, and I only want him.” It was his birthday. I had just arrived in California, having uprooted my new, very pregnant wife and all our few possessions from the Midwest and driven there, jobless, penniless, hungry and wondering how we’d keep up the rent on the insanely expensive house we’d just rented, and waiting to receive “emergency assistance” which was going to take about two weeks. Some fricking emergency! I’d called my first-born 7-year-old son to resume visitation with him after having been traveling for over a year and trying to heal from my then-SO leaving me for my best friend in the entire world. I’d had NO idea that my absence would affect him so profoundly, though he did have his mom (my ex) ruthlessly whispering ugly things in his ear. I was insane and dangerous, I wasn’t his “real” dad because we’d never gotten legally married (we lived together for several years, and I’d step-parented an older child as well, as if she were my very own. Yes, I lost her too.) I was an asshole that didn’t deserve him. I don’t want the birthday present you brought me. Just throw it in the trash, where it belongs. I knew from his tone of voice that he was serious, and that I’d never see him again in any meaningful way. Now, over 50 years later, it’s still sadly true. I was an innocent, peace-and-love hippie. I somehow imagined that the “free-love, everybody-do-their-own-thing” zeitgeist of the time would just sort of automatically be absorbed by my son. Today, after raising 10 kids and seeing my 6 grandkids regularly, I’m stunned at my ignorance during that time. I was a complete idiot. It honestly didn’t dawn on me that I could ever lose him through staying off in my own little world long enough. (Just a suspicion – all the drugs I was doing at the time probably didn’t help, especially the booze.) I honestly didn’t hear from him at all until about 10 years later. He was in “rehab.” He’d been in a gang, doing massive amounts of cocaine and wandering the park with his “bros,” looking for “black people to beat up.” Yep, that’s right, my hippie sensibilities had been utterly trashed and my son had become a skinhead! The only reason he called me then is that it was part of his “making amends” process. He’d said “no hard feelings” but it didn’t ring true, then or now. He also cut me off before I had a chance to explain things – how ripped apart I’d felt by his mom after the breakup – how I’d wandered the streets for almost 3 years, haunted by command voices, exhibiting bizarre behaviors. I marveled at how ruthless she’d been about preventing me from seeing him. She cut me to ribbons, emotionally. Fact is, I was very childish – I was so injured that I just turned tail and ran. I ran into drugs, into a lot of pointless, only-for-sex relationships (which usually ended because I’d fall head-over-heels-in-love with whatever partner,) off to Maui for a season, back to my hometown for a bit. I was truly a Lost Boy. Finally, FINALLY, I’d made it back to resume things with him, but it was too late. I wrote it all in a 10-page letter to him which I doubt he ever saw, since I was trying to get it to him via his treatment center. No matter. By then, he just plain didn’t give a shit. I can’t say as I blame him. I utterly betrayed him, without even realizing it. Fast forward a few more decades. I’d raised all my kids, even managing to avoid the obvious pitfall of being overprotective or overly-permissive with them to try and make up for my most painful loss in life. I’d gotten a little bit of news from a family member who was still in touch with him. He’d become a police officer in a major city, working the toughest ‘hood, and being a cage-fighter in his off hours. I hope the irony here isn’t lost on anyone. Myself, an ex-con who’d been a “fuck da police” semi-militant hippie most of my life, learning that I’d spawned a son who passed through a skinhead phase, only to become a tough cop, a Republican, and a cage fighter! I learned that he’d cut off communication with his mom and his “real dad” when he came of age. I reached out one more time, just a few years ago to try again to establish contact. I even enlisted the help of an investigator, and wound up getting a brief message through to him at his work. He called me ONCE. He was NOT happy with me. He said that if I ever tried to contact him again, there would “be consequences.” I just said “OK, I hear you.” When a big city cop uses the word “consequences” I assume they mean it. He was especially pissed that I’d contacted him through his precinct. I get it. And so, all I can do is let go. I’ve had so many successes in life, especially on the relationship front. I’m happily married and in a 35-year-long honeymoon with the most amazing woman I’ve ever known. I’m close and loving with all my other kids, and with all my grandchildren (that I know of, anyway – I was a VERY busy boy during the “free love” era.) I’ve produced several albums of original music, and spent quite a few years providing psychotherapy that helped people with addiction problems immensely. Though retired, I still wind up as the guy people call when they’re at the end of their rope, because they know I’ll hear them without any judgment. I’ve done a great deal of personal growth work, and I know (as well as one can) what runs me, what stops me, what pleases me, and what I will not tolerate. I still produce records in my home studio, and I’m having a blissful retirement. We two love and adore each other in a very active, affectionate, creative way. Having said that, hearing those words from my first-born son that day, I knew absolutely that it was the last time I’d ever truly communicate with him. It hurt, more than I could ever express. It hurt worse, because I had to admit that I’d caused it myself, by my absence. It was agonizing because I knew there were no do-overs for this one; that I’d well and truly lost, and all I had left was grief. I’ve lost people to death, and I can attest that this is worse. When someone is dead, they’re gone for certain, and all you can do is grieve them until you heal enough to go on. In my case, I knew that he was alive, walking the world, living his life, and I could never hold him in my arms again, comfort his pain, change his diapers, or have a man-to-man talk about the world we live in. He wasn’t gone. He was just gone for me, and every time I’d think of him, it would just reopen old wounds. I’ve healed about as much as I can in one lifetime from this terrible loss. I actually go for months at a time without wondering what might have been, had I been just a bit more willing to stick it out and keep dealing with “that bitch,” and “that asshole.” I can wonder, yes, but I’ll never know. I’ll just never know. Thankfully, I did manage to heal my friendship with him many years later. In some ways, I missed him a lot more than I did her. Peace, Love, and Flowers, man! Everybody get together and love one another RIGHT NOW! Let the sunshine in. All you need is LOVE. No, really. Love is enough, if it’s a verb.
column9: Patrick, if it makes you feel any better, I too was divorced as my wife “fell in love” with the guy across the street. That’s a story I KNOW you wouldn’t believe so…….But I stayed around until my kids were grown and off to college. I did the dutiful dad thing, every two weeks, paid my child support, went to their school functions, etc. Now they don’t speak to me or care whether I’m dead or alive. They love their step-father, of course. Why? Because my ex, in an effort to justify her leaving for the bigger better deal, lied to everyone, including our kids about me. Stories with no basis in fact, but she had them since they were 6 months and two years old so they grew up believing the stories while I took the high road ( ha ha ) and never talked about their mother while they were growing up. What did it get me? Nothing. Your ex trashing you to your son doomed you from the start, you didn’t stand a chance.

column1: What did Charles Darwin honestly have to offer that was better than religion?
column3: Let’s talk about finding meaning in life. Specifically, let’s imagine finding it in the worst thing a loving parent can imagine, let alone experience: the death of a beloved child. Let’s suppose the child had a sweet and affectionate nature, numerous talents, intellectual curiosity, and an openhearted kindness that brightened the lives of everyone around her. Now let’s give her a name, devoted siblings and adoring parents. Meet Annie Darwin.(Forgive her sour expression. The photographer demanded she put on a solemn face and sit absolutely still for two whole minutes—a torment for a jolly nine-year-old.) I’m a parent, so the very idea of losing a child fills me with horror and sympathetic grief. I can’t even imagine what her parents, Charles and Emma Darwin went through. But like a lot of parents in that age before modern medicine they did go through it. When she died, her father Charles whose health wasn’t great at the best of times, became so immobilized by illness and grief that he couldn’t even make it to her funeral, but afterwards he wrote to a friend,She was my favourite child; her cordiality, openness, buoyant joyousness & strong affection made her most loveable.1 Poor dear little soul. Well it is all over.This happened in 1851, when Darwin was still keeping the idea of Evolution by Natural Selection hidden away on the shelf in what he called his “Transmutation Notebooks” and concentrating on his less controversial book about barnacles. His wife Emma, a devout Christian, seemed to take more comfort after Annie’s death than Charles could. Charles wasn’t religious and his beloved daughter’s passing didn’t do much to convince him that a just and loving god was looking after things. But despite his overwhelming grief and ill health, he continued working on his barnacle book until it consumed five years and ran 267 pages. At that point in his life, the answer to “what did Charles Darwin offer..?” would have been, “more about barnacles than you ever thought possible.” How was that better than religion? Emma probably would have said it wasn’t, and you might agree, but Charles had tried being religious and found that no matter how he tried, he couldn’t put aside his doubts, so: barnacles. We all do what we can to get by and what we do, depends a lot on who we are. Though we might demand that Charles find spiritual solace in Christianity the way his wife did, that would be like asking him to wear her shoes. Even if he thought he should, they wouldn’t fit and the effort would cause him more pain, not less. That’s almost always how it works with other people’s ‘guaranteed’ solutions. Fortunately for both Charles and Emma, their child’s death didn’t drive them apart as it might some couples. Instead, they grew closer to each other and their remaining children, who ran underfoot in their father’s study and decorated the manuscript of his new work, On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection with their delightful paintings.(a cavalry battle between garden crops and insects)(Birds eating insects…are you detecting a theme here?) Emma remained devout in her own quiet way, she came to accept that Charles needed to pursue his work in Natural History and Biology even if it led to some conclusions that seemed to undermine the story of Creation in the Bible she loved so well. Couples often reach these kinds of accommodations in marriages that go the distance. By 1855, Emma no longer objected to Charles expanding the notes on Evolution by Natural Selection in his notebooks, but still he delayed. Why might he have done that? One reason might be that he was a modest man who loved living a quiet life in the country, where he studied, wrote letters, raised pigeons to observe their wonderful variations, and playing outside with his children, whose paintings showed such an intuitive understanding of the epic struggles for survival happening every minute in every garden, forest and stream. The idea of publishing a theory as likely to cause a fuss as Natural Selection had no appeal for him. He wasn’t a troublemaker like his grandfather, Erasmus had been. Erasmus had published his own, much less scientifically grounded book on Evolution years before. When Erasmus’ book hit the market, many religious people denounced him as a dangerous heretic and he didn’t improve matters by openly carrying on sexual relationships with a series of young women. It took a full generation for the Darwin family to live down the shame. His mild-mannered grandson didn’t want any of that sort of notoriety, so he put off publishing the work for which he became known until 1859 when it appeared that a naturalist named Alfred Wallace was about to beat him into print with the same theory. It appeared in print, and it caused exactly the sort of fuss with a certain type of religious person that he had hoped to avoid. There were denunciations from the pulpit and a famous smackdown debate between one of Darwin’s early devotees and a well-respected Anglican Bishop named Wilberforce. A society lady told of Darwin’s theory sniffed, “let us hope it is not true, and if it is true, let us hope it does not become widely known.” He never sought this controversy but it was happening, so what was he supposed to do? On the plus side, his simple theory explained in straightforward language, exactly how and why one species of animal can change into something very different over the course of thousands and millions of years—a phenomenon Natural Historians had begun calling, “Evolution” years before. Scientist, Thomas Huxley did a big facepalm when he first read Darwin’s simple and logical explanation for Evolution, and his reaction was typical:“How stupid not to have thought of it!”Though the theory was simple and logical, Huxley and a lot of others could be forgiven for not having thought of it, because it’s based on the kinds of hard truths most us spend our lives avoiding. At the risk of making people uncomfortable all over again, these hard truths are:Truth #1: The Earth is much older than any person, generation, lineage or anything else human or animal upon it. It was here before we arrived and will be here after we’re gone. Over millions of years, the pressure of magma from the molten earth elevates deep ocean beds until they become landlocked mountains and the fossilized bodies of extinct sea creatures are found on their summits. Why it’s So Uncomfortable: We can’t see this happening because we don’t live long enough and never will. All those slow, tiny changes that add up into ocean beds on mountain peaks are still happening but we won’t live to see them because we are here such a short time compared to the age of the earth. We die too soon. Ouch.Truth #2: Just as ocean beds oh-so-gradually push up into to mountain tops over the course of millions of years, species of animals like pigeons, barnacles and apes also undergo tiny changes over thousands of generations and when enough of these changes accumulate, the result is a completely different species. Why it’s So Uncomfortable: All this gradual change isn’t happening on any time frame that we can ever observe and it’s not leading to any grand ultimate conclusion that is all about us. We’re not central to the story in any way; we are just another twig on the huge, running river of time and change. Ouch.Truth #3: Species members change over many generations into other due to the awful fact that not all offspring survive to have offspring of their own and the ones who do survive pass on the traits that helped them survive in their environment. In time those beneficial traits accumulate into a whole ‘nother animal. Why it’s so Uncomfortable: One of the offspring that didn’t survive was sweet Annie Darwin, who seemed to have all the advantages of intelligence, talent, beauty, good character and family wealth going for her, but died before adulthood nonetheless. She wasn’t able to fight off or recover from her childhood illness. That was the only difference between her and the homely, ill-tempered child who survived the same disease and went on to have kids herself despite her indifferent brains, temperament and upbringing . Even some of Darwin’s followers had problems with this stark reality. They tried to turn his theory into a contest where ‘survival of the fittest’ meant, ‘survival of the most intelligent and physically attractive members of a societally privileged race’ but that distorted way of thinking only made human societies much, much worse whenever it was applied. Darwin knew better. Fitness meant being adapted for survival, not having virtue, brains or beauty. If it had, Annie Darwin would have lived. But she didn’t.After all that pain, where was the meaning in what he gave us? Well, there was truth and understanding that shone a light on how life develops and changes on earth. It’s simply not possible to understand how living things grow and change without Darwin’s explanation of Evolution. That knowledge has made us healthier, longer-lived and able to defeat the sort of diseases that killed dear, sweet Annie Darwin. But there was a moral, and even spiritual lesson as well, for those who had the courage to look, and that lesson was this: Stop looking for moral justifications for your actions or inactions in a divinely ordained natural plan. Nature does what it does, for its own mechanistic reasons and produces its own results—beautiful or awful, from a particular set of circumstances in a particular time and place, nothing more, nothing less. If we as human beings decide we should be kind when we might just as well be cruel, generous when we get no direct benefit and generally reject nature’s remorseless logic in favor of a kinder human way of life, we can and should. Nobody and nothing is stopping us.

column1: What is your biggest failure in life?
column3: Who Murdered My Ex-wife? This is a very long answer, and I apologize if it’s too long. It tells a story of a series of lifelong failures that compounded to bring me to believe, at a subconscious level, that I murdered my ex-wife. After a lot of therapy, I believe this goes back to a childhood where I failed to bond well with either parent at a young age. My entire family lived in fear my father’s business would fail at any moment. I and all my siblings worked tremendously hard in the family business, fearing if we didn’t work exceptionally hard, our entire world would fall apart in public failure. This situation from birth through high school created an environment where, at a young age I would do anything to gain the praise of my parents in the name of doing my part to “save” the family from disaster. I wanted to be the perfect “white knight” that “saved” my family. Sad, but irrationally true. These dynamics resulted in many significant and some less significant “failures” in my life:Marginal student K-12. Felt like a failure.Sexually molested at age 12 in Boy Scouts. Very confused, didn’t tell a soul for nearly 40 years. I told my ex-wife 2 months before she filed for divorce. Contributed to failed relationships throughout life, and was a “trigger” for my ultimate divorce.Dysfunctional and unhealthy relationships with girls in high school and college. I was overly sexual, failed to be truly intimate, in these and future relationships. I never had a “normal” stable relationship. I didn’t know how to do that.Hyper sex drive from a young age. Responsible for an abortion in college. I held her hand in the operation room as the abortion was conducted. I’ll never forget it. Tremendous sense of shame, guilt, regret and desperation. I held this secret to myself for about 30 years, disclosing it only to my ex-wife, 2 weeks before she filed for divorce.Successful at college level, a degree in accounting - a choice I made to get a job, not because I loved it. I never explored other options as I felt pressure to “get a job “ ASAP. I was desperate to escape the economic fear of failure I had grown up with and “prove” I could assimilate to a “professional” level.Struggled to pass the CPA exam, taking it 5 times before finally passing. Embarrassed and humiliated that I had to take it so many times when most passed within 2 trys.Practiced as a CPA for a major national firm, a “dream job”. I felt socially and professionally out of place, hated it, quit. Felt like a loser who “dropped” out of a huge opportunity. I had professionally failed after years of preparation in college.Married a sweet, beautiful career woman that I thought I loved - and as you read on, I did. I admired her most for her career drive and accomplishment. In hindsight, I was a “ human doing” rather than a “human being” and I sought the same in my mate. But I didn’t know how to truly love her at the time.We had a beautiful child. Her mother postponed her career to raise the baby girl. I was “busy” providing for my family, traveling and working tremendous hours. What I was really doing was “disconnecting” from my wife and daughter, but I didn’t recognize it as such at the time. I was failing as a husband and a father, but I was a “provider”.My wife and I slowly became separate entities, more like roommates than lovers. Our daughter became our only real common bond. Sex had not been part of our relationship for a number of years. I was failing in love, but did not recognize it.In frustration, I was unfaithful when I traveled. Thousands of dollars spent on escorts. I become heavily dependent on “extra curricular” sex. I was ashamed, as I had violated a basic belief and character trait I valued. While I had cheated on my wife, I had failed myself even more, I had violated my core principles.My wife discovers my unfaithfulness. She demands I take a lie detector test. I pass the test, but the details send my wife into shock.I’m diagnosed as a “sex addict” by a psychiatrist. I attend 12 step programs for two years. I continue to act out. My wife and I become two ships in the night, never to connect or cross paths. My marriage was failing because of me.I am a failure at controlling my addiction. I disclose my sexual abuse as a boy and the abortion in college. My wife questions my sexual orientation / identity. Two weeks later, my wife of 23 years files for divorce.I am a failure at marriage, love snd fatherhood. I move to an apartment pending divorce. I fear the loss of my relationship with my college age daughter. My world is collapsing around me in failure. I am alone, embarrassed, ashamed. Thank God for my few friends and extended family.I lose approximately 50% of my assets and investments in the divorce and am required to pay support for at least the next 10 years. My life savings in a 401(k) became a 201(k)! I feel like a financial failure, with my ability to ever retire in question.After divorce, my ex-wife announces she is moving to California to be as far away from her sex - addicted ex-husband as possible. I am ostracized from all her family members I have known as family for some 25 years.She gives my daughter instruction that I am to know absolutely NOTHING of her life beyond making sure I pay my support. I am now a divorced, alone, isolated, sex addicted failure of a man, worried he has destroyed any relationship with his daughter. I thought this was the lowest point in my failure. Not so, there was more to come. Keep reading.For three years, I lived in isolation, making my support payments, knowing my ex-wife lived in California. That’s all I knew. When I did speak to my daughter, she was careful not to share details. The isolation felt like solitary confinement. I couldn’t understand my feelings. I was supposed to HATE my ex-wife, but the experience only told me I still loved her. It hurt.After 18 years at the same company, I received the news I was laid off at age 58. I called my daughter to let her know I had failed at yet another job, but that I’d be okay.When I called, my daughter broke into tears. She was in an airport catching a flight to California. She told me her mother was in intensive care, sick with a rare autoimmune disease she had been fighting for 2 1/2 years.My daughter told me she may need me in California if things turn for the worse. As I hung up my phone, I felt terrible all of this was going on and I was in the dark. I felt guilty that my accumulated failures had stressed my ex-wife, resulted in divorce and essentially made her severely ill. My moral failures and character flaws had done tremendous and life threatening damage to two people I loved.The next day, my ex-wife died with my daughter by her side. My daughter called and I got on a plane to California to support my young daughter as she planned a memorial service for her mom’s California friends and co- workers and a family funeral two weeks later in Pennsylvania.At the California memorial service, I felt tremendous pain, as I was not “part of the family” at the service or in the eulogies. People there knew who I was, but nearly all avoided me as if I were a pariah. I was alone, in a back pew, at the memorial service of my ex-wife, listening to eulogies, including that of my daughter, that failed to mention that she was married for 23 years. Her marriage to me and my presence was “the elephant in the room”.I felt I was nobody, perceived as evil, treated as a pariah. I left the funeral to cry alone on a park bench. I have never felt more failure, grief and shame in all my experience and memory. I’ve never cried more violently. It tore my guts out and there was no one to talk to.For the first time, I seriously considered taking my own life in shame and guilt. Helping my daughter at this time became my saving grace. I believe that purpose in that moment is what kept me alive.Two weeks later, my daughter and I went to Pennsylvania for a funeral and burial. The family welcomed me and were kind, however, to this day I have no contact with any of the people I knew for over 25 years.Two weeks after that, we returned to California to clean out my ex-wife’s apartment and dispose of her possessions. When we found her important papers. She had adjusted the bennificiary of her investments and insurance policies to name our daughter. But when we found her will, she had not changed it since before divorce. I was named the executor of her will. A strange twist. Was this simply an oversight - or intentional? I’ll never know.These events tormented me greatly. I sought mental health services to help me. I was severely depressed and still unemployed. I was often unable to get out of bed, I had lost weight and was unable to focus on finding a new job.After working with several psychiatrists and psychologists, I came to understand I was experiencing what is called “complex grief”.PTSD often is a component of complex grieving. I finally discovered a psychologist who specializes in treating PTSD using a technique called “EMDR” which involves re-experiencing traumatic events in ones life and “reprocessing” them rationally and clearly. Almost by definition, the EMDR process is very emotional, can be painful and is time consuming.After several EMDR sessions and very emotional work, I realized the combination of life long events above lead me to believe I was such a failure, in my mind, I believed I was not only responsible for the death of my ex-wife, but that I believed I had essentially MURDERED my ex-wife.This situation, from my youth to the aftermath of the death of my ex-wife, has been a series of failures that built on one another. The death of my ex-wife was a culmination point of a series of traumas.I no longer struggle as much with feeling failure, as the EMDR treatments have helped me tremendously. I now recognize that I am not God. I did not murder my ex-wife. In fact, I never stopped loving her in my own crippled way.Throughout this, I’ve become very close with my daughter, but I still ask “at what cost?”Again, I apologize for the length.
