column1: What is your review of Mary Poppins Returns (2018 movie)?
column3: WARNING: Spoilers for Mary Poppins Returns I was really looking forward to Mary Poppins Returns. I’ve got a lot of nostalgic affection for the original 1964 film – even more so after watching Saving Mr Banks, far better than the pitch would suggest (it’s basically a massive studio making a film about how awesome another one of its films is!). You can’t argue with the pedigree of the talent involved, on both sides of the camera. And the early clips looked great. What we got was… okay, I guess. It probably shouldn’t go without saying, but it very often does, that the film looks fantastic. Robert Stevenson’s original is strikingly effortless in its creation of magical effects, with no computer generated imagery available (although Disney did have better blue-screen than anyone else, thanks to Petro Vlahos’s sodium vapor process which other technicians at rival studios had been unable to replicate). Rob Marshall’s follow-up keeps the same easy and unfussy integration of magical elements into a believable, but storybook world and Dion Beebe’s photography smartly keeps a ceiling on the brightness until the world explodes into colour and light towards the end. And if the new songs by Scott Wittman and Marc Shaiman aren’t quite in the league of those by the Sherman Brothers, they’re tuneful enough and they get the job done. But from fairly early on, a lot of elements don’t seem quite right. We are (re)introduced to the Banks children, now grown up and played by Ben Wishaw and Emily Mortimer. Wishaw’s Michael is living in his childhood home on Cherrytree Lane and now has three children of his own, and all four are mourning the death of their mother. Aunt Jane (Mortimer) is staying with them and in a needlessly chaotic scene we gather that the plumbing needs seeing to, the groceries need to be got, the house is being repossessed and the kids, especially Annabel are really running the show. They’re certainly more practical help than housekeeper Ellen (Julie Walters, taking over from Hermione Baddeley). Lo, while flying Michael’s old kite, Mary Poppins appears and with a bit of help from lamplighter Jack (Lin-Manuel Miranda), they descend into a cartoon world inside a china bowl, pay a call on Poppins’ cousin Topsy (a delightful Meryl Streep) and save the house from the clutches of the bank. In outline, I suppose, this all sounds fine. But, rather like Star Wars: The Force Awakens, the new film treats the original less like a springboard from which to find new ideas, but rather as a template to be followed closely. So just like in 1964, we get a magical tidying up, followed by a journey to a cartoon world, followed by adventures with an eccentric friend of Poppins’ up on the ceiling, then a trip to the bank which goes wrong, rescue by Bert/Jack and his gang of workers, then a resolution at the bank, followed by aerial delights with the whole family in the park while Poppins slips away. But while the structure is followed rigidly, it seems as if writers Marshall, David Magee and John DeLuca are working from a half-remembered version of the original, in which Dick van Dyke plays a chimney sweep (he has a different job in each section of the film), in which Mary Poppins repeatedly transports the children to magical lands (this only happens once) and in which fantastic sequences end with the children waking up as if from a dream (this never happens). In fact, as the cameos from familiar faces start piling up, this begins to feel less like From Russia With Love and more like Operation Kid Brother. But the original film is also smart and subtle enough to realise that while the source books feel very episodic, movie audiences of all ages need a bit more connecting tissue. So, every episode contributes in some way to the rehabilitation of George Banks. Motifs like “a spoonful of sugar” and “supercalifragilisticexpialidocious” are all part of his journey back to his family and the least well-remembered sequence (Ed Wynn on the ceiling) is the cornerstone of this process. Here, nothing in the underwater “Can You Imagine That” sequence is ever referred to again, and it’s questionable whether we needed either “Turning Turtle” or “Trip A Little Light Fantastic” either. And if it sounds like I’m criticising the film when it copies the original and criticising it again when it doesn’t – well, I suppose I am, but that’s the problem that sequels are often faced with, especially sequels to beloved films which are a very long time in coming. And it’s not particularly a point in the new film’s favour that a lot of the new sequences are drawn from PL Travers’ writing either. Who the hell actually read the books? (Actually I read the first four avidly as a child, but that’s not the point.) No, here’s the real problem with this film. What’s it actually about? As I’ve said, it was the Sherman Brothers and producer Don Da Gradi’s inspiration that the golden thread uniting all of the elements of their story was that Mary Poppins had arrived not to straighten out unruly kids, but to save their father from himself. What is Mary Poppins’ mission this time round? Well, at first it seems as if the natural order of things has been reversed. The kids are having to parent their father (Annabel at least). Is this the problem that supernanny is here to solve? Well, Georgie, the youngest, doesn’t suffer this affliction and when she’s done summoning a plumber (who never arrives) and setting off for groceries (which she never buys), Annabel just basically becomes a child again and so does her twin brother John. Wishaw seems a bit absent-minded, but it’s not clear whether this is brought on by grief or whether it’s a character flaw. Either way, it wouldn’t work for Mary Poppins to make him more organised and rigid, and she clearly isn’t going to bring his wife back from the dead (can you imagine!?), so he isn’t the problem either. And Emily Mortimer’s Jane seems pretty self-reliant and together throughout. The film hints that she might need a man to be whole, but never quite sets off down that rather parochial path. One interesting thread which is presented is that as they recollect their time with Mary Poppins, the adult Michael and Jane have rewritten their memories, and now believe that their magical adventures were nothing but an overactive imagination. They conclude this in the foreground, as Emily Blunt sails up the bannisters behind them, in what is possible the best shot in the entire film. But they both feel the same way, which is dramatically inert, and they don’t really alter this point of view over the course of the story. At the climax, when the whole family is soaring through the sky, buoyed aloft by Angela Lansbury’s balloons, Lansbury lumpenly spells it out for us – the adults won’t remember this the next day. No change. No growth. No transformation. No point. In other words, Mary Poppins isn’t doing anyone any good by being there. She’s a fun source of magical adventures, but that isn’t a story. Disney realised that in 1964. Why has no-one clocked it this time round? Absent a needed emotional transformation of a family member, what does drive the plot of the new film? An achingly tedious find-the-McGuffin routine, over-familiar from countless other films before it, allied with an even more over-familiar race-against-time device. This requires the presence of something which the first film had no need of: a bad actor; a villainous character who is actively and purposefully seeking to cause the Banks family harm for his own personal gain. It was during the otherwise lovely Royal Doulton Bowl sequence, with its wonderfully nostalgic hand-drawn animation that I began to feel as if something was badly wrong. Why are the Banks children in mortal danger? Why is a bad guy rubbing his hands with glee? Why does the sequence not end properly? What the hell is going on? And Colin Firth is required to jump through any number of nonsensical plot hoops to make all this work. He gives Wishaw a job, even though he wants him to default on the loan. He voluntarily stays at the bank till midnight, even though he could go home at 5:00pm and guarantee that his scheme succeeds. He allows himself to be suckered in by the incredibly lame device of Miranda and co turning back the hands of Big Ben so that the deadline can be extended (a literal race-against-time, yawn) and then every single action anyone has taken in the last half hour is rendered moot by the Deus Ex Van Dyke at the end. Without Indy, the Nazis would probably still have found the Ark eventually, but at least because he was there, it ends up safe in the hands of the American government, who have the wisdom not to try and weaponise it. Without Mary Poppins’s return… I don’t know. Everything is exactly the same, I guess. Because she’s there to give the kids adventures, but the plot revolves around a bank loan. The pieces don’t mesh, and I don’t feel anything when I watch it. The nearest I got to being moved was when the kids sing The Place Where Lost Things Go to their dad, who realises that they’ve been parenting him. Yes. Briefly. Before Mary Poppins showed up. But this epiphany doesn’t actually change Wishaw’s behaviour in any way, so – again – what’s the point of it? And it doesn’t help that this is the latest in a too-long line of supposedly insightful bon mots which attempt to recapture the simple truth of “A spoonful of sugar” but none of them quite make the grade. Different point of view.” “If it makes no sense it can’t be true.” “A cover is not the book.” And most vacantly of all “You can’t lose what you’ve never lost.” Eh? Even the shot of Firth’s balloon sinking to the ground at the end, leaving him humiliated and earthbound just seems wrong to me. Mary Poppins is about taking crusty adults who have forgotten the elation of being childlike and giving them that joy back again. It’s not about sorting adults into winners and losers and then laughing cruelly at the losers. Ugh. One of many reasons why the 1964 film works so well is that its makers were in no way in awe of the books. They disregarded PL Travers every chance they got, in order to put their vision of Mary Poppins on screen. As Saving Mr Banks tells us, they then had to defend and fight for every single one of those changes, which is perhaps why the final film feels so perfectly balanced. The new film has been made by people whose reverence for the original seems overwhelming, and yet at the same time, who didn’t really understand it at all. It’s a cargo-cult version of the original, with a smashing cast, decent songs, a good sense of fun and some eye-popping visuals. But it has no engine and that’s why it can’t ever actually take off and fly.

column1: Which Attack on Titan character has suffered the most?
column3: An interesting question. Many people say it’s Eren, but look at it this way, he’s also the protagonist. We see everything and all the details of his suffering. I am in no way saying Eren hasn’t suffered. Since he was a young boy he saw the horror of his mother getting eaten in front of him. And many more tragedies in his teenage years. His young age and the lack of someone to teach him how to properly move forward, as Levi had with Erwin, makes it more difficult because he felt alone and had multiple feelings that he couldn't understand, leading him to make poor decisions and leave friends behind which in turn nearly brought the world into extinction and a sad ending for his friends. On the other hand, compared to Eren; we have not seen Levi’s past. The details of his life in the underground city, what it was like before and after his mother died. What it was like to be raised by Kenny and soon following his abandonment. Then of course, his life in the survey corps before the series takes place. You see? There are lots of pieces we don’t know about Levi. I’ll admit, Levi is the reason why I watch the show so I am going to go into deep thought about some speculations and ideas of what could have happened. Hope you enjoy it! INTRODUCTION His mother gave birth to him but she didn’t raise him for that long before she died of an unknown illness. He never knew his father, and he lived in poverty.Levi was just a kid when his mother died, what about his life before she died? Did he have to find food for the both of them, what kind of things did Levi see or do in that time? Kenny found him a while after his mothers death, he was alone, and starving to death. I’m sure before Kenny found him, Levi probably never slept, considering he was starving that would leave him with malnutrition which causes A LOT of problems within the body. (I’m thinking about real life kind of health here. That includes things such as the list below that affects the body. Sleep deficiency, starvation, thirst, lack of proper foods and nutrients are required to allow growth, brain function, mental and emotional health. All of these things would be affected from his childhood. Which explains why he’s so short as an adult. His body was permanently affected by lack of food so he’s so short compared to all the other characters no matter how much more he grows, it wouldn’t have made him taller than them. At least we know Kenny wasn’t one of those kinds of relatives that was abusive towards him. Since it shows Levi visibly confused/hurt on him leaving without a word. Not to mention the, Why … Why did you leave me? He cared about Kenny as the last family member he knew. I’m sure when he left, Levi felt some kind of abandonment. Wondering if he had done something wrong to be left behind. So, Kenny’s leave when he was still a kid clearly affected him for a long time since he asked,Now the question is, how difficult did his life get after Kenny left? He had to raise himself, get money, and learn how to keep himself alive. (Luckily that shouldn’t have been too hard with his training and Ackerman blood). In the OVA, no regrets, it was shown that he had others relying on him for money and perhaps other things (who knows). He could have made other friends before Furlan and Isabel. There could have been more people he knew that could have died from illness, starvation, and so on. (I understand I’m overthinking this. But, it’s what I do when there’s so many theories and speculations). We just don’t know what else happened during the rest of his time there. Life in the underground city was not an easy life. Basically, it was survival of the fittest down there. Kill or be killed. Medicine was not an option, food was scarce, first aid was probably hard to come by, people were cruel. Pretty sure Levi had to do some crazy stuff to become a notorious criminal as he was in No Regrets. He could have had some thoughts about: Why am I still here? Will I ever go up to the surface? Will I see Kenny ever again, is he dead? Or does he even care about me? Things like that I guess. In his OVA, he had two best friends. Isabel and Furlan. He grew to genuinely care about them. Isabel was a sweet girl who considered him her older brother. Furlan was a friend of Levi’s before he met Isabel so I’m sure how close they were. They were both important to Levi, and were the first friends he trusted and depended on.He wanted to keep them safe but unfortunately, their deaths happened because Levi trusted them to be safe while he went out and killed Erwin. He let his pride get the best of him and blind his eyes for what was more important in that moment, his friend's safety or killing Erwin. His reaction to seeing dead bodies of the soldiers in the fog slowly made him realize his friends were in danger. But when he arrived, he was too late.Their deaths clearly affected him (as we saw when he brutally killed the titan responsible for killing them). His subsequent encounter with Erwin was heartbreaking because he was shown the fake document and realized his best friends had died for nothing. His plan failed, and they were gone. Fortunately, and unlike Eren, he had Erwin tell him not to regret it or else his future choices would be influenced by his doubts. Levi permanently joined the Survey corps afterwards, choosing to move forward his own way. He went on many many more expeditions outside the walls. How many more friends did he make? We're not sure if he made more than one squad during those years before the series takes place, or how many friend’s deaths he had to witness being eaten by the titans. But we are sure he saw many more tragedies and losses of the comrads he knew. So much so, that he grew numb from expressing his emotions. By the beginning of the series, he is unable to openly express his emotions through tears or facial expressions of regret. (Although, if you pay attention you can actually see that his comrades dying does affect him. He just handled it in a way that made it seem like he wasn’t bothered much by it). From what I've heard, some thought he was an emotionless captain who was only concerned with the mission. But that's not true; he's simply witnessed an infinite number of deaths, and his reactions to witnessing the deaths of his men make him appear heartless. But if you pay attention to his character, you'll notice that he's far from heartless; in fact, he's quite emotional. It's just that, unlike the other characters, he is able to move past his pain due to a life filled with it, but he’s able to move on in order to progress. Season 1: He loses his entire special operations squad to the female titan. No matter how you look at it, he was angry/sad for their deaths. He couldn’t make it in time to save them and arrived to see them dead. These were his friends that he cared about, that he chose for a team! But he was able to pull himself together and go after Annie in order to rescue Eren and save Mikasa’s life; in spite of his friends' deaths. In season three, he sees his uncle Kenny again after all these years; they fight a couple of times and it ends, his uncle dies right in front of him, his last family member; gone. Levi got the answer to his long waited question of Why … Why did you leave me? Kenny answered him saying he wasn’t fit to be anyone’s parent. What if Levi already thought of him as his parent? Making the abandonment really feel like it was his fault when he was a kid. Tears man! It was just so sad that it was their final conversation.In the mission to retake Wall Maria; Erwin was planning on fighting. He’s only got one arm and he plans to fight. In the scene we see Levi trying to convince him to stay where he is and lead the survey corps from his desk. It’s easy to see the desperation Levi says through his words and tone of voice that he really doesn’t want Erwin to die out there. To a great deal that he threatens to break his legs. In case nobody realized, that’s how Levi expresses to those cares about. The, “I'll break your legs” was him saying I don’t want you to die! Erwin is like what Eren is to Mikasa. Levi greatly cares about Erwin; as the only person he can truly put his trust into time and time again. But in that moment, he put his own feelings aside for Erwin’s dream to know the truth about the world. And he carried out his orders to the very end, knowing Erwin is going to die.The following episodes display a level of emotions rarely seen in Levi. Schock, anger, sadness, desperation, grief. He watched Zeke kill the majority of the survey corps and sacrifice their lives so Levi could get close to Zeke and kill him.The picture above was an awakening to me that he really was devastated how fast hundreds of soldiers and Erwin were getting wiped out. He might as well have been feeling an incredibly painful jarring shock as he watched everything unfold before his eyes. Yet … He still did what he was told to do. He snuck up, took out the titans guarding Zeke, and ambushed him; fury and all. The dub does a fantastic job at letting us hear just how angry he was in that moment. He fought Zeke furiously and nearly killed him. Zeke made a run for it but Levi, upset over the death of Erwin and hundreds of soldiers, chased him down, refusing to let go of the promise he made to Erwin. He later returned, and looked at Erwin’s dead body. Exhausted from the fighting and the grief of losing his best friend, he knew he had one last chance to save his dear friend, and whether he showed it or not, there were certainly several feelings running through his head about who to save while Mikasa and Eren argued about Armin being the one to save. Remember Isabel, Furlan, and his squad? He wasn’t able to save them; only to arrive and see their dead bodies. This is the first time Levi has a chance to save his friend. But no, he remembers what Erwin desired above all else and that’s when he decided to choose to save Armin instead. He knew after all that Erwin went through, he deserved rest. I can’t imagine what it was like for him to think at that moment that he has to let go of the ONE CHANCE he’s ever had to save the life of his friend.Consider Levi's thoughts here! He wanted to save Erwin more than anything else, but he kept his cool regardless of the current situation and made his decision, even though it wasn't the one he wanted to make. Season 4 part 1: Zeke betrayed him and titanized all 30 of his comrades. There were only two options: die at the hands of his titanized comrades or kill them. He had no choice but to kill them all in order to capture Zeke. Levi has lost countless of fellow comrades, his closest friends, and the only family he ever knew. And now he was faced with killing all 30 of his comrades. AN IMPOSSIBLE CHOICE. There is no one in the series other than Erwin that would be able to toss feelings aside, for the sake of surviving.Prior to that, he had doubts about the numerous times he had saved Eren's life, only to result in the deaths of more of his comrades. All of this, only for Eren to turn evil, Sasha’s death on the airship, and set off the rumbling that kills Hange and 80% of humanity. He is the last surviving veteran who ends up physically and emotionally broken for the rest of his life. This probably isn’t considered much of an important death to most but, his horse that he’s had since the very beginning dies in the thunder spear explosion. I have no idea how he felt about it, but bits and pieces of the series showed he did like his horse, so that’s sad. Many instances Levi expressed sadness over losing soldiers under his watch as he shows with Hange. He wasn’t able to save them.Throughout the whole show, Eren still had people who cared about him in season four. He even had the yeagerists (a devoted army of former soldiers and others. Not that I'm officially counting that). Those same individuals attempted to kill Levi after the thunder spear explosion. Mikasa was completely devoted to him due to her love for him. Armin was his best friend. Connie and Jean were still concerned about him and thought of him as a friend. Eren lost everything because he saw no hope for the future, so he pushed everyone away and devised a plan that would result in more deaths and sadness for his friends. (Not that i’m blaming only him for his foolish actions, I’m not sure what was going through his head at that time but he was definitely having personal struggles). Levi, on the other hand, has lost everything: eyesite in his left eye, two missing fingers, an injured leg, and a scarred face. He lost everything important to him because he wanted to fight for the safety of humanity and the protection of his friends. NOTHING MORE. Remember what he said to Erwin: “Great. Perfect. I’ve spent all this time, all this energy”. (Granted that was his shock over learning that titans are humans) BUT .. He’s spent all that time and energy killing titans. The end result of it all was the death of everything he knew throughout his life!Levi, in my opinion, had experienced an enormous amount of loss and grief his entire life. Beginning to end. That’s not to say that other characters have not suffered. Attack on Titan is a tragic anime with numerous tragedies, horrible deaths, and sad backstories. However, Levi appears to be the most broken on the inside than anyone else. His story was dreadfully filled with an endless amount of death he had seen. There is no doubt in my mind that no character could go through what Levi went through and still maintain their sanity, strength, and hope the way he handled it. He had to kill his own comrades and witness their deaths on several different occasions. But he kept fighting, even after being seriously injured, and was there for the others during the final battle. But his ending was the saddest. We saw Hange reunite with everyone, but not him. He shed a tear when he saw them, and then... the last we saw of him was passing out candy (or manga ending: with Gabi and Falco). The best ending for a character who has been through as much horror as he faced, he should have been with everyone he has lost. His mother, Kenny, Erwin, Isabel, Furlan, Hange, his squads, and Mike. A sad ending for a broken character. ANYWAYS: I’ll admit I had a problem with his ending. The ideal kind of ending I was thinking of that would have actually made me appreciate his conclusion would have been in a happy afterlife with LITERALLY EVERYONE special he ever lost. And them all being happy with all the time in the world to talk. Nothing to worry about, just happiness. Hope you enjoyed this, if not, it’s fine. I know I go crazy with these kinds of explanations but I liked writing this. I wasn’t able to write out everything that makes Levi such a broken character because this guy’s level of complexity and depth is really hard to write! But, I think I got the gist of it down. Thanks for reading. BAM! HAVE A GREAT DAY!

column1: How can I overcome a family loss (my grandmother)?
column3: This too happen for me 3 years back. My grandmother departed 3 years back. It's difficult for me to think of my home withour her at initial days. As days passed I habitated without her presenceShe is one of my dearest person in my family and I'm also her favourite grandchild. When i was kid I supposed to stay with her more than my mother. Sometimes we quarrel, sometimes we love each other and sometimes with stand for eachother. At the end of the day we will be with each other. I remember her everywhere Like…. She is very good at preparing some recipes, pickles and also different types of powders( edible powders)( Image from Google). I still remember her when a pickle bottle comes in front of me. Sometimes she use to prepare a home medicine(vasantham) for me when I'm suffering with cold/ cough She is the first person who care me more, other than my mom. She always wants to take care me and during meals time she definitely asks me “Had your meal?” “Wash your hand and feet"— when i come from outside. “ Study well"— when I'm leaving to school. “Be careful”— when i go to agriculture field with her. Most of the time she made me to a deciplined person. She never allowed me to ride a bike/ bicycle. Because she still thinks me as a kid. On 25 nov 2018 she departed from us. The same day I turn into adult and then no one tried to care me. I experienced depression for somedays. But later I moved away from it by focusing on studies. I still remember her while taking my meal and also when i come to home from outside. And the happiest part is I have so many memories with her. There is a movie in telugu “Oh Baby". While watching this movie i lossed control emotionally. But no one is with me to share my emotions. But now I'm completely okay after 3 years. I get smile on my face when i remember her.( My granny on my first birthday). This is all because I have somany memories with her from childhood. Finally, it's difficult to lead life without there presence. But, it's easy to hold there memories.Keep there memories with you till you turn grandmother/grandfather 😊

column1: Why are Harry and Meghan the only royals not to see a boost in popularity after Prince Philip's funeral?
column3: In the U.K. there has been a very trying time for the last 24+ months with everyone suffering from the restrictions that the government has introduced to fight the virus. The prime minister has been hospitalised; members of the royal family have been following the restrictions imposed, when they have made public appearances it has been at times when the country was allowed to , or they used remote video conferencing to carry out there job of bolstering morale to the population, the Queen even made a special broadcast to the nation, which is a very rare event , I think only the third or sixth time in her nearly 70 year reign, excluding the regular Christmas Day broadcast. She and some other royals have been seen to be following the same restrictions as everyone else, even Prince Charles was a victim to the virus and recovered. The senior royals have suffered with the nation they serve. on the other hand there is the royal couple who have stepped back from their duties, seeking to be independent from the role of the royal family, and reportedly not wanting the publicity that the active members of the royal family get while engaged in duties representing the Queen. They have made inconsistent statements during the pandemic, while seeking publicity to further their aims, it is sen from a British perspective as seeking publicity from afar and commenting on events they have not been part of, they moved out of the country, a decision they made freely by themselves. They were given support for 12 months to let them reflect on what they wanted to do in the future, which was to progress along a different path to other senior royals; there are several minor senior royals, who have progressed along similar paths, carrying out jobs to fund their lifestyles they have chosen, sometimes catching the odd headline when carrying out a public engagement. The decision by Harry and Meghan is not one that is unique in the extended family. But they made it known before the end of the 12 month period they would not be returning as members of the small group of working royals, supporting the monarch in her duties. Again several other members of the royal family have made and followed similar decisions. What those members have not done is aired their grievances in public in an attempt to gather popularity and keep their names in the press. They complain that they not have to pay for their own security, well they stepped away from their duties, it has been estimated that each of them are very wealthy perhaps multimillionaires, yet they want others to pay fir their lifestyles, they complain of events that happened 3–4 years ago as though they were very recent, while one of the senior members of the family is in hospital having been admitted due to issues with his health, as 99 year olds are prone to have, which then resulted in heart surgery, st that time when the nation was hoping he might be strong enough to recovery, but deep down knew it would not be long before he lost the final battle ; AT THAT TIME they mounted their attack on the royal family, the Church of England and insulted the people of the U.K. and those nations that have the Queen as their head of state ( some 15 separate commonwealth nations). Their public image was more important than the grief of the royal family, so they chose to inform the world of their complaints, which now go against all reports of events when they happened. Their was a false and very low key announcement after the broadcast that Harry did not mean to be disrespectful to his grandparents. Which has since been followed up by an attack on his father and his grandparents, and new revelations that from his ‘new’ recollections they were bad examples of parenting. He has an older brother who has experienced the same early trauma of losing their mother in horrendous circumstances, Mandy other families have experienced a tragic death of a mother who has young children, the families have supported those grieving from the loss, the royal family has been the same as all those families in similar situations. Yet Harry is somehow unique in the world? Following his views, could his taking up a new role involving mental health charity have any bearing in his interview contents and timing, he is continuing his narrative of being a victim, a recent programme has been aired on British television where Harry’s relationship with his father was explored using archived footage of their interactions, which shows that Prince Charles did change his behaviour after the death of his first wife towards his children. But there is no manual on how to be a perfect parent as many will know, Prince Charles was trying to do his best as a single parent whilst being a focus of media attention, he had a far harsher childhood and had tried to not make that mistake with his children. The British public see that it succeeded in the case of Prince William and his family. They accept the roles and are moulding them as they wish, to suit them. Prince Harry on the other hand while publicly announcing nearly every other interaction he might have had with his family has only complained that his father cut off his allowance and would not take his calls. After the Oprah interview there are rumours that Prince Harry write a personal letter to his father, but that content is still private, as it should be. Prince Harry did manage to return for his grandfathers funeral and observed the abbreviated quarantine that was allowed with testing to make his appearance. But he returned to his family in the USA the day before his grandmother’s 95 birthday, while she was still in official mourning. Now he is back in America he is continuing his attack on his family. His blame culture extends to his grand parents and father, but surprisingly there is no admission that he or his wife have erred at all , always someone else is at fault.

column1: What episode or episodes best describe Meredith Grey’s character development?
column3: OBVIOUS SPOILER ALERT, SEASONS 1–14! Oh, there were many episodes that defined Meredith as a complex character- and more than the cute girl she was first believed to be in the very beginning. Obviously I can’t nail them all, but here are some of the most memorable that comes to my head right now (I might add more later):Into You Like a Train (Season 2, Episode 6) Meredith drunkenly awaits Derek to show up at the bar announcing that he’s leaving Addison, when an actual trainwreck puts everything in another perspective. While the most emotional and memorable part of the episodes is naturally the strangers stabbed together by a pole (I only remember the name of the woman, Bonnie…), this episode also gave us one of the show’s most famous lines: “Choose me. Pick me. Love me”. Meredith literally begs for Derek to return her love but out of duty he cannot leave Addison (yet). When the doctors decide to leave Bonnie and focus on saving the other guy, and Meredith keeps trying to save her yelling “you can’t just leave her!”, it’s not only a tragic situation but also a clear analogy to herself and how she feels. BUT let’s take it even a step further: Meredith’s father Thatcher has left her and her mother Ellis when she was a little girl, and she was essensially left alone as Ellis stopped being lucid and became amnesiac (after a lifetime of giving her hell). Meredith has serious abandonment issues REGARDLESS of McDreamy. And things are just getting started…It’s the End of the World… As We Know It (Season 2, Episodes 16–17) Also known as “The Bomb Episode”, this is arguably the first indication that the show could sometimes go batshit crazy with insane disasters and circumstances, and back then whenever a character was caught in the crossfire it was intense. When Hannah the paramedic pulled her hand from the wound and ran away, we were shocked to find Meredith in her place- touching the bomb. At the time we mostly saw it as an excuse for Derek to reflect on his feelings for her, but it was actually an indication of two major characteristics of Meredith: 1) her dangerous dance with death (much later revealing suicidal tendencies that gives clue to her past); and 2) her nobility and willingness to sacrifice to save other people’s lives (which will repeat many times in the series). The interesting thing about it is, at the time we didn’t realize all this- only the gradual exploration of the character would shed another light on this event in retrospect.Walk On Water / Drowning On Dry Land / Some Kind of Miracle (Season 3, Episodes 15–16–17) These three episodes puts several characters on the edge, but Meredith even slipped over it (literally). The first episode of the trilogy begins as Meredith actually seems to be attempting suicide in a bathtub and Derek pulls her out of the water, so we just KNOW dark days are ahead. In a symmetrical move, that same episode ends with Meredith (trying to save a dying man who won’t stop moving while a lost little girl stands by) falling in the water. In the following episode we see Meredith fighting at first, but then giving in. We realize just how damaged and broken she really is. Then Derek shows up and carries her out of the water like a modern-day-prince-charming. But even as she is brought to the hospital we understand there is still great risk to her life- throwing all the characters off guard- and the most interesting part is her temporary purgatory. She sees Denny, the Bomb Squad guy, Bonnie, that nurse who worked with her mother, and eventually, her mother Ellis herself (who meanwhile actually dies). There’s a poignant moment when Denny says to her: “Moments… that’s all we have”, and Meredith realizes she doesn’t want to die, she wants so much more; and purgatory-Ellis tells her what actual-Ellis never could: “you are anything but ordinary”. And in a miracle, she survives, and gets to hear of Cristina’s engagement and live on. In her mind she already knows her mother is dead, and she has made peace with it. This second chance in life is something that shapes Meredith a great deal, even if she still has many misteps and shenanygans later on, at a core level something has shifted. She even reflects on it in Season 14 when April’s life is in danger, realizing that despite all she went through over the years, everything after that near drowning was a gift.Losing My Mind (Season 4, Episode 15) While there is only one major scene in the episode I remember perfectly (I had to look for what season and episode it was!) it is nonetheless a HUGE reveal into Meredith’s past that explains so much about her AND Ellis. The long-forgotten arc when Meredith goes to therapy, brings her to face some of her inner demons: the shrink lists all her near-death experiences as proof for Meredith’s suicidal tendency. But at the end of the episode comes the real shocker- Ellis tried to commit suicide by slitting her wrist in front of Meredith who was a child. No wonder Meredith is so dark and twisted. This detail puts everything we think we knew into a whole new light, and now we know just how much Meredith had to deal with (and unfortunately WILL have to deal with). In a courageous move, Meredith tells her therapist: “So you think I’m broken? Fix me. Because I’m no quitter.”Now Or Never (Season 5, Episode 24) In what many people describe as the most suspenseful season finale of the show, two characters other than Meredith face near-death experiences (from which one dies). Meredith and Derek get married on a post it, since they can’t find the time to do it properly, but surprisingly that’s not the development I’m interested in. Meredith treats John Doe who was hit by a bus because he pushed a stranger out of the way, when suddenly he spells “007” on the palm of her hand and she realizes… it’s someone she knows. The shock and terror on Meredith’s face as she says “Oh god! Oh god!” is mindblowing, and then she sprints into the hall and screams: “IT’S GEROGE! IT’S GEORGE! JOHN DOE IS GEORGE!”. The development would only be felt in the next season following the aftermath of George’s death… Meredith (and everyone) should ceize the day, say what they feel and not wait around, ’cause there might be no tomorrow. Meredith has since managed to make herself a brilliant surgeon, surround herself with a bunch of good friends (even after Izzie and Cristina left), create a wonderful family with Derek and despite all her tragedies, collect perfect moments with loved ones. Here’s the brilliant voice-over:“Did you say it? 'I love you. I don't ever wanna live without you. You changed my life.' Did you say it? Make a plan. Set a goal. Work toward it. But every now and then.. look around. Drink it in. 'Cause this is it. It might all be gone tomorrow.”Sanctuary / Death & All His Friends (Season 6, Episodes 23–24) These crazy episodes changed A LOT of characters, including Bailey, Cristina, Lexie, Derek and more- but for the sake of the question, Meredith loses something here that no other character has thus far. The mass shooting puts many people in awful situations and sees many characters selflessly sacrificing themselves to help their friends and loved ones. When Cristina operates on Derek who’s been shot, and the shooter walks into the OR with a gun, Meredith volunteers to die instead. But even as the day is saved (with many casualties) and Derek eventually lives, Meredith has apparently lost her unborn baby. While this event brings her closer to death again, this time it’s definitely not suicidal, but all out of love and putting other people’s lives ahead of her own. The loss she experiences here is more than physical, it is a loss of a promise to a future, her hopes, her dreams- and it shakes her to her core. She would repress her grief and not deal with it for a long time in the next season.Unaccompanied Minor (Season 7, Episode 22) Season 7 dealt a lot with the trauma and reprecussions of the shooting. It was no picnic for a lot of characters. Meredith in particular was strong for other people, not allowing herself to fully feel the pain and mourn the loss of her child, and she didn’t share it with Derek initially. As the season progresses, she slowly becomes ready to try and have a baby again, and due to fertility problems, that baby ends up being the gorgeous Zola which she and Derek adopts. However, following her cheating on the Alzheimer trial to save Adele, everybody is mad at her and she gets fired and Derek is furious with her, leaving the house to sleep on the roof (of the hospital I guess?), while she sleeps alone with Zola, and a pregnant Cristina downstairs. It’s a nightmare come true, and it’s also not a life-threatening ridiculous disaster this time, only good old fashioned drama. Her voice-over here perfectly sums up the idea:“There's a reason I said I'd be happy alone. It wasn't 'cause I thought I'd be happy alone. It was because I thought if I loved someone and then it fell apart, I might not make it. It's easier to be alone, because what if you learn that you need love and you don't have it? What if you like it and lean on it? What if you shape your life around it and then it falls apart? Can you even survive that kind of pain? Losing love is like organ damage. It's like dying. The only difference is death ends. This? It could go on forever.”What’s interesting is, Ellis Grey lost love (Richard) and never recovered, because she knew he didn’t choose her, and he’ll live to love Adele. And Meredith would eventually lose Derek to death, but never lose their love. So this could be one hell of a clue for what’s coming next.Flight (Season 8, Episode 24) + Going, Going, Gone (Season 9, Episode 1) Unusually, I will discuss two episodes from separate seasons together. These are a season finale and its followup, so it’s not that strange- and the reason I will treat them as one is simple: it is yet another disaster and its aftermath, this time one that takes double toll on Meredith. Not only did Lexie, her (first..) half sister die after a plane crash- but after returning to Seattle, Cristina has left to work in a faraway hospital. The things this lady goes through, the hardships she suffers, the people she loses, I swear… Do you remember when, in Season 2, after Izzie cut Denny’s Lvad wire Meredith said furiously (and very naively): “SHUT UP! No one is leaving, and no one is dying!” ?.. Well, it took her years, and seven hells of pain and anguish and trauma to realize: "It's not the same. Nothing is the same. Everyone is leaving and everyone is dying”. I bet not a whole lot of people made that connection, I wonder how long Shonda has planned this irony… Frankly, that sums up the entire show. So this far in her development, Meredith is far, far from the blushed girl from Season 1.Only Mama Knows (Season 11, Episode 4) Perhaps one of the best episodes in the entire series, one that doesn’t need a super-freak-accident or a super-complicated-love-triangle or a super-complex-surgery to deliver. This episode was all about Meredith’s past with Ellis. Who knew that all these years after her death, Ellis would be such an important character still? In the episode we finally learn the actual truth of why Richard didn’t leave Adele for Ellis: he was jealous of her winning the Harper-Avery Award and was afraid of a lifetime living in her shadow. The day at the carousel was the day he left her for good, and that’s also the night she attempted suicide. But the really big twist was, Ellis was PREGNANT WITH RICHARD’S CHILD. No wonder she drove Thatcher away… Now, after all these years, comes that “child”, in the form of the lovely Maggie. And all of a sudden, Meredith gets a do-over, some form of a bandaid after Lexie’s loss, and maybe a way to reevaluate her mother. One of the best quote in the entire series comes from Ellis in the first or second season, makes so much more sense now: “It’s a shame. It’s awful being a grown up. But the carousel never stops turning… You can’t get off”… Even after a nearby future event that supposedly should SHATTER the carousel altogether.. more on that right now-How to Save a Life + She’s Leaving Home + You’re My Home (Season 11, Episodes 21–23, 25) Well, this is probably the BIGGEST event in Meredith’s life, more prominent in its importance than any of her friends’, family members’ deaths or departures… The death of her husband, best friend, lover, father of her children, Derek, McDreamy, her knight in shiny armor, her one true love- the pillar that together with her held that show in the first place. The episode of his death was one of the most heartbreaking things I ever watched, and it even had a trip-down-memory-lane-montage of moments of them together that broke me to pieces. What made it even more powerful was comparing it with her dream from the Season 5 premiere when she dreamed he died- only to now realize this isn’t a dream. The following episodes show how the other characters react (stunned, obviously) and how Meredith copes the only she knows how to: she takes the kids and LEAVES. For awhile I was actually worried she’s going to leave the show (or that the show would end like this). Anyhow, eventually she does return, and by the season’s finale- she allows herself to be a little bit happy again, and dance. Like I said, the carousel never stops turning.I could probably go on and on about Meredith and her big moments (there sure are many more of those), but I think that’s enough to build her character and draw a line of her development. Meredith was a fragile, lonely, naive and sensitive girl, who went through a rough childhood to say the least. She then met the love of her life, found the job of her dreams, befriended people she’ll never forget, started a wonderful family, and went through unbearable pains and disasters that took away almost all of them. She has gone through so much, and with every stumble she arose a better and stronger person. Her current confident, forcible and smart self is unrecognizable next to the mumbling intern she used to be. I think she truly deserves to be the protagonist of the series and I love her more than I can express, I almost wish she was a real person (if that didn’t also mean all the SHIT would have to happen to her LOL!). I used to think Izzie was more interesting, but I now realize as good-intentioned as she was, she turned out to not be able to think of others before herself and just quit and left for good. I don’t know what Meredith’s finale fate would be, but whatever the outcome, the journey has been amazing. And as Cristina said wisely as her parting gift: “He’s (Derek) not the sun. YOU ARE.”

column1: How would you summarise your childhood in 3 words?
column3: I really can’t explain my childhood in 3 words but I can keep writing about those days endlessly. I was a trivial south Indian kid of the 1990’s and these are some of the most beautiful memories. Spending childhood days in a trivial village of South India being born in a family that renders immense affection is the most beautiful thing on the earth for me.And yes, I was such a happy 1990’s kid. Both of my parents were working and it was my Avva(maternal grandma),who took care of me like a princess.She was an epitome of love,care and affection. I am a 21 year old engineering graduate now.I turn on the alarm in my smartphone on most days,dismiss it regularly when it beeps and sleep till my mom shouts at me to get up.But in those days,I would always wake up hearing Malar Akka(person who resides near my Avva’s home) sweeping the front of her house with a handheld sweeper made from coconut tree fronds and pouring water on the floor. My Avva would be busy cooking.When I go out of my home to the street,there would be an adorable kolam(traditional rangolis drawn with white rock powder in South Indian homes) in front of everyone’s house.Women would be standing near the street tap,chatting,with colorful plastic pots and silver pots to fetch water.I would come back to look at the clock.I had not learnt how to calculate time from it.But the only thing I knew was that,whenever I came back after gazing at the kolams,the small hand of the clock would point to 6. My thatha(maternal grandpa) was an officer in the govt. education dept. of our state and he was my first teacher too.He,at first,taught me Ganapati mantra,which he made me to recite daily when we go to the main temple in our village.I actually loved going to temple along with my grandpa daily just because the priest there would give me a handful of sugar candy to eat.Thatha was my first inspiration in life.When I woke up,he would have left for his workplace because he had to travel for hours to reach there and would return at night.He always insisted on the proverb “Early to bed,early to rise”.Even now as a septuagenarian,he wakes up so early in the morning and actively does all the activities.A strong interest for poetry was inculcated in me by him because it was he who taught me the poems of many renowned poets and he made me to recite it on a regular basis. Going to school is the most horrible nightmare every kid has.I was no exception to it.I was in total grief when I was admitted in Holy Cross matriculation school which was located in the town nearby make me get used to schooling and to make me stop crying,my Thatha decided to send me to a govt. school in our village for a week which was just a few meters from our home.Crying all the way,I left for school with Mama(mom’s brother).On the first day,he took me to a nearby shop,got me two coffee bite toffees and promised me that he would pick me up from school before I finished eating those.But to his dismay,the toffees never consoled me. Pets are the best companion one could ever have.My Avva got me two colored chicks,one pink and the other green.Whenever I came back from school,I used to play with those.Days passed and chicks became my favorite that I always kept them by my side.I don’t know if it was because I was a girl,I was much fascinated by the pink colored chick.I thought it was cuter than the green one and sobbed when my mom told that they were artificially colored and it would go off when they grew up.One fine evening,I was playing with the chicks in the street. My pink chick ran to the end of the street,a dog came pouncing towards it and took it away.I bursted into tears and ran to my Avva. She said that the dog would have eaten it.I was inconsolable,wept all that night and even refused to look at my green chick fearing that it too would be taken away like this someday. We Indian girls yearn to have a very long hair when we are small.But once we grow up,we cut it short to look trendy.I too had that strong desire to have a long hair like my mom.But she didn’t like that.She always kept telling me that I would catch cold and suffer from fever if I had a long hair. Murugan, a dark and tall man with sharp eyes was the most sought barber in my village and it was my Mama’s duty to take me to him whenever my mom felt that my hair had grown. Murugan never bothered about my prettiness and after he cuts my hair,I would like as if I had tonsured just ten days back. To add to my sorrow,my cousin sister had a long hair and they said it was because she had been learning classical dance. On an auspicious day,all the women in my home were wearing flowers.I too took one of them,ran to my Avva to get it pinned to my hair. My mama who was standing nearby said that the only way I could wear flowers was by hammering a nail onto my head and keeping flowers around it.How frightening would it have been even to imagine! But I used to put a bath towel around my head and told everyone that I too had a long hair. Whenever I wanted to wear mehandi(paste made with maruthani leaves),I would rush to Banu Akka(one of our neighbor).She makes it ready very swiftly and puts beautiful designs on my hand.And I had no fear that it contained ammonia and some artificial substances that would ruin my skin as of now.Instead I knew that it was very healthy. The month of margazhi(December to mid January) was sacred for all hindus and special rituals will be performed in the temples right from early morning.My thatha said me to keep pullar(a ball made of cow dung) on the kolam in the front of our home.We all girls would decorate our pullar with flowers and argue about the best ones and beautiful ones among those. My Perima(mom’s sister) was the apple of my eye.Whenever she comes to my Avva’s home,she would bring me a beautiful rose from her garden and she puts forth a condition to give me that rose.The condition was that I should allow her to bite my arms(she loved doing so).I would hesitate at first but the love for that rose always provoked me to bear that pain. One thing which always induced my curiosity was the almirah in my Avva’s home.There was a big ladder,climbing which,the almirah could be reached.I would climb half the ladder and return back to the bottom because I feared that I would fall.But when my brother and my sister(Perima’s children) came home,they would help me to reach it.We three used to play with all the utensils kept there till our Avva yells at us to get down. No one restricted us from scribbling on the walls and we did it wherever it was possible.The biggest fun we had which makes my heart jump with joy even now was playing with tube water.Whenever the main tank of our home was full,some elder would make the three of us to stand in the portico and start splashing water on us with the tube(provided it is sunny).This was the way we took bath many times. Farming was the main occupation in our village.People grew crops like rice,paddy and millet,vegetables like tomato and lady’s finger.There were plantain farms and coconut farms everywhere around.They used the produce of their farms for their own purposes and also sold it to earn money. My favorite juice from those days was the water of tender coconut.We celebrated Pongal grandly as a tribute to the Sun God. To me,my Avva was an invaluable treasure. No one could ever care for me like her.Whenever I came back from school,she would hug me tightly and kiss me on my forehead and chin.She is no more with me but I could still feel her warmth.Wearing bhindis on forehead was our custom.I knew that my Avva had never went to school.But she followed a different and cute way of teaching me.She would look at my school book and would put the alphabets and numbers there as my bhindi.She used to make a sweet with roasted gram and sugar,the taste of which would never leave my tongue. But this care and love didn’t last for long. My Avva was becoming fragile day by day.The doctors said that she had less immunity power.She was admitted in a hospital and I had to stay with my mom and dad in city thereafter.One day,a major operation was being performed to my Avva and all my family members were waiting dreadfully in the hospital.I was unaware of what was happening actually and was busy watching how Magic Pop(a crackling candy) made sound inside my mouth.After a few days,my Avva became normal and was discharged from the hospital. January 13,2001,11:20 AM-It was Pongal holidays for me.We were getting ready to go to our hometown.Mom and dad were busy packing.The phone bell in our house rang and it was my grandpa who called us. My mom started weeping. My dad suddenly came to me to dress me up.I asked him what had happened and he told me that Avva has gone to God.But I didn’t understand what he told and just kept saying ‘no’ several times.And when we reached my Avva’s home,I was simply starring at her face without even realizing that I am losing the love of my life very soon. My friends used to tell me that it was interesting to hear love stories of their grandma and grandpa.I didn’t have a chance to hear such things.But two incidents made me realize the unconditional love they held for each other.Once my Mama made fun of my Avva telling her that my Thatha was missing,she instantly started crying like a child.It has been fourteen years since our Avva left us and recently I heard that my Thatha has constructed a hall in the main temple of our village named after my Avva.Yes,now I agree that true love never dies. Well,I got the idea of posting about my childhood after seeing my 2 year old niece who is either with an ipad or a smartphone round the clock and my 5 year old cousin brother who is available online most of the time.The kids of today are very much smarter but when they think of their childhood,would they have such evergreen memories as we have?.Not at all. I really pity that they're losing their childhood :(

column1: What are the backstories and abilities of every known Uzumaki clan member in Naruto/Boruto?
column3: -Ashina Uzumaki: Leader of the Uzumaki Clan during the founder of Konohagakure. He and his clan met Hashirama and the Senju Clan in order to deal with a gigantic beast which was on the loose. Using his prowess in fuinjutsu, he and the Uzumaki’s were able to seal the beast away once it was cornered.-Mito Uzumaki: Was a kunoichi who originated Uzushiogakure’s Uzumaki Clan. Mito became married to the Hashirama, the First Hokage, and would help Konohagakure flourish with him. After Hashirama gained control of Kurama after his battle with Madara, Mito used a sealing jutsu and sealed Kurama within herself, becoming the first jinchuuriki of the Kyuubi. The seal almost broke due to her giving birth to the one who would become one of Tsunade & Nawaki’s parents. Towards the final years of her life, it was decided that a new host for Kurama would have to be found. Kushina Uzumaki was selected for the role for her special chakra. Terrified by the idea of having been taken from her home to become a jinchūriki, Mito comforted Kushina, and told her that in order to counter the fox's hatred, she needed to fill herself with love. Some time after that, Kurama was extracted from Mito and sealed inside Kushina.-Kushina Uzumaki: Was a Konohagakure kunoichi who originated from Uzushiogakure’s Uzumaki Clan, Minato Namikaze’s wife, Naruto’s mother, and the second jinchuuriki of the Kyuubi. Born into the famed Uzumaki clan of Uzushiogakure, Kushina lived most of her youth being caught up in war, making her seek for a daily peace. At a young age she was sent to Konoha and enrolled in the Academy. Wanting to make a strong first impression, she proclaimed to her class that she would be the first female Hokage. The other kids laughed at her statement, and began calling her "Tomato" (トマト) because of her then-round face and fiery red hair. This prompted her to lash out and pummel the kids who teased her. This, in addition to her red hair flying wildly around her as she did so, earned her the nickname of Red Hot-Blooded Habanero. Kushina was eventually told why she had to leave her home of Uzushio and go to Konoha; because of her special chakra, she was to be the next jinchuuriki of the Kyuubi. Kushina was terrified by the idea, but she was comforted by the Nine-Tails' then-current jinchūriki, Mito Uzumaki. Before the transfer was performed, Mito advised Kushina that love was the only way to tame the Nine-Tails and overcome its hate. When she was 12 years old, Kushina - now a genin - was captured by Kumogakure who wanted to make use of her special chakra in order to gain control of the Kyuubi. As they escorted her to Kumo, she secretly plucked and left behind strands of her red hair to mark her trail in the hopes that someone would find her. Minato Namikaze, one of her former classmates that Kushina believed to be a wimp, was the only one to pick up on this. After rescuing her, he informed her that he had always admired her red hair. Since Minato proved himself to be anything but, accepted her, and liked the one thing she hated about herself, Kushina fell in love with him, now considering her red hair as the "red thread of fate" (運命の赤い糸, unmei no akai ito) that had brought them together. Ultimately, Minato's reciprocated feelings helped her with overcoming the Kyuubi. As she grew up, Kushina became renowned for her beauty and unique ninjutsu style including the sealing jutsu of her clan. At some point, Kushina married Minato. She was later present to witness her husband's reign as Fourth Hokage, being very excited for him when first learning of it. During her ten-month jinchūriki-influenced pregnancy, she was secretly kept guarded by Minato's top student, Kakashi Hatake under Minato’s order. Midway through the pregnancy, the expecting parents decided to name their unborn child “Naruto” after the main character of Jiraiya’s first book. When Jiraiya asked if they were sure about it, stating that it was a name he had just came up with whilst eating a bowl of ramen one day, Kushina said that it was a beautiful name. They even approved of Jiraiya to be Naruto's godfather. Kushina also hoped that her son and her best friend Mikoto Uchiha’s youngest son, Sasuke Uchiha, would become friends in the future. Because the seal keeping the Nine-Tails within Kushina's body would be at its weakest during childbirth, special arrangements were made. Kushina would leave the village in secret and give birth in a remote location. Minato would help maintain the seal and ANBU would guard the area. Soon after Naruto was born, however, they were found by a masked man (Obito Uchiha). Obito killed all of the Anbu, Biwako Sarutobi, Taji, and took the newborn baby Naruto hostage, threatening to kill him as well. Minato was able to take Naruto back, but this gave Obito the chance to escape with Kushina. Wishing to use the Nine-Tails to destroy Konoha, Obito released it from Kushina’s body. The vitality inherent to the Uzumaki clan allowed her to survive the extraction, though she was greatly weakened by the experience. The masked ninja tried to have the Nine-Tails finish Kushina off but she was saved by Minato and brought to Naruto, who she stayed with while Minato went to help in the village's defence. To stop the Nine-Tails' attack, Minato was forced to bring it to Kushina and Naruto's location, and both of them to its. While still weakened, Kushina used her diminished chakra to restrain the Nine-Tails. Despite fearing the trauma would kill her in her current state, Kushina volunteered to have the Nine-Tails sealed back into her body so that it would die with her. Willing to sacrifice herself for Minato and Naruto; her thanks to them for giving her such a happy life. Minato suggested using the Reaper Death Seal on the Nine-Tails and sealing it into Naruto instead, choosing to believe in him as his father. As this would also mean Minato's death, and consequently give Naruto a horrible and lonely life, Kushina naturally objected. Minato, while understanding her concerns, convinced her that it was for the best because he believes in Naruto, and that doing this would also allow Kushina to see Naruto when he was older. After Minato sealed the Yin half of the Nine-Tails' chakra inside himself, the demon shrunk significantly, losing the chains. Realising the Hokage's intentions, the weakened Nine-Tails tried to kill Naruto, but both Minato and Kushina used their bodies to shield him. As Minato performed the sealing, and already at the point of death, Kushina told Naruto how much she loved him and gave him her best advice for the future; her final act in this world was to fill her son with as much of her love as possible. Minato then sealed the rest of their remaining chakra into Naruto. In the anime, before dying, the Third Hokage appeared. Kushina told Hiruzen the child's name and begged the elder to protect Naruto, dying shortly afterwards. Kushina would later reappear years later when Naruto was trying to finally tame Kurama and get him to work together with him.-Nagato: A former shinobi of the Rain Village and Uzumaki descendant. Forming Akatsuki with his friends and fellow war orphans, Yahiko and Konan, Nagato dreamed of bringing peace to the violent shinobi world. However, following Yahiko's death, Nagato adopted the alias of Pain and, along with Konan, began leading a new Akatsuki; one that would force the world into peace using any means necessary. Nagato lived with his parents on the outskirts of the Rain Village and when he was very young, an elderly Madara Uchiha secretly transplanted the Rinnegan into Nagato. During the 2nd Ninja War, Nagato and his parents took shelter in their home to avoid the fighting going on around them. One day, two Konoha shinobi broke into their home looking for food and Nagato and his parents tried to sneak out unnoticed. When they were discovered, his parents attacked the shinobi so that Nagato could escape. The Konoha ninja killed his parents in self-defence and, upon realising they were only civilians, tried apologising to Nagato. Overcome with grief, Nagato used Madara's Rinnegan for the first time to kill them and avenge his parents. After burying his parents

column1: In the Batman franchise, why are so many of the Rogues' Gallery regularly locked up in Arkham Asylum?
column3: bane: Bane is an escaped convict from an island prison in South America and a super-villain/assassin. Bane has abnormal physical strength as a result of having undergone experiments involving a derivative of the drug Venom. He became known as "The Man Who Broke the Bat" when he broke batmans back, forcing Bruce Wayne to give up the Batman persona while he recuperated. bane likely has schizoid personality disorder + drug addiction (venom) and most likely anger issues schizoid personality disorder: Schizoid personality disorder is an uncommon condition in which people avoid social activities and consistently shy away from interaction with others. They also have a limited range of emotional expression. Causes: What causes the development of schizoid personality disorder is unknown, although a combination of genetic and environmental factors, particularly in early childhood, may play a role in developing the disorder. Treatment: psychotherapy/group therapy/medications can be used to lessen the affects of schizoide personality disorder. drug addiction: Drug addiction, also called substance use disorder, is a disease that affects a person's brain and behavior and leads to an inability to control the use of a legal or illegal drug or medication. Substances such as alcohol, marijuana and nicotine also are considered drugs. causes:history of addiction. Drug addiction is more common in some families and likely involves genetic predisposition. ...Mental health disorderPeer pressureLack of family involvementEarly useTaking a highly addictive drug (the main reason as to why bane uses venom)Treatment: rehab. anger issues: you may have anger issues if: you feel angry often. you feel that your anger seems out of control. your anger is impacting your relationships. your anger is hurting others. causes: There are many common triggers for anger, such as losing your patience, feeling as if your opinion or efforts aren't appreciated, and injustice. Other causes of anger include memories of traumatic or enraging events and worrying about personal problems. treatments: anger management as-well as therapy clay-face/basil karlo: Basil Karlo, the original Clayface, was an actor who was driven mad when he heard of a remake of the classic horror film he had starred in, Dread Castle, and that he wouldn't be in the leading role. Adopting the persona of "Clayface", the villain of one of his old films, he became a serial killer targeting the cast and crew. He was eventually stopped by Batman and Robin.Later versions of the character reimagined him as being transformed into a behemoth of shapeshifting, clay-like flesh.
