column1: How was Theodore Roosevelt able to rise up and overcome adversity in his life despite all the tragedies and illnesses he suffered as a child?
column3: It’s a study in grief, is what it is. Leave his later life aside, and not indulging in psychological profiling to explain politics, the simplest facts about his childhood and early manhood are kinda probative for what molded TR’s grown character: TR was a sickly child who got the best care not only from rich, doting parents but also from a huge network of relatives. He was part of a vast extended family, even confined to the Oyster Bay Roosevelts, all founded on huge holdings in the center of Manhattan pioneered by Claes two centuries prior. (A solid choice of ancestor by our 26th President.) Excepting only his individual health, about as secure as life gets. Yet he very early got a vivid sense of the world beyond his home, in the starkest way: his dad was trying to kill his mom’s brothers. His father (TR, Sr.) was the epitome of old money in NYC, a powerful pro-Union patriot in a city that wasn’t unanimous about either the Union or abolition. Theodore Senior raised huge amounts of money for the Cause. But he didn’t fight. Like most at his level, he indulged in an ancient (and about to be outlawed) practice — he hired a soldier to take his place. (My great grandfather was a substitute — he was hired for $300 from the Army and I don’t know much paid by a guy named Andrew Anderson, in 1864. I was kinda disappointed to find that out — I’d been hoping for at least a Vanderbilt.) Thus, Junior’s father. His mother was Bulloch, literally a model for Scarlett O’Hara in Gone with the Wind. (Her two brothers, who became traitors and pirates, inspired Rhett Butler. They lived in what became Tara… you get the idea.) So the years he was a little weakling playing with metal soldiers on the Persian carpets, Teedy was coming to the understanding that his uncles were heroic while his father was patriotic. Meanwhile, Senior was busy. Not an aloof father, but TR had the ‘from afar’ vibe Churchill said about his mother. But where the former Jenny Jerome became involved in her son’s life “when he grew up and become interesting”, Junior’s childhood was not interesting. It was alarming and time-consuming for his father, instead. So the most and best attention Junior got from his dad was during his worst asthma attacks, when he’d blow cigar smoke into his feeble child’s lungs (the latest thing in 19th century medicine: it’s a miracle the future President didn’t get laudanum in his coca tea while being bled) or, when it looked like it might even be fatal this time — riding at full speed in a coach, the horses at a gallop and the kid trying to take the air forced into his lungs at 25 mph. Until, one day, Senior lost patience and told young Teddy a simple truth: You will either master your body or it will master you. Not long after, Junior went to Harvard where he began to work out obsessively. He was there when his father flat-out died. Thus, a study in grief: all agree that Junior was a prolonged case of a kid admiring his father to an extraordinary degree, even at a time when that was an ideal and not uncommon in fact, either. There was nothing largely wrong about his Dad even in retrospect and definitely not among his contemporaries. But TR himself never got to experience his father as an adult, so his eventually clear understanding that by the son’s standards, the father had failed his country’s call wasn’t tempered by the direct experience of talking it over with him. Many people have noted TR’s eagerness for combat might have had something to do with that. Yet sticking within the question, Junior was away from home and his parents for the first time, living the life of an elite college student at the old school — for the right person, one of the finest lifestyles ever conceived. By all accounts, he liked his studies but he spent his time bodybuilding — again, it’s unlikely that’ll show the paterfamilias was wholly missing from that energy. He was a solid if not fascinating (or fascinated) student, so mere books wasn’t how he worked off his profound shock and sadness at losing his father, either. Whose advice he had already taken. He resolved it wasn’t going to rule him, so the young man mastered his body. It was at Harvard, beginning even before Senior’s sudden passing, that Theodore Roosevelt transformed from the weakly breathing boy to a born again hard young man. It was absolutely a factor that he was going to finally show the old man a son who wasn’t weak, “master of his fate and captain of his soul”. He was cheated of the kind of victory sons crave to share with fathers. It’s a curious crux of the moral and spiritual with the physical for the young man. One of the first things anybody learning any kind of physical combat has to learn is what if feels like to get hit. “Everybody has a plan until they get punched in the mouth,” as that noted military strategist Mike Tyson put it. Junior’s training at Harvard was like that — he was instructed by experts how to improve his wind by working his heart by building up muscle through painfully difficult, monotonous exercise. Doing 100 curls of 25 lb barbells punctuated by bouts of wrestling and boxing in which the 26th President really was socked in the mouth. A lot. A typical Harvard day for Junior might begin with a short run, breakfast then two or three hours of pushups in various positions, chin ups, pull ups, squats; he’d throw a heavy medicine ball to himself or play violent games of catch with friends and coaches. Indian clubs were a thing at the time — a truly odd method of bodybuilding now sadly retro. He might (or might not) attend a lecture around lunch, he’d invariably return several books and take more out of the library: then all afternoon he’d punch somebody in the face, or get punched, or both; he’d wrestle guys under various rules. A fine dinner and then reading until sleep. For most guys that age, steady physical exercise is a joy: even the unathletic are still young and benefit in every way from working out. For Junior who had been such a weakling to be able to face the worst likely competitive results, being literally knocked down and thrown for a loop, over and over, it was liberating. Then it became exhilarating, because this was his education, after all. His Harvard coaches weren’t high school bullies. They were healing his grief, not exploiting it — they weren’t beating him up, they were teaching him to fight. Soon enough the young Roosevelt was a stocky, hard little man with real fists and the energy to fight violently, with or without rules. Something was waiting to happen when all that force could focus. He fell in love. If you believe his childhood sweetheart and second wife, Junior’s first wife was practically a living doll — pretty and wholesome and sure to be boring to her always boiling over husband, soon enough. She didn’t bore him at first, though: they were expecting within a year. In any case, Junior wasn’t prepared for his lovely young wife to die in childbirth the same day as his mother. Yet how he remolded his whole body in part driven by grief for Senior taught him the way to resolve his shock and horror at losing wife and mother all at once, being left with a baby girl. He handed her to his clubfoot sister Bamie and, as Huck Finn put it, lit out for the Territory. So that’s the answer — Theodore Roosevelt developed his ability to overcome adversity along the same arc as most people, only his particular epic was on a higher economic and cultural level (the Harvard gym in the late 1870s was rare air), punctuated by some of the worst things that can happen to anybody: losing a father, mother, and wife each suddenly and the last two simultaneously, isn’t lessened by being rich and well-connected. Nor were either of these documented, witnessed instances in TR’s young career, which show the man he’d become because of all that straining: in a tavern in the Dakotas, Junior — an orphan and widower, albeit a particularly young-looking dude in his well-made clothes — was challenged by a larger, meaner and older drunk. He looked like this wasn’t his first bar fight. He was more likely to have friends in the room. And there were guns everywhere, when the guy squared off and raised his fists like John L. Sullivan. Junior simply ran right at the guy from a few feet away, lowering his head to ram him in the solar plexus before he had any chance to block with his arms, that had been expecting a punch. TR grabbed his legs as he fell back in a wrestling move he’d done hundreds of times at Harvard. The bigger drunk went down hard, possibly both sick and with the wind knocked out of him, while TR knelt on his chest and punched him in the face, putting his whole weight into each fist every time. When Teddy was pulled off the guy, the fight was over and nobody wanted another one. Except possibly the young man. When Theodore Roosevelt went back East (no longer using Junior) to get elected to Albany, he was not immediately accepted by the New York state elite. A group of his colleagues took an instant dislike to him, mocking his obviously over-eager to please Western rancher legend: they probably already knew this guy, certainly the family — Wyatt Earp, he ain’t. Besides — though a father and a widower, he was also a young unmarried man who looked sorta effeminate in those days, even with the mustache. The combination of his money, bumbling charm and exceptionally nice clothes even prompted some of his more mean spirited colleagues to suggest Teddy looked like a young man who’d suck on the knob of a walking stick: not exactly subtle. But it was when the Republican leader in Albany apparently gave the green light to a hazing ritual that they really did in the State Legislature every so often, to take a new Member down a peg or two — they’d grab him, fling him onto a largish carpet held by a couple members at each corner, 8 men, who would fling the newbie up in the air a few times, laughing like hell at his utter humiliation. Theodore Roosevelt was tipped off by a gesture from a friend. TR spun on his heel, marched up to the guy and said: If you even try that, I’ll hurt you. I’ll break bones. Gouge at your eyes. I’ll bite. I’ll kick you in the balls. I can punch so your teeth come out. Don’t. You. Try. It. They didn’t. Does that about cover it?

Alex Mercer (Prototype): After saving New York from a nuke after it was infected with a viral outbreak he becomes a lone wanderer, going around the world and witnessing the bad side of humanity until he eventually comes across a family which he befriends until the family is approached by members of a gang, Alex kills the gang members and learns from the leader that the father he had befriended was originally apart of said gang. After learning this Alex confronts the father and despite his insistence that he had changed Alex murders him. He then goes to the daughter hoping to leave with her, he goes to collect some money he had stored away to find it missing, the daughter reveals that she had taken it and shoots Alex in the head however he easily brushes it off and kills her. Completely disillusioned Alex reaches the conclusion that stopping the outbreak in New York was a mistake and goes about causing another one in order to change the world into a hive mind with him as the leader Lucy/Kaede (Ellen Lied): she was raised in an orphanage in which she was constantly verbally abused by the other kids for her horns (something she was born with) and all but neglected by the caretakers as the viewed as more of a bother then anything else. Lucy had no friends and put up with the abuse as she rationalized that the kids were taking out their own frustrations on her as she was an easy target that is until one day she came across a puppy that she began to care for and see as her friend. Eventually Lucy couldn’t feed the puppy anymore with the scraps of food she was giving it as it was getting bigger, so in order to help with her friend Lucy got another one of the kids to help her while also telling her not to tell anyone else as the bullies would find out and do terrible things to it. Sadly however the bullies do find out (it’s not explicitly stated how they found out from the girl whether they bullied her as well or she willingly told them is unclear), the bullies then hold Lucy in place as they savagely beat the puppy to death while making her watch. Driven mad with grief over the loss of her puppy and the betrayal of her other friend Lucy lashes out with something called vectors (which are invisible arms Lucy is able to conjure and control) and murders everyone in the room. After burying her puppy and leaving the orphanage, Lucy (now with a complete disdain for humans) begins to murder entire families in order to use their houses as a place to stay. Eventually she meets a boy named Kouta (who she initially wants nothing to do with it but warms up to him) and they develop a friendship. Kouta eventually mentions a festival that he is going to attend with a cousin of his and (sensing Lucy’s discomfort and shyness) lies and says the cousin is a boy as a way to spare her feelings. However this is shown to backfire as Lucy makes her way to the festival and sees that the cousin is actually a girl which causes her to reach the conclusion that Kouta “already had someone”, she is then approached by hallucinations of the orphanage kids and Kouta who begin to mock and degrade her until she is approached by another voice that pretty much tells her that the only way she will ever be truthfully happy or accepted is if the world was filled with people like her a distraught Lucy is easily convinced to go along with this. Lucy then murders Kouta’s father and sister in retaliation for his supposed betrayal and comments that the only reason he is still alive is because they were friends. Kouta then tackles her to the ground and tearfully tells her to stop which causes her to do so and flee. After a while of infecting men so they give birth to people like her Lucy ultimately comes across a girl named Aiko who she befriends and actually entertains the thought of being able to Coexist with humans. However this friendship is cut short as an organization (which devotes its time into hunting people like Lucy down and either killing them or doing experiments on them), finds Lucy based on her activity in the area and tries to take her however Akio is ultimately shot in the confrontation, the people from the organization say they will get her medical attention if Lucy goes with them which she does. Despite this Lucy is approached by a man in captivity who tells her that her friend died and that he blames her solely for her death as according to him her kind had done nothing to coexist with humans, enraged by this hypocrisy Lucy promises the man that if she gets free she is going to kill everyone close to him (while leaving him alive) so he can experience the pain she has experienced. Ayato Naio (Angel Beats): Ayato was raised in a house known for its pottery making and his twin brother was amazing at it much to the approval of his father while he was pretty much ignored by his father, never acknowledged. One day his brother died but since they were twins Ayato’s father came up with a plan to keep up the illusion that his other son was still alive by having Ayato pretend to be his brother, which caused him to be forced to learn how to make pottery as great as his brother less his father berate him for it. Ayato eventually dies due to some unknown cause but according to him he was the one that died when his brother died as he was never acknowledged as Ayato again (not that he was acknowledged much in the first place before then anyway). Father Gascoigne (Bloodborne): Father Gascoigne was like many characters in the series a Hunter of beasts, however he like all hunters had to fear of going “blood drunk” which is where a music box from his family came in as he would take it with him on hunts in order to keep him sane. One hunt however he forgot the box which caused his wife to go out in a attempt to give it to him, this failed however as she is ultimately killed (how it happened is left ambiguous either Gascoigne killed her in his maddened state or he had to watch as his wife was killed by beasts). His tragedy doesn’t end their however as the new Hunter (you) come across him and have to kill him in self defense, this seems like a bittersweet ending but he actually had a young daughter who had sent you to look for them so now both of her parents are dead. Mrs Voorhees (Friday the 13th): she’s simply a mother who was driven insane with grief over the loss of her beloved son, her and Jason both are pretty much a victim of the world’s shittiest luck. Jason Voorhees: his motivation is similar to his mother (to primarily keep Crystal Lake free of what he perceives as trespassers). He like his mother is driven by the loss of a loved one Niklaus Mikaelson (The Originals): he was abused by his Viking father as in his mind it would make the boy “strong”. He was abused verbally, physically and psychologically by his father. This was made worse by the fact that not only was his mother completely indifferent to the abuse she actually made it worse as she gave Klaus a necklace that made him weaker (it was to suppress his werewolf side as his mother had had an affair with a werewolf who were prone to anger easily and could kill people in a violent rage which would cause them to unlock there werewolf side). Thomas Brown Hewitt/Bubba Sawyer/Junior Sawyer/Leather Slaughter (The Texas Chainsaw Massacre series): Leatherface was born into a family of cannibals who were easily able to convince him to go along with what they were doing and bullied him into submission, he’s pretty much the giant family attack dog who like Jason attacks those who invades his territory however unlike Jason his motivation for doing so is driven by fear of those who enter his house. Lady Maria (Bloodborne): she was involved in the attack on a village called the Fishing Hamlet, this eventually caused her to end up in the Hunter’s Nightmare where she now guards the Astral Clocktower which acts as a gateway to the Fishing Hamlet, this guarding is self imposed. Gherman the First Hunter (Bloodborne): Gehrman waits in the Hunter’s dream for new Hunters to arrive, he will instruct them on how to go about the night but eventually once the hunt is over he tells the Hunter that he will show them mercy by killing thereby freeing them from the dream. If a Hunter were to refuse his offer he stands and begins to fight them, however it is revealed after he is killed what he was trying to protect the Hunter’s from, the dream creator itself a celestial being know as The Moon Presence, Who now that Gehrman is dead requires a new occupier of the dream. The being will then forcibly make you the new “Gerhman”. Baldur (God of War): he was made invulnerable to anything (excluding mistletoe) which eventually revealed that he was actually incapable of feeling anything, which drove him insane and caused him to look for ways for him to feel something and wanting to take revenge on his mother (who was the person who bestowed him with the “gift”) Jason Voorhees (Friday the 13th): he was born with physical and mental disabilities which caused him to be the subject and endless bullying which eventually caused him to be shoved into a lake and supposedly die of drowning, however he survived and lived out the remainder of his childhood years alone in the woods which caused to have to learn how to hunt in order to survive. Eventually he returned to Crystal Lake one day and saw his mother (the only person to show him any love and compassion) be decapitated, the causes him to hunt down her killer (a woman named Alice) and kill her in retaliation. After this he returned to Crystal Lake to act as its guardian and would be merciless to those who he perceived as trespassing (pretty much everyone excluding kids or animals such as dogs) Savitar (the Flash tv series): he was created for a specific purpose and then was tossed aside by everyone Garra (Naruto): he had a monster placed inside of him when he was a baby which caused everyone in his village to fear and loathe him he was constantly sent to be assassinated by his father in a attempt to test the monster inside of him, the monster inside of constantly told him that if Garra slept he would be free to kill everyone which caused him to develop insomnia and finally the one person he thought was his friend willingly tired to assassinate him as he blamed Garra for the death of his sister as she died shortly after giving birth to him. Helbram (The Seven Deadly Sins): he was an idealistic fairy who wanted to interact with humans but this want was ultimately taken advantage of as he and others were captured by humans and had their wings torn from their backs (according to Helbram this was done slowly so they weren’t damaged and their captors could profit off of them). Helbram was driven insane by this experience and started to ultimately kill humans and set out to kill them all which ultimately lead to him having to be killed by his best friend Harlequin/King. Despite This Helbram’s tragedy continues as his body was found and was resurrected and on the off chance he was killed again he would slowly lose more of himself each time he was brought back until he was nothing more then a feral animal, this ultimately leads to King having to (reluctantly) kill him again.

column1: Who are all of Magneto's children in Marvel?
column3: He also inadvertently caused the deaths of millions of mutants by gathering them on Genosha, making them an easy target for Cassandra Nova and her Sentinels. Fortunately, women in the Marvel universe really dig a man with a past, and over the years, Magneto has used his most potent superpower -- procreation -- to spawn sons, daughters, clones and even genetically engineered uber-beings. Here are 15 of his most magnetic children. 15 ANYA“Classic X-Men" #12 describes the tragically short life of Anya Eisenhardt, Magneto's first child and the sister that Pietro and Wanda never had a chance to meet. Magneto's original name was not Erik Lehnsherr, but Max Eisenhardt, who changed his name to Erik after escaping a Nazi concentration camp with his girlfriend, Magda. After the end of World War II, Erik and Magda came out of hiding and married, giving birth to Anya shortly afterwards. The family moved to Ukraine, hoping to find a fresh start, but Erik's powers manifested at his new job, drawing unwanted attention to the family. One night Erik returned home to find his house on fire but was unable to rescue Anya because police officers arrested him for assaulting his boss with his newfound powers. In retaliation, Erik killed everyone in the city of Vinnitsa; terrified by her husband's powers, Magda fled, not telling Erik that she was pregnant. This event reinforced Erik's hatred for humanity, setting him on the path to becoming Magneto. 14 SCARLET WITCHCreated by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, Wanda Maximoff first appears with her brother Pietro in "X-Men" #4, as a submissive member of the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants who is often abused by Magneto. It's not long before she joins the Avengers and couples up with Vision, but her unstable powers frequently put the world in jeopardy. Eventually, after she is responsible for the death of Hawkeye and the destruction of Vision, the Avengers begin to contemplate killing her. This leads to a chain of events that produces the infamous "House of M" storyline, in which Wanda warps reality to create a world where everyone has their heart's desire. In this reality, Wanda and her brother rule by Magneto's side until her father discovers what she's done and kills Quicksilver, prompting Wanda to depower 90% of the mutant population. Although a recent retcon revealed that she's actually a non-mutant who was given powers by the High Evolutionary, she's been the daughter of Magneto for the last 40 years, which qualifies her for this list. 13 QUICKSILVERPietro Maximoff, has had a long and tortured history with Magneto, who up until recently was his father. His original origin story described his mother Magda fleeing to Wundagore Mountain and hiding the twins from their father Magneto after witnessing him kill an angry mob. But unlike his father, Quicksilver would become a superhero, joining the Avengers and then X-Factor. Over the years, he's both opposed and aided Magneto, serving at his side when he ruled Genosha and savagely beating his powerless father in "Son of M." Like his father, he also has a dark side, being the one who persuaded an emotionally vulnerable Wanda to warp reality in "House of M" and attempting to release the Terrigen Mists upon the depowered mutant population, despite its hazardous effects. Although he's no longer truly the son of Magneto, Quicksilver has also inherited his father's sense of superiority, viewing all humans as inferior. 12 POLARISThe result of an affair between Magneto and her mother, Lorna Dane's father believed that she was his daughter until she was three years old. Lorna's magnetic powers manifested while flying with her folks and the resulting magnetic pulse destroyed the plane and killed her parents. Her powers remained dormant until her first appearance in "X-Men" #49 when Mesmero forces her powers to manifest with his Genetic Stimulator Machine. In a bizarre turn of events, an android then reveals that Magneto is Lorna's father, a fact which is confirmed in "Uncanny X-Men" #431. Lorna bonds with her father when she goes to aid him in Genosha, enjoying the training he gives her in the use of her similar powers, but it's not long before he attempts to use her as a weapon in the Genoshan civil war. The Sentinels destroy Genosha in "New X-Men" #15 and Lorna is left utterly broken after witnessing the massacre, becoming a darker and more violent version of herself. When Havok breaks off their engagement and leaves her for Annie Ghazikhanian, she falls to pieces, requiring Juggernaut to knock her out and Professor X to put her back together again. 11 MAGNUSA bright light that burned for only two issues before being extinguished, Magnus had the potential to become one of Marvel's greatest heroes; unfortunately, it wasn't to be. Born on Earth-27 to Magneto and Rogue, who were both outlawed X-Men and reformed villains, Magnus survived a traumatic birth to enter a relatively happy childhood. As a boy, his powers of magnetism surpassed his father's, giving him mastery over all magnetic forces and the ability to remold all metallic substances, including adamantium. His second mutation manifested at age 13 and that's when things took a turn for the worse. In "Exiles" #1, we read that he manifested an ability similar to his mother's, only far more deadly. Upon touching Rogue, she became a statue of solid steel and the young Magnus became distant and lonely, while his father returned to his former villainous ways. He found redemption by joining the Exiles, a group of time and space traveling superheroes, but their partnership didn't last long, for Magnus was soon required to make the ultimate sacrifice to stop Charles Xavier's A-Bomb. He was created by Judd Winick and Mike McKone. 10 CHARLES LEHNSHERRThe next child of Magneto had the same parents but with a different twist. In "X-Men: Alpha," Earth-295's Magneto and Rogue realized their similar magnetic powers made Magneto immune to Rogue's absorption abilities and they began a relationship. Rogue gave birth to Charles, who Magneto named after his deceased friend Charles Xavier. This took place in "Age of Apocalypse," an alternate timeline that was created when David Haller traveled back in time and accidentally killed his dad, Charles Xavier, instead of Magneto. Don't mess with time, everyone! Charles' childhood was soon ruined by Bishop, who realized that he had fractured memories of the original timeline, inspiring Magneto to send out groups of X-Men to attempt to change history. Bishop and Magneto were captured by Apocalypse's forces, and Charles was sent into the Morlock Tunnels under the protection of Nanny, his guard robot. After his dad slew Apocalypse, Charles came to live in the rebuilt mansion once owned by his namesake, Charles Xavier. Sounds like a happy ending, right? Wrong. Charles was apparently killed in front of his father by Demon Ock, the "Age of Apocalypse" version of Doctor Octopus. 9 NINA GURSKYBased on Anya Eisenhardt, Nina Gursky appears in "X-Men: Apocalypse," where her death serves as a catalyst for Erik's third transformation into the supervillain Magneto. Ten years after the events of the movie "X-Men: Days of Future Past," Erik Lehnsherr is living a relatively normal life as Henryk Gurzky, a steelworker. Erik inadvertently reveals himself as a mutant after using his powers to save a coworker, and upon returning home that night, tells his wife Magda that they must leave immediately. They find their daughter Nina in the custody of police officers who now know Erik's real identity and that he was responsible for the events in Washington. Erik surrenders to the police in exchange for his family's freedom, but Nina loses control of her mutant abilities, resulting in a swarm of birds attacking the police. Nina and Magda are killed when one of the officers accidentally shoots them with an arrow and Erik then kills the officers with Nina's metal locket. Once again, he loses his family and becomes Magneto, paving the way for Apocalypse to recruit him. 8 PLAGUEHere comes another child from an alternate reality, but be warned, it's a strange one! "X-Men Millennial Visions" #2001, the one-shot series, offers us a glimpse into a twisted future where our favorite heroes are radically different. In "Brother(hoods) Keeper," we discover that Magneto and Rogue Darkholme, a combination of Rogue and Mystique, had a child named Plague. Together they make up one disturbing family, all swearing allegiance to the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. Rogue is also less than faithful to Magneto, regularly cheating on him with Gambit. Standard stuff, really. Their daughter Plague is a devilish creature (picture the girl from The Exorcist) with the charming ability to create and control tiny robotic viruses, dubbed "Microsentinels," which she uses to burrow into a victim's skin and unleash all manner of nasty diseases. The story comes to a conclusion when Peter Wisdom, a British MI-13 agent, infiltrates the Brotherhood and manages to persuade Plague to betray her family. Hopefully, she'll never visit the Marvel canon universe! 7 ZALADANEGerry Conway's Zaladane is another comic book enigma that is still unsolved today. In "Astonishing Tales" #3, we're introduced to Zaladane, the self-proclaimed half-sister of Polaris and a power hungry priestess of Garrok the Petrified Man; a god worshiped by the Sun People in the Savage Land. After somehow discovering that her sister had powers, Zaladane (real name Zala Dane) was immensely jealous, venturing all over the world in an effort to obtain her own powers. Eventually, she came across the Savage Land and there claimed power for herself, becoming a master sorceress and using technology to mutate herself. Interestingly, her powers bear a slight resemblance to those of Scarlet Witch -- could Magneto could be her father too? She certainly shares his desire to subdue the earth. In "Uncanny X-Men" #275 we read that she's stolen both Polaris' and Magneto's powers and, along with the Savage Land Mutates, is attempting to manipulate the Earth's magnetic fields. She meets her end in that issue when Magneto regains his powers and reverses her blood flow. Ironically, Magneto is unaware of their possible blood connection at the time. 6 VISIONWould Magneto make a good father-in-law? Probably not. Created by Roy Thomas and John Buscema, Vision was originally the "child" of Ultron ("Avengers" #57), but quickly rebelled against him to join the Avengers and help them defeat him. Vision soon became involved with the Scarlet Witch, married her and using Wanda's hex powers, conceived twin boys. But unfortunately, all of Magneto's children are cursed with his own bad luck in relationships and Wanda's unstable powers destroy both their marriage and Vision himself. Vision is repaired by Tony Stark and Hank Pym, and in "Avengers" #24, he goes to Utopia to confront Magneto on Wanda's whereabouts, accusing the Master of Magnetism of ruining his children's lives. Magneto subdues Vision but spares him, knowing that Wanda still cares for the synthezoid and that she would never forgive Magneto if he killed him. Then again, he does end up destroying Vision in "Exiles," when he hurls a large asteroid at Earth. So, it's not the closest relationship. 5 CRYSTALMagneto's former daughter-in-law, Crystal, has had a turbulent relationship with his son Quicksilver, who like his father, is unable to keep a woman for long. The first marriage between a human and an Inhuman, Crystal first met an injured Quicksilver in "Fantastic Four" #131 and their romance began when she nursed him back to health in Attilan. They eventually married and had a child named Luna, who surprisingly was without powers. After learning the truth of who his children are, Magneto reveals himself as Pietro and Wanda's father in "Vision and the Scarlet Witch" #4 where he also meets Luna, who softens his heart towards humanity. Over the years Crystal and Quicksilver have split and reunited several times, with Crystal finally calling it quits after Quicksilver kidnaps Luna and exposes her to the Terrigen Mists in an effort to give her powers ("Silent War" #1). Crystal is able to manipulate the four basic elements (fire, water, earth and air) and is now happily married to Ronan the Accuser, who she married in order to forge an alliance between the Kree and the Inhumans. She was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. 4 JOSEPHFrom his first appearance in "Uncanny X-Men" #327, Joseph was believed to be a younger amnesiac version of Magneto by both the X-Men and the Acolytes. Upon meeting him, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch were also shocked by their father's apparent transformation into a kind and generous soul, and the X-Men accepted him into their ranks when he joined the fight against Onslaught. Unsurprisingly, he was attracted to Rogue, who turned him down in favor of Gambit. In "X-Men" #87, he is revealed to be a clone of Magneto, who lost his memories when his creator Astra sent him to kill Magneto. But before he has a chance to contemplate his true identity, he's required to face Magneto for the second time, an event which ended in Joseph sacrificing himself to save the world from Magneto's magnetic destruction ("X-Men" # 87). In some ways, Joseph's death is a missed opportunity for Magneto, who could have had a fresh start as a hero. He was created by Scott Lobdell, Andy Kubert and Joe Madureira. 3 ALPHANot content with having mutant children, Magneto decided to create one of his own after stumbling upon the wreckage of a long-abandoned Deviant city while imprisoned in the center of the earth. Inside the city he found experimental evolutionary technology placed there by the half-Inhuman, half-Deviant Maelstrom that would enable him to create the ultimate mutant. Xavier and the Defenders attempted to prevent Magneto's creation from hatching in "Defenders" #15 but they were defeated by the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants and Alpha entered the world. Initially a speechless brute, the continually-evolving Alpha defeated the Hulk and teleported the Brotherhood to the United Nations at Magneto's command, who then ordered the creature to slay the Defenders. Magneto was convinced by Charles Xavier and Dr. Strange to abandon his mad plan and Alpha left Earth to pursue its own destiny. Alpha possesses unmeasured telekinetic, teleportation and telepathic powers, as well as a highly advanced intellect and was created by Len Wein and Sal Buscema. 2 EXODUSAlthough not his biological son, Exodus is the closest thing Magneto has to the perfect son, being a mutant who shares all of his values and completely dedicated to his cause. He's also an omega level mutant, possessing vast superhuman powers including telepathy, telekinesis and teleportation, as well as superhuman durability and healing. His high power levels are most likely a result of his encounter with Apocalypse, who he met in the 12th century during the Crusades. Apocalypse sought to use him as a weapon, but Exodus rejected the false god and was imprisoned in stasis for his rebellion. Centuries later, in "X-Factor" #92, Magneto found and freed him, indoctrinated him into his violent ways and selected him to lead the Acolytes. His criminal career highlights include turning a S.H.I.E.L.D carrier into a Cerebro type device, defeating the combined forces of the X-Men and Avengers, and forcing Charles Xavier to face his greatest failures. Like Magneto, he often shows no regard for human life, viewing humans as inferior to mutants. Exodus was created by Scott Lobdell and Joe Quesada, and like most of Magneto's kids, has recently turned against him, oddly, in a bid to impress him. 1 ONSLAUGHTThe world isn't ready for Magneto and Xavier to couple up and procreate, but they did have a child together and it wasn't the IVF kind. Enter Onslaught, the terrifying result of an angry Charles Xavier shutting down Magneto's mind after he removed Wolverine's adamantium. Making his first full appearance in "X-Men" #52, we discover that Onslaught is a near-omnipotent being formed of Magneto's anger, grief and lust for vengeance combined with every negative feeling Xavier has suppressed over the last 30 years. Despite resembling Magneto, Onslaught is made of psionic energy and possesses the combined powers of both Magneto and Xavier. Fueled by Xavier's failure to unite humanity and mutantkind, Onslaught planned to transform the entire human race into a collective consciousness, absorbing Franklin Richards and X-Man to gain enough psionic power to do it. The non-mutant members of the Avengers, the Fantastic Four and Doctor Doom all seemingly perished trying to stop him in "Onslaught Marvel Universe" and although they would later return in "Heroes Reborn: The Return" #4, so would Onslaught in later issues. Scott Lobdell, Mark Waid and Andy Kubert were the disturbed minds behind Onslaught's creation.
column9: • Vision, Crystal, Alpha, Joseph, Exodus, Onslaught. What a dumb list.

column1: Who is Elena Gilbert?
column3: Elena Gilbert is a fictional character and protagonist from the television series The Vampire Diaries. In The Vampire Diaries, set in the fictional town of Mystic Falls, she is portrayed by Nina Dobrev. In the books, Elena was blonde, popular, selfish and a "mean girl". However the show's producers, Julie Plec and Kevin Williamson, felt that it wasn't the direction they wanted to go with their heroine in The Vampire Diaries television series. Instead, she became a nicer, relatable and more of "the girl next door" type, until her life gets flipped upside down when she meets the Salvatore Brothers. In April 2015, Nina Dobrev announced that she would be departing the series after the sixth-season finale. Much of Elena's story revolves around her relationships with vampires Stefan Salvatore and his older brother, Damon. It is revealed that Elena is a Petrova Doppelgänger, which is thus responsible for her being identical to her ancestor, Katherine Pierce (née Katerina Petrova). This also has the implication of making her a supernatural creature. Dobrev portrayed the "conniving" Katherine as well, who is opposite of Elena. The actress stated that it has been a challenge distinguishing the two, and enjoys playing them both. In the television series's fourth season, Elena becomes a vampire and dies then deals with the struggles that come with her change. She took the cure and became human again towards the end of the sixth season. In the finale of the sixth season, Kai linked Elena to Bonnie's life by magic. Elena will only wake up when Bonnie dies in around 60 years. She was locked inside the Salvatore tomb, then relocated to a warehouse in Brooklyn, New York in the seventh season, then back to Mystic Falls. In late 2016, when it was announced that the eighth season would be the final season, Dobrev was in talks about returning to the television series to reprise her role in the final episode. After much speculation. Dobrev's return was confirmed on January 26, 2017, via an Instagram post. Dobrev appeared in the final episode of the show as both Elena and her evil doppelgänger Katherine Pierce. March 9, 2009, it was announced that Bulgarian-born Canadian actress Nina Dobrev, known for her portrayal of Mia Jones on Degrassi: The Next Generation, had joined the cast of The Vampire Diaries as Elena. [2] She was the second cast member to be announced following Steven R. McQueen, who plays Elena's brother Jeremy Gilbert. [3] Steve West Cinema Blend said the vampire brothers' battle over Elena will wreak havoc on the entire town.". [2] Executive producer Kevin Williamson recalled Dobrev auditioning while having the flu, which he described as the "worst audition ever", and they "didn't even look at her a second time". Dobrev went back home to Canada, yet, still wanting the part, she submitted a videotape audition, which saw her cast as Elena Gilbert. [4] Dobrev said that after reading the script, she was drawn to Elena because she was "this average girl who was damaged in many ways". [5] Initially, she believed that she would be playing the "bad girl" Elena from the books, but the show wanted to go in a different direction for the character. [4] After researching, Dobrev discovered she would also play Elena's 534-year-old vampire doppelgänger Katherine Pierce whose characteristics are the "complete opposite". [5] Dobrev described this as "one of the rarest, coolest opportunities in television, to play two people on the same medium". She had confessed that she enjoys playing Katherine more than Elena. [5] Dobrev stated that she changes her appearance to distinguish Elena from her doppelgänger, Katherine; "Changing my hair helps me transform," she told Glamour. [6] Additionally, she said "I think I have one of the coolest characters on the show — I get to play two completely different people on opposite sides of the spectrum and I just have so much fun doing it". [4] Dobrev felt that her biggest challenge on The Vampire Diaries was distinguishing Katherine and Elena, and found it "interesting" to create a whole new character. [1] In the novels, Katherine originated from Germany. However, in the television series, she is Bulgarian, as is Dobrev, who can speak the language fluently . Dobrev said, "The writers heard me speaking Bulgarian to my mom on the phone while I was on set one day. One thing led to the other and voila". [7] Development CharacterizationNina Dobrev, who plays Elena Gilbert, at PaleyFest 2014 In the books, Elena is considered "one of the popular girls" at her high school and always gets "anything she wants". [8] Executive producer of the television show, Julie Plec, said the Elena from the books was "really kind of selfish". In The Vampire Diaries, Elena's "selfishness" in the books as a human was never explored, because it "didn't ever feel like a characteristic" the show wanted for their heroine. [9] Plec said "We kind of abandoned that queen-bee popular complex that in a lot of ways defined early Elena in the books", while feeling that Elena's actual flaw is her "deep, deep connection to other people". [9] In the books, Elena had blonde hair, but has brown hair in the television show. [10] Describing Elena from the books, Dobrev said she is "one of those mean girls that gets what she wants, popular . . . and she's blonde and blue eyed". Williamson told her that "the angle we wanted to go for was the relatable, nice, girl next door, who the audience roots for". [4] Katherine, on the other hand, is penned as a "conniving, narcissistic, bitch". [4] Describing Elena years later, Dobrev said she evolved from a "younger, naive, sad, young girl" to a "strong woman". [1] Romances Before The Vampire Diaries, Elena dated Matt Donovan (Zach Roerig), who was unable to move past his feelings for her initially after their break-up. [11] Elena began dating Stefan Salvatore (Paul Wesley), and later discovered he was a vampire. [12] As the episodes progressed, she developed a connection with Stefan's adventurous brother Damon Salvatore (Ian Somerhalder), who consumes human blood, unlike Stefan, who has an animal blood diet. [13] Speaking about the different qualities Stefan and Damon bring to Elena, Dobrev said they have "different qualities that are very appealing", which combined make "the perfect man". She said "Stefan is committed and sweet and protective and loving, and Damon is spontaneous and crazy and fun and exciting". [5]Dobrev with her Vampire Diaries co-stars Paul Wesley (Stefan) and Ian Somerhalder (Damon) at the 2012 San Diego Comic-Con International. After Elena became a vampire, she became sired to Damon and they slept together. According to Plec during an interview with TVLine, Elena "really believes what she feels is 100 percent genuine and real", and the couple "wants to be together and realizes that they shouldn’t, yet really wants to. So what do they do?" [14] Stefan became heartbroken, feeling angry and betrayed, and lashed out at Damon and Elena. [15] In the season 4 finale, an unsired Elena confirms that she is in love with Damon, and the two kiss passionately. At the end of season 6, the two plan to become human, get married, and have children together, but their dream is abruptly compromised by Kai, who puts Elena into a magical coma. Damon remains entirely devoted to Elena throughout the remaining two seasons as Elena sleeps peacefully. In the season 8 finale, she is revealed to be happily married to Damon. Transition Executive producers Julie Plec and Kevin Williamson agreed that in the book series, Elena was turned into a vampire too early, which was around page 200 of The Awakening. [16] Elena's transition into a vampire was planned for two years. Plec said: "That felt obviously too soon, and rushed, and we didn’t want to make a show about a teenage girl who instantly becomes a vampire. But we always knew that her journey would take her there eventually". [16] At the second season's conclusion, Elena was nearly turned into a vampire. [1] Dobrev was happy that she wasn't, because she felt "it would have been too soon", and also didn't think it was something Elena or she wanted. [1] In the show's third season, Elena has a brain hemorrhage which was initially thought to be a concussion, and begins to die. [17] In what was described by the International Business Times as "the moment Vampire Diaries fans have been waiting for", Elena had to choose whether to be driven to Damon or Stefan to say goodbye to. At the time, Klaus was killed, meaning all vampires sprouting from his bloodline also die, which includes Damon and Stefan. She picks to say goodbye to Stefan. [17] However, all these vampires end up surviving when Klaus never really dies. To save her, Doctor Meredith Fell (Torrey DeVitto) fed Elena Damon's blood. Rebekah Mikaelson kills Elena on Wickery Bridge, unaware of the vampire blood in her system. She woke up as a vampire at the end of the season. [17] The Hollywood Reporter interviewed Plec, and described her transition as "monumental changes" which would have Elena in for a "wild ride". Plec said Elena becoming a vampire is "an awakening of a person who is about to go through a lot of changes", and "she is going to evolve as a person and her relationships are going to evolve accordingly". [18] While Stefan was afraid she would hurt someone, Damon thought it was inevitable and wanted to "rip the band-aid off". [18] Plec felt that "She’s, unfortunately, not getting the same advice from the two people she values most in the world. It’s going to make it more difficult for her", [18] while describing the situation as "a whole new Elena and it’s a whole new day. It’s a different dynamic between the three of them especially". [18] Television series Backstory Elena Gilbert is born on June 22, 1992 in Mystic Falls, Virginia to John Gilbert (David Anders) and Isobel Flemming (Mia Kirshner) while they were still in highschool. With the help of John's brother Grayson, Isobel and John flee town days later, leaving Grayson and his wife Miranda to adopt Elena as their own. A doctor, Grayson fakes a birth certificate so that it appeared Elena was his daughter with Miranda. The next year, Miranda and Grayson had a child of their own, Jeremy Gilbert. Elena dates her childhood friend Matt Donovan, who was her first love. On 23 May 2009, Elena is picked up by her mother and father after getting in a fight with Matt while attending the party. The three of them later end up in a car accident, with their car driving off a bridge. Stefan Salvatore finds them, and saves Elena, but it was too late to save Grayson and Miranda, who died. It remained unknown for months who saved Elena, and it was considered a miracle that she lived. Her relationship with Matt ended when they broke up. Storyline Season 1 Elena, still empty after losing her parents, begins to fit back into school. She meets a mysterious new student named Stefan Salvatore. They connect instantly, and begin dating. She meets his older and malevolent brother, Damon. After researching, Elena realizes Stefan was alive in 1953. It is later revealed that he is a 162-year-old vampire. Damon also begins falling for Elena. Elena finds a picture of a woman named Katherine Pierce who looks exactly like her. Stefan reveals that it is the woman who made him and Damon feud 145 years ago, and the person who turned them into vampires. He also told her that he is the person that saved her the night of her parents death. At the end of season one, Elena discovers that Grayson and Miranda weren't her biological parents, and that a woman named Isobel and her uncle John, who she grew up hating, were. Season 2 In season two, she learns that she is a Petrova doppelgänger, having an appearance just like Katherine Pierce, which means that she has to be sacrificed to release Klaus' werewolf side. The sacrifice later happens, but Elena is saved, because John sacrificed himself for her after being put under a spell by Bonnie. However, her aunt Jenna is turned into a vampire and, as part of the sacrifice, is killed by Klaus, leaving Elena without a guardian. In the season two finale, while Damon is dying due to a werewolf bite, she forgives him for forcing her to drink his blood and kisses him with the thought that it might be Damon's last day, however Damon gets cured by drinking Klaus' blood. Season 3 In season three, Elena does everything in her power to make Stefan get his humanity back, which was turned off by Klaus as payment for saving Damon from a werewolf bite in the latter part of season two. Meanwhile, she grows closer to Damon while working together on saving Stefan and trying to defeat Klaus, eventually even sharing a kiss. She later admits to Stefan that she has feelings for Damon as well but that she never stopped loving Stefan. While in Denver together, Elena kisses Damon, later telling him that she doesn't know how she feels about him. It is eventually revealed that Elena met Damon the night of her parent's death, though he compelled her to forget. She eventually chooses Stefan in the season finale but before she can tell him, Elena drowns while having vampire blood in her system. During the last moments of season three, she awakens as a vampire in transition. Season 4 In season four, Elena is faced with the tough decision of whether to die or to feed on human blood so she can fully transition into a vampire. Elena, after realizing Stefan's desperation to keep her alive, decides to complete her transition. Her relationship with Stefan ends, allowing her to begin a proper romance with Damon. Although, it is later revealed there is a sire bond between them. Sometime later whilst searching for the cure for vampirism, Jeremy is fed to the immortal Silas by Katherine. As a result, Damon used the sire bond to convince her to turn off her humanity, due to her incredible grief over losing her brother and the last remaining member of her family. Elena became ruthless without her emotions, going on killing sprees and being very hateful towards her friends. Towards the end of season four, Damon kills Matt in front of Elena to trigger her grief. After revealing that Matt had the Gilbert Ring on, Elena's humanity was switched on and her emotions were focused on hate towards Katherine for killing Jeremy. Season four ended with Bonnie as a ghost after bringing Jeremy back to life and Elena fed Katherine the cure for vampirism in a moment of desperation as she was about to be killed. Elena had chosen Damon as the Salvatore that she loved, leaving a devastated Stefan. Season 5 In season five, Elena starts at Whitmore College and is happy after spending the summer with Damon. There she realises that Silas has taken Stefan's place and that Stefan is in that safe in a river constantly drowning. She and Damon then find the safe, only to find a dead body there meaning that someone opened the safe and Stefan is a Ripper again. However, Qetsiyah had fried Stefan's brain causing him to suffer amnesia. While trying to bring him back, they almost kiss meaning that she still feels something for him. Qetsiyah soon brings back Stefan's memories and says that Elena and Stefan were always meant to be as the Universe had to unite the doppelgängers of Silas and Amara. This leaves Damon and Elena questioning their relationship. Later on, she is kidnapped and experimented on by Wes Maxfield, and she learns that her father also used to experiment on vampires. Later, when Katherine is about to die as a result of all of her years catching up with her as a result of having the cure in her system, Katherine uses a spell and possesses Elena, a fact that her friends were initially unable to deduce. But once they did, they trapped Katherine and left her with no escape. Stefan stabbed her with the traveller dagger, but ghost Katherine reveals to Bonnie, shortly before trying to cross into the Other Side, that she had injected Dr Maxfield's enhanced ripper/werewolf virus into Elena's body, infecting Elena. The gang is eventually able to find an antidote. She, unfortunately, loses trust in Damon, partly because he killed her friend Aaron, so they break up, but realise they cannot survive to be apart and get back together. Once Markos and his traveller army begin to take over Mystic Falls, setting an anti-magic barrier around the town, the gang comes up with a plan to take out the travellers by killing them all at the same time, overpowering the anchor to the Other Side AKA Bonnie and creating a possible way out of the now-collapsing Other Side. Elena and Damon drive into the gas-filled Mystic Grill with most of the travellers in it, blowing it up and killing most of the people in it, including Elena and Damon. She wakes up as a ghost and finds her body, sending her to Bonnie, where she passes to the Other Side, and she and many others are able to pass back to the land of the living afterwards. But the spell that allows this is broken before Damon passes back through, and as Bonnie is the anchor, she is a part of the Other Side and shall, therefore, disappear along with it. This leaves the gang mourning the loss of Damon and Bonnie in the season finale. Season 6 In season six, Elena starts back at Whitmore, and is unable to set foot in her hometown. She is also unable to recover from Damon's death and starts lurking the borders of Mystic Falls in order to grab civilians, drink their blood, then compel them to forget, but as spirit magic no longer works in Mystic Falls, any of her victims who cross into the town remember the ordeal, putting her identity as a vampire at risk when one of her victims, Sarah, comes to town. Elena begs Alaric to compel her to forget that she ever loved Damon, which Alaric is able to do, due to him being an Enhanced Original, with the ability to compel other vampires. She eventually wears him down and asks her friends to never remind her once the compulsion had been done. After a number of failed attempts, Alaric successfully compels her to forget her love for Damon. She however leaves Alaric with some of her reminders of Damon, should she ever need them again. She is told of her former feelings for Damon soon afterwards, but decides to stay the way she is, as she doesn't want to go back to being unhappy again. She starts to date her classmate, Liam. Once Damon comes back to life, Alaric tries to convince Elena to allow him to undo the compulsion, a decision she is reluctant to make. She eventually decides to have him undo it, but Alaric goes back to being human again after crossing into Mystic Falls, causing him to lose his vampire status (he only stayed alive because his once fatal human injuries were healed), meaning he will not be able to do so. She is then left to finally come face-to-face with Damon and see if she'll still feel the same way about him. They eventually rekindle their relationship, Elena takes the cure that Bonnie gave Damon. At Alaric's wedding, Kai ruins their wedding and casts a sleeping spell on Elena, linking her life to Bonnie's. She makes a sacrifice to let Bonnie live out her life until it is her turn. She bids goodbye to her friends and loved ones before parting ways but knows that she will see Damon, Stefan and Caroline again one day. Season 7 Elena doesn't make an appearance but is heard calling Damon's name when he visits the Armory vault. It was a way of Sybil, the Siren, luring him into a trap. Season 8 In the final episode, Elena makes an appearance. When a weakened Bonnie dies from the sounding bell, she meets Elena in a dream-like forest. Elena hugs her and wonders if she really has died. Enzo appears and says it isn't her time and takes Bonnie back to the world of the living. When Bonnie wakes up, it was Stefan who resuscitated her. Elena, asleep, is then taken to the Mystic Falls High School by Katherine and places her in the boiler room. Stefan tries to rescue Elena, but Katherine had Kai spell the boiler room, so that Elena can't be taken out of the room. After Bonnie had deflected the hellfire back into the bell, Bonnie passes out. Elena wakes up and wanders the school. Stefan meets up with her. It looks like Bonnie has died, but in fact Elena is still sleeping and Stefan's ghost came to visit her in her dream. He had taken the place of killing Katherine instead of Damon, since Damon is human after Stefan gave him the cure. He came to say goodbye. After a tearful hug and saying goodbye, Stefan goes into afterlife. Elena finally wakes up because Bonnie has broken the spell over her. Elena reunites with Damon and the rest of the gang. Elena gives Caroline the message Stefan whispered into her ear, saying he did hear her voice message and will love her forever. In the epilogue, Elena continued to study at medical school. After finishing her education, she went back to Mystic Falls and lived together with Damon, happily married for a long time. After living out her life, she crosses over to the afterlife where she finally reunites with her parents, Aunt Jenna and Uncle John. Post-season 8 The second-to-last episode of The Originals, "The Tale of Two Wolves", features Elijah and Hope Mikaelson visiting Mystic Falls, where the window of a doctor's office reads "Elena Salvatore, MD", showing that Elena established her own medical practice. Reception Elena has received mainly positive reviews. Steve West of the Cinema Blend compared the story of The Vampire Diaries and the character of Elena to the popular vampire franchise, Twilight, and its protagonist Bella Swan. West said "Clearly Elena is way hotter than Bella, she has two immortal vampires fighting over her". [2] After she transitioned into a vampire, Carina Adly MacKenzie of Zap2it hoped that the "fierce" and "ripper" side of Elena would emerge when "someone messes with the people she loves". [19] McKenzie noted that when a person becomes a vampire, "their strongest personality traits are heightened", and hoped that wouldn't see Elena's "compassion and selflessness" double into "helping old ladies with their groceries and nursing injured animals back to health". [19] Robyn Ross of TV Guide also hoped that after Elena "has had a taste for blood", she would lose control. Prior to her becoming a vampire, Ross thought she was less fun and "slightly boring", and wanted Elena to follow her instinct and "stop protecting everyone's feelings". [20] Elena's romances with Stefan and Damon have become a popular craze with viewers, who have nicknamed them "Stelena" and "Delena". [21] Andy Swift of the website HollywoodLife praised Elena's relationship with Damon, which was a combination of real love and a sired bond, hoping they would live "happily ever after". [21] Vlada Gelman of TVLine, however, felt that their romance was "over in a rather mature way for a young love triangle" and questioned whether Elena was "ready to jump into a relationship with Damon right away" while Stefan was still in the picture. column1: What is your life story?
column3: Throughout life things that people don’t expect are bound to happen at one time or another. These can be either joyous or painful moments that have the power to change a person’s life completely. Some people experience more powerful moments than others but in the outcome somebody with the wisdom of life is created. I was the second born of three children. I had an older sister, Chloe’, who was absolutely a control freak. She constantly told me what to do and forced me to do things for her, but we still enjoyed each other’s company even if we got on each other’s nerves. Lexi, my younger sister, was as pure as a river. She was around a year and a half younger than me and was one of my closest friends. She was born with a birth defect which unfortunately restricted her to a wheel chair and had made her go through multiple surgeries. Despite being disabled she saw herself as a normal kid and did not see any difference. She still danced, played, and sang just like anybody else would. Her disability was not completely visible to me as well and I saw to it that she could overcome whatever obstacle that was put in her path. She and I were very close and we spent almost every minute together. Early life was peaceful. I was given a pretty normal childhood with loving parents. There was not one care in the world. Life was optimistic for my siblings and I and we hoped for a promising future. I enjoyed myself by playing with my sisters day and night and we loved it along with each other. One day Chloe’ was not home so Lexi and I wanted to enjoy the freedom of riding scooters of the driveway while she could not stop us. The moment the pavement was touched we were ecstatic. The next five minutes were full of happiness as we rolled around talking with one another. We laughed while we made fun of our older sister, imitating her in silly voices. “Hi! I’m Chloe’ the blah blah blah!” we would say while sticking out our tongues and pointing, as if we were scolding somebody. Both Lexi and I had a good relationship with her but at moments we thought she acted too strict and more like a parent. We thought it to be hilarious and soon went on to imitate our parents, friends, extended family, and pretty much everybody else we knew. Eventually my mother came looking for us. “Lexi, Athena!” She stormed onto the driveway and was livid. “You’re not allowed to go outside without somebody watching you! You could be taken! You can’t defend yourselves! How dare you come onto the driveway!” She continued to scorn us for several minutes telling us stories of children that were stolen and killed. I never thought what I was doing was wrong. Never specifically was I told that I was forbidden to go onto the driveway. I was allowed to go into the courtyard, how was the driveway any different? This was my wakeup call and I soon became scared of being alone. The outside world was not seen as the bright happy place as it once was in my mind. It had morphed into something that terrified me. Before this moment I never realized that my siblings and I could be harmed, and we could do nothing about it. Middle school was just around the corner. I was eleven years old and felt completely grown up. For the first time in my life I felt independent. The concept that I was going to a brand new school where I would have multiple teachers along with my own locker was liberating. At first I thought middle school would be the best, but I wasn’t aware of the hardships to come. The first few weeks of school went smoothly. I had great teachers, was making new friends, was learning to play the guitar, and had good grades. Lexi was enjoying the fourth grade and was excited to have wonderful classmates surrounding her and Chloe’ was ranked the top student in the eighth grade. Life was running smoothly when suddenly it was stopped abruptly. I walked home after school in a great mood because I had just learned some new notes in guitar class that day. We were taught the notes B, C, and D on the second string of the guitar. Now I knew 6 complete notes on the guitar and could play a simplified version of “Ode to Joy” by Beethoven. As I strode toward the house I hummed the melody while pretending to place my fingers on the strings. Chloe’ had reached the house around the same time as I and we were greeted by my grandmother, who looked overly worried. My grandparents had come to visit us while Lexi had to undergo another surgery so my parents could both be at the hospital. Lexi had surgeries so often that I thought nothing of it and it seemed normal, but I never knew anything wrong could happen during a surgery. Chloe’ asked what the matter was as she could obviously tell that my grandmother was very anxious whereas my eleven-year-old self was too oblivious to see her feelings. She stumbled over her words and couldn’t seem to find the right ones to say. After a long pause she sighed, looked up at us and said, “The surgery didn’t go as planned. Something has happened. While the doctors were operating they accidently pulled out a piece of Lexi’s spinal cord. Lexi is paralyzed.” Chloe’ had a stunned look on her face but yet I still had no idea what was wrong. What did the word “paralyzed” mean? Surely it couldn’t be that bad. “What does paralyzed mean?” I said, perplexed. Grandmother proceeded to tell and spoke softly to make sure it wouldn’t upset me, “It means that she isn’t able to move from her neck down. She can’t speak, can’t move, and can’t eat. She has to be fed from a tube. We will be going to see her this evening. The doctors say in a few weeks she will be able to come home.” Even though she had told me what happened I still somehow didn’t believe it. I kept telling myself that Lexi was just fine and nothing happened. When evening came around we drove the thirty minutes to the children’s hospital. It did not occur to me that the pathway to my sister’s room would forever be engraved in my mind. We walked in the front doors, made a right onto the elevator, traveled up to the fifth floor, sat in a room and waited for the ICU doors to open, went straight down the hallway, and made another right turn into Lexi’s room. The intensive care unit had tile floor with animals all over it to try and brighten the mood but it was ineffective. The moment I walked into her room my eyes could not believe what they were seeing. There she was lying on a bed with tubes sticking inside her everywhere. I looked at her face and I could see the pain that she felt. Just by giving her a quick glance was enough to tell she was broken down and hurting. The sight was extremely heart wrenching. Though the next few weeks my grandparents, Chloe’, and I would all go to see Lexi and my parents every single day. Occasionally I would look into her face and see how much pain she was in. I could see her screaming in terror and pain, devastated, but to her dismay nobody could hear her, for she would never be able to speak again. I felt powerless, for I could do nothing to take her pain away. I would have traded places with her if I could and take all the pain upon myself just to take the despair out of her eyes. School became harder since then. One day during my physical education class I broke down sobbing in front of everybody. My friend was the only person who knew the situation I was in. The teacher took us aside and tried to get me to say what was wrong, but I was hyperventilating and had lost the ability to speak. My friend had to explain for me and the only words I could get out were “She’s gonna die!” The teacher put her hands on my shoulders and told me looking at me straight in the eyes said confidently, “Athena, your sister is not going to die,” but I could not quite believe her. Lexi had transferred hospitals and was now in Primary Children’s Hospital in Utah. It was weird not going to see her every day. I had to go about two weeks without seeing her until I could go up to Utah. When I finally got to see her again I could not stop hugging her since I had missed her so much. The new hospital was so much brighter and colorful. They had people come and do crafts with us, had a slurpee machine, a play room, a restaurant, and tons of toys and books. I felt so much relief since I now had Lexi by my side. I spent my time with her watching TV and making her jewelry. One night my mother took me for a walk far away from Lexi’s room. She had me sit down on a couch and told me, “Athena, I think Lexi is going to die soon.” I couldn’t believe my ears. Had she just said Lexi, my only younger sister, was going to die? She repeated it again, “Athena, I think Lexi is going to die soon.” I still didn’t believe her, but she continued to explain that she had gone through enough suffering and that God was going to take her up soon. I sat up straight on the couch sobbing embraced by my mother. She held me tight and I didn’t want her to let go, but eventually she had to. A few days later the volunteers wanted to do an activity with my family. They gave Chloe’, Lexi, and I each a balloon and they told us to write all our wishes on them and we would release them into heaven. I wrote things like, “I wish we weren’t in pain,” and “I wish Lexi was all better and could come home.” My mother wrote on Lexi’s balloon for her. Lexi had put down things like, “I wish I wasn’t in pain,” “I wish I could talk again,” “I wish I could walk.” Chloe’ and I went outside with the balloons while Lexi watched from her window. We let go of the balloons and watched them go off to heaven and I wished with all my heart that they would come true. Eventually they did come true, but not in the way that I had hoped. Everybody had a moment alone with Lexi. I was not able to think of anything to say so I just joked with her. She was trying to say something to me but I couldn’t hear her. I watched her lips slowly, carefully. She was saying, “I want mom.” Cheerfully I told her, “Sure! I’ll go get mom! I’ll see ya later! Love ya Lex!” and I proceeded to get my mother. That was the last time I ever saw Lexi. In the hotel room I sat bored out of my mind. There was nothing on TV so my grandpa had just put on the Mormon channel. All what I could think of was wanting to watch Disney and switch it off of the Joseph Smith documentary. My thoughts were interrupted when my parents walked through the door and my mother cried, “Heavenly Father wanted Lexi back.” From just hearing that one sentence my world fell apart. The moment those few words escaped her mouth I had automatically started wailing in greif, and I collapsed on the floor. I was pounding and hitting the ground as hard as I could. I began to kick and scream when my family all told me that I had to be quiet. How could I possibly be quiet at a time like this? I had just lost a sister who only lived nine short years. Is one supposed to be quiet when hearing about the death of a loved one? I tried to muffle my cries but nothing would work. I could do nothing but scream with no control. My father had to take me out for a walk so I would not disturb the others in the hotel. As we waited for the elevator to open I quietly said, “Am I the youngest child now?” He embraced me in a warm hug and said in between his sobs, “No, You’re not. You’re still the middle child,” then took me on our stroll around the lake. After losing Lexi I became out of touch with my emotions and didn’t know how to cope with my loss. I became hostile towards my family, isolated myself from my friends, had major anxiety, and began to shut off my emotions. I hated myself for not saying something before the surgery. The only thing I could think was if I could have prevented my parents from taking Lexi to the hospital she would still be with me. In my mind I tried to think of what the future was going to be like without her, that I was responsible for her death. My family didn’t speak to one another and I locked myself in my room all the time. If I did speak to a family member nothing but my anger came out and I constantly yelled at them not knowing how to handle my grief. I never was able to tell anybody how I felt and bottled up all my feelings inside. Due to isolating myself from everybody my best friend drifted away from me. Now I truly had nobody. I contemplated suicide at the age of twelve so I could rejoin my sister again and take away my pain. I would imagine walking in my kitchen pulling out a giant, perfectly shiny, pointy knife, quickly piercing it into my heart, and slowly falling to the floor. Even though my desire for death was great I was too afraid to take the last step and pierce my heart. I didn’t want my mother have to bury another child and the last thing I desired was to give her more pain. I tried to live with myself. As I grew older I began to hate myself more and more. To try and cope with the loss I began to take it out on how fat I was. I was actually normal weight but when I looked in the mirror all what I could see in the reflection was a huge and hideous monster. Eventually I stopped eating to give myself control over at least one thing. Soon it grew into an obsession and I tried to eat as little as I could every single day. I had a journal in which I documented all the calories I in took. Everything that went into my mouth, even just a small grape, had to be written. If I ate at all during the day I would only consume around 300-600 calories. Every meal that I ate was thrown back up and finally a little bit of control was mine. I didn’t talk to my parents at all and stayed out of the house as much as I could. Ever since Lexi had passed they would constantly belittle me and compare me to my siblings. I knew without a doubt that I was the least favorite child and knew I never would be. I gave up all hope and was only living to go to dance classes. Dance became the only thing I cared about and it was a way to express myself without the need to tell anybody. At my studio nobody knew my past so I could make myself into whoever I wanted to be and they would still love me. The people at my studio became my true family and I forgot about the pain in my life whenever I went. The only thing my parents wanted from me were good grades. I never had a real conversation with them because they would mention nothing but school or how inferior I was. I eventually stopped doing my work in school believing that I was inadequate. Homework had a negative connotation to it and mad me fearful of the future. If I did a homework assignment, I would not turn it in or turn it in very late due to the fear of being seen as a failure. Every time I placed a homework assignment in front of me I would cry from sheer frustration and give up on myself, even if I was capable of doing it. My parents blamed dance for causing me bad grades, but they never truly looked inside to try and see the big picture. They thought I was being a slacker so they took me out of dance for three months, and I was devastated. The day after they took me out of dance I went to school extremely depressed. I could feel nothing inside and it felt as though a black hole had just engulfed me. I blocked out everything around me and thought of nothing but trying to figure out ways to kill myself, but I never would go through with it. During my English quiz the only thoughts I had were, “I’m a failure,” “I wish I were dead,” “Could a bus please hit me?”, and “How many pills would I have to take in order to kill myself.” I doodled some of these words on the blank quiz I held and thought that nobody would see them or pay attention to them. Later in the day I got called to the office and anxiety quickly rushed through my entire body. My hands were shaking and I could barely walk and I made my way down. My little scribbles were seen and I had to explain what I was feeling, and if I intended to hurt myself. I felt nothing but fear. Never before this moment had anyone wanted me to tell them my true feelings and I didn’t quite comprehend that somebody was willing to listen. I poured out a tiny drop of the emotions that had been overfilling in my bottle and couldn’t share anymore. Every single day I still thought of Lexi but I could speak her name to no one. It had been five years since the incident and I was afraid people would judge me for not overcoming my loss yet. I still was coping and someone listening to me vent was the first step in trying to sort out my life. A lot has happened so far in my small sixteen years of life than most will not even experience in a lifetime. Even if life is not always the easiest I try and cope the best that I can. I was put back into dance and I finally feel like I have a place in this life again. Life is still hard and it is ok if the only thing I can do is lie in my bed, and hope to fall asleep before I fall apart again. Challenges are necessary to learn, grow, and become better people even if they seem impossible to overcome. I hope that through these learning experiences that I will be lead to much success and am looking forward to the adventures coming in my near future. (To those who have made it this far, thank you. This is actually a paper I wrote for my English class. That teacher saved my life.)
