column1: How would you plan to secure yourself financially for retirement and other long-term goals especially in a country like India that has high inflation, no social security, mostly no pension, etc.?
column3: How would you plan to secure yourself financially for retirement and other long-term goals especially in a country like India that has high inflation, no social security, mostly no pension, etc.? The answer to this question depends upon the current age of the person and the retirement age. In the previous generation, the retirement age was typically 60. Many private companies, particularly IT/Tech companies reduced this to 58 in India. In the modern age, one is unlikely to last that long, if in IT field. See here: Prasanna Bhalerao's answer to Where do software engineers disappear after the age of 38?. As the question says, India there is no cushion once we stop earning. So whatever the current age, it is imperative to plan for the future. To answer this question, one must ask oneself: what will be my main expenses once I retire? I will assume that you have no dependants at that time, home/car/other loans are paid off. Basically no long term liabilities. So I will list the major expense heads:Daily/Monthly running expenses for food, transportation, utilities, communication, TV/cable, maid servants, etc.Occasional once a month or so cinema, eating out, etc.Annual expenses for medical insurance, car insurance, property taxes, housing society AMC, etc.Vacations and holidays as and whenInsurance Needs Regardless of the age group, I will advise one thing that everyone must do:Set up a pure term insurance for every earning member - typically husband and wife. The insurance sum assured value must start at ₹ 1 crore and increase as the age increases. Stop the term insurance once you retire / each earning member retires.Set up a comprehensive medical insurance that covers all members of your family. See if parents can also be covered or not. The medical insurance should not have any sub-limits such as ICU cap, room rent cap, Ambulance expense limit, etc. Each member should be covered for at least ₹ 5 lakhs at today's cost. This must increase every 5 years.Besides the comprehensive health insurance, you must also have a family floater top insurance of twice the value of comprehensive insurance with deductible. It must cover all family members. For instance:if you are a family of 4, insured for ₹ 5 lakhs eachthe top-up insurance could be ₹ 10 lakhswith ₹ 5 lakhs as deductible.So suppose, and God forbid, you run into a major medical emergency, your first line of cover is the employer's insurance. If that gets exhausted, use personal insurance. If that too gets exhausted, use the family floater top-up.Family floater top-plans are quite cheap.Emergency Funds: After taking care of insurance, one must plan emergency funds:Emergency Job Loss Fund: This fund protects you from sudden job loss and to keep you running while you hunt for a new job. The value must be 6 months of gross (or net) take home pay. As you get older, plan for longer/larger fund because it will be difficult to find a job then. Cap it to max one year of pay.Parent’s medical emergency: This is optional in case parents do not have any medical insurance, have no own funds, etc. This must be at least ₹ 3 lakhs per living parent at current costs.These above funds must be kept in a Liquid MF (better than bank FD) and must not be touched otherwise.Financial Goals: Next comes the individual financial goals. Each goal must be independently planned. I cannot advise for each and every person, but here is a helpful list:Buying home for self occupation or as an investmentBuying the dream carUndergraduate (Bachelors degree) education of childrenPost Graduate higher education (Masters degree) of childrenChildren marriageVacations abroad (optional)Retirement (the final and most important goal)The value of each goal in Rupee terms will depend upon your current age, the goal age and inflation rate. Current inflation rate is around 6% and assume this to be the same throughout. A few things about goals (1) and (2):Renting can be cheaper than buying. But rent is pure expense, will rise and you cannot have stability because landlord may not renew the lease. Secondly, you cannot plan your furniture, appliances, and interiors to your liking. At the end of every year, you are not paying off to build your asset.It is also advisable to look at a resale property, especially a distress sale. Such properties are available at a discount and for the same budget one can either plan property+interiors or buy larger size or get closer to the centre of the city.You may want that latest Hyundai Creta or Kia Seltos or Tata Harrier. Know that car is a heavily depreciating asset. Even as you drive the car out the showroom, it has depreciated by 5%. My advise is - you need a car to commute - don’t buy a new car and go for a used one instead. Do the due diligence, of course.It is very crucial that you follow the following exercise for at least 6 months, forever if you like:Every day note down the expense. Even the tiniest expense such as chai, cigarette, snacks, etc. must be noted down as Debits.Every expense/debit should be classified as: essential, nice to have (once in a while), totally unnecessary and extravagant.Make a pivot table on expenses (essential, OK to have once in while, extravagant).Cut down on extravagant and even “OK type” expenses.Do not eat outside too oftenCut down visits to the multiplex and cinemaTry to find cheaper subscriptions to TV/DTH, mobile/internet, etc.Try to car pool; it is good for environment alsoYou will know where to cut downAlways remember: Net Monthly Income - EMIs - Compulsory Savings into Investments = Money left for Expenses.Goal Planning and Achieving Now that you have assigned inflation adjusted values to the goals, the next is to plan for them. For instance, if your current age is 30, your family is 2 parents, spouse and one child and your monthly expenses are ₹ 35,000 today (not including rent and EMIs or insurance), then approximately 28 years later, at 6% the figure reaches ₹ 1,79,000 pm. But at the age of sixty, you may be just 2 (you and your spouse). So this figure will reduce by some amount - say ₹ 1,50,000 pm or ₹ 18,00,000 per year. This is in the 58th age year. Your life expectancy can be assumed to be 80 years. So it will continue to grow with inflation. So depending upon age, for this single goal, you will need to invest as follows (assuming 10% return on investment):The above corpus will last you till the age of 80. Not all goal plans need to start at the same time. You can set own priorities. For instance, to some buying own home is important. For others, planning for retirement is important. As can be seen above, it is important to start as early as possible in life. Learn the advantages of compounding. Just ₹ 10,000 per month invested for 20 years in a good MF that returns 10% on annual YoY basis results into a corpus of ₹ 76.57 lakhs (your own contribution is ₹ 24,00,000). A lot of contribution towards each goal depends upon current net take home salary (all earning members). Hence setting priorities is important.I hope this primer helps all. I may have missed out something. In that case, please, I welcome comments and suggestions.

column1: Is it a common narcissistic behavior to abandon your "loved one" when they're in a health crisis or dealing with the death of a family member?

column1: Why do narcissists keep tabs on you?
column3: 3 Reasons That Narcissists Keep Tabs on You: 1. They Want You as a Backup Source of Narcissistic Supply. When a relationship with a narcissist ends (whether it's a friendship, family member, romantic partner, colleague, etc.), they will quickly find a new person to be their source of narcissistic supply. However, just because they have a new source of supply doesn't mean they are done with you. Since you were once a valuable source of narcissistic supply for them, they feel entitled to maintain power and control over you for as long as they want. This means there's a strong possibility the narcissist in your life is still monitoring you, just in case their new source of narcissistic supply doesn't fully meet their needs. They want to keep you available as a backup option. Narcissists rely on external validation and control from others to feel stable, and they will try to maintain access to their previous sources of this narcissistic supply, even after a relationship ends. 2. They Want to Watch You Suffer. The reason for this is that deep down, narcissists have a lot of painful thoughts, feelings, and emotions that they can't deal with in healthy ways because they lack emotional skills. One way narcissists try to protect their own emotional stability is through a defense mechanism called projection. This is when they take parts of their own identity that they don't like, and put those onto someone else instead. By putting those down on others, belittling and degrading them, the narcissist can then point at the other person and think "I'm not the unlovable, inadequate one - they are!" So the narcissist in your life may be keeping tabs on you because they want to see the pain they've caused you. Whether it's the grief of a breakup, the loss of a loved one, or financial troubles - the narcissist wants to see you suffering so they can reassure themselves that they aren't the broken, worthless one. 3. They Want to Control How Others See You. Narcissists are actually terrified of the people they abuse. Absolutely terrified. You see, narcissists spend their whole lives carefully building and protecting the public image or persona they present to the world. This public persona makes them seem charming, confident, intelligent, successful, etc. This public persona is how narcissists get the validation, admiration and control they need to feel good about themselves. But the people they abuse can see past this false public image, because they've experienced the narcissist's true abusive nature. This is terrifying for a narcissist, because they know that if they lose power and control over the person they're abusing, that person could expose their true self to others and ruin their carefully crafted public image. One way narcissists try to prevent this is by using "flying monkeys" - people they manipulate into helping them isolate, discredit and silence the person they're abusing. So a big reason narcissists keep tabs on you is to maintain control over how others see you. They want to make sure you stay isolated, that your credibility is undermined, and that you're unable to speak out against them. column1: From the perspective of a stillbirth mother or a close family member, what does it feel like to give birth to or participate in the birth of a stillborn child?
column3: I worked as a Labor and Delivery nurse for 30 years. During that time, I took care of many patients who did not have that happy outcome that most people expect. Many of those patients were friends of mine. I came from one of those small towns where you know everyone. Mothers place a high expectation on themselves to protect their children. This can be seen in schools, on athletic fields and in all of those other instances of the helicopter moms who are always hovering to make sure that their child is safe. We feel that we are obligated to buffer our children from harsh realities and from pain. These feelings start from the very beginnings. When your child gets hurt, you many times suffer a feeling of guilt that you didn't prevent it. This feeling is compounded over and over when you lose a child at any stage. When a mother delivers a stillborn child, they suffer pain and many times guilt. They wonder if they could have prevented it. They wonder if there is something inherently wrong with them that prevents them from being able to deliver a healthy infant. Sometimes, they suffer a type of survivor's guilt as they wonder why they are all right when their baby is not. They are filled with many self doubts. The main advice I would give is to offer support. Encourage them to talk about their baby if they want to. Do not act as if there never was a baby. Ask if they are going to have a funeral. Remember them on Mother's Day. They will never forget that child, no matter how many other children they may have. You would not ask them to act as if their husband had never existed so don't act as if their child had never existed. Most of all, just be there and offer support without asking what is needed. Go to their house and mow the yard, do the laundry, wash the car, take out the trash, take them a meal or several. Arrange for meals for awhile after she goes home. Treat her with the same love and respect you would treat anyone who had just suffered a devastating loss.

column1: Why did you go no-contact with your family, and how long has it been since you saw them or spoke to them?
column3: My parents had four kids: my older sister, my older brother, my younger brother and myself. My dad died in 2001. My older brother died unexpectedly in 2011. My older sister died in 2012 and my brother-in-law, who was a brother to me, died a year after his wife, my sister, died. That left me and my younger brother and our mom. In 2013 my mom began showing signs of dementia. She was diagnosed with Lewey body dementia and it's progressing quickly. I've had to move in with her to keep her out of a long-term facility and in her own home. In doing so I lost living with my kids for the last couple of years I would've had with then before they moved out. I've not only become her caregiver, I've become her ONLY caregiver. Everybody has disappeared. EVERYONE. Including that younger brother of mine. Four years ago I finally told him I needed help, I'm taking care of everything including all the bills, and I am doing it all without a normal outside-of-the-home job and without a car. His two kids contacted me on Facebook, cussing me out, calling me names, accusing me of lying just to make their dad “look bad.” His son was so nasty and persistent I ended up blocking and reporting him to Facebook. Then my brother himself sent me a message, also calling me names, mocking me, and basically whining about the cost of having two kids in college (yeah, I know all about that - my daughter is a nurse and my son will soon be a teacher….they had to go to college for those degrees) and pretty much rolling around in self-pity and excuses. He then blocked me from contacting him. It's been four years since he called our mom, sent her a birthday card or Mother's Day card, it's been four years since either of us have heard one single sorry word from him. Our mom loved him, did nothing but love him and do things for him. She'd already gone through devastating losses of two children, plus her adored son-in-law, and then the diagnosis of dementia. Now she's lost another child in a way far worse than death - she lost him because of his selfishness, self-centeredness, greed, and complete lack of love for her. Who the hell, knowing the time's coming when they'll be forgotten entirely, goes ahead and ghosts their own mother first?? What kind of character does it take to do this? As far as I'm concerned I only had two siblings and they both died. I'm working from home, 5 jobs right now, so I can pay all the bills, the co-pays, the groceries, etc. My mom's Social Security check pays the rent and that's it. I have been unable to get my kids Christmas and birthday gifts I wanted to give them, I was unable to help my daughter pay for her wedding, I was unable to help my daughter purchase things she needed and wanted for her first baby, I was unable to help my son when he got his first car…..it was my ex-husband who did all of that. Every cent of my money goes to this. I get no vacations, I get no breaks, I am a nurse and cook and bill payer and house manager and plumber and repairer and problem-solver and I am all these things by myself. He takes his kids and wife on two vacations a year, his kids have all the latest toys and cars - as do he and his wife. They live in a house her mom gave them so he's not even making house payments or rent. He and his wife both make very comfortable yearly salaries. Meanwhile I'm trying to keep my promise to care for her, to keep her in her own home, for as long as possible. It was my choice, I could've said no I suppose, I could have turned my back on her like he's done. I love my mom but this entire situation has broken our relationship into tiny pieces. I'm stressed, exhausted, isolated, so when her dementia causes her to cuss at me, call me names, tell me to get out or to go to hell, I'm not as able to deal with it calmly as I'd like to be. She no longer recognizes me as her daughter and I find myself having conversations I never thought I'd have. I give her her meds every day, make the meals, and try my best to still be a mom to my kids and now a grandmother to my newborn granddaughter, to pay some of my OWN bills, to deal with my own grief and depression and heartbreak. I am losing my mom every day. I am going through the daily death of my mom, the only family member from my original family I have left. Sometimes the pain and grief for my lost sister and for the change in my mom knocks me flat on my face. I hope my brother has the sense to know not to show up when my mom dies. I have more than enough anger and disgust built up to have no problem at all throwing him out of a funeral home or this house. When she does ask about him and I have to cover for him to keep from hurting her it just makes me even angrier at him. He's entirely out of my life and I see absolutely nothing that could make me let him back in. Ever.
column9: I’m sorry for your troubles Lynna. Who’s to say that when his turn comes, his own kids won’t do to him what he did to your mother?! After all, they learned from the best. And you’re a wonderful daughter for taking care of her the way you do.

column1: Which is the most interesting character ever played in Malayalam cinema?
column3: My vote for this would be the character of Shammi played by Fahad Faasil in the movie Kumbalangi Nights.Although he is seen as the main antagonist in the movie, many people will secretly know that a son-in-law like him would often be seen as an asset to the family in several households in Kerala. He is shown as being impeccably dressed at all times. That perfectly done moustache steals the show.He is super protective of his in-laws. He takes care of his wife's sister as if she were his own sister and tries to shoo away a loser that she is romantically involved with saying that she deserves much better than the guy she has chosen.He does not approve of a home-stay guest inviting men over to spend the night with her and tells her so in no uncertain terms.He claims to be a self-made man. And he is very ‘caring’ towards his wife… calling her moley (an endearment in Malayalam that literally translates to daughter but… uh… never mind) and all that.But people who have watched the movie and saw the situation as a story unfolding would remember how much of a psycho he was. That madness in his eyes is unmissable. With every passing scene, our disgust for that character grows and grows. But if someone were to ask why do you hate him so? What has he done? You'll probably find yourself at a loss of arguments that seem like plausible reasons. And you might just keep repeating yourself that he's a psycho!This actually shows a very well-concealed aspect of Kerala society. Such characters actually exist in a much larger percentage than we'd like to accept. And all their deeds are whitewashed under the excuse of them being ‘responsible’… the ‘son and not a son-in-law’ phrase… the way many families tend to overlook behavioural oddities in new members of the family in the name of maintaining their image in society.There is a scene where Shammi is having a meal at somebody's house with his mother-in-law beside him. And you can see the way he talks on her behalf and on behalf of his wife's family… without even discussing it with them. And the mother-in-law meekly agrees with everything he says.She no longer cares what her daughters might have to say about it. The man of the house has spoken. And so it will be. So although he is a newlywed, he is already asserting his position in the household. Many people would ask… so what? They are the ones who don't see the red flags until somebody shoves a red flag down their throats.Shortly after the movie was released, I received a very interesting write-up about the character of Shammi. It's a bit lengthy but worth a read. Sharing the Google translated version here…Who is Shammi really? Psychologist's post goes viral A note written by psychologist Dr. Boban Eranimos about the character of Shammi went viral. The post is as follows: Shammi in Kumbalangi Nights comes in after having shaved and polished his face, the edges of his mustache have been neatly trimmed, his clothes have been washed and ironed and he has a naughty smile on his face. Shammi, who is outwardly dignified, deserves to be the definition of a representative of male Koima, who seeks to establish authority by subjugating others through advice and keeping women on a line. Is he just a representative of the average Malayalee's malevolence, who insists that only what he says is right, and thinks that a woman's voice should not be heard at home? Some signs of a pathological personality can be seen in Shammi, beyond the definitions of a man of power. Some of the symptoms of personality disorder/personality disorders can be found if you look very carefully. Personality disorders are one of the things that confuse mental health practitioners. (Personality Disorders) It is not something that can be diagnosed as quickly as a cardiologist using an electrocardiogram to detect heart rhythm disturbances in his patient, or a pulmonologist using a spirometry test to detect respiratory diseases. People with this disorder believe themselves to be normal and blame others. That is why such people do not approach mental health therapists for treatment. Shammi's character evaluates himself in such a way that the sick person sees himself as perfect, which makes it difficult for those who live with the patient. People at home understand personality problems more than others. Children and family members look at Shammi's behavior with a look that penetrates inside like the edge of the mustache and a frightening laugh. When Shammi is there or with Shammi's arrival, the house in Kumbalangi is unable to make a sound and goes into silence. Shammi, who behaves outwardly as a gentleman, does not immediately detect abnormality. Shammi, who cares for his family, cares for others and likes to work, is different from Napoleon's sons. While Shammi outwardly appears to be the perfect son-in-law for any mother-in-law, one can see the symptoms of a morbid personality disorder lurking on the other side of the spectrum. Shammi, who sends his dinner plate to his wife's house, which he eats within days of the wedding, may have lived in situations where he had to eat alone without family members during his childhood or teenage years? Many such unusual habits can be seen later. The character maintains the perfection beyond cleanliness in the dress, face and edges of the moustache. It's not because of Shammi's profession as a Barber. Shammi in Kumbalangi Nights is someine who cannot tolerate even a blemish seen in the mirror. With the thought of harming the perfection of his image, he scrapes it with a blade and throws it into the wash basin with a smile. By looking at his own body, the character who utters Raymond's catchphrase "A Complete Man" convinces himself that he is perfect in every way. Behind the dignified dress and the soft calls of "moloo", you can see some abnormalities lurking somewhere in the behavior and character. People with personality disorder or personality disorder are usually dressed modestly. If you look at it from the outside, you can't immediately find anything sick like Shammi. The society evaluates them as a person who is overly angry, a little strict, and has certain habits. Most of them will have a persuasive speaking style. Those who can influence others with tact will behave in such a way that others say that I am not a problem in front of the public. Such people do not have much difficulty in gaining the opinion of a person of good habits. But those who live with them can soon detect and understand the sickness in behavior and character. But if they tell this to others, they may laugh at it, dismiss it, saying that it's just a feeling and that you shouldn't slander a decent person. The day after the wedding, Simi's chest must have been tight with fear when Shammi was laughing and talking while revving the accelerator of the bullet. She is very scared and backs away. From there, the viewer begins to understand that Shammi is a person who finds fun in scaring others. Children who come to play in front of the house also understand that peculiar character. “He's not right” they discuss. Picking up the batted ball becomes scary for them. They come home in fear to search for the missing ball.Shammi stands in front of Simi and talks to them with love. It can be done by knowing that children cannot do the instructions that are given by suppressing the anger that is building up inside them. Shammi reminds the children through his cruel act that if they don't obey after one warning, there will be no question or answer. The character tries to make the impression that he is a poor man by behaving very respectably in the barber shop and at the wedding house, suppressing his mind to react, and gives his mother-in-law the freedom to comment on his wife's sister's marriage in front of the general society. It is his suspicion and not wish fulfillment that prompts him to sneak into the rented cottage. Hiding behind the kitchen door and asking, “You're not talking about me” (Suspiciousness). He is not satisfied with his wife's answer. He keeps asking again and again and again and again and again and again without any expression until the patience of the answerer wears out. The character who uses sharp words very mildly creates total fear in the family. Simi prepares to reply “nothing” as he asks her to swear to be frank and is sure things will change when he is done. She knows that if she enters the bedroom, Shammi can bring out whatever is inside her through mental torture. Here you can see the reflection of the morbid doubt within. Simi's response to Shammi who insults her sister after taking power by pulling the chair is unbearable. Shammi faints in front of his wife and others as if he has been slapped. Shammi, who goes to the corner of the room and turns her back like a child, may have had a childhood of crying in the corner of the classroom or home after hearing punishments and reprimands? He turns away silently and frightens others and puts him under a lot of mental stress, and returns to his old state with a smile. The fluctuations of emotional states can be seen on a large scale (Emotional Instability) at this time. It can be understood that this is not the first time that Shammi has behaved like this many times before the wedding and from the friend's conversation that "it will change after a while". Shammi laughingly saying "just miss" can be considered as symptoms of illness, where subjugating others through force beyond words is seen as fun like playing a game. The other characters cower in fear at the manner of the attack. They always realize that they cannot win by force. We don't know anything about Shammi's family or childhood. But it is unlikely to be a happy childhood. The reasons for Shammi's personality disorder may have arisen from the distressing, frightening and tortuous experiences of childhood and adolescence. Kumbalangi Nights reminds us that there are many Shammies among us with personality disorders who have grown up through unpleasant experiences.Do please excuse the grammatical errors. Google translated stuff is still shoddy but it manages to get the idea across. If you haven't watched the movie, go watch it, guys. Highly recommended! 👏🏼

column1: Do all NPD parents feel they need a scapegoat?
column3: Do all NPD parents feel they need a Scapegoat? The answer is Yes! If the parent is a ‘fully-fledged NPD’ they will allocate the role of family Scapegoat to whichever of their children is the most sensitive and empathetic member of the family! This is why the role of Family Scapegoat is such an insidiously cruel and traumatising experience for this caring and compassionate child. Had the child been born into a healthy family rather than this toxic ‘cult-like’ family headed by a sick and disordered toxic parent, the child would have been loved and cherished for being the beautiful caring human-being that they are, but instead they experienced a lifetime of abuse. One of the reasons why a dysfunctional ‘enmeshed’ family headed by an NPD parent, is able to function or should I say “appear to function albeit dysfunctionally” is because the disordered parent made one of the other members of the family a ‘Scapegoat’. The NPD parent will Project all of their own failings and faults and toxic traits onto the Scapegoated child, and the other members of the family will accept this as their reality. It becomes their truth! The chosen ‘Scapegoated’ child is forced (unknowingly) from a very young age to bare the brunt of the families problems, taking the blame for all that is ‘bad or rotten’ in their enmeshed family. The NPD parent is unable to carry their own shame, or take responsibility for their faults, floors, failings and toxic behaviour, so the parent projects these negative traits and behaviours onto the innocent family Scapegoat. Over time the Scapegoat is gradually devalued, belittled, criticised and abused…..but because they have been conditioned to accept the negative treatment since a very young age….they simply don’t know what is occurring? This has been their life! The Scapegoat has likely protested their innocence on countless occasions throughout their life, the familiar feeling that life was unfair, but they don’t know anything other than this, so just like the rest of their family, they too eventually learn to accept this as ‘the norm’. Eventually the Scapegoated child starts to believe the relentless negative messaging… they start to internalise the messaging that they are ‘not good enough’ and their own needs and feelings ‘don’t matter’. All of which of course is not true. It exists for the sole purpose of ‘avoidance and distraction’, and allows the toxic NPD parent to avoid any accountability for their abusive behaviour… successfully masking the ‘real issue’ within the family. ——————————————————————— WHAT ARE YOU WORTH? Imagine if you will that the NPD parent has allocated each member of this ‘enmeshed’ family a ‘value’ between Zero (Worthless) and 10 (Very Important). You literally have no control over your value, this being especially true for a young child who is simply just being a child? In the Scapegoated child’s case, they are penalised and abused for no reason other than being an empathetic human. Nobody in the family talks about this….it’s not a conscious thought, nor is it ever acknowledged…but it’s how the family operates, and each persons ‘position’ can change around in the blink of an eye….just like that! The Narc Parent is always and forever valued at 10 and this never changes! This is rule number one….and it must not be challenged. The Golden Child is a 9 and rarely ever drops below this value unless the Golden Child does something that warrants them being devalued……which is rare! The other parent and other children can hover anywhere from a 5 to an 8….depending on their conformance level and their dedication to the selfish demands of the NPD parent. The Scapegoat however sits at a two or a three, or maybe even a four if things are good, which is usually because the Scapegoat has been 100% submissive. But no matter what…..whatever they do, or whatever they achieve….the Scapegoat will never, ever, get THERE? The Scapegoat will always and forever be devalued! It’s literally impossible to change this dynamic, because it’s the one thing that allows the remainder of the family to ‘maintain’ the false image of perfection? It’s a subconscious strategy of survival! Without a Scapegoat the rest of the family would be forced to face reality which is something they cannot do for a whole bunch of reasons. Everyone’s forbidden from acknowledging the REAL dysfunction in the family (the NPD parent) thus there will ALWAYS be a Scapegoat wherever there is a disordered NPD parent ruling a ‘dysfunctional’ family unit!After a lifetime of being unheard, ignored, overlooked, lied to and mistreated……it is because of our unlimited access to the wealth of information on the internet in the present day that Scapegoat’s have an even greater chance of ‘Waking Up’. When the Scapegoat works through their pain after breaking free from the abuse, eventually the Scapegoat will find the strength to accept ‘Reality’, instead of the ‘False Reality’ created by their NPD parent. This false reality being something the Scapegoat had forced upon them for the majority, if not for their entire life. If and when the time comes, the Scapegoat will challenge the NPD parent and ‘name the abuse’ to the other members of the family…..even going as far as to share the abuse with extended family members. In doing so the Scapegoat will cause the NPD parent to incur a mortal Narcissistic Injury, and this will be the final straw for their Toxic parent! This will (in most cases) result in the Scapegoat being disowned and discarded…..and with extreme prejudice! Yes…..the Scapegoat will more than likely lose their entire family over the coming months, however by confronting their evil parent and ‘demanding’ that the truth be allowed to breath…. for the first time in their life, the Scapegoat is on their way to discovering their real true-self! The innocent victim of parental abuse and family mobbing will finally understand the meaning of, and will finally have, or at least…they will be capable of having…. genuine ‘Self-Love’. At last…the Scapegoat is free from the toxic behaviour they have been an innocent victim to for their entire lives! When the Scapegoat ‘Awakens’ they will almost immediately find themselves alone and isolated, living in their pain….shell-shocked by the absolute terror of what is happening to them? The depth of the betrayal is incomprehensible for anyone else to truly understand….but that’s OK! This is YOUR pain. This is the Scapegoats pain! You know it’s there…the pain is immense! The Scapegoats ‘family’ will do everything they can to dismiss and deny everything, not even allowing the Scapegoat to have their grief or their anger……they dont even get to have their sadness. FUCK THAT? Don’t let them take that away from you. Stand in your truth, and you Grieve it! ‘Feel’ your feelings. Grieve your loss. Grieve for the hundreds of losses that you’ve had throughout your life that you were never allowed to feel because others wouldn’t let you? Educate yourself about who you were in your ‘Enmeshed’ and dysfunctional family? Understand why you were chosen as the Scapegoat? Sure….do whatever you feel you must to try and save certain familial relationships that you feel you cannot lose, but just make sure from the very start that you accept the ‘possibility’ that your only true salvation in the end will be to just ‘Let Go’. You deserve more…..and all you have to do to have a life that is Truly yours is simply understand that you can! You just have to go and live it! And you will. Use the pain to fuel the birth of the new you…. the birth of your new life. Love yourself and admire your own strength. column1: Am I Over-Reacting? To give a bit of background, I've been diagnosed with C-PTSD, and my husband has been disabled for going on 16 years. He has repeated health crises, which cause me lots of worry and stress due to triggers with seeing people I love suffer and my fears of loss. Another huge trigger from the past is being repeatedly leftalone in crisis as a child without help from my mom. Recently, my husband was struck with a very painful attack that left him unable to walk for 11 days. Early on, my t texted me to see how he was doing. A few days later on my Zoom session, I told her he still couldn't walk, but I was handling it OK. However, 3 days later, the situation became overwhelming, and I texted to let her know we were both at the breaking point, and my energy and resolve were crumbling. Instead of acknowledging my feelings or offering any words of comfort, she said, "I hope you've contacted your congregation for support...errands, meals?" Then...nothing. 3 days later, I sent another text, telling her that I'd felt a bit pushed away by her response, but that I knew she probably didn't mean it that way. I acknowledged that it's important to get outside support. She didn't respond. Later, I texted to tell her that my husband was able to walk some now, I'd probably be able to come for my session in person if she still planned to be there (it's scheduled for today. She's Jewish, so doesn't celebrate Christmas). She didn't reply to that message either. By then, I really was feeling pushed away and ignored, so I said so. She replied that she wasn't ignoring me. In her busyness, she didn't realize I needed a response. This didn't help me feel any better. If anything, it made me feel that she was not aware of, or in tune with, my feelings or situation at all. She knows how stressful the situation with my husband's health is, and I'd let her know previously that things were reaching a breaking point! Also, we've worked together for many years, and she well knows that not getting a reply from her when I'm in crisis triggers all my old "stuff" from the past. I feel very hurt! It feels like when I reached out in crisis for support, she more or less advised me to get it elsewhere and then promptly forgot about the whole thing and put me out of her mind. Am I over reacting? She has always told me I can reach out when I need to.
column3: Your situation reminds me very much of a situation I was in with a good friend of mine… except… I am not a therapist & I was on the other side of the situation. Perhaps me sharing it tho can help something… I hope… My friend and I, we both have mental health issues and would gain support from one another, it was a fairly enjoyable and reciprocal relationship for quite a while. However, when things in life shifted… for both of us… schedules changed… my friend ended up wanting me to meet up in ways that no longer worked for me. I told her that it didn’t work for me… (I shared what would work but that didn’t suit her…ok) she was not pleased with this fact… she felt I was being mean by “withholding” what she needed from me. I told her “you don’t NEED me” and this kinda made lots come crashing down. I was mad at her for holding me responsible for meeting her “needs” and felt it an unfair burden to place on a friend. She was now placing an expectation on me to meet… irregardless of if I felt it was reciprocally beneficial anymore or not. I guess she thought I should sacrifice for the friendship in the way she wanted and was asking for it. I disagreed… vehemently so. What friend wants me to meet up against my own will?? What friend wants me to meet when to do so actually is causing me harm in some areas of life? …Cause she “needs” me to?! So… here is how I tried framing it… needless to say… it all ended poorly… she didn’t agree at all to my framing… I feel my situation and your situation can be thought of in pragmatic terms as a difference between the term support vs the term dependent. I resented that my friend was behaving like my dependent… she suddenly “needed” me and tied her sense of mental health stability to my presence in a certain way that she came to expect. This way of organizing a relationship is simply not adaptive. For her to hold me in such position… well… (according to her & I don’t deny such) it caused her harm to herself for me being not able to meet that expectation. If my friend is having a crisis… my thought is… she doesn’t need me. She needs 911 or some crisis intervention team or such. That is not to say that I would not be there to support any of my close friends in a crisis situation. I will gladly be with a friend needing admit into a hospital and needing support… or some other urgent care situation… now here tho is the caveat… so long as I also can self-care and maintain my role as the caregiver of my own family. It cannot interfere with my other life roles and responsibilities and ultimately I do need to self-care for me lots. Now… on the other hand… my son IS my dependent. He is disabled and needs help advocating for himself at times and sometimes needs basic care stuff done for him. Not always… but I do consider him my responsibility. I do tho also expect that he seek out other care team members as appropriate and as he is able. He does. I do not expect to be in a codependent relationship with him where he is expecting me to perform tasks for him that he is able to do without me. So what is different for me having a dependent… I literally will change the structure of what is my responsibility when he is in crisis. I will take off work as able when he needs urgent care… I will pause some self-care and prioritize his needs and pause my own self-care when he is in distress. I won’t tho do what I do for my son for a friend or person I work with at my job… not usually… not as a default. It may happen… I have taken off work to be with someone at a high risk birth… but as a default… as an expectation… no… I cannot forfeit my own care for others. It isn’t good for me and isn’t a good example to anyone else. My friend tho was “falling apart” and blaming me for not being there for the friendship. She felt my presence and support would help her maintain her mental health. I felt that maybe she look into what the friendship is providing and seek that in her life since I couldn’t offer what she was asking. She is not my dependent. I am still and was adamant about that fact discussing this with her. It is not my doing that she enlisted me into a role that I did not sign up for. If tho… she needed some emotional support or even physical support and I was available… I absolutely would fill in for that role if able. I tho see this way different than my child who is a dependent of mine. A support role is just that… it is nice to have… and something to be glad to have good friends… but it is NOT my job and ongoing expectation to drop my life… my literal job… my other responsibilities to fill it. It is by choice if I happen to… not by obligation at all. When you were a child and your mom neglected you… she neglected allowing you to be her dependent. You were literally dependent on adults for your survival… for the fact of being a child. That is no longer the case now. You are not a ward of the state. No one is your guardian ad liden… even a legal guardian ad liden can only be as available as they can after they care for themself too. So… as an adult… while we may still carry the longings of unmet child needs of expectation of another adult to rescue us… the reality is… unless you give up your freedom to choose decisions alone by assigning for yourself a legal guardian… you are solely responsible for you. As it should be. It is nice to be able to form a support network to help relieve stress to make functioning manageable… like asking people at church to bring you things… and utilizing available resources. Being reminded of available resources IS support. It sounds tho like you were depending your stability on some particular way of speaking to you or “holding your hand through it” kinda support. Sounds like you had in mind a kinda support you felt you were promised by her… a kind it sounds like she isn’t intending to offer. I bring up the idea of support vs dependent cause I see support can happen in many forms. It is something to be grateful for whatever level we can receive from others that they are able… not something to demand of them. The contrast… is that of a child… they demand a caretaker who assumes full responsibility for their outcome… they are dependent. When you ask if you overreacted… my answer is… well… perhaps your feelings are not rooted in what happened today. Perhaps they are mixed with feelings from the past of not getting what you fully needed and deserved as a young child and being aware of the source of your feeling disappointed… it may be helpful to realize and hold in mind… that you were a young child and not only was it reasonable to expect your caregivers to take responsibility of you… and demand that… they should have. They should have cared and nurtured the dependence in safe healthy ways so that such feeling integrated into all of who you are and helped build your internalized self worthiness for much. I’m sorry this didn’t happen as it should. I hope some of this makes sense and is heard with love for much that is worthy of loving. 🙏

column1: How do I tell my 9-year-old foster son that we will be adopting his younger half-sister, but not him (he'll be removed to a group home)?
column3: I was adopted. I too went through the foster care as well as orphanage at different points. I was lucky - to an extent with my family. My twin sister and I were both adopted by my parents. My adoptive uncle - adopted 3 of my brothers The other 4 children - went into the system (they were older) Growing up - I knew me and my sister. My brothers by my uncle were cousins and only that. We lost the “close family” connection - even though we lived a few blocks away. My uncle and my adoptive parents were in different financial classes so im sure that affected some of it. The other family members i had - i knew of - remembered but never saw until i found my bio family after the age of 18. With that said - Im going to be completely unrepentantly brash and open about my opinion on this. Note: this is not directed specifically to the OP - but is more of a general statement.I don’t understand how this is allowed.Children already have lost family in some way. Either to neglect, loss of life (parents) or some other crazy situation that none should be in to begin with.These children have already at a young age - have been through things adults may never have to experience - the sense of loss - lack of self-worth - no real home to call your ownNow - in your situation - you want to take a 9-year-old boy - and say You are not good enough for our family. Your sister is though. You will be leaving and may never see your sister again. Does this sound overly harsh? Good. No matter how you twist the words - this is how the child will see it. There is not a good way to tell a child they are not worth the effort. It disgusts me that this is still possible. People can procreate - and if responsible, raise the kids regardless of like/dislike of behaviors. I liken then adoptive process to getting a dog. These children are put on sites - with their good behaviors and interests outright. You can pick and choose children like a freaking vending machine and separate those you don't want. I don’t agree with your decision. But it is my opinion and that alone. I share it to give a different view. You did not mention this in your original question. I will ask here. Are you planning on allowing the children visitation to one another - or to be able to communicate? Or do you plan to set it so they are not allowed to do so.

column1: Why do Republicans think refugees are illegal immigrants when we all know that they come here through a legal process?
column3: Refugees are people displaced by an actual war or natural disaster, like a major earthquake. See: TPS Program. They are not immigrants or migrants. Refugees are people seeking temporary shelter until the war is over or the natural disaster ends and is cleaned up so it is safe to go back. Then they go back. They don’t stay after the emergency is over. Asylum seekers are not refugees. They are people seeking protection from government persecution in their home country for specific issues such as their race, religion, or political affiliation. They should come to a legal port of entry and claim asylum. If they sneak across the border, they are illegal aliens, at least until they are confronted by Border Control and request asylum. If their claim is not granted and they do not self-deport, then they are illegal aliens subject to capture and deportation with loss of privilege to reapply. Economic migrants, those escaping domestic violence or gangs, or seeking better jobs, or free education, medical care, and birth citizenship for their kids, or to be united with other illegal family members already in the US, are not asylum candidates, refugees, or legitimate immigrants. Unless they obtain legal documentation and enter through an official port of entry, they are illegal aliens subject to capture and deportation. Hope that clears it up for you.

column1: What are the potential consequences of the Trump Administration changing the "public charge" rules?
column3: We were never supposed to look like this. Until 1965, immigration to the United States was determined by a blatantly discriminatory national quota system. The brainchild of Congressman Albert Johnson, this system used the findings of a 1907 Congressional Report, the "Dictionary of Races or Peoples", to determine what ethnicities to prioritize for entry into the United States.People coming from Northern and Western European countries were heavily favored over those from countries like those Trump now derides. More than 50,000 immigrant visas were reserved for Germany each year. The United Kingdom had the next biggest share, with about 34,000. Ireland, with 28,000 slots, and Norway, with 6,400, had the highest quotas as a share of their population. Each country in Asia, meanwhile, had a quota of just 100, while Africans wishing to move to America had to compete for one of just 1,200 visas set aside for the entire continent.Despite fierce opposition from President Truman in 1952, this system continued mostly unchanged until 1965, when, in the wake of the Civil Rights movement, advocates sought to bring immigration policy in line with other anti-discriminatory measures. Congress found itself in a pickle. There was sizable pressure to undo the codification of discrimination in immigration law, yet few wanted to change the ethnic makeup of the country.“The people of Ethiopia have the same right to come to the United States under this bill as the people from England, the people of France, the people of Germany, [and] the people of Holland,” complained Senator Sam Ervin, a Democrat from North Carolina. “With all due respect to Ethiopia,” Ervin said, “I don’t know of any contributions that Ethiopia has made to the making of America.”Representative Micheal Feighan, a Democrat from Ohio, came up with a compromise. Instead of using national quotas, America would prioritize the family of United States citizens. It was simple, the vast majority of Americans were white, and prioritizing their relatives meant that the vast majority of future migrants would be white. This would prevent an officially discriminatory policy, while retaining the then current ethnic makeup of the United States. As described in an issue of The American Legion Magazine:It preserved the bulk of the national-origins base of immigration to the United States, but keyed it to a system of preferences rather than quotas.But Feighan had made a huge miscalculation. In the following decades, immigration from Europe would fall flat, while immigration from Asia and Latin America would rise drastically. The phenomenon that followed, in which these immigrants would migrate to the United States and go on to sponsor other members of their family, would result in the exact diversification that many supporters of this bill sought to prevent. This law is still the basis for our immigration system today, and while refugees and employment-based migrants do represent sizable portions of our legal non-citizen population, the majority still come via family-based migration.Of the more than 1 million new green-card holders in 2016, 48 percent were immediate relatives of U.S. citizens, 20 percent entered through a family-based preference, and 12 percent via an employment-based preference. Another 13 percent adjusted from refugee or asylee status, and 4 percent were diversity lottery winners.It is this prioritization scheme that President Trump, with his proposed expansion of the public charge rule, hopes to undercut. This executive order would give the Trump Administration great leeway in determining the makeup of immigrants to the United States, without legislation from Congress. The impact of this change would go far beyond incoming migrants, with potentially severe ramifications for public health, intergenerational mobility, and the American Economy. This would be the most significant change in federal immigration policy in decades and among the most consequential decisions of Trump’s presidency. What is a Public Charge? The best description would be an immigrant deemed an excessive cost to the United States government. Under the current federal policy, if an immigrant is deemed excessively dependent upon government benefits, they can be considered a “public charge” and thereby made inadmissible to the United States.For purposes of determining inadmissibility, “public charge” means an individual who is likely to become primarily dependent on the government for subsistence, as demonstrated by either the receipt of public cash assistance for income maintenance or institutionalization for long-term care at government expense.The current policy was set following the 1996 Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Act, under which the public benefits available to recent immigrants were drastically reduced. Right now, only cash benefits (TANF) and government-funded institutional care are considered, with only 3% of current immigrants using benefits that could be used in a public charge determination. The Trump Administration intends to modify this rule, with the proposed revision including cash, healthcare, food, and tax benefits. Below is an overview of the proposed changes.In light of these changes, there would be a new determination scheme with the following negative and positive factors. NegativeAuthorization to work without employment prospectsCurrent use or receipt of one of these benefits/tax credits.Use or receipt of public assistance within the last 36 monthsPresence of a medical condition and presumed necessity of government means in paying or treatmentA previous public charge determinationOther factors as warranted, according to DHS discretionPositiveFinancial assets. resources, and support of at least 250 percent of the federal poverty levelWork authorization and current employment with an annual income of at least 250% of federal poverty guidelines.Other factors as warranted, according to DHS discretionBenefit use by individuals and their dependents would be considered. This would drastically increase the number of immigrants that could be deemed a public charge, going from 3 to 47% of the non-citizen population. States with larger immigrant communities and more immigrant-friendly welfare systems, like California and New York, would be especially affected.The latest draft indicated that the Administration has not decided if a public charge determination should be grounds for deportation. If this were to occur, the number of unauthorized immigrants within the United States could drastically increase, and many previously legally present immigrants could face deportation for their or their families use of public benefits. Children's Health The ramifications of this rule change go far beyond these migrants. Millions of them have citizen children, a significant portion of whom have Medicaid/CHIP coverage.Most of these parents work, yet 67% have incomes below 250% the FPL encouraged by these new guidelines. This could make permanent entry into the United States very difficult for these parents, and risks destabilizing the lives of their American children.This policy could drastically reduce use rates of benefit programs among immigrants, even among those who couldn’t be deemed a public charge. After the 1996 bill several non-determinable immigrants and their relatives (refugees, beneficiary children) stopped using welfare benefits, a decline not accounted for by increased naturalization or rising income. The fear of losing future citizenship, coupled with the possible threat of deportation, and the hostility surrounding immigration today, could result in a massive exodus of children from public benefit programs. The Kaiser Family Foundation estimates that around 75% of disenrollees would become uninsured. If the dis-enrollment rate is high enough, millions of American children could lose access to health services.The positive effect of healthcare on children’s health is well documented, and such a mass exodus could spark a miniature public health crisis. Current immigration rhetoric and fear towards this proposal has already sparked a downturn in benefit applications in Central Texas.Under the proposed change, if family members receive government services — even if those family members are citizens — it would ding the applicants' chances of approval for permanent residency. “We are seeing families having to make this impossible choice,” says Maria Hernandez, the founder of Vela, a non-profit in Austin that helps parents who have children with disabilities.Moreover, widespread withdrawal's from SNAP could result in these children losing an essential means of combating food insecurity. As noted by the Children's Health Watch:These data suggest that young children from families that have been cut off from SNAP or had their SNAP benefits reduced when their income exceeds eligibility limits are significantly more likely to be in poor health, be at risk for developmental delays and experience child food insecurity than those whose families currently receive benefits.These changes could harm the prospects of some of our greatest economic contributors, second-generation immigrants. Generational View of Immigrants While immigrants may, on average, earn less than American citizens, it’s important to consider their fiscal impact from a generational perspective. The tax contributions of first generation immigrants are significantly lower than the native born. However, their descendants’ tax contributions are noticeably higher than their own, and are even greater than third-plus generation immigrants.Wages across immigrant generations reflect this trend, with second-generation immigrants again outperforming their predecessors and successors.We see the same in education, though our incoming immigrant population is more educated than it was in the past, resulting in less of an educational disparity than previous generations. However, first-generation immigrants compare remarkably well when considering federal benefit use per capita, with these immigrants likely to use less federal benefits over the course of their lives. This is particularly noticeable among the elderly, with elderly immigrants averaging thousands less per year in received benefits than succeeding generations. While the first generation is more costly to the government due to smaller tax contributions, their lower benefit usage does not support the notion of excessive dependency.Moreover, low TANF usage rates and high employment rates in immigrant families suggests that immigrants are likely to use welfare policies as work supports, with non-citizens and naturalized citizens in benefits receiving families being employed at higher rates than U.S born citizens.Altogether, we see clear evidence here of upward progression across generations. Many immigrants come here poor, yet they work at higher rates when receiving benefits, average less benefit use per capita when factoring in age, and their children tend to earn more and make higher tax contributions than other natives. Role in the American Economy However, it would be a mistake to delineate the contributions of first-generation immigrants to some tax dollar to benefit use ratio. Immigrants, poor and wealthy, make up sizable portions of many American industries. They work in numerous sectors that are unpopular to American citizens, and increasing specialization has seen their representation in several fields go up over time.Over time, low-skilled immigrants have become more specialized in particular lines of work. The share employed in immigrant-intensive sectors in 2015 reaches 14.8 percent in construction (from 7.8 percent in 1990), 11.3 percent in eating and drinking establishments (from 8.7 percent in 1990), 7.2% in personal services (from 6.9% in 1990), and 6.9 percent in agriculture (from 5.7% in 1990).That isn’t to say all aspects of immigration are positive. Immigrants may slightly decrease the wages of similarly skilled natives, and costs associated with immigration are disproportionately assigned to state governments. Yet the benefits provided by these immigrants are manifold. They are responsible for the continued growth of our labor force, increase aggregate demand, increase productivity, are critical to the “care economy”, and their communities often serve as fertile grounds for new businesses.These communities are especially important. They provide a social and economic bedrock for these immigrants and serve as incubators for many hopeful entrepreneurs among them. Immigrants account for 90% of self-employment growth since 2000, with growth among “low skilled” immigrants being especially high. Altogether immigrants are on average far more entrepreneurial than American citizens, and as noted by Representative Zoe Lofgren,I often say I am glad that Google is in Mountain View rather than Moscow. Like eBay, Intel and Yahoo!, Google was founded by an immigrant. But it’s worth noting that none of the founders of these companies came to the U.S. because of their skills.There’s also evidence to suggest that low-income migrants exude an upward pressure on natives in an increasingly automatized economy, causing them to pursue higher wage productive occupations and protecting them from many of automation’s pitfalls.The increasing number of low-wage positions, such as manual-intensive personal services, was mostly filled by immigrants, thus moderating the resulting upward wage pressure. This contributed to push natives to upgrade their skills and join better paying production occupations, even as employment of computer capital continued to rise. This reduced the ‘de-routinisation’ of native employment and boosted natives’ routine and analytical wages through an increase in aggregate demand.The benefits provided by low income immigrants might not be obvious when only considering taxes. But they are an important cog in the American machine, and their loss would be felt. Looking Ahead In threatening the legal status of these immigrants, we risk increased unemployment, an increased unauthorized population, a labor shortage in several key American industries, a loss of entrepreneurship, a spike in the uninsured population, increased hunger, increased child poverty, and endangering some of our most productive future taxpayers. These immigrants are not on the periphery waiting to enter, they are contributing inhabitants of our country. They work in our fields and hospitals, our homes and restaurants, our roads and our factories. Their children attend our schools and share our playgrounds. The Trump administration has often questioned the place of immigrants in the United States, and in light of this proposal, Americans have an important choice to make. These immigrants have worked to become ours. Will we allow them to? Glossary and Miscellaneous Information Non-Citizen: Any person in the United States, legally or illegally, who is not a citizen. Non-Determinable Immigrant: immigrants who cannot be determined a public charge Beneficiary children: benefit receiving children with non-citizen parents Care Economy: “Part of human activity, both material and social, that is concerned with the process of caring for the present and future labour force, and the human population as a whole, including the domestic provisioning of food, clothing and shelter. “ Graphs showing wages, tax contributions, education and benefit usage display averages per age.
