column1: What is it like to be discreetly wealthy?
column3: I grew up with a lot of wealth on one side of my family. My step father was extremely wealthy, worth in excess of $300M (in Italy) in the late 80's and early 90's, which was at the time like being worth $3B in the US today. Attaining that kind of wealth in Italy (from nothing) is significantly more difficult than in the US. My actual father did fairly well, over time building a company from scratch to a $10M operation. But he let his ego and greed go to his head, ultimately it cost him pretty much everything. By the time I was 14 it was clear that if I was going to make it in this world, that I would have to do it on my own. Truthfully, I think it's the best route to take. I started working as soon as I was allowed to by my mother and step father, which was 15. Growing up around ridiculous wealth on one side of my family gave me a front row seat to all of the positives and negatives that come along with it. Not so much for my mother, step father and me, but really the other wealthy people around us. The wealthiest people I know, they're some of the most cursed ones too. One thing that my mother and step father made sure to make clear, was that the reason he obtained that wealth, was through almost two decades of 18 hour days and quite frankly making the business the main focus of his lifes work. It's not to say that he wasn't a good father, he was, in fact he was a better father than my real dad. I wouldn't see him that often, but the time when he was home, it was really quality time. To see a man, so exhausted by his endless passion to keep his business thriving, reach within and find a way to connect with me in a more meaningful way than my real father, well it's something that has had a massive impact in my life. I also want to note, that my step father too didn't get caught up in his wealth. I didn't know it when I was young, but one of the main reasons he worked so exhaustively, making the business his main focus, was really more about keeping the 500+ people he employed in a good standard of living. He was incredibly generous with all of the people who worked with him, even to the point of hurting the business at times. He didn't call people his employees, but instead family members or team members. The only thing I'd say that he did that some might find to be conspicuous consumption, was spend a lot of money on really amazing suits and clothes. He also had sunglasses custom made that were about $1,500 a pair, but it wasn't to show off by any means because no one but me and my mother knew that. He was just a really stylish and cool guy. My life, unique as it was, and being able to look at these two men, who couldn't have been more different, it's shaped who I am, personally and professionally. About four years ago I finally worked through a really bad period of my life where I was just really depressed and unsure about what I wanted to do or if I even cared about life at all. I thought about living in the woods just to be completely alone and I'm sad to say, at times, I thought seriously about taking my own life. I finally got serious about life, and attaining certain goals and just being a better person in general. So within about a year and a half after pulling myself out of a five year funk, out of nothing I created a company that I would personally net about $1.3M from. (technology/advertising) So from the absolute edge, and truly a path of self destruction, to finding peace with life at last and great success, all within about 18 months from that turning point. My closest friends, who kind of watched me self destruct, now they often say things like, "We knew that you were capable of doing all of this, we knew that the real you was going to come back, we're just really glad you survived it all." So the first pretty good exit, the $1.3M, I didn't do anything crazy with the money, one thing I really didn't do was tell anyone at the time. I mostly just reinvested it into a new business. I did buy an investment house in which I lost about $400,000 on, waterfront, bad timing, such is life. I also invested into a business I shouldn't have that I couldn't run or help with, another $200,000 loss. But the rest went into this new business, or really I should say businesses. Fast forward to today, all of these businesses, collectively are worth far more than I ever imagined. I run three of them and a few more I'm the majority owner of. This, is just a result of me working like my step father did, and I'm also doing it now, pulling 20 hour days so I can actually be around when I have kids. My biological father taught me how people let money ruin them. He showed me how greed and ego can destroy a man, a family and have consequences that carry over further down the line if you let it. Now, my father is looking at me as his retirement fund, wanting to invest in everything I create. By invest I mean throw $15,000 into one of my companies and ask for a massive stake in exchange. Having to say no, well I've come to start to enjoy it, I'm not proud of that. He just cares about the money, and it really never stops hurting. Even though I don't care about money and plan on giving most of what I earn from the sale of these businesses to friends, family and self sufficient charities, his goal, of wanting to have essentially what amounts to a piece of "me" meaning, reap the rewards of my hard work, well it is something that has just created an even larger divide between us. It's also making me really question how I would even consider letting him be around my own kids in the next few years. I'm getting married soon to an amazing woman who has been with me before all of the recent businesses had taken off. She also doesn't mind that I drive an eight year old Mitsubishi and rarely dress like someone with "money". She's my muse and a big reason I was able to move out of my downward spiral. I spent 50X as much time with my biological father than with my step father. Yet, I don't know who I should give more credit to for helping me become the person I am today, me the man who just doesn't give a shit about money and cares about things that truly matter. The person who realizes that money is that thing that can so easily ruin what should be something great, family. My step father, he was/is a great man. My biological father, well he's just someone who I wish was so different but I know never will be. My advice would be the following: Money can come and go. You can do both great and terrible things with it. If you make a lot of money quickly, people will most likely find out, even if you drive an eight year old car and dress down. Just never let money become something that forces you to hurt the people you should actually love.
column9: With regard to how I was able to pull myself together, it came as a result of me putting myself into the wringer. My downward spiral really came to a close when I just finally took a step back and started to appreciate what was actually meaningful in life. I got to a point where I was ready to get away from everyone, I just needed time away. To learn from my mistakes and remove negative influences from my life. I basically moved away from my friends and family for about a year. I stayed in touch, but I needed space and a new place to just really reflect on what had brought me to this point, the point of needing to learn from everything and make things better on my own. Sometimes people say they need to move away to reinvent themselves, wipe the slate clean, but I feel like that's bullshit and a crutch. Don't try to forget the past, embrace it. If things aren't great, then start to actually sit down and think about everything that has led to that point. Go way back, to when you were a kid, maybe there's something there. I honestly think that by the time people are 16 years old, all of your life experiences to that point, they've basically molded you into who you are and fundamentally will be. Now that doesn't mean that if you had a terrible or tragic life that there's no hope, in fact I think it can be the opposite. I'm also not saying that people don't mature beyond that age, or that they can't modify their behavior or learn to better control personality traits that they might have that negatively impact their lives. Of course you can make adjustments, but if you were ignored or under appreciated as a child it might force you to be too willing to please others as an adult. On the flip side, if you displayed an extraordinary amount of athletic ability at age five, and were told by a parent from then on that you had no peers, well you might end up playing a sport professionally, but you might also end up being an outrageous arrogant and selfish person because no one taught you about humility or struggle. If I had to pick three things that really made a difference, and allowed me to remove myself from the path of self destruction.. It was finally accepting who I am. I'm the guy ignored by my biological father and truly loved by a man who wasn't but treated me like the son he never had. I never wanted to admit that someone, who at times in my life I've sincerely loathed, that he actually influenced me so much, but he did. I had to learn to accept that there's no going back and he is who he is, and I either get over it and keep him within my life on my terms, or frankly kick him the fuck out. It's difficult, because you want to not give up hope. "Maybe one day he'll actually figure out what a great kid I was and that he will regret that he missed out on being a great dad. Maybe he'll be embarrassed that his son learned to play baseball from his mom." (It's cool, she was very athletic) So accepting that my biological father had such an influence on who I am and how I would react to things in life in general, it was hard. The second thing, it was accepting responsibility for my mistakes. In order for me to move on with my life, I had to be willing to accept that it was my own actions that brought me to that place. I can't use the past as a crutch to absolve me of my bad behavior or as a way to make future poor choices acceptable. Learn from the past, don't ignore or bury it only to repeat the process again and again. Accept it, remember it, keep it in your mind when you're presented with life's choices. You end up learning a lot about yourself and how to make changes for the betterment of your life when you can just accept all of the things that you personally did. I know that maybe you think I didn't have it so bad, growing up around and or with a lot of money. You're wrong, as charmed as some moments of my life were, there were lots of terrible ones. Some moments were brutal and if I really were to put it all out for all to read, you might think I should probably be dead, in prison, or in some terrible moment capable of taking someone's life. The last and final thing I had to do, was give myself the opportunity to be what I really wanted. I know what you're thinking, "well thanks for that gem captain obvious." But the thing I really wanted was to be happy, I just didn't know what happy was. I couldn't do that, or figure it out until I was ready to deal with the other things listed above. I had some things that I had to accept and move on from. Because until I could accept those things, the hard truths and accept them and learn from them, how in the hell could I ever think about my career or a meaningful relationship or really anything. I basically had to say to myself; "Yes, you have an unnecessary need to please everyone because of him. Yes, you get into altercations and physical fights because you're really mad at him. Yes, you have been focusing on shallow things and chasing money because you feel some need to show him how amazing you are and how he had nothing to do with it. And finally, yes, you are on this path of self destruction because you hate who you have become and it kills you to think that you are becoming more like this man every day." Clearly, my biological father really fucked up my life for a long time. It's not like it was intentional, he's just one of those people who should have never had a kid and what do you know, despite the fact that he was married 4X over, I'm his only child. In the end, once I was ready to accept those things, well it allowed me to really see things clearly and modify my behavior in a way that actually helped me attain some goals. Imagine being able to take a step back in a heated moment and say, "wait, I know why I'm doing this". But even if you think that you are beyond the point of no return, or a lost cause, well fuck you, because you're not. It took a long time but I learned (and its an evolving process that never ends) to make what were once traits that really negatively impacted my life, well they're now key assets. I'm very competitive, that can be very helpful in business. You just have to find a healthy way to balance it. I'm very analytical, that's very helpful especially within my industry. It's allowed me to identify inefficiencies in areas and leverage that. I don't dimiss anyones ideas because they aren't mine. I want to always work with people on a team who are smarter than me. I never think I'm the smartest person in the room or that I know better, because of ego. This again I owe to my biological father. He has an inferiority complex and growing up I heard countless times, "You think you're smarter than me? I don't give a shit what the IQ tests said." (I had a slight learning disability which now I think is a benefit at times. But at 5, 11 and 16 I had to get tested and my IQ test would always seem suspect to him) I've learned that money doesn't equal happiness, that's allowed me to focus on building great working relationships. If you find a way to make something fair for your side and fair for the other, you'll get a lot done. In business, I'm not a jerk, or rude, I'm just direct and honest and I don't try to short-cut things. I try to find humor in almost everything because being too serious or always negative is just a waste of energy. I learned from my step father that a great business that you can really love, it can be like a family. I tell my team members (I don't call people employees) that I appreciate them always and often. When I sense that someone is down or going through a rough spot personally or professionally, I will usually try to compliment them on their work and give them a hug. Also, I'm far from perfect and I have my moments where I regress backward. When I do, I go back and figure out why and then try to make adjustments. But that's the thing, no one is perfect and we will always make mistakes and poor choices. Plato said "necessity is the mother of invention", I absolutely believe that. However I've found that failure and conflict play an important role as well. In closing, I think if you can just learn from your experiences and embrace life, the good parts and bad, value friendship, encourage collaboration and just keep your head up, I really think you can overcome anything. Don't give up hope ever, because if this messed up turd can do it, so can you. Find passion, truth, friendship, collaboration and love and never stop learning from life.

column1: How did your life change after losing 100 lbs?
column3: How did my life change after losing 100 lbs… I honestly do not know where to begin. How hasn’t it changed? I’m a very interesting individual (toots my own horn). If you happen to sit down and have a conversation with me, I’m sure you’d agree (or maybe you can tell by reading my Quora answers - I don’t know). But I would rate my personality a good 10/10. If not a solid 11 when I’m feeling great about myself. I’m very proud of how I’ve developed as a person and who I’ve become. But who I was as a person was often overlooked and treated with disdain because of my outer appearance. Who I was as a person didn’t matter to most people because my physicality gave the impression I had no respect for myself. Something I came to realize recently while talking with a friend is that I grew up used to being bigger than my peers. I was like in the 99th percentile in height by the time I was age 7–8 and I stayed there till I stopped growing. I was used to being taller, heavier, etc. because I grew up with that being normal for me. My size stopped bothering me because I was always bigger. I accepted that as my reality. I was always bigger. I was always the biggest. I would always be the biggest. My height was something I couldn’t change, and I began looking at my weight the same way. Somewhere along the way, being bigger stopped meaning by height, and began meaning by weight. But I didn’t notice. Due to my appearance being generally unfavorable, or unattractive, I had to win people over with my personality. I’m rather quiet, reserved, and introverted, but I am also passionate, creative, empathic, and understanding. I was a big girl who had a big personality to match, but few got to really know her. Cue the fat pictures.I have very strong opinions. I am a deep thinker. But I often kept quiet (except for online) because I stutter a great deal and because I was afraid people would target my weight if I said things they didn’t agree with. I was afraid of the opinions of others. With the weight loss, and with the war I was finally winning when it came to loving myself, my personality magnified. I never considered ‘fat’ as something that defined me. For me, it was less about the weight loss and more about the belief that I was deserving of my own love. I was losing weight, but like I said, I’d never let it define me. I didn’t expect people to treat me differently because of my weight loss. I thought people were treating me differently because I was working on my mental and emotional state. I was working on loving and caring for myself. Due to the work I was putting in to caring about myself and my happiness, my confidence grew. My personality was loud. Losing weight wasn’t going to make me happier. I knew this from the beginning. I knew that it was something I would have to work on. Truth be told, I get slightly irritated when people attribute my happiness and my self-confidence to my weight loss. It discredits all of the work I put in to consciously changing how I felt about myself. Just answer the question, Reilyn. I’m getting to it. So how did my life change after losing 100lbs? It opened my eyes. (That wasn’t supposed to be a pun since as you can see, my eyes look nearly closed in my pictures above lmaoo but it is what it is) It opened my eyes to how focused people are on weight. It opened my eyes to the importance of weight. The way you look is paramount. Nothing else about me f*cking mattered. I lost 100lbs and everything was about my weight. No one cared about the ups and downs of my emotional well-being. No one cared about the struggles I faced with my mentality. No one cared about the conscious efforts I had to make daily. That I had to find little things throughout the day that made me happy or made me smile. No one cared that I had to choose every day that I wanted to live. People acted and continue to act like it came as a packaged deal with weight loss. Lose weight! You’ll be happier, sexier, more confident. It’ll improve your social skills, your love life. People even market it like this. No. No, no, no. It’s a f*cking lie. Because I lost 100lbs and I was still unhappy with myself. I still hated myself. I hit my 100lb loss in February and I still vehemently hated myself. I had more energy, yeah. I could do things easier, yeah. Clothes looked nicer on me. People were paying attention to me… Can you imagine the mindf*ck though? When more people are paying attention to you and you think they like you because of your colorful personality but in reality, you realize it’s because you look better? I mean, f*ck. I could be a shell of a human being with nothing going on upstairs and people would still give me attention because I was decent to look at now. For a while, I hated that I lost the weight. I lost a lot of friendships because my personality grew louder through the confidence I built while losing weight, and they attributed that to my weight loss and thought I was becoming egotistical because my appearance was improving. My humor was taken differently. I can no longer make crude jokes around many people without them thinking I’m flirting now. People act like you lose weight and your life improves significantly. It doesn’t. You get healthier, you have more energy, and physically, you feel better. Yes, yes, and yes. But they aren’t all positives. Your relationships change. You’re no longer the fat friend or the fat family member. When people who were your friends begin treating you with contempt, you wonder if they kept you around because you were fat. Now they’re forced to recognize the fact that you’re a whole actual person, and they don’t like it. Some people also start feeling competitive with you. Sh*t, you look better, now I have to start looking better. Can’t have you, the fat one, looking better than me. Your view of the world changes. You may get cynical. I know I did. Hell, I fell back into full on depression mode for a while. You can choose to dwell on it, over things you can’t change, or you can take it as a learning experience (always easier said than done, of course). I don’t suddenly love working out (I wish I did though). I’m not turning into a gym rat but I am a little obsessed over the loose skin I’m beginning to notice. But I mean, whatever. Losing weight will change your life. There’s no doubt about this. But it will change your life in ways you won’t even think of and can’t imagine until it happens to you. It’s different for everyone. It’ll be better and it’ll be worse. Simultaneously. It’s weird. But you are more than the weight you’ve lost, and you deserve the credit for the hard work. Don’t let anyone invalidate that. So here’s some after pictures.Thank you for the A2A. I hope I somehow answered the question o_O.
column9: I don't know what to tell you but your writing skills are far better than me. you inspire me to work on myself. thank you so much. keep doing what you are doing. good luck. Enjoy.

column1: For what reasons are people reluctant to spay/neuter their dogs?
column3: While working as a volunteer for an animal clinic a few years back, I heard many excuses for not getting male dogs neutered. Most of them were due to anthropomorphization - basically giving reasons why the owner themselves wouldn't jump at the chance to be neutered. Over the last several decades dogs have held a very different position in our lives. They've had to evolve their behavior quickly to adapt to their expanded role. We include them in many more activities than they were initially bred to. They live as a family member in many cases. Humans apply their own thoughts and emotions to their dog's behavior and feelings, and sometimes it doesn't work out so well for the dog. Making the decision to neuter is just one example. *For anyone really interested, there's a video at the end that shows and explains the procedure. In my experience, these are the most often heard reasons not to have a dog neutered and those most adamantly against it are, you guessed it, men. I may want to breed him Unless you're a professional breeder this isn't a valid excuse. Breeding is expensive; there will be veterinary bills for vaccinations and unforeseen medical treatments, advertising costs and providing room & board for each new puppy you bring into the world. And for each one you sell, another unwanted dog will be euthanized in a shelter. He won't be as protective Yes, he will. The dog's willingness to protect his family and property comes from having a sense of belonging to your pack. It's far more important to establish a bond with your dog and socialize him properly. A neutered poodle and an un-neutered rottweiler will both protect their pack to the best of their ability. Also, aggressive and protective are 2 different things. An aggressive dog is a liability — a protective, well-socialized dog is an asset. His personality will change Only for the better, if at all. Neutering doesn't alter a dog's personality other than to help curtail roaming and aggression. The source of these behaviors is testosterone and neutering effectively shuts down the manufacturing plant. He'll have less of a tendency to mark territory too. Since your dog’s priority will no longer be looking for a mate, he will show a marked increase in concentration and attention span, making him a better companion and easier to train. There's no real reason I added this photo other than to break up a long answer. It's not my most flattering pose, but it's a nice view of the dog. BTW, I'm pretty sure those drool spots are his.My dog stays indoors This is irrelevant. Most people tend to only think of neutering in terms of reproduction. By neutering an indoor dog, you will protect them from impregnating a female on the off chance they escape from the house. A male will travel a long way if he senses a female in heat. He'll tunnel under the neighbor's fence or into their basement to get to their female dog. Aside from this, you're giving them a host of health and behavioral benefits. The dog will become overweight Only if he was already heading in that direction. Dogs who are neutered after reaching sexual maturity may show an increased appetite as neutering can affect hormonal balances. However, dogs who are overweight are usually so because they're fed too much, do not get enough exercise or have an underlying health issue. It isn't natural I’m not sure there is much we can still consider natural when it comes to our dogs. They partake of a lot more activities with humans than they were originally bred to. We’ve made them an integral part of our lives and that comes with the responsibility of watching out for their health. We have made them dependent on us and quite incapable of caring for themselves in our world. He'll lose his sense of "manliness" No. No he won't. Dogs don't have any concept of manliness — no sense of sexual identity. There will be no loss of self-esteem. In fact, dogs do not experience any sort of emotional reaction to neutering. Dogs don't reproduce to experience the joys of fatherhood; they do it solely to fulfill an urge. Your dog has no understanding of or attachment to parenting. A dog's desire to form a romantic or sexual relationship is about the same as his desire to pen his autobiography. Here is a video showing the neutering procedure from start to finish. It's surgery, so it's a little graphic, but it's pretty simple and straightforward.Note: For the purpose of keeping my answer a readable length, I've only discussed the neuter aspect of the question. For more gender specific information see this link to the Humane Society on spaying female dogs. Spaying Thank you Anonymous for the A2A.
column9: I would say that if you get a shelter animal, most likely they've already been neutered so the owner doesn't have to feel guilty about being the one to do it. Both of our cats were neutered before we even met them. I am fairly certain that, at an appropriate age, it's standard operating procedure, no? Another reason to get a shelter animal! column1: Why do some homeless people prefer cash over food when offered?
column3: Why do some homeless people NEED cash over food when offered? As I sit reading these comments I am absolutely overwhelmed and in tears. A lot of this was why I didn’t ask or panhandle. I understood very well that people everywhere are struggling that nearly 50% of the population was at, below or just barely above the poverty line and had children and other family members to take care of. People are often thoughtless and cruel. I was homeless for about 6 years. Most of that I was lucky to get a meal a day if that. If I was given food, which is rare if you're not actively begging, I didn’t turn it down, I gave it to someone else who needed it if I just ate or couldn’t eat it.Homeless people don’t have: fridges, stoves or pantries. They have to carry everything.Money is lighter.Some who have cars do have coolers or small camping stoves: in order to keep a few perishables and to cook soup in a can, heat coffee and get warm periodically only when needed the most and short spurts at a time to conserve fuel.Personal Hygiene: Showers, washing clothes, laundry soap, soap, shampoo, deodorant, toothbrushes, nail clippers, haircutsTransportation: Purchase a Decent Bike, Bus fare or if disabled a taxi from time to time.Storage: purchasing a wheeled luggage bag, storage fees for belongings if they actually have some left and are trying to keep it until they find housing, storage lockers rental.Money Meets those Needs. In winter money allows a homeless person to get out of the cold and legally hang out in a fast food joint to warm up. They usually don’t let you stay long unless you make a considerable purchase though that’s no guarantee. They may have to jump from one restaurant to another trying to keep warm from inclement weather all day every single day… Money Meets that Need Rarely… Even for a coffee and a dollar sandwich $2–3 min. per person, per restaurant. So for a couple that is $4–6 per visit. When you regularly purchase the bare minimum you are automatically stereo-typed MOST of the time and encouraged to leave as soon as possible. They may need help with a motel for all kinds of reasons:A couple doesn’t want to be at separate shelters and alone.maybe one spouse is disabled and needs more care than a shelter can offer,perhaps *GASP* a married couple would like to have sex once in awhile. They are human, or should homeless couples also refrain from sex ever again even when they are married?Maybe they have:allergiesa medical conditionORreligious beliefs that limit their food choices.Health Care:Prescription drugs, Aspirin, Midol, Cough Drops, Other over the counter medicinesVITAMINS to help maintain health despite improper nutrition.GAS for vehicle IF they have one. A vehicle that must be moved all day long most of the time from one parking lot or parking space to another in order to avoid tickets, cop hassles, drama, or worse, getting impounded, leaving no shelter from elements at all and loss of the few items you own. Also to get to an actual campground OR an otherwise expectable area.Fines for simply being homeless.Fees for filling out housing applications.Work clothes/Clothes/Well Insulated Winter Clothes/Winter Boots/Good ShoesNecessary to attempt to obtain a Job. Not run around naked or in rags. Too Keep Warmer since most likely you will be in the enclement weather a lot. Decent Footwear for warmth, transportation, and durability as they walk nearly ever where every day that takes a toll on shoes. Money Helps Meet those Needs. TWO very essential Items:Tampons & Toilet paper/Baby Wipes - keeps you much cleaner and less aromatic if you will -between showers & allows sponge bath of sorts if needed.Use of the FACILITIES: Money to keep local convenience store or other business one may frequent HAPPY so they’ll allow you use of a restroom. Money Helps Meet those Needs. Getting Outta DODGE:Bus fare to leave town and try to find some place less violent or somewhere with more housing and employment options.Funds for other transportation sources to do this like fixing a car.There are a lot of things they need besides food. Food is generally appreciated and needed. However, just like MOST of YOU they aren’t too keen on eating food or candy from strangers. Self-explanatory I think? And did you know: Cigarettes curb hunger (as does CoFFee). Helps cope with stress and calm you down in stressful situations. For many it is pleasurable and one of the FEW they experience. Typically they are VERY FRUGAL in this department. Cigarettes can also help KEEP the PEACE and a way some try to help each other out on occasion. Most homeless buy cheap bags of tobacco and/or roll them. They have been known to smoke snipes and a cigarette is NEVER wasted. Ashtrays are frequently locked to prevent the theft of all those almost not smoked cigarettes with two drags off them. Supposedly a health issue….it’s mainly GREED folks they make money off the homeless smokers too!!~! Can’t LOSE that stream of cash flow. Gotta love how much smokers are targeted for TAX REVENUES in the extreme but everyone wants to complain tell them to quit while at the same time making a profit. Contradictory. Very. WHY do homeless people have to be PERFECT SAINTS? Are ANY of YOU perfect? Cast the first stone if you are. They weren’t perfect before becoming homeless most likely. I’m taking a wild guess they weren’t Mother Teresa. I’ve been there. Didn’t beg. Didn’t drink. Went hungry a lot. Froze nearly all the time or had no refuge from heat. I’ve had to survive pneumonia on the streets after being resuscitated three times and pushed back out on the streets. Hospital apparently didn’t care I had just died three TIMES in less than a half hour and had no problem discharging me into a rainstorm, raging fever with nowhere to go. WOW, really? I even asked the man who resuscitated me…WHY? Just let me die. I meant it. Ironically, when I was homed hospitals often tried to persuade me to be hospitalized over far less to keep an eye on me through the night which I of course declined as it was very unnecessary and minor. I’ve been raped on the streets. Had everything stolen a number of times. Constantly stressed out with my life in near constant jeopardy most of the time. Hungry, disabled, having to move constantly despite being exhausted from walking-ish ump-teen miles a day because someone might be offended to see a homeless person. Who cares if you can barely walk and blisters on your feet - better move - even if you’re at a park doing nothing wrong - we don’t want to offend anyone. And that’s just skimming the surface, sweetheart. I could go on but I digress… To those who shared: Thank you for caring, sharing and trying to make a difference!!~! The world needs more people like you all! There is ANOTHER SIDE to the story. There are REAL people out there just trying to survive the best they can and have as much normalcy as possible. Not everyone is a druggie or alcoholic. Just like any other aspect of society. You have the good apples and the bad. There are other many other acceptable and reasonable things people need besides food. Many of those who are buying these things are trying to survive without being too much of a burden and still having some freedom or are determined to get back up on there feet. The intent here isn’t to compel you to give money either. Just Informative. If you want to help or already do but just don’t assist in the money department that is fine. That is your choice. You have Freewill. I respect that. Perhaps this can offer some ideas on how to help if you choose to. Edit: Altered for easier reading though I did make other alterations I felt were appropriate to make.
column9: Oh, Jamie…I cannot thank you enough for writing this. It’s so brave, and so painful, and I’m choking back tears. I’ve been there myself, multiple times over decades, including with children many years ago. The judgment from people who have places to go, beds to sleep in, food to eat, is sometimes near insanity inducing. I listened to a podcast episode a while back (on 99% Invisible, I think) discussing the design trend of “anti-homeless” public spaces, like bus benches where one can’t lay down, or spiked walls to prevent sitting, that sort of thing. It’s so cruel. The cost of being poor is monstrous, and invisible to anyone who isn’t. And it increases as one’s meager resources decrease. The electricity to keep a refrigerator running in a housed person’s home costs far less than constantly buying ice for a cooler to try to keep some perishable foods available—if you even have a place to keep a cooler, as you noted. I once walked into a social services office in a city I had just arrived in. I had an infant and a toddler, and was destitute—literally had nothing but what I was carrying. Asked for help, to apply for assistance. After reams of paperwork, was told there would be an answer (for which I’d have to come back, since I had no address) in 30–60 days. Meantime, they directed me across the hall where I was given a 5-lb. block of fake cheese. That was it. Now I had an infant, an exhausted and crying toddler, my bags…and 5 more pounds to carry. I’m so sorry for all that you went through. I’m sorry for all of us that have and continue to suffer with this. I hope even a few people here will read this and choose to be less controlling of others when they decide to help. Those few dollars will never make anything worse.

column1: How can I get over and feel better after being cheated on, long term relationship?
column3: I'm really sorry to hear that you've experienced infidelity in a long-term relationship. Coping with betrayal can be incredibly challenging, but with time and self-care, you can heal and start feeling better. Here are some suggestions to help you navigate this difficult situation: 1. Allow yourself to grieve: It's important to acknowledge your emotions and give yourself permission to grieve the loss of trust and the future you had envisioned. Allow yourself to feel the pain, anger, sadness, and any other emotions that arise. 2. Seek support: Reach out to trusted friends, family members, or a therapist who can provide a listening ear and emotional support during this time. Sharing your feelings and thoughts with someone you trust can help alleviate the burden and provide perspective. 3. Take time for self-reflection: Reflect on the relationship and the factors that may have contributed to the infidelity. While it's important not to blame yourself, self-reflection can help you gain insight into any patterns or dynamics that can be addressed in future relationships. 4. Practice self-care: Engage in activities that promote self-care and well-being. This can include exercise, hobbies, spending time with loved ones, practicing mindfulness or meditation, or seeking professional help if needed. Taking care of yourself physically, mentally, and emotionally is essential in the healing process. 5. Set boundaries: Establish clear boundaries with your ex-partner to create space and protect yourself. This might include limiting or cutting off contact, unfollowing them on social media, or avoiding places that trigger painful memories. 6. Focus on personal growth: Use this experience as an opportunity for personal growth and self-improvement. Engage in activities that help you discover your strengths, passions, and goals. Invest in your own personal development and work towards becoming the best version of yourself. 7. Forgive and let go: Forgiveness is a personal journey and doesn't necessarily mean condoning the actions of your ex-partner. Forgiveness can be a way to free yourself from carrying the burden of resentment and anger. It's a process that takes time, but it can ultimately bring you peace and closure. Remember, healing from infidelity takes time, and there is no set timeline for recovery. Be patient and compassionate with yourself as you go through the healing process. With time, self-care, support, and a commitment to your own well-being, you can rebuild your life and find happiness and fulfillment again. Take care, and know that you deserve love, trust, and respect in your relationships.

column1: How can I stop feeling like the girl my ex left me for is better than me?
column3: Always remember a few things in life: 1. The person who truly knows who they are is that person himself/herself. Even though you may get vibes that this new girl in his life is way better than you, she is not. You are YOU and she is SHE. What you bring to the table is so unique to you that nobody else can take that away from you. Even though you may feel that your ex is seemingly happier with her, trust me every relationship has its ups and downs. The same bumpy ride he had with you, he is on the same journey with her. Every day for your ex is not going to be rosy with her. There are going to be bad days and also good days. 2. Remember she is just another girl like you. There is nothing special about her. If you sit and reflect about all the hard times you gave your ex, she will give him hard times too. If you think back to the times when you fought with him or gave him a hard time, there will be days when she will do the exact same thing, in fact she could be worse than you. 3. Always remember everybody has a only a role to play in your life. That's all. The lead actor of your life is you and only you. Maybe it was really for the better that he left you and went with her. I know how you feel right now, you feel like you will never find anybody else like him. You feel like you were a perfect fit for each other. But that is not true. The only person you actually truly need in your life is YOU. You are the star, you are amazing beyond any other girl can be. See, you are at least feeling the hurt and the pain of him leaving you, that shows you are a great girl who actually cares. And this quality will make you a great partner for another guy who is deserving of you. 4. Write a self gratitude journal. Everyday write down 5 things you love about yourself. How smart you are , how funny you are , how vehemently you love the people that are deserving and in your life, applaud yourself everyday. If you are still not convinced let me share my story with you: I was crazily in love with this guy. But out of the blue he started acting weird and distant and was always losing his temper on me and was very irritable. 'I started sensing that he might like somebody else. Eventually he made up some reason that his family will not approve of me and finally dumped me. After two three weeks I got to know he was with another girl and he will marry her eventually. That was the reason why he dumped me. I was in the same spot as you are. I knew this girl from a distance only meaning I used to see her pics on FB etc. I used to see her posts. It is safe to say I was obsessed with this new girl. Lets call her A. Everyday I used to try and find more information about her. How many siblings she has , where she graduated from, what she has studied, where she works. from her check ins I used to try to understand if she met my ex or not over the weekend. I used to read between the lines of all her posts. In short I concluded how she was better than me for him. She was the same caste as him, she was the same financial status as him, she was beautiful, she was thinner than me, her hair was nicer than my hair, she had good height which was complimentary to my ex, she seemed funny, she seemed like she had a nice heart, she was from a good family. So, my conclusion was Miss. A is much better than me and there is no way my ex will ever get thoughts of me. Mind you, all of this is just from her pics and posts and other stalking on all social media platforms. Never met or spoke to Miss. A till date.I was shattered. My self worth started to dip, I was losing my self confidence, I really felt worthless. 1.5 years passed like this. My ex married Miss.A. I could see all their love crazy pics and posts on FB everyday. I used to feel so dejected and lost. There were many nights that I cried myself to sleep. Slowly I got used to the pain, started feeling better, started doing my own stuff. Out of the blue after 2 years I get a call from my ex. Miss. A had walked out on him after 1 year of marriage!!! Hope you read above what all I concluded about Miss.A. Now I'll tell you how she really was from the person who lived with her day in and day out for 2 years: 1. She was extremely moody. 2. She used to give him the silent treatment. 3. She used to cry at the drop of the hat. 4. She used to discuss the most personal things between her and my ex ( her husband) with her brother and father. 5. She physically assaulted my ex 2-3 times. When he got angry after these incidents, she went and told her family members that he hit her. This is just the gist. Apart from this there were a ton of good qualities about her. So the basic thing I am trying to say is every person is the same. everybody has their plus points as they have their minus points. This new girl your ex is with .. she is no angel. She has not climbed down a ladder from heaven. There is nothing special or great about her that you do not have. If your ex does end up with her for the rest of his life, remember that: 1. you helped them somewhere in this journey to get together. 2. Be glad for him if he is really happy with her. 3. DO NOT and NEVER ever measure your self worth because another human being rejected you. 4. Always remain confident, he rejecting you does not define anything. Only you define what you think of yourself! So always think very highly of yourself. 5. During those 1.5 years, my ex used to think of me often. so there is a high chance your ex still thinks of you. This is no way determines your self worth , irrespective of if he thinks of you or not, you are awesome. 6. If you feel she looks cuter than you, prettier than you, remember that good looks take a relationship only "this" far. If she does not have solid character, or she is not interesting enough as her face she will come across as boring to him in the long run. Again this does not mean SHE is worthless. She has her own amazing unique characteristics , just like YOU do. 7. Seriously many of us need to stop taking our significant others approval as a yardstick of our self worth! I ve done this for 2 years. Instead I should have just mourned the loss of the relationship, yet continued to remain awesome in my head. This is my advice to you, mourn the loss but also know how awesome YOU are. Good luck to you ! :) Stay happy, never let any man or woman dim your sparkle.

column1: I have become a sensitive person after few incidents in life and now get easily perturbed by people's remarks and behavior. I practiced meditation for some years but it hasn't helped me. How do I improve myself?
column3: Greetings mate! Firstly I’d like to tell you that everything is fine… You are an awesome person and being sensitive is good. As it is many people dont possess it. Coming to your problem, I understand that few incidents in your life have shattered you and you might not be feeling confident and strong anymore. You might be questioning what went wrong and why can’t you become your old self which you picture as a strong person. Believe me I’ve been through it and still sometimes get flashes from the past, but that makes me more stronger more hopeful to move ahead. I am not an expert in meditation but I do know a fact that, you possess the power to control your life. Meditation is a path which helps you in understanding your sub-concious mind and your inner being. It’s very much possible that meditating didnt suit you, cos it never suited me :) Our main agenda here is strengthening your inner core, your mental core. People say things sometimes which could be intentional or accidental. If you believe yourself to be right, or believe that it makes you happy ( which should be towards humanity), you don’t have to give a thought to others. I dont know which incidents have been harsh on you, I’m assuming it might related to : family member loss, peer pressure or comments, friend’s group acceptance, love issues or office colleagues. Whatever has happend is over now, you must gear up, and learn from your past and not let it happen again. Thinking of past and getting scared to try new things or society’s comments, these are all sorts of baggage which is stopping you from changing, Evolving! Always remember, everything happens for good, and incidents occur cos they help you survive the worst for future. Flashes from past are past, they will never come again until you worry about it. Just let Go of everything. Don’t care what the world will say. Now practically to improve yourself, just do the following activities:Maintain a diary. Keep two parts in it. One for happy and the other for sad or negative memories. This will give you a proper track to find yourself if you are deviating.Write down the 10 things you are proud to be. Work on those. Use it for you benefit and you loved ones, then the societyDo some activity which you love: Dancing, Swimming (any sort), Reading clubs, singing, painting, camping, hiking. Get an insight into it and others who have similar interest like yours.Stay away from toxic people. Just hear them, Don’t listen ;) There’s a lot of difference !HOPE! The world is enormous! You are gifted! You just dont know itIt’s OK to be sensitive. Just channelize it. Realize who is worthy to get to know your emotionLastly, never self pity… It’s a vicious trap one falls into cos it feels cozy and it’s the instant mode of defense. But it’s lethal in the future.Hope my words aren’t too long for you :) Sorry for the lecture, but I wish you all the best , because You are the BEST! Good Day!

column1: What is driving the campaign against Dominic Cummings in the UK? Is it zeal for obedience to laws and regulations, personal hatred because he works for Boris Johnson, a desire to overturn Brexit by any means, or something else entirely?
column3: The Government’s advice at the beginning of this lockdown, nearly nine weeks ago, was this: “If any member of a household has symptoms, do not leave your home for any reason”. It’s right here: Self-isolation if you or someone you live with has coronavirus symptoms - Coronavirus (COVID-19) Let’s repeat that, just to make sure it’s completely clear. If any member of a household has symptoms, do not leave your home for any reason. Pretty straightforward and unambiguous, right? That, not incidentally, is part of the strategy that Cummings himself was part of formulating. It also hasn’t changed with any of the changes - the ‘easing’ - that have been made since. It was that at the beginning. It’s still that. Despite some apologists trying to convince you otherwise. Nine weeks is a long time to be in lockdown. A lot has happened. Here’s a list of some things that have happened:13-year-old Ismail Mohamed Abdulwahab died in King’s College hospital after testing positive for coronavirus. His family were not allowed to visit him and were also unable to attend his funeral because of self-isolation rules.A friend of a friend had a sister who died after a week alone. Her mother had to identify the body by facetime. Again, the family is not allowed to come together for support and grieving.Helen Goodman, the former Labour MP for Bishop Auckland, wasn’t allowed to see her father before he died in a Durham care home.Dr Catherine Calderwood, Scotland’s former Chief Medical Officer, was forced to resign (April 6th) after it emerged that she had made two visits to family. She didn’t, and doesn’t, have symptoms.Epidemiologist Professor Neil Ferguson was forced to resign after having visits from his lover at his home. He doesn’t, and didn’t have symptoms.It’s vanishingly unlikely that the families in the first two bullet points are the only families in that position. There are 36,000+ dead in the UK from this (confirmed cases). I also don’t recall any of Cumming’s defenders on this thread or any of the dozen or so others that have sprung up leaping loudly to the defence of Professor Ferguson or Dr Calderwood. Perhaps they were too busy brushing up on their Niemoller. The reason we’ve all been in lockdown in the first place is to stop this spreading like a wildfire - to try to control it, and ‘flatten the curve’. That’s why those families have had to make that sacrifice, as horrific as it is. That’s why we’re taking what will be an insane economic hit. So having seen how the Governments advice is absolute in these circumstances (do not leave your home under any circumstances), how high-profile figures have been forced to resign for doing less, and outlined the how’s and why’s of this national sacrifice, let’s now talk about the defence of Cummings. We’ll start with the cabinet.Matt Hancock: “it was entirely right for Cummings to find childcare for his toddler”Dominic Raab: “two parents were anxiously taking care of their child. Those seeking to politicise this should take a long hard look in the mirror”Rees-Mogg: “caring for your child is obviously reasonable”Suella Braverman: “Protecting one’s family is what any good parent does”Rishi Sunak: “Taking care of your wife and young child is justifiable and reasonable”Gove: “Caring for your wife and child is not a crime”Huh. That being the case, one is somewhat forced to ask oneself the obvious question: why is it ‘obviously reasonable’ when Cummings does it, but the rest of the population is prohibited from doing it? A follow-up question that springs to mind would be why those other high-profile figures were forced to resign, but Cummings shouldn’t have to? Another follow-up question that springs to mind is ‘they really had to go to Durham? With a small child? Meaning they would have had to stop probably multiple times for toilet breaks and petrol? A senior government advisor really couldn’t have found childcare in London?’ Edit: another good question that has recently sprung to mind is to wonder about the odds of these not-one-but-two absolutely essential trips just so happening to co-incide with Cummings mother’s birthday, and his wife’s birthday. Weird, huh? To answer the question: what is ‘driving the campaign’ against Cummings is anger. Because he, and his cabinet cronies, have been exposed as arrogant, plague-spreading hypocrites, who care nothing for anyone except themselves. While the rest of the population has to stay where they are, come what may. They have to suck up their loss of income, their family members dying alone, their children out of school, the critical care workers exhausting themselves to death, the doctors and other professionals who have had multiple horrendously difficult conversations with families about why they are not allowed to see their loved ones….. Fuck Cummings, and fuck anyone defending him. You are beneath contempt.
column9: Thank you Richard! Some sense in this particular collection of answers at last! This whole argument has nothing to do with politics, as other contributors would have us believe, but public anger, as you conveyed very well. It's the sacrifices that millions of families across the country have made compared with the arrogance of a man who was instrumental in the making of a policy that is the reason they all made those sacrifices - a man who went against the instructions the rest of the country followed, breaking, if not the law, the spirit of the law. It's the hypocrisy of him and his boss. It's the lack of judgement of his boss in this situation, which makes us question his judgement in other situations. Personally, I don't like Boris Johnson. I don't know him personally, but mistakes he's made in the past and his buffoonary combine to create a negative image for me. I don't know Dominic Cummings, but the impression I got of him, even before this debacle, was one of arrogance, unwarranted self-confidence, and dodgy and inappropriate fashion sense (I have become more casual in what I wear when I go into the office in the past few years, but I still make an effort to look reasonably smart - not dressed as though I got dressed in the dark and forgot to check my appearance before leaving the house to ensure I've at least tucked my shirt in) - his actions during the lockdown simply reinforce the impression. They also reinforce the view of the public that it's one rule for the masses, and another one for those with the power over them.

column1: Did Larry Holmes ever admit he made a mistake in insulting the legacy of Rocky Marciano before he fought Michael Spinks the first time?
column3: First, Larry almost immediately apologized to the Marciano family. Secondly, the vast majority of people who hold this against Larry Holmes forget all about the context in which he said what he did…CREDIT PICTURE FIGHT CITY People always like to remember the bad, and through the years much has been said about Larry’s comment that Rocky couldn’t carry his jock. But they never mention the baiting Larry took that night, and the racial abuse. They also forget Larry apologized for the comment, saying:“I never wanted to hurt anybody, especially the Marciano family. I was probably a little pissed off, [at the baiting he was taking]”People who hold this comment against Larry forget to mention that when the World Boxing Council gave the city of Brockton a statue of Rocky Marciano valued at $250,000 and soaring 22 1/2 feet tall, one of the fighters there to honor the Rock was Larry Holmes, who had nothing but good things to say, and happily mingled with the Marciano Family… What happened when Larry commented on Rocky is not what is generally reported What is usually forgotten is the vicious racism that surrounded Larry’s chase of Marciano’s record, and the baiting he took along the way, before the Spinks fight, and at the after fight press conference from members of Rocky’s family and the press. Sad, since when Rocky had a statue dedicated to him in his hometown of Brockton, who was there to honor Rocky? Larry Holmes. Larry was a victim of appalling racism, which is either forgotten or overlooked when he is criticized. I am a great admirer of Rocky, but that humble, decent man, the first heavyweight champ to completely break the color barrier, would not have approved of the way Holmes was treated, the baiting, any of it. Larry was never a beloved subject of media coverage. He made no secret of thinking that most boxing writers knew little about actual boxing, and he also thought certain members of the media were biased against him. Perhaps it was a self fulfilling prophecy, but the coverage of Larry Holmes certainly seemed biased and unfair. Larry also had to overcome a repulsive undercurrent of racism, especially as he closed in on Rocky Marciano’s record for an undefeated heavyweight champion. He literally got death threats. Larry’s poor relationship with the media really blew up at the press coverage on Larry after his loss to Mike Spinks. There was open jubilation reported by the supposedly unbiased media at Holmes failure to break Marciano’s record, and the fact that Larry was being heckled by some members the late former champ’s family at a post-fight press conference was both sad and nasty. The media never bothered to report the taunting from Marciano’s family - which would have angered the Rock, who did not go in for that sort of thing - and the fact that their baiting, and open jubilation by the media after Larry’s defeat by Spinks, is what led to his explosion at the press conference. Nor was this the first time racism reared its ugly head in Holmes career Never was the ugly undertone of racism more apparent than when Holmes fought “the Great White Hope” Gerry Cooney. The promoters insisted Cooney, who held no title, be introduced second - where the champ is introduced - and generally demeaned Holmes. There were rumors reported in the media of President (Ronald Reagan) wanting to call Cooney in the dressing room if he won. It was truly ugly. Cooney said last year:“You know, leading up to our fight, a lot of ignorant people said a lot of ignorant things. And you know what else, I regret that. The truth is, I've come to love Larry Holmes."Cooney was bothered that his fight with Holmes was sold as a black vs. white thing. He was astonished and happy when Holmes called him after the Las Vegas battle to say that wasn’t what he wanted either. Cooney recalled the conversation:“Larry said, ‘Listen, that’s just people talking, that’s not us,' ”But more, Larry called to offer his support. The same media that had hyped Cooney as the “Great White Hope” mocked him after his defeat, despite his having put up a terrific struggle, and it wore on Cooney, depressing and disheartening him. It was Holmes that again called him to help:“After our fight everyone picked on him except me, I called him and said ‘Get out of the house.”Cooney now regards Larry as a close friend:“he reached out to me and things got good between us.”All this is generally forgotten when Larry’s comment about Rocky is brought up - a comment he swiftly apologized for! Larry had the misfortune to come along after Ali and before Tyson, the two most charismatic heavyweights of history Manny Steward said it best:“I have no doubt in my mind that Larry Holmes’ entry into the heavyweight championship position is definitely hampered by him falling in between two of the most dominant, I would say, personality charismatic style-wise type fighters in the history of our sport—meaning Mike Tyson and Muhammad Ali.”Heavyweight History With Emanuel Steward: Part 1 Of 3 • East Side Boxing • News Archives Ironically, Larry Holmes learned the professional boxing game as Ali’s sparring partner, (and then Joe Frazier’s) and Ali looked upon the younger fighter as a mentee and student. A few months over 44 years ago, in June of 1978, Larry Holmes and Ken Norton, both trying to succeed Ali as the world’s premier heavyweight, had one of the greatest fights in history. The two men were even on the judges scorecards going into the 15th round. With pure determination and the best jab in heavyweight history, Holmes prevailed and became the new heavyweight champion of the world. Larry saw the other fighters in the Golden Age, and had no doubt that he was the heir to the Greatest. He had no illusions though, that any fighter reigning after Ali would not feel the weight of that comparison. And Larry did suffer from it. Especially since Larry, a very private man, was not the bombastic character Ali was. Add in a very testy relationship with reporters - who Larry despised, for the most part, and Larry had a rough time replacing Ali. Who did Gerry Cooney call when he needed money for his foundation to help boxers? Larry Holmes. Larry’s many charitable endeavors included having quietly paid for Joe Frazier’s care after a car accident, (including 4 back surgeries), Joe’s subsequent cancer treatments and taking care of Joe as the champ grew increasingly frail. It should be noted he asked that his charity not be made public, he did not do it for acclaim, but to help a fellow fighter, as Larry said. Indeed, when Frazier’s family let it be known Larry had paid for Joe’s back surgeries, and the media asked Holmes about it, he refused to confirm it, saying only:“Joe Frazier is my friend, and what I choose to do for my friends is my own business, if I do anything for a friend, it is not done for the purpose of making myself look good and getting my name in the paper. But know this about my friendship with Joe: If I had $4 left in my wallet, two of those would go to Joe.”Larry reached out to Gerry Cooney when he needed help the most, as he did with Joe Frazier, and other fighters. He never forgot the boxing world and tried to help where he could. Holmes never forgot where he came from, either. Larry Holmes, alone of the great heavyweights, stayed in his home town to help Larry, alone of the great heavyweights, never left his home town. Indeed, a brief move to Florida after hs original retirement in 1985 brought him right back. Oh, he had plenty of offers! Though more opportunity for branding and money awaited in LA or New York, as time made Holmes more popuar, Larry Holmes chose to stay in Easton, Pennsylvania, where his charity has helped many, and his investment in his home town has lifted more. Since defeating Ken Norton for the heavyweight crown in 1978, Holmes has invested heavily in his home town. At the height of the recession, with Easton, like other small towns hemmroging jobs, Holmes quietly opened two restaurants, a training facility, an office complex, and all with his own money to hire people from, and put money into, his home town. In 2015, the city of Easton unveiled a statue of Holmes in Scott Park. Gerry Cooney said it best:“Larry was a great champion, and he is a great guy.”CREDIT TO: Boxrec for stats and records Ring for historical rankings Bill Caplan's 20 greatest heavyweights - The Ring Fire Still Burns Inside Smokin’ Joe Frazier (Published 2006) From THE RING: The greatest heavyweight of all time - The Ring https://www.boxingnewsandviews.com/2022/07/06/george-foreman-on-3-strengths-larry-holmes-had-other-than-his-jab/ Heavyweight History With Emanuel Steward: Part 1 Of 3 • East Side Boxing • News Archives Larry Holmes: Against the Odds by Phil Berger Larry Holmes on Rocky: ‘The man was tough’ Panel: What was Larry Holmes' best performance? | Boxing News The Ten Great Heavyweights of All Time: | BoxingInsider.com Top ten heavyweight boxers of all time revealed with Muhammad Ali the greatest and Mike Tyson missing out c THE GREATEST HEAVYWEIGHTS Of All Time Through Their Eyes: Larry Holmes vs. Gerry Cooney | Irish America

column1: How do you react to suggestion of Intra-family distancing, like isolating the elderly members in the family from the younger members, as the elderly have more chances of contracting and transmitting the COVID19? Wouldn't it be emotionally shattering?
column3: I didn't react emotional . I am more practical and responsible. When my son and his team, a twenty four members returned from london, we told him to request office to arrange for self quarantine. Office obliged and arranged accommodation to all of them. After fifteen days all were teseted negative then they were sent home on their 18 th day along with reports. With Medical clearence. Since me and my husband were in fifties with health issues, and we have a six months old grand daughter, we made one room separate for my son for six more days on doctor’s advice since he had cold.he was not allowed to come out. We arranged every thing. He wore mask. We all talked to him from distance. He had home food in disposable trays. He kept those trays under sun for 24 hours before disposal. After almost 24 days he joined us back. It's true we all felt pity and emotionally sad for him. We missed him. But this is necessary. We should be responsible. We have no right to pass it on to others. Loss of Elders and kid's life is more traumatic in this scenario. More trouble for them. Ps. I got few messages accusing me of emotionally stone hearted, bankrupt, not to be called a mother, selfish blah blah. When hospital ambulance comes and takes our own people away, except crying you can't do anything. with teary eyed you see them off, You can't visit them, you can't sit next by them and console, you can't feed them fruit, you have to leave them with medical staff in isolation is more painful to a mother. Doctors , medical staff, ambulance drivers all those helping people are not some mother's children? Why they have to risk their lives to take care of you? Did you do any favor to them any time? Don't test their humanity and patience and kind heart. So I feel I did the right thing.
column9: You did the right thing. Wish more ppl acted responsibly like you. We have educated ppl acting irresponsibly here.

column1: If you could give advice to your younger self, what would you say?
column3: Try harder to save your sister’s life. Most of the time I believe that I did everything I could to save her life, but it is cold comfort. I failed. This is a tale of the American Medical System. In 2006 my sister fell down some stairs. The fall caused her small intestine to fold over on itself, causing an intestinal blockage. She was hospitalized a few days later after fainting from the pain while trying to go up those same stairs. Surgeons unkinked her intestine, and in a couple of says she was home again. She was a small business owner. She worked 14 hours a day. She didn’t have medical insurance. She was terrible about keeping her follow up appointments. She said couldn’t afford to keep them, and when I offered to pay, she said she felt fine anyway. Two months later she called me. She was screaming. Screaming like she was being murdered. She begged me to help her, she felt like someone was cutting her open with a knife from the inside. She lived on the East Coast and I lived in the West Coast. I grabbed another phone and called an ambulance to her address. It took a while to figure out what was wrong. Which was everything. The surgeon who opened her up was the same one who had done the initial surgery, and he was shocked by the change in her small intestine. It was dying. The intestinal blockage from a couple of months previous had poisoned it. Bile ducts on her liver were so inflamed the surgeons we shocked they hadn’t burst just moving her onto the table. And her pancreas was inflamed, too. They figured that was the source of the really intense pain. Every time she ate, her pancreas tried to produce digestive enzymes, but it couldn’t anymore. It just made her hurt like the alien was trying to eat it’s way out of her. She almost died. They installed a J-tube. Gave her digestive enzymes. Liquid vitamins. Gave her instructions on her self care. I took a month off from my work in accounting to take care of her. I brought her to Key West, away from the cold New England weather. Nursed her, cajoled her. But something in her spirit was broken. Her existence was pain, and it wore her down. I made sure she was stable and left her in the hands of her boyfriend. A good man. Six months later he called me. A grown man in his 40s, he put his mom on the phone. She’s a pharmacist. She’d come to visit and took one look at my sister and said she needed to get to the hospotal, but my sister refused. I was told my sister was dying and I needed to get there immediately. So I dropped everything and flew to New England. In six months, the change in her was profound. She was 37, but the vibrant, amazing woman I knew was gone. She looked 80. She moved slowly, shuffling, holding her body so as to minimize the pain. Her legs were full of fluid, her face and upper body were skeletal. She’d lost 60#, but she was carrying at least 30# of fluid in her legs. She was malnourished. Her mind was foggy. She faded in and out during conversations. I took her to the doctor, I tried to be her advocate. The doctor was fairly indifferent. He told me that she was medically non-compliant, that she had checked herself into the hospital 5 times in the past 6 months, and each time, pulled her IV out after a few days and walked out of the hospital without letting anyone know she was leaving. He put her in a diuretic, told me to elevate and wrap her legs, gave me new scripts for digestive enzymes, and was skimpy with the narcotics. He didn’t want her becoming addicted, he said, despite the fact hat she was in constant excruciating pain that her mind was hiding from. She wasn’t “there” because it hurt so much to be present enough to interact with us. She just twitched and moaned most of the time. I’d cared for 2 family members with terminal colon cancer by then. Since then, I’ve cared for two family members with lung cancer, one terminal. I’ve seen terrible pain and suffering. What my sister went though—far surpassed anything I’ve ever seen. I asked her doctor is she should be in the hospital. He said yes, she should be, but there was no point admitting her if she wouldn’t stay. I tried to get her to go. I begged and cried. She wouldn’t go. So I did the unthinkable. I tried to have her committed to care against her will. I didn’t know what I was doing. I should have hired a lawyer. I should have done a better job of gathering her medical records, I should have… I stood in front of a judge and told him that my sister needed to be held involuntarily at the hospital because she refused to remain in care. The police went and took my very sick sister to jail in handcuffs. Some psych person talked to me, talked to her. We both stood in front of the judge again. I begged him. It was August. I told him she would be dead before Christmas if she didn’t get the care she needed. The judge said that the court had tried to find a facility that could provide the medical care she needed on an involuntary hold and could not. The judge extracted a promise from her to be medically compliant, and closed the proceedings. My sister refused to talk to me. She had been humiliated by me. She’d sat in a jail cell, in terrible pain, for hours. She banished me from her life. I went back to the West Coast. Her friends kept me informed of how she was doing. She lived past Christmas. Her boyfriend emailed me a photo of her on New Year’s Eve. She was angelic. Fragile. Glowing. The light of her spirit shone through her skin. She almost looked like her old, vibrant, tenacious self. She died January 8. She showed up at the hospital complaining of intense pain in her head. They wrote her off as medication-seeking and discharged her with instruction to take Tylenol. Two hours later she was dead. She’d had a brain aneurysm. The repercussions were immense. Her business closed. The organizations that relied on her to personally help fund programs for inner-city kids suffered a huge loss. My parents had two other daughters dealing with cancer. Her loss was extremely depressing and disheartening. My mom didn’t get out of bed for weeks. My dad broke into jagged pieces. The youngest sister, the one closest to her, lost it. Literally, she had a psychotic break, killed herself and was revived, had her children taken away from her, and ended up in jail like so many of our mentally ill in the US. Dear 10-year ago me: You must fight harder and smarter to save your sister’s life.
column9: So so sorry you have to experience this.

Fraud and scams affect people emotionally and mentally, we hope this information here helps you you find ways to help yourself if you’ve been victimized, or what you can do to help a friend or family member who has been victimized.
