column1: What is the best way to tackle the problem of care for a wife who has just been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease?
column3: I am sorry to hear that you and your wife are facing dealing with Alzheimer's disease and I am glad to hear that you are doing this together as a loving team.It is a good idea to start researching nursing home vs assisted living -or- in patent vs out patient care. This will be an important resource to help you with your wife's care. Good sources include WedMD or the official U.S. government site for Medicare.Read the '36 Hour Day' because it is gives excellent guidance and clear information of a kind that your family needs. The authors give realistic and good advice that sometimes it is better to concede the patient's frailties (i.e. acceptance/quality of life) than try to do something about them (i.e. 'fight the disease'), and that a compassionate sense of humor often helps. A difficult truth about dementia is that you can't predict which symptoms will appear, so this book covers all of them. And it goes over some of the science behind the more frustrating symptoms, like when the patient is in total denial about their condition, which definitely helps the caregiver with coping.Research do-not-resuscitate orders for the end of life scenario. Look to emphasize "comfort care, focusing on quality of life." Include cooperative family members in end-of-life discussions. Fill out this paperwork and keep a copy in your freezer as it is fire-proof.As hard as it might seem, look at the positives. When we get sick, it's often a wake-up call. I've heard many people say after a serious diagnosis that 'I've never felt more alive. People sometimes wander through life. They go through the paces. They work, they take care of their families, they enjoy things, but they are not living as deeply or as fully as they'd like.A lot of people with a life-limiting illness find it helpful to open the door of exploring relationships, making lifestyle changes, getting back in touch with religious beliefs —whatever is meaningful to you as a couple. For example, I read the Psalms over with my Christian patients as they are a comfort. Journal these explorations or see a therapist with processing all the changes you are going through. A lot of people want to learn something from the experience of their/her illness.Along the lines of journaling and therapy start processing your grief and loss as Alzheimer's disease takes your loved one first mentally then physically.Find a good medical doctor or PCPs who has experience with geriatrics. Prepare yourself to be open and honest about concerns that you have with your physician. Educate yourself about the evils of polypharmacy and the benefit of Alzheimer’s meds.No matter the day-to-day demands of caregiving for a patient with Alzheimer’s or dementia, it’s imperative that you carve out time for your own self-care. I've covered some of these ideas earlier like getting respite care. Learn to ask other family members, friends, or members of your place of worship for help. Seek out help from volunteer organizations, support groups, day care programs, and residential respite care facilities.Don't lose yourself in the care-taking. Take time out to pursue hobbies and interests, and stay on top of your own health needs. Seek professional help if you recognize you're exhibiting any warning signs of caregiver burnout.Regular exercise not only keeps you fit, it releases endorphins that can really boost your mood.Talk to your resources. Talk to a trusted friends, family members, religious leaders, or therapists, about how you feel and what you’re going through.Laughter is the Best Medicine. Watch videos that tickle your funny bone together. ‘Fail videos’ on youtube are great for slapstick.Count your blessings. A daily gratitude list can chase away the blues and let you focus on what your loved one is still capable of, rather than the abilities he or she has lost.Celebrate what is possible. Your loved one still has many abilities. Structure activities to invite participation on whatever level is possible, and you will both find real enjoyment.Cherish your wife's good days in order to rough out the storm of the bad days.Practice relaxation techniques. Meditation, deep breathing, visualization, mindfulness, yoga, or rhythmic exercise can calm, restore, and promote happiness.Make eye contact with your wife, hold her hand or stroke her cheek, talk in a calm, reassuring tone of voice. When you connect in this way, you’ll experience a process that boosts your mood, reduces stress, and supports your physical and emotional well-being. And it can also have the same effect on your loved one.
column9: Dan, from one healthcare professional to another, thank you kindly for this investment of time and energy to write this excellent list of helpful things for couples in the slow-burning prolonged crisis which is Alzheimer’s.

column1: What was the worst thing your parents ever did to you?
column3: My Mom was a beautiful looking woman. I know because she told me so often enough. Men adored her, women admired her ... she was beyond special. She was also an abusive monster and compulsive liar. She raised my Brother and I in almost total isolation. We were told her Dad (my Grandfather "Opa") was an only child, raised in abject poverty. In actuality Opa had 8 brothers and sisters. I was also told her Mom (my Grandmother "Oma") came from a small family, when in truth she had five siblings. Obviously I never had the chance to know these relatives and/or their children. I heard tiny snippets about my Dad's Mom (my Grandmother "Kleintje" Little One). They were mostly derogatory and centered around her so called scandalous bohemian lifestyle, and the fact she was Jewish. Mom told me a lot about Dad's Father (my Grandfather "Grote Vader" Big Daddy). How my last name came from royalty. That the Barkemeijer de Wit's had been fabulously wealthy spice traders, with a castle and vast estates. Lies upon lies upon lies. For the past 5 years I've been researching my family tree. I discovered no royalty and no fabulous wealth. The Barkemeijer de Wit family "I" was born into were all tradesmen ... for literally hundreds of years. Mom had said The Barkemeijer de Wits were devout Catholics and had hated the fact that their son Dirk had married a Jewess. So they excommunicated them from the family. My Mom told so many lies it's taken me almost 60 years to ferret through them. My identity, clues to who I am and where my talents evolved from were kept from me.​Remembering SarahMy Dad's Mother Sarah was born on 27 March 1889, in Amsterdam, Netherlands to Mozes and Betje Bleekrode. Her family was Jewish. She had eight brothers and sisters, most of whom died in concentration camps (along with their families) during the war. So many relatives were killed during WWII, that it almost defies imagination. Other than my Grandmother, I have never met any surviving members of the Bleekrode family. I was 57 when I learned how large my Grandmother's family had been, and how many hundreds of my Dad's Aunts, Uncles and Cousins died in Nazi ghettos or were killed Nazi death camps. For reasons of his own, Dad rarely spoke about anyone other than his immediate family. Obviously he suffered horribly during the war; the memories of which must have been harrowing. My Dad suffered grand mal seizures when he saw holocaust photos and/or spoke about dead family members. Picture of my Dad and his parents out for a day in an Amsterdam park [1925].​Who am I and here did I come from? From an early age I felt as if Mom was ashamed that my brother and I were of what she called "mixed" blood. Mom constantly told me I was more Fontijn (aryan) than Barkemeijer, that the "one quarter" (in truth half) Jewish part of me was so small as to have no bearing on who I was or ever would be. "For God's sake Never tell people your Father is a Jew." She'd say. "Too many people hate the Jews." When I asked why, Mom told me that people hated Jews because they were greedy people who controlled too much of the world's money. She told me a lot of people wanted all Jews dead. Mom said if I told anyone about my Jewish heritage, I would be putting ALL our lives at risk. Mom believed another war was coming. She said people's hatred of Jews was so strong that when war came we would all be killed. I've always been an artist and a musician, always written and my Mom always told me any talent I had came from her. The fact that she couldn't play an instrument and didn't value my artistic gifts, never came into play. The fact that there were no artists in her family, no musicians and no writers, never entered her mind. Her Father, my Grandfather, was a draftsman and an architect, which in her mind was all the proof of inheritable talent she needed. As a child I told my Mom I wanted to be an artist and she laughed. When I was invited to join the National Children's Orchestra, she said no. It was too far away, I'd get raped or killed. When I was invited to Join the Young Americans, she said no as well. She said no when I was invited to tour Hawaii with Jack Coleman's choir. No. No. No. When I was ready to start college, I told my Mom I wanted to major in art. As usual, her answer was a resounding NO. She argued an art major was a stupid waste of time. College (free in those days) would be wasted on me. Mom said because I'm a woman I'd just get married, have a pile of kids, at which point my life would be over. She swore I would never use what I learned in school. Women were created for men and men didn't like educated woman. She of course was the single exception to that rule. Except she never finished high school, never had a career, never accomplished anything beyond the relationships she had. She told me endless stories about her beauty, all the men who had loved her, the gifts they lavished on her, and how she could get anything she wanted from any many she chose. She also forced me to listen to inappropriate stories about sexual escapades. How soldiers developed instant erections at the sight of her, and all men who knew her wanted to marry her. She made it clear she'd NEVER pay for my college education, and would NEVER pay for me to major in art. The ONLY education she'd pay for was a nursing degree, which she said would help me snare a doctor husband. "Marry a doctor" she had said. "That way you'll never have to do it, because he'll be too tired and busy to have sex." When I winced, she told me she was only trying to help. "Sex leads to babies and everyone knows that once you have children, your life is over. Trust me, I should know." "Way to make me feel loved Mom." I thought to myself. I yearned to leave home ... though I believed the only thing I could do was to move in with my best friend, my then boyfriend Michael. Fearing how people would view "her" my Mom forced us to marry. So I married, just to get away from my nightmare homelife. I went from the fat to the frying pan. My marriage quickly failed and we were divorced after only 3 years. I eventually put myself through school (twice) earning certifications in both respiratory therapy and computer programming. I continued to learn all I could about art, drawing, painting whenever I could. Continued with music, and taught myself to write, eventually taking college writing classes when I was in my 30s. I was taught to never valued my artistic talents, and thought I must look selfish and self absorbed to spend so much time doing things I love to do. Irony of Ironies being the awards I garnered for my artwork, music and stories. I was 57 when I first learned the truth about my entire family. I also learned about my Grandmother's family ... renown artists, musicians, writers, diamond cutters and more. One of Kleintje's brothers was a well known graphic artist, the other a world class Violinist, all were educated. My Grandmother's friends and family were the stuff of magic, musicians the likes of Arthur Rubinstein visited her home. Yet in my Mom's eyes Dad's family members were nothing more than tiny blips on her radar. Despite everything, I managed to learn that the Bleekrode family has been part of Amsterdam for over 600 years. Their names and stories are part of Amsterdam history. Astonishingly, Bleekrode survivors of the Holocaust still reside there. Now I know what my Dad couldn't speak of, the heartbreak he kept to himself. The unimaginable loss of all those he held dear, dozens of relatives, ALL his relatives except a small handful. The birth of his only son, my Mom forcing him to choose between leaving his remaining family (who he loved) behind or never seeing his son again. Heart break upon heart break. Mom also used the threat of leaving to convince her entire family (who hadn't wanted to leave Holland) to emigrate to America. She was going to America, no matter what, with our without any of them. If they wanted to see her or my brother again, they should leave with her. Mom's Father (my Grandfather) and Mother gave up everything, their business, livelihood, happiness, and eventually their health, to follow her to California. At age 65, my once wealthy and respected Grandfather was unable to find work in America as an architect or draftsman. He ended up drawing up plans for sidewalks and driveways for Orange County city planning. A once proud man, my grandfather was reduced to a mere shadow of his former self. He died frail and almost penniless, five years after the death of his wife, his children still bickering over who would take possession of his few remaining things. Mom loved telling people how she gave up EVERYTHING to immigrate. She was proud to say that the ONLY reason she left Holland so soon after the war, was to save my poor ailing brother. She said fruit was in short supply, that my brother had rickets, and needed vitamin C to make him healthy again. California had orange trees and unlimited sunshine, free vitamin D. So she had to go, to save his life. Irony of ironies -- I was born with Celiac Disease, and developed rickets soon after birth. When I was 49 I learned I still had rickets. I now take vitamin D supplements. The truth was much more slippery, and hid her dark past. Mom lied constantly, so the full details may never be completely revealed. My Mom had been a wild child during her early teens. My Grandmother described her as a wilful and unstoppable force of nature. My Uncle described her as a teenage whore who got knocked up and then gave the baby to our "Mom and Dad" to raise as their own ... and then went back to partying. Picture of my Mom as a teen - taken during WWII between 1936-38​As I said, Mom lied constantly, so just how much of what she said was true, and how much imagined, will never be known. When I was little, I'd heard my Grandmother telling a friend member how my Mom had shamed the family. While still in her teens, she moved in with a physician without benefit of marriage. The most shocking part of this story is that this physician was also a Nazi SS officer. Mom told a story, to anyone who would listen, about her love for a physician named Carl. How they had worked for the underground to save people from the Nazis. She more or less glossed over the fact that Carl was an SS Officer. My Mom spoke often about how her Dad removed her from school and sent her away to care for her Mother before she gave birth to Wouter. Both my Mom and her brother Maarten had been born at home. Why would a rich woman, who had never gone into confinement before, suddenly leave town with her teenage daughter? By all accounts my Mom's relationship with her Mom was strained difficult. So why wasn't my grandmother attended by her own mother? When I asked my Mom, why her Mother took her along during confinement, she had no answer. The only fact I know, is that she went away to give birth in the country, possibly as a Lebensborn participant. Her 46-year-old mother accompanied her, and later told people the boy born to my Mom was her own. When I asked my Mom how old she was when Walt was born, she paused for a moment and said she'd just turned 12 years old, which made absolutely no sense. What mother would take a 12 year old child along to assist during her birth? I eventually learned Wouter was born on 19 May 1937, when my Mother was actually 16 years old. After the war my Mom was arrested and labeled a collaborator. She was possibly paraded in the street with other collaborators. My Mom said her Dad had saved her from having her head shaved. Another story was that she was the last person in line, and they got tired of shaving girls heads ... and just let her go. Obviously people viewed my Mom differently after the war. After all, being branded a collaborator wasn't something one could easily escape or hide from. I imagine life was hard for her. So I understand why she applied for U.S. citizenship as many times as she did. Her requests were denied 4 times. I never understood, why a woman who had dated so many rich and famous men, would marry a poor man like my father. It was also confusing that someone as anti semitic as my Mom obviously was, would marry a jew. Mom often spoke about how she met my Dad (a holocaust survivor and jew), just after the war. He had been working as a prison guard at camp for Nazis, collaborators, and other war criminals. What was a spoiled rich girl doing at a prison camp? She intimated she was there visiting a friend. Carl perhaps? When Dad proposed marriage, why did Mom tell him her little brother Wouter was really her son? When Dad told her he didn't care, and loved her anyway, she told him she was just testing his love for her. Like thousands of other children, my brother developed polio in California. My parents were achingly poor when they arrived in the U.S., they were well off in the Netherlands. The question being, would my brother have developed polio in Holland? While rickets can be easily treated by various means, polio cannot. Walt fathered many children who I'd always believed were my cousins. The truth is, they're my nieces and nephews. I wasn't able to put all the pieces together until a few years ago, when I started searching for information on my family. I uncovered way too many lies, and the truth about my Dad's family. In 2012 I sent my Brother a DNA test from Ancestry, Genealogy, Family Trees & Family History Records at Ancestry.com. I had taken the same test a few months earlier, and told him I hoped to discover if he and I shared the same Father. For reasons best known to my Brother, after agreeing to take the test, he never followed through. A year later he died ... so I'll never know if he was my full brother. By the grace of God I've been able to prove a biological connection with 3rd and 4th cousins related to my Grandmother's side of my family. The Jewish side of my family. So odds are in my favor, that Dad was really my biological father. Why Mom put so much energy into making me believe that Dad wasn't my biological father is something I'll never know. Perhaps she had been fooling around at the time, and didn't know herself.​The Bleekrodes - Sarah's Family Five of my Grandmother's relatives were killed in Auschwitz on the 22nd of August 1943. They had been living together in an Amsterdam apartment with a non Jewish family member. A non Jew residing in the Apartment complex reported my Grandmother's family to the Nazi's, who removed the Bleekrodes at gunpoint. Eventually all were transported to Auschwitz and killed that same day. My Great Grandfather (Sarah's then frail 82-year-old Father) had been living with family when Nazi soldiers took him away. My Dad had been there when Nazi soldiers removed his Grandfather from their home at gunpoint. After being beaten nearly to death on the street, Mozes Bleekrode died in a Dutch Concentration camp under Nazi control. Sara's brother Abraham Bleekrode had been a concert violinist before WWII. During the war, he became a Nazi resistance fighter. His exploits are part of Dutch history. He died in Buchenwald, a little more than a month before the camp was liberated. My Grandmother Kleintje died in Amsterdam in 1985 (long after the war), she was 96 years old. Mozes Bleekrode (Sara's Father) - Diamond Cutter - Death 1 April 1944 in Westerbork Concentration Camp Rachel Bleekrode - Birth 24 May 1887 in Amsterdam, Netherlands - Death 22 October 1943 in Auschwitz - husband: Abraham Vogel (Rachel's second husband) - Death 22 October 1943 in Auschwitz - daughter: Rebecca (by her first husband) - Death 7 September 1942 in Auschwitz Abraham Bleekrode Violinist, WWII Resistance Fighter - Birth 17 April 1891 in Amsterdam, Netherlands - Death 20 February 1945 in Buchenwald - Abraham's first wife was Maria Petronella Blom, with whom he had two children. His children (Betje and Mozes Bleekrode) went with their Mother after she remarried. Both children of hers survived the war. Samuel Bleekrode - Birth 17 June 1893 in Amsterdam, Netherlands - Death 11 February 1944 in Auschwitz - wife: Vrouwtje Presser - Birth 28 October 1892 in Amsterdam, Netherlands - Death 11 February 1944 in Auschwitz - son: Mozes Bleekrode - Birth 29 September 1924 in Amsterdam, Netherlands - Death 30 September 1942 in Auschwitz at age 17, same age as my Dad. Benjamin Isaäc Bleekrode - Birth 16 May 1895 Amsterdam, Netherlands - wife: Johanna Daniëlla Garms Regina Bleekrode - Birth 27 March 1895 in Amsterdam, Netherlands - Death 22 October 1943 in Auschwitz - son: Paul Bleekrode - Birth 23 August 1923 in Valburg, Gelderland, Netherlands - Death 22 October 1943 in Auschwitz​Leendert Bleekrode - Birth 3 November 1901 in Amsterdam, Netherlands - was in Australia with his wife Ester when the Nazis began rounding up Jews. Their son Ralph was born in Sydney. His remaining family still resides in Australia. Hartog Bleekrode - Birth 20 October 1902 - Died Maartensdijk 22 April 1945 - wife: Berendina Alida Meeuwig - Death unknown - daughter: Maria Clasina Bleekrode - Died in Auschwitz 6 March 1944 Eva Bleekrode - Birth 9 January 1906 - Death 22 October 1943 in Auschwitz along with her husband Samuel Gobits and their son Samuel​Who am I?Some days I don't know why I'm still here. Everyone in my family is dead. ​My Mom, Dad and Brother have all passed. After all I've survived and all I was forced to endure, the abuse, torture, pain and illness ... I can't understand why I'm the only one left.​The last photo taken of my parents together.​The last photo taken of my brother and his wife Angie. They died less than a month apart in 2013. Last year added my Family's name to a monument built on Ellis Island. "Barkemeijer de Wit - Family" is inscribed there and will be for generations to come. I did so to honor the memory of my Family and their journey to America ... where "I" was born.​Who am I and who will I become? My life and my identity were stolen long ago. I'm 60, is it too late for me to feel hope ... long for a future ... and believe things will be better? For now I'm busy cataloging the lives and deaths of my Grandmother Sarah's entire family. It's slow work and heartbreakingly sad. My prayers are to all who passed in the Holocaust. May their souls find peace.​I've written so much about my past and the abuse I suffered, I felt like I needed to add something about the blessings in my life. I was blessed to have a man named Melvin C Johnson as a Father-in-law. But he was much more than that. In every way except by blood HE WAS MY DAD. It was he who taught me what it felt to have unconditional love. It was he noticed I was suffering from physical illness and "I wasn't crazy". Mel got me to doctors who diagnosed the various autoimmune disorders I was born with ... and got me to treatment.He's one of the biggest reasons I'm alive now. He passed in 2008, at age 94. Even now almost 8 years later, we keep a candle burning for him every day. I will miss him until I die.​In October of 2015, our Greyhound Harvey (also a service dog) succumb to cancer. In many ways he was one of the last links I had to Mel, as Harvey was very special to Mel.​
column9: Hi Jeanne, such an interesting family history you have. Have you discovered Eva Kor here on Quora? She is a holocaust survivor from Auschwitz, one of the twins Mendele experimented on. You might find solace in some of her answers. :)

column1: How is your life turning out? Has it been better or worse than what you expected?
column3: Well - dear diary - be prepared for a lengthy - ‘hanging out my dirty laundry’ - baloney. I never aspired to do anything in life as a kid. Bit of a bouncing ball all over the place. Primary, secondary school. I did what I want, felt nothing interested me much and just followed what came easy (finance/economics/maths). Some teachers told me - hey chap, high school ain’t for you after I failed my last year in high school - go to LDN - study something there and join the financial industry. Between 15–18, I was a truant, not listening to anything, I wasn’t a bad kid, not a dreamer, didn’t do drugs or destroy things - that would be just as silly as studying standardized texts some high school teacher would force me to study for - knowing it wouldn’t be relevant anyway. I was just a wandering soul. At that point, I’ve had a shit childhood - lived in 3 countries over 18 years - and had various foster dads and moms given my dad/mom divorced at a young age and my (biological mom) had a psychosis, various physical and mental diseases and entered in up a psycho ward for >20/30years hopping over various countries until she passed away. I’ve been treated like a piece of crap for 15 years by various foster parents as a pay cheque, laughed at, beaten, slept outside, ‘told me I was an idiot’, Germany, United Kingdom, Netherlands. I was not fed. But do you think I was ‘crying’? Laughing? I was a kid. There was an adult - telling me; ‘this is how it is supposed to be’. Kids trust adult. I didn’t think of future, hopes, dreams, nothing. Albeit by definition I felt and realized I am an outsider - and even though I realized I was one - it didn’t hurt me. So be it. Can’t all be the same. It didn’t hurt. I had no need to blend in with others. I am OK to be alone. Furthermore, I realized puzzling, maths, banking, all that stuff came relatively easy. Well, if it came easy, it meant less effort - and given money and everything around it attracts low life degenerates - it was extremely easy to be 1 step ahead of a whole group, my entire life - which means by the help of others I was slowly guided in a simple life trajectory - banking. I didn’t want it - but once I joined - I felt as a fish in the water. I definitely didn’t pursue it on my own behalf. Never cared about long term goals. Never cared about tasks or shit that had to be done. Just cared about material issues of today, tomorrow and what’s coming. If I was told to do X by COB today, I try to pitch X to some dummy on the floor and chit-chat with a more senior colleague to see if I could help him. Yeah - respect for authority after my childhood went away. From junior to managing director. Whenever I went - wherever I went - flat hierarchy for me. Banking isn’t difficult. If you can convince A or B that what you propose impacts their pnl (on top) or on the bottom (costs) they will listen. All the time. I didn’t need 14 certificates to realize that. I job hobbed from M&A related roles to quantitative roles to consultancy to anything in between and most of all I enjoyed it. I married - lovely wife, and money came in - I truly saw the world, had fun (nothing of this was planned, I never plan more than a few days or weeks in the future) - and then suddenly around 2015/2016/2017 -the stench of political correctness affected my worksuddenly meritocracy didn’t mean anything any more - we required identified helicopters from Madagascar, preferably a boy who turned a girl who turned cisgender with poor upbringing who was going to be our Equity Derivatives head of desk - the 50 white males who applied for this job weren’t eligible for it any longer.We suddenly introduced random male 50%/female 50% ratio’s without any scientific rational - there are simply more men supply wise than female’s - focusing random 50/50% ratio’s simply means you dilute quality in a ‘for profit business’ and I have yet to tell and convince me that this is the exact right thing to do. This has been going on for a while - and so far results are appaling.No-one cared anything about the bottom, the kids - as I feel if you give kids (of all backgrounds) the equal chance to make something of themselves - they’ll be alright - but suddenly adults forced kids to focus on subjects they generally had no interest in. I remember when I was a kid - when adults would say do X, kids would do Y. And the kids who would do X - eventually once adult would resent/despise their parents as they felt they were pushed into something they never wanted. My biological dad never cared for what I did. He just wanted me be to be happy.Suddenly, managers had checklists that they had to pass 50% diversify inclusion as their annual targets. Ridiculous.Not surprisingly shit like Brexit and whatnot came knocking - with an even less surprising Google News headline (after the vote) - ‘gosh what does brexit actually mean’. I think I once more shat myself of hilarity. Not sure whether to laugh or cry.HR interviews were more standardized than everything - everyone had to get a fair chance. Made a lot of sense if you compare an Ivy League kid who never had to fight for a bloody thing or an autodidact student from Belarus who had to fight tooth and nail to get there. Riiiight.I was told (pre-corona office times) my swearing wasn’t professional. I told them - I do this out of passion, happiness, I’m glad a plan gets together. I feel joy. They looked at me like - how can you swear if you are happy? I felt I should take a single-ticket to Mars at that point.ALL JOY LEFT - work. Not overnight, slowly but surely. Up to 2015/2016, i’ve had a amazing life. Fun, success, lovely wife, travelling, did what I want, progress, everything moved on. I was able to look back and I felt I ticket off my bucket lists 4/5 times. But the midlife crisis sifted into my head. AKA - Quora joined in my ranks - and I started rambling this as my dear-dear diary after visiting my shrink/dad and saying - well, traditional banking, it might not be for me anymore. In the Post Brexit 2016–2020 time, I was still responsible for the ‘moving area’ from UK to mainland Europe - but that also stopped roughly when Corona entered. Well, that’s where all the trouble started. I’ve lost various co-workers (and their parents & families) on corona in 2020. In 2021,my wife got into the hospital due to heart related issuesacquired coronayelled at me at the phone - if you don’t fucking move on without me I’ll haunt you in your dreams (she wasn’t afraid of death - never was)she passed awayher will was done and settled - and we gave away quite a bit of extravaganza to her family.Well, her family disagreed - and they wanted more - so suddenly all the low-life degenerates crawled from nowhere - and said - if your wife was alive - I would have been in her will and I am ‘entitled’ to her money.I got suedagainagainagainwell, you get the pointGiven these were all cases based on ‘emotions’ - and I work in ‘risk’ as a profession where emotions aren’t part of my day to day job - it was mostly a walk in the park - but I had no time to mourn anything in my lifeone family member on her end got so crazy and desperate she crashed the car - ended up in a psychiatric hospital - suicide - and poof - gone. I knew money is the root of all evil. I didn’t need another evidence for this.Somewhere in the middle of this summer - my dad got ill, 3rd time around, cancer - and that it’s progressing.So that was a merry-go-round after all the ‘sued, sued, merry go around’ - back to being a care-taker - talking about our past etc.That is where we are, atm.This year has been absolute shite. Understatement. I’ve seen all the worst characteristics of humankind in 1 year. Did I tell you I visited the hospital my wife was in - while there were protests outside, Corona didn’t exist? I was too weak and numb to say anything, my head went through a tumble dryer.Am I where I want to be?I have a contractual obligation to mid-year February 2022I have flights booked to US by end February 2022.I am excited what the future holds.I can’t wait to close this book, I hold no resentment - it’s their loss, not mine.I won’t marry again - but perhaps a new family - who knows.I don’t know where I want to be - because in my entire life that never crossed my mind. But every ‘new’ emotion in my life. Well, I can place it.Until recently, Omnicron Persei 8 - new Corona variant. Dad and myself on a DIY test got tested - results were not what we wanted. It’s the end of the year. And there I was once again - hey, another shit - storm heading our way.It won’t put me down. Family, friends, loved ones, strangers, experiences, life, real life, is why I am on this planet. Prestige, pride, wealth, ego, it can all kiss my ass. I love life. I always did. I’ve buried family. Friends. Loved ones. A tear here and there. Have I changed some of my values this year, of course I have. I realize my wife was a shield between me and my in-law family. I also understand above all - I need to pursue the ‘fulfilment/purpose’ in life - as banking has nothing but been a big kindergarten for adults to have fun. My wife was the one who knew where to put the money (foundations, charities, trusts, etc) I earned. That wife ain't there any more. I surely ain't trusting any blind soul on their blue eyes to give them money for a good cause. Trust will come first. I know what I need to;stay in motionthat meansmeet new peoplenew opportunitiesthey might spark ideasideas I might supportI can work for that and help thoseAnd above all - those times will come, and I am looking forward to it.Every time you feel life overwhelms you - you feel down - I look out the window, think for a second. I don’t have it bad. I never had it bad. I only need to do one thing. Motion. Keep moving. Don’t stay in the same place. Look up new things. Investigate new stuff. Stuff you feel drawn towards to. Follow whoever talks to you - their line of reasoning. They talk with a political agenda? They do? Fuck them. They don’t - fire back and see if they follow your line of reasoning. Eventually new opportunities will cross your path - your flame will be that big you’ll need new underpants every 2 hours - and a group of new friends, old friends will hop on your slipstream like before to follow in new adventures you are going to pursue, no matter how far you sunk the year before. But if you stay and drown in self-pity, cry, mask pain with drugs, alcohol and cigarettes, jump in a rebound, hang out with the wrong friends. Let’s speak again in 10–20–30 years - you’ll regret your choices. Perhaps not you - but statistically the majority will.
column9: Keep it going. A lot of folks like us appreciate the banter. Love the writings of a lovely dinosaur. Godspeed Uncle Ross.

column1: What are some things that people don’t tell you about being pregnant and giving birth?
column3: With the sight of two pink lines on the test kit comes whooping congratulations from everyone! You are all set to grow a new body inside you. People shower you with blessings and good wishes for your good news.It must be the most beautiful thing ever, right? But, oh wait! Good news…is it? Did you know these facts most of the pregnant women go through:Farting accompanied with constipation - In the first couple of months you may pass a lot of gas or burp a lot. You may also experience heartburn from time to time. Embarassing right? But that's how it is as your body produces high levels of progesterone which slows down muscle contractions hence slowing down digestion process. This results in a lot of gas buildup, flatulence and acid reflux.Washroom becomes your second home - You will pee, a lot. Every 15 minutes you will feel like rushing to the washroom and also get a little leak here and there. With the growing uterus putting a pressure on your bladder with each passing day you may even pee your pants when you laugh, or cough or sneeze. In my office, the washroom was only 15 steps away from my seat but it felt like eternity during my pregnancy to rush to washroom everytime my bladder filled up.Extreme mood swings - Thanks to your hormones going haywire, you will feel every emotion to its extremity. At one moment you will feel happy, you will be bawling at the next. You may even want to murder your husband if he ate your favourite last piece of sweet.Nausea can last till you give birth - Nausea is common in pregnancy, specially in the first trimester. For a lucky few (like me), you may not feel nausea at all. But some unfortunate women face a condition called Hypermesis Gravidarum occurs. It involves severe and persistent vomiting that can lead to hospitalization for dehydration.Pelvic girdle pain- PGP or Symphisis Pubic Dysfunction(SPD) affects few percentage of women during pregnancy making it extremely painful for women to walk, turn sides in bed, go upstairs, get in and out of car etc. This can turn pretty serious and extreme pain in pelvic region should be treated with utmost care.Sex takes a backseat - Sex can be pretty uncomfortable and funny while you are pregnant both for you and your partner. The growing belly, the fear of hurting ourselves or harming the baby, pain during intercourse and the hormonal changes all contributes to hating the idea of having sex.Goodbye to your favourite food for 9months - About half of all expectant mothers end up with one or more food aversions. All of a sudden, they cannot stomach certain foods, even ones they used to love. For example: You have loved morning tea your whole life and can no longer stand the smell of it or your meals started and ended with eggs, meat and fish and you can no longer sit in the same table with other people having them. Your sense of taste and smell are at their peak during pregnancy. You may even crave for weird non-food items.Time to buy new set of lingerie - As your body keeps on changing with each passing day, your old lingeries may no longer fit you or add to your discomfort. It's always a good idea to get some new pairs with the right size and fit.Vaginal births can have painful after effects too - There's not an ounce of doubt that vaginal birth is the best, both for the mother and the baby. But during normal delivery, skin and tissue around the vagina will stretch and may tear as the baby moves down through birth canal. The tearing has to be stitched immediately . Without stitches, it can negatively affect urine and bowel function. This stitch may leave mom with some pain in the perineum — the area between the vagina and anus. And sitting straight can be painful for some days.Risks and aftereffects of C-section - Some women has to listen to the rants of people that they are not mom enough because they birthed their babies via C-section.With a C-section, mom has a higher risk for blood loss and infection. There’s also a higher risk for injury to the bowels or bladder and for blood clots. The risk of the death of the mom due to blood clots, infections and complications from anesthesia is three times greater with a C-section when compared to a vaginal delivery.My experience after giving birth - I had and emergency C - section after 12 hours of labour. After delivery on one hand drips was going on with all the antibiotics and saline. A catheter was attached to the bladder for draining the urine. I was not able to lift my body up without help. I was extremely exhausted, bleeding profusely, was having a very bad headache due to the epidural anaesthesia. Forgetting all that, my priority was to breastfeed my baby every 2 hours or on demand, to learn how to latch the baby properly, how to hold him, how to soothe him. At the night, I was so tired I couldn't keep my eyes open but still had to feed the baby as new borns won't sleep at night.There's no point in being shy with your body - I was an extremely shy person throughout my life. I wouldn't even dress up in front of my mother. My pregnancy changed the whole ball game. From the day of my labour pains till my 3 nights in the hospital,my body was exposed to every nurse, every doctor, the lactation consultant, the physiotherapist, my family members ( my mother and my mother-in-law were taking turns to help me feed the baby properly, helped me change clothes, saw my body being washed etc.,). You never know when who will come and check your body parts. And the fun part was, you are so exhausted and worried to keep your baby well you don't even feel shy or self-conscious.This tumultous journey of 9months, the pain, the fatigue, the tears of childbirth vanish when we look at and hold our most anticipated angel. This is me a few hours after my baby’s birth.This is a day after (look at my swollen hand and fingers after the drips taken off). Hope my answer helps!
column9: You have just described what my wife went through during her pregnancy. She was in 18hrs of labour before going through emergency c-section. After that she got the headache due to anesthesia. I was next to her all time. Reading your answer brought all those memories back.

column1: If someone pays their mortgage for five years in advance, what happens to that money?
column3: That’s not a smart thing to do. Let’s say your family member died and left you $100K. You want to use all that to make house payments. I would tell you, “bad idea”. Contact the lender and ask them how to make a principal reduction payment. Then make that principal reduction payment with $50K or half of the money. Your monthly payment will not go down, you will still need to make monthly payments each and every month. However, the end date of your loan just got closer. For example, your original loan needed monthly payments until 2053, after making that principal reduction payment, you loan end date has moved to 2050 (that’s three years of not making payments and saving three years of loan interest payments). When you get a loan statement, you’ll see that $$$ was paid to reduce the principal and $$$$$ was paid for the loan interest. At the beginning of a loan you pay a large amount of your payment toward interest and a small amount toward principal. Toward the end of the loan period you pay the large amount for principal and a small amount toward interest. When you pay principal reduction, the interest part of the payment vanishes - you never have to pay that interest. The half of the $100K ($50K) should be split into half $25K put into a savings account in case of emergency (you’ll have money to make house payments). The other $25K goes into a self directed 401K retirement plan where it can grow and provide you with some of the funds you’ll need when you retire (social security only gives you about 1/3rd of the money you need to retire). If you pay 5 years advanced mortgage payments, then you’ll live for 5 years without having to make mortgage payments. Sounds good, but you will become accustomed to having significantly more money to spend and maybe get a new expensive car and boat. The end of 5 years will come up really fast and suddenly you have to make mortgage payments that you haven’t been paying for 5 years. You have been using that mortgage payment money for other things. Now those other things need to go away because you need that money for mortgage payments. Now the 5 years are over, you start having money problems because you changed your lifestyle to the no mortgage lifestyle. Now that dreaded mortgage has returned and you will have to change your lifestyle again (sell the car, sell the boat at a loss). When anyone comes into a large sum of money, they need to be careful what they do with that money. We’ve all heard about the lottery winners that went from nothing to millions and back to nothing. Don’t be that guy.
column9: Good advice, but I don’t think that you can even pay 5 yrs in advance on a mortgage even if you want to? I think the lender would just apply it all to principal and you will still need to make your full payment the next month.

column1: Who was the most toxic person in your life that you let go?
column3: My mother. I grew up a Jehovah’s Witness. I remember in my earliest of years; she was loving, kind, and compassionate. I’m the eldest of 6. It wasn’t until after her 3rd child/ son that her perceptions towards life began to change drastically. She became resentful of her non-conforming husband. And began acting out as result. She became extremely emotionally and physically abusive towards us. She also had her own set of mental issues that manifested into a nightmare: 1) she never sought out help 2) she believed doctors weren’t legitimate 3) her religion taught against seeking outside help 4) the elders taught witnesses to come to them with they’re problems; that they had the solution. Because of these variables; her mental disorders got worse and worse over the years and we (the children) experienced the result first hand. She had 4 different fathers for her 6 children. She hated our fathers and in turn; we experienced some of the most hateful acts because of that hatred. We were being emotionally, psychologically, and physically abused sometimes on a daily basis. She would make remarks such as: “I wish I never had you!” “You’re a waste of oxygen!” “I wish you had never been born!” “You’re just like your dad” “do you think I wanted to have all these kids?” If we were clearly upset; she would laugh hysterically. We would cry and go to our rooms and cry some more. If she didn’t want us around she would scream “GET AWAY FROM ME!” She was always screaming; after my second brother came I cannot remember any time in our childhoods that she wasn’t screaming with demands. I told her I was molested when I was 5 when I went to visit my father. Her response was “SO WHAT; my father raped me when I was a child.” Any time I needed someone to confide in; her answer was to completely strip me of my humanity, validity, and instill me with more fear. These are experiences from my perspective and do not include what my younger siblings have seen, felt, or endured. When she was in psycho-mode; she’d gang up on us; singling out the weakest and smallest. Our bodies stood frozen as she would push the smallest child to the floor. Sometimes it was me; but really she would grab anyone she could reach; the ones that were too slow in running away, the ones she knew wouldn’t fight back, the ones she hated the most. She’d get me to the ground, fight or fight mode would set in, panicking inside my mind, I’d cover my head with both my arms balling up into the fetile position. She would hover over my body like an ape. Pounding her fists against my back, head, tummy, legs, arms, and pulled our hair. She would beat the skin until red marks and scratches lined the skin from head to toe. I’d close my eyes tight and pray that she would have her fill, find satisfaction, and stop. We’d whimper beneath the wretched screaming that echoed through our ears; and I can still hear her screams when I close my eyes- today. Though I remember countless times in childhood; watching as a helpless bystander hiding in a hallway, behind a bookshelf, or standing behind her as she raised both her fists and using all her might and strength to repeatedly smash her knuckles and fists against her helpless crying children. Afterward when she had her fill- they/we/I would stand up- shaking with fear, hands, arms and entire little bodies trembling. Sweating, tears smother our faces, snot dripping from our noses. We’d try to collect what was left of ourselves, walk to our rooms, crawl into our beds, and sob for hours. Because we knew that our mother did not really love us. We were a reminder, a burden on her life, and our births had stolen the life she could have lived- had we never been born. I tried really hard not to set her off into psycho-mode; but it wasn’t always something we could individually gage. She would turn evil in an instant. I remember asking if I could spend the night at a cousins house. I was about 13. We were in the kitchen and she pushed me against the wall. She said “I SAID NOO!” she became enraged in a split second. After she pushed me; she used both her hands and began to strangle me- there against the wall. Her grip was so tight. I could feel the pressure building up behind my eyeballs. I tried to pull her hands from my neck but her grip was so tight. All she had to do was say no. But saying no wasn’t enough. She had to degrade me, humiliate me, and strip me of whatever was even left of my humanity. Really we were just there for her entertainment, it didn’t even feel like i was a real person, and I wanted so badly to have a different life. I hated my life. From the outside looking in mother was an extremely great actress. No one would have known; and the people I did tell didn’t care either. I was told to respect my mother; that whatever I did- I probably deserved. And the abuse I told other family members about- they called me a liar- that I was exaggerating. Or flat out ignored. And so this is how my childhood quickly manifested into a nightmare that I and my siblings were unable to escape from. We endured the abuse and we tried really hard to accept this as punishment even though it clearly was not an ‘acceptable’ form of punishment. Sometimes she would run after the littlest ones. I’d yell for my brother to scoop up the children and go to his room and lock the door. He would. I would gladly spare them the tears and would face the monster head on. By this time I was a teenager; however I was physically, emotionally, and psychologically abused until age 21. I would stand before her in the peak of her red, screaming, hateful face. As a teen we were the same height but I was a tad taller. I could have easily hit her back. I never did. I was so scared of her and what she could do if I didn’t let her get her beatings in. So I would just stand there facing her. She would bring her raging fists into the air in full over head swings; by this age I could at least block the hits directed for my face or top of head. Sometimes I didn’t block well enough and she would indeed punch my face. The children could hear her screaming at me from the other room; but at least they didn’t have to see it, or be the ones to take it, I was old enough that I could protect them, and I had no choice in the matter, the instinct came naturally. It was my unspoken responsibility. They were in diapers; what kind of a person would I be to allow her to torture them? I wanted to save them all but I just didn’t know how. At the time I didn’t understand what civil rights even were, laws, or that child abuse and neglect could create jail time. I struggled with chronic depression and anxiety as a result of never adequately being loved, valued, appreciated, etc. By the time I left the house at 21; I had zero self esteem; and I had daily suicidal thoughts. This manifested into a full blown eating disorder- anorexia. I struggled with my disorder for at least 5years. I spent my early 20s filling my voids with one night stands, drinking, adderal, and too much weed. My antidepressants dulled out my emotions. I thought- I’d rather feel nothing- than every emotion drowning me at once. I stayed on the antidepressants and anxiety meds for 6–7years. 2015 I was 28. My middle brother became severely ill, he was 22. They had moved across the country 3years prior. The 3 other children were still under 17 at the time. March 27th he died in one of the most inhumane ways possible. Mother called me ONLY the night before his actual death; to tell me he was dying and that he had acute leukemia. A disease that had potential to be treated, or prevented had she cared about his health, if she cared about taking him to the doctor, etc. He did not have an Advanced Directive and in turn; she became his proxy end-of-life decision maker. He needed a blood transfusion. The Doctors said he had the leukemia for at least 5 or more years. He had been having multiple nose bleeds a day for over a month prior to his death. Because of the persistent nose bleeds that she shoulder shrugged the seriousness of the reoccurrence. Sure he was 22; but when your mother pulls you from public education system at age 14; you lose out on some very valuable life lessons had you had that opportunity to an education that every child in America should have a right to. He still lived at home. He was the children’s protector. Because of the nose bleeds- there was an enormous amount of blood putting pressure on his brain. He would have needed several blood transfusions to extend his life, brain surgery, and he would have needed morphine to aid his suffering and anguish as his body slowly shut down. And over night- with only 12hours notice; my darling brother had died in the most in un-compassionate way. I never got to say goodbye. My world began to dissolve in itself. Losing my beloved brother in this unfathomable way exasperated my Eating disorder. I was in mourning; and I didn’t know how to cope. I already was sitting just below 95lbs; and one month later I had lost 10lbs. By August of 2015 I was at 75lbs at 5’5”. I was a walking skeleton. The longest I’ve gone without food or water was 4 days. All my family had turned they’re backs on me and I was completely abandoned. Mother told our family lies, made up stories, and slandered my name to people I once called family. January 2016. I spoke to her on the phone and she said “you’re an apostate; and there’s no more room for you in my life.” And in an instant I was shunned. (The true definition of an apostate is someone who simply doesn’t believe in particular religious beliefs). It’s true- you will be shunned for simply not conforming or believing in they’re ‘truth.’ It happened to me; and I personally know at least a dozen young people who have been shunned in similar ways by they’re loved ones. There’s no way around the shunning- and one must simply accept this as a process of life. I did also speak ill of her religion- Jehovah’s Witnesses; who teach against the acceptance of blood transfusions, the acceptance of organ donations, or acquiring a donated organ. This religious belief is in part why my brother died the way he did. I simply don’t support religious policies that kill people- seeing as how many of these illnesses could have been prevented- I mean we’re not living in a pre-Christ era… Modern science and medicine is a gift to millions/ billions of people and has made a significant impact in uncountable lives. I almost died from my eating disorder: anorexia. There are many variables that influenced my disorder. I also had a difficult time accepting myself as a woman. I felt that my gender fell to equally of both feminine and masculine attributes. I identified with both. And on October 9, 20I7 I began my gender transition. Having access to my medication completely changed my life. I could be who I wanted and didn’t have to answer to anyone but myself. My expression has always been neutral; but this is in part because men’s clothes were far to large to fit my body without looking awkward. I keep it simple I do identify a particular way- but to minimize the questions or comments I simply use male pronouns and anything else about that aspect of gender is no ones business in knowing. Some of us prefer to blend and don’t enjoy being singled out for others entertainments. Being shunned was a blessing in disguise and though my transition has brought on a different set of obstacles. For me the people I surround myself with now love me without judgements and fully accept me for who I am. Where my family absolutely would have never accepted and would have found obscene ways of belittlement and put downs. I simply do not exist to accomplish other peoples expectations of me, who they think I should be, how they think I should live, or what they think should be done with my life. If you don’t like how I live; I don’t have time to entertain you. I spoke to my mother two other times last Summer 2018. She wanted to talk about my transition and I didn’t want to discuss the matter with her. I wanted her to give me an apology for the horrible pain she had caused us. She refused to admit anything and said I was exaggerating. She did not apologize but did say “I could have done some things differently.” She also refused to admit that she had shunned me Jan 2016. In that moment I knew- I would never receive a real heartfelt apology. I told her that hearing her voice literally made my stomach curdle. Hearing her nagging voice could roll me into a full blown relapse. Agony rushed back through me as anxiety manifested from my stomach, I felt qweezy, and my hands trembled as I held the phone to my ear. In a few moments of word exchanges- I felt very small, succumbing to her rich fear, like an abused child all over again but in my adult body about to have a blackout panic attack. I blocked her number and I told her I never wanted her to contact me again. She is the very trigger to my doom. While anorexic I could feel inside my body and my organs would scream with pain in anguish. August 2015 marks the beginning of my recovery journey. None of my family was present in this journey. I had to completely restructure my life and family was no longer my #1. I was shunned and not permitted to make contact with those I loved. I had to learn to live without them. And I did, I learned, it was effing hard. I’ve never been hospitalized; though I should have been countless times. I’ve had over a dozen IV saline drinks, over a dozen relapses, and here I am four years later-50lbs stronger in solid gains! I’m the happiest I have ever been in my entire life, the strongest I have ever been, and through trial and error have found that I am capable of more than the limitations I once had set upon myself. I am capable of more than the limitations others once made me believe as if it was fact. And I am beautiful and am absolutely lovable. I haven’t been on antidepressants for close to 3 years and only take anxiety meds as needed- I do occasionally have body disabling panic attacks that can lead to blackouts and vomiting; however these have become rare occurrences which I’m thankful for. I didn’t drink alcohol for 2.5years of my recovery pursuits, I quit smoking weed 9mo ago, and no longer seek to engage in risky behaviors to fulfill momentary voids. The void gap has almost entirely closed and my losses no longer rule my life and decision making. After you cross out the negatives in life- you actually are creating and manifesting positive change. I have ptsd; sure but I no longer suffer from chronic depression and my anxiety is the most minimal it’s ever been. I refuse to allow ptsd limit my ability my ability in having a full and abundant life. After the source of pain had been removed fully; I was finally able to provide myself with self love, balance, I relearned how to eat, enjoy food, cooking, and being fully present in my life. Though it wasn’t initially my choice to remove her from my life; i absolutely would have died if I had allowed her to have an active role in my life. I also have two of my siblings back in my life; they both have extremely minimal contact with our mother. And both will need extensive therapy and self love in rebuilding what had been stripped of them growing up in that nightmare. It’s definitely not imperative that you keep your parents in your life if they attempt to destroy you. You can end the cycle of abuse; you simply must walk away from everything that is familiar, everything and everyone you love to reach that goal. And I know; it’s not exactly a simple task to attempt. But in order to live your best life; you must firstly live your worst life. You’ll be far more grateful for what you have. Perseverance is key in dream catching. You can become your own hero; this is what I gave to myself. Though I cannot change my past- I can change the course of my future with these lessons I have learned in losing everything yet gaining so much in reward back. And for the first time; I have real hope for my future. It’s close and I am indeed making something of myself to live my best life in the future I dream. I miss my brother and I mourn him still; but I know he’s at peace and he watches over me smiling and he’s proud of the person that I’ve worked to become. This is my story of overcoming and triumphing through adversity and immeasurable loss. I’ve also added my sick to fit progress pic. Now that I can call myself an eating disorder survivor. It’s rather amazing what this 50lb gain has done to my body. Not a single bone or rib exposed! Everyday I am grateful. I made this account so my brothers music could live on, be appreciated, and induce smiles- please enjoy these songs of musical bliss…Thank you for reading. thynamewasjohn.bandcamp.com
column9: You deserve to be incredibly proud of your tenacity; to endure all the hardships you have and come out on top is a testament to your resilience and strength.

column1: Is it normal to want to reach out to a narcissist after they discard you?
column3: It is normal because you care about your ex and loved them. You have formed a deep emotional connection with this person. In normal relationship reaching out could result in a reconciliation or healthy closure. However if it's a case of one person having high narcissistic tendencies, you may more than likely be even more hurt if you reach out, because this is an opportunity to gain even more supply from you and make the narcissistic individual feel even more important, in control and powerful. This is what they ultimately want, along with material things and admiration. Ask yourself what would your relationship be like if you reached out and they accepted you back? Would they respect you more because of it, or less? Would they treat you better or feel even more empowered to mistreat you because you decided to come back after everything they did in the past? Ultimately you teach people how they can treat you by the way you respond to their actions. I understand your pain and I ask myself the above questions almost daily. All I can say is that if your partner, friend or family member is highly narcissistic, reaching out is not worth the pain, emotional scars and loss of your self respect. Thank you for the A2A.
column9: I don’t know what will happen if we become friends again. I was on my way to discard phase anyways. I finally called him out for lying and he really got ballistic like GTA ballistic. My thoughts on this is that he has a mental disorder and as person I should been more… understanding. But I’m only human will be prone to act like one as well.

column1: I've been working on getting over my ex and I've been feeling good. But I just found out she's getting married and I'm shattered. Why?
column3: Remove her from your immediate daily thoughts by living your life. Might sound hard, but you have to let go completely and move on. In time, maybe you'll be happy for her or not care about any of her “news.” I was struggling to not let thoughts of my ex creep in, but I also self abused myself by searching for info on my ex long after it was done. Everything I heard about his new fabulous life without me hurt. Everything He purposely told friends who repeated it so that I might find out, killed me. Losing friends who were his more than mine, bonds with his family members, was hard too. It was awkward to keep mutual friends, so I lost more than him. I lost places we went together..my whole life had to change. As long as I allowed myself to mourn it and stay stuck there, I hurt. I started being brave and said to myself when those feeling were creeping in, “Its over. He's gone. Life goes on. It's okay. You're gonna be ok.” I was honest with myself. I wrote things I would never admit to anyone else, but for myself, I needed to say those things and DEAL WITH IT. I delt with set back by walking, writing and crying if I needed to but also, I made it a effort to fill up where those losses were with new things. Not new people at first. I still had enough sense not to jump into relationships to fill the void. I started volunteering again. Helping others really does feel good and takes a lot of negativity out of your life. Trust me! I just started doing things I hadn't in awhile.. Like painting. I also started going to book stores and reading ..met a few nice people. I made a effort not to add more negativity to my life so no drinking or stupid stuff. You have to feel better on the inside but also take care of your health. Mind, body & soul. It's true. So filling my time and living in spite of occassional bouts of hurt and anger helped me move on. Bet it will help you too! Good Luck!

column1: What is an incident that changed your life?
column3: Start spending the time with the RIGHT people – Surround yourself by people who inspire, challenge, value, love, and appreciate you! Also, be with the ones who make you work harder and raise your game.Start facing your problems – The first step is just acknowledging something is not right and needs an adjustment or solution. No sense in sweeping anything under rug! We all know that is just a temporary fix, so get in there and mix it up with whatever is not in alignment and do something to make it better.Start being honest with yourself –The only one who knows how you really feel, what you really think, your needs, what is working and what is not is YOUPut your own needs on the FRONT burner – This is a toughy, especially being a strong believer in doing service. But what it comes down to is honoring your own self-care and priorities so you CAN be available to others.Be yourself – Any other options? I didn’t think so.Live in the moment – We all have stories about our past but they are just that, stories. The most powerful thing you have on any given day is the moment you are in, so plant and be where your feet are.Feel free to fail – That’s right! Know that mistakes are going to happen, you have a right to be imperfect and one of the best ways to succeed is to fail miserably, correct, then kick ass.Practice self-forgiveness – You did this but “should’ve” done that. Years spent in a certain relationship, career, addiction, negativity, shitty health, fear – the bottom line is, it is all okay. You cannot really move on until you forgive yourself for being human.Buy groceries not happiness – There are certain things money can buy. Like organic grapefruits. Other things, not so much. Like happiness! Happiness is one of those states of mind which don’t have a price tag. Certain things create the sensation of joy, passion, love, pleasure, but HAPPINESS, that is a certain place inside you, accessible by choice.Look to yourself for happiness – It is not going to come from someone else. Not the soulmate, career changer, guru or family member who finally stops nagging you on the holidays. All these people can be appreciated but are not IT.Get moving! Don’t think I have to tell you this one :)Believe you are ready now. This is a great one to practice every day. I’m not saying you are ready to go in and perform open-heart surgery without med school but probably there are things you are STILL putting off bc you don’t think you’re ready when in reality, you ARE.Get involved in healthy relationships for the right reason. If you are looking for someone to save, fix, complete, or solve any emptiness in your heart that is NOT the right reason to be with someone! If you are looking for someone with whom to share your happiness, love, abundance, pleasure, joy and various highs/lows of life’s journey while maintaining your own sense of self, that is the RIGHT reason to be with someone! : drops the mic:Be open to new relationships even if old ones didn’t work. Any previous relationships are just driftwood, lily pads, stepping stones, a little piece of patchwork on the soccer ball of life. Be thankful for every moment.Compete with yourself. You will save a lot of energy if you only seek to be YOUR BEST SELF every moment of every day.Be inspired instead of green-eyed. If someone else is manifesting their greatness, let that be a source of inspiration and motivation. If jealousy grabs you by you know what, notice it and then make a shift. Life is too short to be bitter.Get off the pity pot. Self-pity and complaints, as far as I am concerned, are the like kryptonite on steroids. They suck energy and then, worse, attract the kind of people who like to join the pity party, so all that’s being created is an energy ball of negativity. Walk away from that behavior and anybody who brings it out in you.Let go of grudges. Sometimes it’s fun to make a list of all the people you are still pissed at and why, then see that most, if not all, of it, is ridiculous.Rise to the level you deserve. Not everybody shares the same standards and this can be difficult to accept. When you begin to dictate to yourself what you need and what you are worth, you will attract the people who appreciate your value.Follow your heart. No need to explain yourself and your choices to other people. Just be you.Give yourself a break! But, we all know that we are human beings, not human doings, so attempts to go-go-go without a break will lead to a loss of perspective. Breathe.See the beauty of the small moments.Accept your imperfections. The world is full of flaws and so are you, truly. It makes you exquisite.Be extraordinary. There are no shortcuts on the path to extraordinary.Be real. If it’s not fine, don’t say it is. If it’s not okay, don’t say it is. If you don’t feel good, don’t fake it! Be real, be real, be real.Take responsibility.“The extent to which you can achieve your dreams depends on the extent to which you take responsibility for our life. When you blame others for what you’re going through, you deny responsibility – you give others power over that part of your life.”Keep your focus on the important people who matter. This is about letting go of being all over the place or “trying to be all things to all people.” Just keep the focus on your commitments and people in your circles of choice.Chill out. Worry is like praying for what you don’t want. Worry is a rocking chair that goes back and forth and back and forth and gets you nowhere. Worry is a wart on the face of hope. ENTER YOUR FAVORITE SLOGAN HERE.Focus on what you WANT to happen. You have energy and you have a brain. You can spend your energy projecting negative outcomes OR you can put your focus on what you WANT to happen. You can visualize it to the extent that it feels real, the details, the people, all of it. It is just a choice of where you want to put your attention.BE GRATEFUL. There are so many reasons to be grateful and when you call up your gratitude, your heart opens, you soften, you become more of who you really are AND into your lap will fall even more things to appreciate.

column1: How does vicarious trauma affect professionals in helping roles?
column3: Vicarious trauma , is trauma occur due to their continuous exposure to victims of trauma and violence especially working as victim services, law enforcement, emergency medical services, fire services, and other allied professions. So as definition suggest it trigger due to victim exposure so in helping role there will be Problem Like the following:experiencing lingering feelings of anger, rage and sadness about patient'sbecoming overly involved emotionally with the patientexperiencing bystander guilt, shame, feelings of self-doubtbeing preoccupied with thoughts of patients outside of the work situationover identification with the patient (having horror and rescue fantasies)loss of hope, pessimism, cynicismStrategies for Controlling and reducing effectIncrease your self-observation - recognise and chart your signs of stress, vicarious trauma and burnout.Take care of yourself emotionally - engage in relaxing and self-soothing activities, nurture self-care.Look after your physical and mental wellbeing.Maintain a healthy work/life balance - have outside interests.Be realistic about what you can accomplish - avoid wishful thinking.Don't take on responsibility for your patients' wellbeing but supply them with tools to look after themselves.Balance your caseload - mix of more and less traumatised clients, victims and non-victims.Take regular breaks, take time off when you need to.Seek social support from colleagues, family members.Use a buddy system - particularly important for less experienced doctors.Use peer support and opportunities to debrief.Take up training opportunities.If you need it, take up time-limited group or individual therapy.

column1: What advice would you give to a man who is trying to care for his severely depressed wife? The couple is in their early 30’s, they have no prior experience with depression, and they’re both scared. She’s in therapy. He wants to help but is at a loss.
column3: Editing since posting: I suggest strongly for her to try TMS (Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation) which is quite successful. It is a non invasive treatment, with no side effects. It’s like an MRI, instead of going through the “tunnel” where the patients get the magnetic pulses, in this case the patient wears a helmet and the technician sends magnetic pulses to stimulate the region in the brain that will help with the depression. Usually this type of treatment is covered by insurance, it lasts about 2 to 3 months, twice a week, each session anywhere from 20 to 30 minutes. She can go out right after the session, and continue her day to day chores (work, study or go home). This type of treatment has shown to be quite effective, and a very high percentage of patients’ depression goes in remission. She might need to do the treatment again in a year or two, depending on her improvement. The difference is between night and day. Many patients have become their old selves again, before they had depression. I have a couple of friends and a family member who had TMS and they are functioning fine. I cannot stress how promising it is. She should still continue to see her therapist. Hi, I am so sorry for what they are both going through. It’s going to be rough for a while, and they will need to work hard at it - she can heal, she can recover. She might still be adjusting to therapy if she just started. The therapist might give her medicine (which might have side effects), she should ask her therapist lots of questions, write them down at home, and I suggest she take notes of the answers at the therapist in order to remember , for an effective treatment. She needs to keep notes of side effects and of the mood swings with each medication; the therapist will adjust accordingly. It can take up to 6 months (sometimes more) for the body to adjust and be fine tuned to the medicine. Her husband might want to join a support group. If he doesn’t want to and/or cannot join a support group, he might want to join a support group online, at least once a week. The therapist can guide them. The following is extremely important: As the caregiver, her husband will need to take time of for self care too, or he can burn out and won’t be able to help in an effective way. He should not and cannot think he needs to take care of her 24/7. Because if he burns out he won’t be of help to either one. He should reach out to family members, friends and ask for help. If they live in a city without their relatives, he might want to ask members of the community they belong to for help (be it a church, or a similar group, religious or not, spiritual or not.) they need to believe in themselves, and keep the faith. Some days they might feel discouraged and have setbacks. It’s okay to have setbacks. Everyday is a fresh day. some tips for self care:self care for caregiversTake a break to remove yourself from the situation if it becomes overwhelmingBreathe deeply and slowly for a few minutesHave a relaxing bath or go for a walkAsk for help, delegate or share responsibilityWrite down your thoughts so they begin to make senseDo just one thing at a timeReduce your standards, if only temporarilyBook a short break if possibleMeet up with supportive friends and let off steamI hope this helps, I am cheering up for them.
